docs.title: About this book
docs.text: The English Book as it was written, in Hinglish (Hindi in the Roman script, with the English terms): the parts of speech, tenses and sentence building, pronunciation and everyday speaking, vocabulary, writing, and the mistakes learners really make. Every chapter ends with practice exercises with answers.

docs.title: Chapter 58: 50 sabse aam galtiyan
docs.text:
50 sabse aam galtiyan — ek hi jagah

Ye chapter padhne ke liye nahi, dhoondhne ke liye hai. Chhe groups hain — articles, tenses, prepositions, word choice, word order aur plurals. Har galti teen hisson me hai: galat → sahi → kyun. Jab likhte waqt shaq ho, is page par aao, apne group me jaao, aur aage badho. Mobile par bookmark kar lo.

Ek line me

In 50 me se lagbhag saari galtiyan ek hi wajah se hoti hain — Hindi ka dhaancha English ke shabdon me. Isliye "kyun" wala hissa sabse zaroori hai. Wajah samajh gaye to poora group theek ho jaata hai.

docs.title: 58.1 Kahan sabse zyada galtiyan hoti hain
docs.text:
Neeche ka chart batata hai ki Indian speakers ki likhai aur bol-chaal me kaunsa hissa sabse zyada pakda jaata hai. Agar time kam hai, to upar wale do groups se shuru karo — wahi sabse zyada farq laayenge.

Figure 58.1. Chhe groups, galti hone ki tarteeb me. Articles aur prepositions Hindi me hi nahi hote — isliye wahi sabse zyada chhoote hain.

docs.title: 58.2 Group 1 — Articles (galti 1 se 7)
docs.text:
Hindi me a, an, the jaisa kuch nahi hota. Isliye ye shabd dimaag me "bekaar" lagte hain aur chhoot jaate hain. Pakka rule: har singular countable noun ke aage kuch hona chahiye — a, an, the, my, this, one… kuch bhi, par khaali nahi.

1–7 · a / an / the

  • Galat: 1. I am going to market.
  • Sahi: I'm going to the market.

  • Kyun: Jo jagah dono jaante hain (mohalle ka bazaar) — wahan "the". Singular countable noun khaali nahi reh sakta.

  • Galat: 2. She is doctor.

  • Sahi: She's a doctor.

  • Kyun: Pesha batate waqt hamesha a/an lagta hai: a teacher, an engineer, a driver.

  • Galat: 3. He is a honest man.

  • Sahi: He's an honest man.

  • Kyun: a/an spelling se nahi, aawaz se tay hota hai. "Honest" ka H chup hai, isliye aawaz "o" se shuru — an. Isi tarah: an hour, par a university (aawaz "yoo").

  • Galat: 4. I like the music.

  • Sahi: I like music.

  • Kyun: Aam baat (general) me "the" nahi lagta. "The music" matlab wo khaas music jo abhi baj raha hai.

  • Galat: 5. He went to the Mumbai.

  • Sahi: He went to Mumbai.

  • Kyun: Shehron aur desho ke naam ke aage "the" nahi. Apwaad: the US, the UK, the Netherlands, the Philippines.

  • Galat: 6. I have an university degree.

  • Sahi: I have a university degree.

  • Kyun: "University" ki aawaz "yoo-" se shuru hoti hai — ye consonant jaisi aawaz hai, isliye "a".

  • Galat: 7. Please pass me salt.

  • Sahi: Please pass me the salt.
  • Kyun: Mez par rakha wahi namak — khaas cheez, isliye "the". Uncountable nouns ke saath bhi "the" lagta hai jab cheez khaas ho.

docs.title: 58.3 Group 2 — Tenses (8 se 16)
docs.text:
Hindi aur English ke tense ka dhaancha kaafi milta hai, par present perfect (have/has + done) Hindi me nahi hai. Isliye sabse zyada galtiyan wahi karwata hai.

8–16 · tenses

  • Galat: 8. I am working here since three years.
  • Sahi: I have been working here for three years.

  • Kyun: Do galtiyan ek saath: kaam jo pehle shuru hua aur abhi chal raha hai = have been + -ing. Aur duration ke saath "for", point ke saath "since".

  • Galat: 9. I didn't went to office.

  • Sahi: I didn't go to the office.

  • Kyun: "Did" pehle se past bata deta hai, isliye verb apne pehle roop me aata hai. Did + go, never did + went.

  • Galat: 10. He have finished the work.

  • Sahi: He has finished the work.

  • Kyun: He, she, it ke saath "has". I, we, you, they ke saath "have".

  • Galat: 11. I am having a car.

  • Sahi: I have a car.

  • Kyun: Maalikana haq batane wala "have" continuous nahi hota. Par khaana-peena ke matlab me chalta hai: "I'm having lunch."

  • Galat: 12. Yesterday I have gone to Delhi.

  • Sahi: Yesterday I went to Delhi.

  • Kyun: Jab past ka samay bataya ho (yesterday, last week, in 2019), to simple past aata hai — present perfect kabhi nahi.

  • Galat: 13. I will tell you when he will come.

  • Sahi: I'll tell you when he comes.

  • Kyun: "When", "if", "after", "before" ke baad future me bhi present tense aata hai. Ek vaakya me do "will" nahi.

  • Galat: 14. She is knowing the answer.

  • Sahi: She knows the answer.

  • Kyun: Soch aur ehsaas wale verbs continuous me nahi jaate: know, understand, believe, like, want, need, mean.

  • Galat: 15. I have my breakfast at eight every day.

  • Sahi: I have breakfast at eight every day.

  • Kyun: Roz ki aadat ke khaane ke saath "my" nahi lagta: have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner.

  • Galat: 16. By the time I reached, the train left.

  • Sahi: By the time I reached, the train had left.
  • Kyun: Past me do kaam hon, to jo pehle hua uske saath "had" lagta hai. Isi ko past perfect kehte hain.

docs.title: 58.4 Group 3 — Prepositions (17 se 25)
docs.text:
Hindi ka ek shabd English me teen prepositions ban jaata hai (me → in/on/at), aur kai English verbs ke baad koi preposition lagta hi nahi. Dono wajahon se galti hoti hai.

17–25 · prepositions

  • Galat: 17. Let's discuss about the plan.
  • Sahi: Let's discuss the plan.

  • Kyun: Discuss ke andar hi "about" ka matlab hai. Isi family me: enter the room, reach Delhi, order two teas, request a copy, consider my application.

  • Galat: 18. He is good in maths.

  • Sahi: He's good at maths.

  • Kyun: Kisi kaam me mahir hona = good at. Good with = cheezein sambhalne me achha (good with kids, good with numbers).

  • Galat: 19. I am afraid from dogs.

  • Sahi: I'm afraid of dogs.

  • Kyun: Dar hamesha "of". Isi tarah: tired of, proud of, ashamed of, capable of.

  • Galat: 20. She is married with an engineer.

  • Sahi: She's married to an engineer.

  • Kyun: Shaadi hamesha "married to". "Married with" ka matlab ban jaata hai "bachchon ke saath shaadi-shuda".

  • Galat: 21. Please explain me the process.

  • Sahi: Please explain the process to me.

  • Kyun: Explain, describe, suggest aur mention ke baad pehle cheez, phir "to" + insaan.

  • Galat: 22. I will reach at the station by six.

  • Sahi: I'll reach the station by six. / I'll arrive at the station by six.

  • Kyun: Reach ke baad seedha jagah. Arrive ke saath preposition lagta hai: arrive at (chhoti jagah), arrive in (shehar, desh).

  • Galat: 23. He died from cancer.

  • Sahi: He died of cancer.

  • Kyun: Bimari se maut = died of. Haadse ya chot se = died from injuries.

  • Galat: 24. I have been waiting since two hours.

  • Sahi: I've been waiting for two hours.

  • Kyun: For = kitni der (duration). Since = kab se (point). "Since 4 o'clock" sahi, "since two hours" galat.

  • Galat: 25. He is angry on me.

  • Sahi: He's angry with me.
  • Kyun: Insaan par gussa = angry with. Cheez ya haalat par = angry about the delay.

docs.title: 58.5 Group 4 — Word choice (26 se 35)
docs.text:
Yahan galti grammar ki nahi, shabd chunne ki hai. Aksar do shabd ek jaise lagte hain par kaam alag karte hain.

26–35 · shabd ka chunaav

  • Galat: 26. I will give the exam next month.
  • Sahi: I'll take the exam next month.

  • Kyun: Student exam take karta hai; teacher exam gives/sets karta hai. Hindi "dena" seedha ulta baith jaata hai.

  • Galat: 27. There is too much traffic — it's very bad.

  • Sahi: There's a lot of traffic.

  • Kyun: "Too much" ka matlab hai "zaroorat se zyada", sirf "bahut" nahi. Bahut ke liye "a lot of" ya "a great deal of".

  • Galat: 28. How much peoples came?

  • Sahi: How many people came?

  • Kyun: Do galtiyan: gin sakte ho to "many" (not much), aur "people" khud plural hai.

  • Galat: 29. I am boring in this class.

  • Sahi: I'm bored in this class.

  • Kyun: -ing = cheez kaisi hai (the class is boring). -ed = aap kaisa mehsoos kar rahe ho (I am bored). Isi tarah: interesting/interested, confusing/confused, tiring/tired.

  • Galat: 30. Myself Ravi.

  • Sahi: I'm Ravi.

  • Kyun: "Myself" reflexive pronoun hai (I hurt myself) — subject nahi ban sakta.

  • Galat: 31. Please revert back at the earliest.

  • Sahi: Please get back to me by Thursday.

  • Kyun: Revert me "waapas" pehle se hai, isliye "back" bekaar. Aur "at the earliest" ki jagah asli taarikh likho.

  • Galat: 32. He has less friends than me.

  • Sahi: He has fewer friends than me.

  • Kyun: Gin sakte ho to "fewer" (fewer friends, fewer errors). Gin nahi sakte to "less" (less water, less time).

  • Galat: 33. Its raining outside.

  • Sahi: It's raining outside.

  • Kyun: It's = it is. Its = uska (The dog wagged its tail). Apostrophe yahan possession nahi, shortcut batata hai.

  • Galat: 34. I can able to finish it today.

  • Sahi: I can finish it today. / I'm able to finish it today.

  • Kyun: Dono ek hi kaam karte hain — ek hi chuno. "Can able to" dono ko jod deta hai, jo galat hai.

  • Galat: 35. Open the light.

  • Sahi: Turn on the light. / Switch on the light.
  • Kyun: Hindi "kholna" English me do kaam karta hai. Darwaza open hota hai; light, fan aur TV turn on/off hote hain.

docs.title: 58.6 Group 5 — Word order (36 se 42)
docs.text:
Hindi ka kram hai Subject – Object – Verb (main khaana khaata hoon). English ka hai Subject – Verb – Object (I eat food). Sawaal me aur adjectives me ye farq sabse zyada dikhta hai.

36–42 · shabdon ka kram

  • Galat: 36. What you are doing?
  • Sahi: What are you doing?

  • Kyun: Sawaal me helping verb subject se pehle aata hai: What are you… / Where did he… / Why has she…

  • Galat: 37. Tell me where is the station.

  • Sahi: Tell me where the station is.

  • Kyun: Jab sawaal kisi bade vaakya ke andar aa jaaye, to kram seedha ho jaata hai — verb peechhe chala jaata hai.

  • Galat: 38. I yesterday went to the bank.

  • Sahi: I went to the bank yesterday.

  • Kyun: Samay ka shabd aakhir me (ya shuru me) aata hai — subject aur verb ke beech me nahi.

  • Galat: 39. She speaks very well English.

  • Sahi: She speaks English very well.

  • Kyun: Pehle object (English), phir adverb (very well). Verb aur uske object ke beech kuch nahi aata.

  • Galat: 40. He gave to me the keys.

  • Sahi: He gave me the keys. / He gave the keys to me.

  • Kyun: Do hi kram sahi hain: verb + insaan + cheez, ya verb + cheez + to + insaan. Beech wala roop galat hai.

  • Galat: 41. A red big plastic box.

  • Sahi: A big red plastic box.

  • Kyun: Adjectives ka kram tay hai: raay → aakaar → umar → rang → kahan ka → kis cheez ka. "Big" (aakaar) "red" (rang) se pehle.

  • Galat: 42. Only I have one question.

  • Sahi: I have only one question.
  • Kyun: "Only" jis shabd par zor dena hai, uske bilkul pehle aata hai. Jagah badlo, matlab badal jaata hai.

docs.title: 58.7 Group 6 — Plurals aur countables (43 se 50)
docs.text:
English me kuch cheezein gini nahi jaa sakti, aur Hindi me wahi cheezein aaraam se gini jaati hain. Yahi tak-raar in aath galtiyon ki jad hai.

43–50 · plural aur ginti

  • Galat: 43. I need some informations.
  • Sahi: I need some information. / I need a few details.

  • Kyun: Information uncountable hai — "s" kabhi nahi lagta. Ginti karni ho to: two pieces of information.

  • Galat: 44. He gave me good advices.

  • Sahi: He gave me good advice. / He gave me a piece of advice.

  • Kyun: Advice uncountable hai. Isi list me: furniture, luggage, equipment, machinery, traffic, homework, research, feedback, knowledge.

  • Galat: 45. My hairs are wet.

  • Sahi: My hair is wet.

  • Kyun: Sir ke saare baal milkar "hair" (uncountable) hote hain. "Hairs" ka matlab ek-ek baal — jo khaane me milte hain!

  • Galat: 46. There are many equipments in the lab.

  • Sahi: There's a lot of equipment in the lab.

  • Kyun: Equipment uncountable hai, isliye "many" bhi badal kar "a lot of" karna padta hai aur verb singular ho jaata hai.

  • Galat: 47. Peoples are waiting outside.

  • Sahi: People are waiting outside.

  • Kyun: "People" khud plural hai (person ka plural). "Peoples" ka matlab hai "kai qaumein" — bilkul alag baat.

  • Galat: 48. I bought two pant and three shirt.

  • Sahi: I bought two pairs of trousers and three shirts.

  • Kyun: Shirt countable hai, isliye "shirts". Trousers/pants hamesha plural hote hain, aur ginti "pairs" se hoti hai — jaise scissors aur glasses.

  • Galat: 49. Each of the students have a laptop.

  • Sahi: Each of the students has a laptop.

  • Kyun: Each, every, everyone, nobody — ye sab singular hain, chahe baad me plural dikhe. Isi tarah: "Everyone is here."

  • Galat: 50. The news are not good.

  • Sahi: The news is not good.
  • Kyun: "News" ke aakhir me "s" hai par wo singular hai. Isi tarah: mathematics, physics, economics, politics — sab singular verb lete hain.

docs.title: 58.8 Teen rules jo 50 me se 30 bacha dete hain
docs.text:
Ratne layak teen cheezein

1. Har singular countable noun ke aage kuch hona chahiye — a, an, the, my, this. Khaali kabhi nahi. 2. Ek vaakya me tense ek hi baar batao — did + go, will + come, has + finished. Do jagah past mat lagao. 3. English me verb seedha object ko pakadta hai — beech me samay, adverb ya "to me" nahi ghusta.

docs.title: 58.9 Pakki jodiyan — inhe rata hi lena behtar hai
docs.text:
Kuch adjectives aur verbs ke saath preposition fix hota hai. Inme logic dhoondhne ka faayda nahi — ye jodiyan hain, inhe jodi ki tarah yaad karo. Group 3 aur 4 ki aadhi galtiyan yahi table rok deti hai.

Jodi Example Jo log galti se bolte hain good at good at cricket good in afraid of afraid of heights afraid from married to married to a teacher married with angry with (insaan) angry with me angry on me angry about (cheez) angry about the delay angry for the delay die of (bimari) died of a heart attack died from a heart attack depend on it depends on you depends from you listen to listen to me listen me explain to explain it to me explain me agree with (insaan) I agree with you I am agree with you interested in interested in design interested for design responsible for responsible for payroll responsible of payroll congratulate on congratulate her on the win congratulate her for the win apologise for apologise for the delay apologise of the delay no preposition discuss · enter · reach · order · request · consider · marry discuss about, enter into, reach at…

docs.title: 58.10 Chhe sahi vaakya — zor se bolo
docs.text:
Har group se ek sudhra hua vaakya. Inhe sunne aur bolne se rule ratne se zyada jaldi baithta hai — kyunki kaan galti pakadna seekh jaata hai.

  • She's a doctor at the hospital near the market. Articles — pesha ke saath "a", jaani-pehchaani jagah ke saath "the".
  • I've been working here for three years. Tenses — kaam pehle shuru hua, abhi chal raha hai; duration ke saath "for".
  • He's good at maths but he's afraid of exams. Prepositions — good at, afraid of. Ye jodiyan fix hain.
  • I'll take the exam next month, so please get back to me by Friday. Word choice — exam "take" karte hain, aur "revert back" ki jagah "get back to me".
  • Could you tell me where the station is? Word order — sawaal bade vaakya ke andar aaya, to verb peechhe chala gaya.
  • The news is good, and each of the teams has its own budget. Plurals — "news" aur "each" dono singular verb lete hain.

Is page ko kaise use karein

Ek baar poora padho — sirf ek baar. Phir ise sirf zaroorat par kholo. Jab ek galti teen baar pakdo, to wo apne aap theek ho jaati hai. Poori list ratne ki koshish karne se kuch nahi hota.

docs.title: 58.11 Practice — 50 galtiyan
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Kaunsa vaakya sahi hai?

  • He is an honest man with a university degree.
  • He is a honest man with an university degree.
  • He is an honest man with an university degree.
  • He is a honest man with a university degree.

Hint: a/an aawaz se tay hota hai, spelling se nahi.

Jawaab

He is an honest man with a university degree.

Honest ka H chup hai, aawaz 'o' se shuru — an. University ki aawaz 'yoo' se shuru hoti hai, jo consonant jaisi hai — a.

Exercise 2

'Main teen saal se yahan kaam kar raha hoon' ka sahi roop?

  • I have been working here for three years.
  • I am working here since three years.
  • I work here since three years.
  • I am working here for three years only.
Jawaab

I have been working here for three years.

Jo kaam pehle shuru hua aur abhi chal raha hai = have been + -ing. Aur duration ke saath 'for', point ke saath 'since'.

Exercise 3

Kaunsa vaakya galat hai?

  • She is married with an engineer.
  • She is married to an engineer.
  • He is afraid of dogs.
  • He is angry with me.
Jawaab

She is married with an engineer.

Shaadi hamesha 'married to'. 'Married with' ka matlab ban jaata hai bachchon ke saath shaadi-shuda.

Exercise 4

Student exam ke saath kaunsa verb lagta hai?

  • take the exam
  • give the exam
  • do the exam paper only
  • put the exam
Jawaab

take the exam

Student exam take karta hai; teacher exam gives ya sets karta hai. Hindi 'dena' seedha ulta baith jaata hai.

Exercise 5

Adjectives ka sahi kram kaunsa hai?

  • a big red plastic box
  • a red big plastic box
  • a plastic big red box
  • a red plastic big box

Hint: Aakaar pehle, rang baad me.

Jawaab

a big red plastic box

Kram tay hai: raay → aakaar → umar → rang → kahan ka → kis cheez ka. Isliye big (aakaar) red (rang) se pehle.

Exercise 6

I have been waiting ___ two hours.

Hint: Duration hai ya point?

Jawaab

for

For = kitni der. Since = kab se. 'Since 4 o'clock' sahi hai, 'since two hours' galat.

Exercise 7

He has ___ friends than me, but they are good ones.

Hint: Dost gine jaa sakte hain.

Jawaab

fewer

Gin sakte ho to fewer (fewer friends, fewer errors). Gin nahi sakte to less (less water, less time).

Exercise 8

Each of the students ___ a laptop.

Hint: Each singular hai ya plural?

Jawaab

has

Each, every, everyone, nobody — sab singular hain, chahe baad me plural dikhe.

Exercise 9

Please ___ on the light, it's getting dark.

Hint: Light 'open' nahi hoti.

Jawaab

turn / switch

Hindi 'kholna' do kaam karta hai. Darwaza open hota hai; light, fan aur TV turn on/off hote hain.

Exercise 10

Galat shabd dhoondo.

I didn't went to the office yesterday.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: went.

Sahi roop: I didn't go to the office yesterday.

'Did' pehle se past bata deta hai, isliye verb apne pehle roop me aata hai — did + go.

Exercise 11

Ek shabd me 's' bekaar hai — us par tap karo.

He gave me some very useful advices.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: advices.

Sahi roop: He gave me some very useful advice.

Advice uncountable hai. Isi list me: information, furniture, luggage, equipment, feedback, homework.

Exercise 12

Kram galat hai — galat jagah wale shabd par tap karo.

Tell me where is the station please.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: is.

Sahi roop: Tell me where the station is, please.

Jab sawaal bade vaakya ke andar aa jaaye, to kram seedha ho jaata hai — verb peechhe chala jaata hai.

Exercise 13

Ek shabd galat hai — use dhoondo.

My hairs are wet because of the rain.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: hairs.

Sahi roop: My hair is wet because of the rain.

Sir ke saare baal milkar 'hair' (uncountable) hote hain, isliye verb bhi 'is' ho jaata hai.

Exercise 14

Galat roop ko uske sahi roop se jodo.

A B discuss about the plan good at maths explain me this afraid of dogs good in maths discuss the plan afraid from dogs explain this to me Jawaab

discuss about the plan — discuss the plan; explain me this — explain this to me; good in maths — good at maths; afraid from dogs — afraid of dogs

Kuch verbs ke baad preposition nahi lagta, aur kuch adjectives ki apni fix jodi hoti hai.

Exercise 15

Shabd ko uski kism se jodo.

A B information 's' hai par singular people hamesha plural, pairs me gine news uncountable — 's' nahi trousers khud plural hai Jawaab

information — uncountable — 's' nahi; people — khud plural hai; news — 's' hai par singular; trousers — hamesha plural, pairs me gine

Ginti wale rules yaad rakhne se Group 6 ki lagbhag saari galtiyan apne aap khatam ho jaati hain.

Exercise 16

Sahi kram banao.

Shabd: very / She / English / speaks / well

Jawaab

She speaks English very well

Pehle object (English), phir adverb (very well). Verb aur object ke beech kuch nahi aata.

Exercise 17

Sawaal sahi kram me banao.

Shabd: What / this / are / evening / you / doing

Jawaab

What are you doing this evening

Sawaal me helping verb (are) subject (you) se pehle aata hai.

Exercise 18

Ye line bolo — isme teen group ke sudhaar ek saath hain.

Jawaab

Bolo: I have been working here for three years and I am good at my job

Tense (have been working), preposition (for, good at), aur word order — teeno ek hi line me theek baithe hain.

docs.title: Chapter 21: Active aur Passive
docs.text:
Active aur Passive — kaun aage, kaun peeche

Voice ka matlab grammar me "aawaz" nahi hota. Voice ka matlab hai — vaakya me kiski kahani hai. Active voice me karne wala aage hota hai ("Ravi ne kaam kiya"), aur passive voice me jis par kaam hua wo aage aa jaata hai ("kaam kiya gaya"). Hindi me hum ye roz karte hain, isliye idea naya nahi hai — bas English ka formula seekhna hai, aur ye jaanna hai ki kab passive use karna chahiye aur kab bilkul nahi.

Ek line me

Passive voice = correct form of "be" + V3 (past participle). Bas itna hi formula hai. Tense badalta hai to sirf "be" badalta hai — V3 kabhi nahi badalta.

docs.title: 21.1 Jagah badalne ka naksha
docs.text:
Active se passive banate waqt sirf teen cheezein hoti hain: subject aur object apni jagah badalte hain, verb "be + V3" ban jaata hai, aur purana subject "by" ke peeche chala jaata hai. Tasveer me dekho —

Figure 21.1. Neela = karne wala (agent). Baingani = jis par kaam hua (object). Passive me baingani aage aa jaata hai aur neela by ke peeche chala jaata hai.

Paanch kadam — active se passive

1. Object ko aage le aao (aur pronoun ho to subject roop me badlo: me → I, him → he). 2. Tense ke hisaab se sahi "be" chuno. 3. Main verb ko V3 me badlo. 4. Purana subject "by" ke saath aakhir me. 5. Agar karne wala zaroori nahi hai, "by…" hata do.

docs.title: 21.2 Saare tenses ka passive
docs.text:
Dhyaan do ki dayein column me V3 (eaten) kabhi nahi badalta. Sirf "be" ka roop badalta hai. Yahi poora table ek hi idea par khada hai.

Tense Active Passive (be + V3) Present Simple She eats the mango. The mango is eaten by her. Present Continuous She is eating the mango. The mango is being eaten by her. Present Perfect She has eaten the mango. The mango has been eaten by her. Past Simple She ate the mango. The mango was eaten by her. Past Continuous She was eating the mango. The mango was being eaten by her. Past Perfect She had eaten the mango. The mango had been eaten by her. Future Simple She will eat the mango. The mango will be eaten by her. Future Perfect She will have eaten it. It will have been eaten by her. Modal She can eat it. It can be eaten by her. Infinitive She wants to eat it. It wants to be eaten.

Do tenses ka passive nahi banta

Future Continuous aur Perfect Continuous (sabhi teen) ka passive practical English me nahi banaya jaata. "The work will be being done" jaisa vaakya vyaakaran se ban sakta hai, par koi nahi bolta. Aise mauke par active hi rakho.

docs.title: 21.3 Sawaal aur order ka passive
docs.text: Kism Active Passive Yes/no sawaal Did he write the letter? Was the letter written by him? WH sawaal Who wrote this? By whom was this written? Order (positive) Close the door. Let the door be closed. Order (negative) Don't touch the wires. Let the wires not be touched. Advice / rule You should submit the form. The form should be submitted.

docs.title: 21.4 Do object wale verbs — do passive ban sakte hain
docs.text:
give, send, teach, offer, tell, show, pay, lend — in verbs ke paas do object hote hain (kisko + kya). Isliye do tarah ka passive banta hai, aur dono sahi hain.

  • Active: The company gave Ravi a laptop.
  • Passive 1: Ravi was given a laptop. Insaan ko aage rakha — bolne me ye zyada natural hai.
  • Passive 2: A laptop was given to Ravi. Cheez ko aage rakha — dhyaan laptop par hai.

docs.title: 21.5 Passive kab use karein — chaar asli mauke
docs.text:
Wajah Example Kyun passive behtar hai Karne wala pata nahi My bike was stolen last night. Kaun chura kar gaya, pata nahi — to "by…" ki zaroorat hi nahi. Karne wala zaroori nahi The road is being repaired. Kaun repair kar raha hai, is se matlab nahi. Kaam zaroori hai. Prakriya / vigyaan ki baat Water is heated to 100 °C and then cooled. Science aur recipe me step zaroori hote hain, insaan nahi. Shisht ya tatastha rehna A mistake has been made in the bill. Ilzaam kisi par nahi daala — office aur email me ye bahut kaam aata hai. Niyam aur soochna Smoking is not allowed here. Niyam sab par laagoo hai — kisi khaas insaan ki baat nahi.

Office aur email me passive ka jaadu

"You did not send the report." → ilzaam jaisa lagta hai. "The report has not been received yet." → wahi baat, bina ladaai. Isi wajah se passive professional English ka zaroori hissa hai.

docs.title: 21.6 Passive kab nahi use karein
docs.text:
Yahan ek badi galatfehmi hai. School me hum passive ko "achhi English" samajhte hain, aur phir har jagah thoos dete hain. Sach ulta hai: roz ki English me 85% se zyada vaakya active hote hain. Passive tab aata hai jab uski wajah ho.

Jahan passive bhaari aur bura lagta hai

  • Galat: The decision to go to Shimla was taken by us.
  • Sahi: We decided to go to Shimla.

  • Kyun: Karne wala saaf pata hai aur zaroori hai — to use aage rakho. Active chhota, saaf aur taakatwar hai.

  • Galat: Tea is being drunk by me.

  • Sahi: I am drinking tea.

  • Kyun: Roz ki baat-cheet me aisa passive banaawati lagta hai. Koi native speaker aisa nahi bolega.

  • Galat: The bus was arrived at six.

  • Sahi: The bus arrived at six.

  • Kyun: Intransitive verbs (jinka object nahi hota — arrive, come, go, sleep, die, happen, laugh) ka passive nahi banta.

  • Galat: He was died in 2019.

  • Sahi: He died in 2019.
  • Kyun: "Die" intransitive hai. Haan, "born" ulta hai — wo hamesha passive me aata hai: I was born in Patna.

Faisla lene ka sawaal

Passive banane se pehle ek sawaal poochho: "Kahani kiski hai?" Agar karne wale ki — active. Agar jis par kaam hua uski, ya karne wala pata/zaroori nahi — passive. Sirf "formal lagne ke liye" passive kabhi na banao.

docs.title: "by" hata dena bilkul theek hai
docs.text:
Lagbhag 80% passive vaakyon me "by…" likha hi nahi jaata, kyunki karne wala zaroori nahi hota. Exam me "by" maangte hain, asli English me nahi.

  • English is spoken all over the world. "by people" likhne ki zaroorat nahi — sab samajh jaate hain.

docs.title: "get" wala passive — bolne me bahut chalta hai
docs.text: be wala passive get wala passive Feel My phone was repaired. My phone got repaired. zyada bol-chaal wala He was selected. He got selected. achaanak hua, khushi wali baat The glass was broken. The glass got broken. galti se hua

docs.title: 21.8 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Passive ki top galtiyan

  • Galat: The letter is wrote by him.
  • Sahi: The letter is written by him.

  • Kyun: Passive me hamesha V3 aata hai, V2 nahi. write–wrote–written.

  • Galat: The work is completed yesterday.

  • Sahi: The work was completed yesterday.

  • Kyun: Tense "be" me dikhta hai. Past ki baat hai to "was/were" chahiye.

  • Galat: The matter is being discussed about.

  • Sahi: The matter is being discussed.

  • Kyun: "Discuss" ke baad "about" nahi lagta — active me bhi nahi, passive me bhi nahi.

  • Galat: The thief was caught by the police yesterday by them.

  • Sahi: The thief was caught by the police yesterday.

  • Kyun: "by" ek hi baar. Karne wala ek baar bata diya, bas.

  • Galat: This book is belonged to me.

  • Sahi: This book belongs to me.

  • Kyun: Kuch verbs ka passive nahi hota — belong, resemble, lack, consist, have (paas hona), suit, fit.

  • Galat: I born in Lucknow.

  • Sahi: I was born in Lucknow.
  • Kyun: "Born" hamesha passive me aata hai — was/were born. Ye yaad rakhne wali cheez hai.

docs.title: 21.9 Practice — Active aur Passive
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Passive banao: 'Shakespeare wrote this play.'

  • This play is written by Shakespeare.
  • This play was wrote by Shakespeare.
  • This play was written by Shakespeare.
  • This play has written by Shakespeare.

Hint: Past Simple ka passive kaunsa 'be' leta hai?

Jawaab

This play was written by Shakespeare.

Past Simple ka passive = was/were + V3. Isliye 'was written' — 'was wrote' kabhi nahi, kyunki passive me V3 aata hai.

Exercise 2

Passive banao: 'They are repairing the road.'

  • The road is repaired.
  • The road is being repaired.
  • The road was being repaired.
  • The road has been repaired.

Hint: Continuous ka passive me 'being' aata hai.

Jawaab

The road is being repaired.

Present Continuous ka passive = am/is/are + being + V3. 'Being' hi continuous ka nishaan hai.

Exercise 3

In me se kis vaakya ka passive NAHI ban sakta?

  • She sang a song.
  • The baby slept quietly.
  • He painted the wall.
  • They built a bridge.

Hint: Object kis me nahi hai?

Jawaab

The baby slept quietly.

'Sleep' intransitive verb hai — iska koi object nahi. Jis verb ka object nahi, uska passive nahi banta.

Exercise 4

Kis haalat me passive sabse behtar hai?

  • Jab karne wala pata nahi hai
  • Jab vaakya chhota karna ho
  • Jab formal lagna ho
  • Jab verb mushkil ho

Hint: Karne wale ke baare me socho.

Jawaab

Jab karne wala pata nahi hai

Passive ka asli kaam hai — jab karne wala pata na ho, zaroori na ho, ya uska naam nahi lena ho. Sirf 'formal lagne' ke liye passive banana galti hai.

Exercise 5

The thieves ___ arrested by the police last night.

Hint: Plural subject, past ki baat.

Jawaab

were

Subject 'thieves' plural hai aur baat past ki hai — isliye 'were arrested'. Singular hota to 'was arrested'.

Exercise 6

Rice ___ grown in many parts of India.

Hint: General sach hai — kaunsa tense?

Jawaab

is

General sach ke liye Present Simple, aur 'rice' uncountable singular hai — isliye 'is grown'.

Exercise 7

I ___ born in Jaipur.

Hint: Ye hamesha passive me aata hai.

Jawaab

was

'Born' ke saath hamesha was/were aata hai. 'I born' ya 'I am born' dono galat hain.

Exercise 8

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — galat shabd par tap karo.

The homework was did by all the students.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: did.

Sahi roop: The homework was done by all the students.

Passive me V3 aata hai. do–did–done, isliye 'was done'. 'Was did' kabhi nahi.

Exercise 9

Galat shabd dhoondo.

My grandfather was died two years ago.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: was.

Sahi roop: My grandfather died two years ago.

'Die' intransitive hai, iska passive nahi banta. Seedha 'died' bolna hai.

Exercise 10

Ek shabd galat hai — pakdo.

This land is belonged to my uncle.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: belonged.

Sahi roop: This land belongs to my uncle.

'Belong' ka passive nahi hota. Aise verbs — belong, resemble, consist, lack — hamesha active me rehte hain.

Exercise 11

Sahi kram me passive vaakya banao.

Shabd: bridge / new / The / next / will / opened / month / be

Jawaab

The new bridge will be opened next month

Future ka passive = will + be + V3. 'Will be opened' — yahan 'be' ka roop kabhi nahi badalta, bas 'will' ke baad seedha 'be' aata hai.

Exercise 12

Active roop ko uske sahi passive se jodo.

A B She writes letters Letters have been written by her She wrote letters Letters are being written by her She has written letters Letters will be written by her She is writing letters Letters are written by her She will write letters Letters were written by her Jawaab

She writes letters — Letters are written by her; She wrote letters — Letters were written by her; She has written letters — Letters have been written by her; She is writing letters — Letters are being written by her; She will write letters — Letters will be written by her

Dekho — V3 'written' har baar wahi hai. Sirf 'be' ka roop badalta hai: are / were / have been / are being / will be.

Exercise 13

Ab ye line bol ke dekho — office me kaam aane wala shisht passive.

Jawaab

Bolo: The report has not been received yet

Yahi baat active me 'You did not send the report' hoti, jo ilzaam jaisi lagti hai. Passive se baat ho jaati hai aur ladaai nahi hoti — isiliye email me ye roop bahut kaam aata hai.

Aage kya karein

Ek kaam karo: apna koi purana email ya assignment kholo aur har passive vaakya ko active me badal kar padho. Jahan active zyada saaf lage — wahan passive ki zaroorat nahi thi. Do-teen baar ye karne se passive ka sahi istemaal apne-aap samajh me aa jaata hai.

docs.title: Chapter 9: Adjective — kaisa hai
docs.text:
Adjective — kaisa hai, kitna hai, kaunsa hai

Adjective wo shabd hai jo noun ke baare me kuch batata hai — kaisa, kitna, kaunsa, kiska. Ek hi adjective badal kar poora vaakya badal jaata hai: a house aur a beautiful old wooden house me zameen-aasmaan ka farq hai. Is chapter ka sabse qeemti hissa aakhir me hai — adjectives ka kram, wo rule jo native log naam se nahi jaante, par kabhi todte bhi nahi.

Ek line me

An adjective describes or limits a noun or pronoun. Jo noun ke baare me batata ho — kaisa, kitna, kaunsa — wo adjective hai.

  • She has a sharp memory. "sharp" bata raha hai memory kaisi hai.
  • Three boys were waiting outside. "three" bata raha hai kitne — ye bhi adjective hai.
  • The tea is cold. Adjective noun ke baad bhi aa sakta hai — linking verb ke zariye.

docs.title: 9.1 Adjective kahan baithta hai — do jagah
docs.text:
Jagah Naam Example Noun se pehle Attributive a heavy bag · an honest man Linking verb ke baad Predicative The bag is heavy. · He seems honest.

Kuch adjectives sirf ek hi jagah chalte hain

asleep, alive, awake, afraid, alone, ill — ye sirf verb ke baad aate hain. ✓ The baby is asleep. ✗ an asleep baby (iske liye "a sleeping baby" bolo). Doosri taraf main, mere, elder, former sirf noun se pehle aate hain — the main road, par "The road is main" galat hai.

docs.title: 9.2 Adjective ke prakaar
docs.text: Prakaar Kya batata hai Examples Quality kaisa hai a clever boy, tall building, red cloth Quantity kitna (bina ginti) some water, much noise, enough time Number kitne (ginti me) five books, second chance, many people Demonstrative kaunsa — ishaara this pen, those chairs Possessive kiska my bag, their house Interrogative sawaal Which shirt? Whose turn? Distributive alag-alag each student, every day, neither option Proper khaas naam se bana Mughal architecture, Bengali sweets Emphasizing zor dena with my own eyes, the very thing Article khaas ya aam a boy, an apple, the boy

docs.title: Emphasizing adjective — "own" aur "very"
docs.text:
Ye adjective noun ke baare me koi nayi jaankari nahi deta — bas us par zor deta hai. Hindi ka "apni hi", "khud ki", "wahi" wala bhaav.

  • I saw it with my own eyes. Maine apni khud ki aankhon se dekha — kisi se suna nahi.
  • This is the very thing I was looking for. Bilkul wahi cheez jo main dhoondh raha tha.
  • She runs her own business. Uska apna business — kisi aur ka nahi.

'very' adjective ya adverb?

the very man — noun se pehle, "the" ke baad → adjective (wahi aadmi). very tall — adjective se pehle → adverb (bahut lamba). "own" hamesha possessive ke baad aata hai: my own, his own, their own — "a own house" nahi.

docs.title: Quick guide — kaunsa prakaar kis sawaal ka jawaab
docs.text:
Type Kaam / sawaal Example Quality What kind? (kaisa?) a kind man Quantity How much? (kitna?) some milk Number How many? / Which order? (kitne, kaunsa number?) three pens, the first boy Demonstrative Which one? (kaunsa — ishaara) that house Possessive Whose? (kiska?) our teacher Interrogative Used in questions (sawaal me) Which bus? Distributive One at a time (ek-ek karke) every child Proper From a proper noun (khaas naam se) Indian tea Emphasizing Gives emphasis (zor deta hai) my own eyes

many / much aur few / little — ye gadbad hoti hai

Countable Uncountable Bahut many books much water Thoda (kam, negative feel) few friends little money Thoda (kaafi, positive feel) a few friends a little money

"few friends" = bahut kam dost (dukh). "a few friends" = kuch dost hain (theek hai). Ek "a" se poora bhaav palat jaata hai.

docs.title: 9.3 Degrees of comparison — teen seedhiyan
docs.text:
Jab do ya zyada cheezein compare karni ho, adjective apna roop badalta hai. Teen seedhiyan hain: positive → comparative → superlative.

Kaise banta hai Positive Comparative Superlative Chhote shabd: + er / est tall taller tallest -e par khatam: + r / st large larger largest consonant + y: y → ier / iest happy happier happiest ek vowel + ek consonant: akshar double big bigger biggest Lambe shabd: more / most beautiful more beautiful most beautiful Bilkul alag (irregular) good better best

docs.title: Irregular comparisons — yaad karne wale
docs.text:
Positive Comparative Superlative Dhyan good better best — bad worse worst — little less least uncountable ke liye many / much more most — far farther / further farthest / furthest farther = doori, further = aur zyada late later / latter latest / last latest = sabse naya, last = aakhri old older / elder oldest / eldest elder sirf parivaar me

Comparative aur superlative ke saath kya lagta hai

Comparative ke saath than — She is taller than her brother. Superlative ke saath the — She is the tallest in the class. Do ki tulna me comparative, teen ya zyada me superlative.

Double comparative — sabse pehchaani galti

  • Galat: He is more taller than me.
  • Sahi: He is taller than I am.

  • Kyun: "taller" me -er pehle se comparative bana chuka hai — uske aage "more" lagana dohraav hai. Ek adjective par ek hi baar comparison lagta hai: ya -er, ya more. Hindi me "zyada lamba" bolte hain, isliye "more" ghus jaata hai.

  • Galat: She is the most cleverest girl.

  • Sahi: She is the cleverest girl.
  • Kyun: Wahi galti superlative me — "cleverest" ke aage "most" extra hai.

Ye adjectives compare hi nahi hote

perfect, unique, complete, dead, round, square, impossible, full, empty — ye absolute hain. "More perfect", "very unique" technically galat hai, kyunki perfect se aage kuch hota hi nahi.

docs.title: 9.4 Adjectives ka kram — chapter ka sabse qeemti hissa
docs.text:
Jab ek noun ke saath do-teen adjectives aate hain, unka ek pakka kram hota hai. Hum log aksar is kram ko tod dete hain, aur phir vaakya grammar me sahi hone ke baad bhi "ajeeb" lagta hai. Native speaker ko rule yaad nahi hota — kaan yaad rakhta hai. Hum rule se shuru karenge, kaan baad me ban jaayega.

Figure 9.1. Adjective train: engine (noun) sabse aage, aur dabbe isi kram me peeche jude hote hain. # Shreni Sawaal Examples 1 Opinion mujhe kaisa lagta hai? lovely, ugly, boring, delicious 2 Size kitna bada? big, small, tall, long 3 Age kitna purana? old, new, young, ancient 4 Shape kis aakaar ka? round, square, flat 5 Colour kaunsa rang? red, black, golden 6 Origin kahan ka? Indian, Chinese, Punjabi 7 Material kis cheez ka bana? wooden, silk, steel, plastic 8 Purpose kis kaam ke liye? writing (desk), sleeping (bag)

Kram todne se banti galtiyan

  • Galat: a red big balloon
  • Sahi: a big red balloon

  • Kyun: Size (2) colour (5) se pehle aata hai. Dabbe ka number yaad rakho.

  • Galat: a cotton white shirt

  • Sahi: a white cotton shirt

  • Kyun: Material (7) noun ke sabse paas baithta hai, colour (5) usse pehle.

  • Galat: an old beautiful temple

  • Sahi: a beautiful old temple

  • Kyun: Opinion (1) sabse door baithta hai, age (3) uske baad.

  • Galat: a steel small Japanese watch

  • Sahi: a small Japanese steel watch
  • Kyun: Teeno ulat gaye the. Sahi kram: size (2) → origin (6) → material (7). Aankh band karke socho — train ke dabbe kis number par hain.

Teen se zyada mat lagao

Rule aath ka hai, par asli English me do-teen adjectives se zyada bahut kam aate hain. Zyada lagane se vaakya bhari lagta hai. Chaar chahiye to comma ya "and" use karo, ya vaakya tod do.

docs.title: 9.5 Adjective se Adverb — kab -ly lagta hai
docs.text:
Adjective noun ke saath, adverb verb ke saath. Zyadatar adjectives me -ly lagane se adverb ban jaata hai.

Adjective Adverb Noun ke saath Verb ke saath careful carefully a careful driver drives carefully quick quickly a quick answer answered quickly happy happily a happy child played happily good well good English speaks well fast fast a fast car runs fast hard hard hard work works hard

good aur well

✓ Her English is good. (noun ke baare me) ✓ She speaks English well. (verb ke baare me) ✗ She speaks English good. "good" adjective hai, "well" adverb — ye jodi hamesha yaad rakho.

docs.title: 9.6 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Adjective ki aam Indian-English galtiyan

  • Galat: My brother is more taller than me.
  • Sahi: My brother is taller than I am.

  • Kyun: Ek adjective par ek hi comparison — ya -er, ya more. Hindi me "zyada lamba" bolte hain, isliye English me dono lag jaate hain.

  • Galat: She is senior than me.

  • Sahi: She is senior to me.

  • Kyun: Kuch adjectives — senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior, preferable — "than" ke bajaye to lete hain, kyunki ye Latin se aaye hain.

  • Galat: This is the most best option.

  • Sahi: This is the best option.

  • Kyun: "Best" khud hi superlative hai — usse aage kuch nahi hota. Isi tarah "most worst", "more better" bhi galat hain.

  • Galat: She speaks very good English… and she speaks English good.

  • Sahi: She speaks very good English… and she speaks English well.

  • Kyun: Pehla theek hai (good + noun English). Doosre me verb hai, isliye adverb chahiye — well.

  • Galat: He bought a new nice phone.

  • Sahi: He bought a nice new phone.

  • Kyun: Opinion (nice) age (new) se pehle aata hai. Dono ulat jaane par vaakya galat nahi lagta, par native kaan ko turant chubhta hai.

  • Galat: I have less friends in this city.

  • Sahi: I have fewer friends in this city.

  • Kyun: Gine ja sakne wale noun ke saath "fewer", aur uncountable ke saath "less" — less water, fewer bottles.

  • Galat: My all books are new.

  • Sahi: All my books are new.

  • Kyun: "All, both, half" possessive se pehle aate hain — all my, both your, half his. Hindi ka "mere saare" ulta utar aata hai.

  • Galat: She is my elder than me.

  • Sahi: She is older than me. / She is my elder sister.
  • Kyun: "Elder" sirf noun se pehle, parivaar me — elder brother, elder sister. Tulna karni ho to "older than" bolo.

docs.title: 9.7 Chhota naksha
docs.text:
Chaar cheezein yaad rakho

1. Adjective noun ko batata hai; verb ko adverb batata hai. 2. Ek adjective par ek hi comparison — ya -er, ya more. 3. Comparative ke saath than, superlative ke saath the. 4. Kai adjectives ho to kram: opinion sabse door, material sabse paas.

docs.title: 9.8 Practice — Adjectives
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Kaunsa kram sahi hai?

  • a beautiful big old house
  • a big beautiful old house
  • an old big beautiful house
  • a big old beautiful house

Hint: Opinion kahan baithta hai, size kahan?

Jawaab

a beautiful big old house

Kram hai opinion (beautiful) → size (big) → age (old). Opinion sabse door baithta hai kyunki wo sabse zyada mera apna faisla hai, aur baaki tathya hain.

Exercise 2

She is ___ than her sister.

  • taller
  • more taller
  • tallest
  • more tall

Hint: Ek adjective par kitne comparison?

Jawaab

taller

'taller' me -er pehle se comparison bana chuka hai, isliye 'more' lagana dohraav ho jaata hai. Chhote adjectives me -er lagta hai, more nahi.

Exercise 3

He is ___ to me in the office.

  • senior
  • more senior than
  • seniorer
  • most senior

Hint: Kuch adjectives 'than' nahi lete.

Jawaab

senior

Senior, junior, superior, inferior — ye Latin se aaye hain aur 'to' lete hain, 'than' nahi. Isliye 'senior to me' sahi hai.

Exercise 4

I have ___ books than you.

  • fewer
  • less
  • lesser
  • little

Hint: Books gine ja sakte hain.

Jawaab

fewer

Countable noun ke saath 'fewer' lagta hai aur uncountable ke saath 'less' — fewer books, less water. Books gin sakte hain, isliye fewer.

Exercise 5

She sings very ___. (adverb form of 'good')

Hint: Verb ke baare me batana hai, noun ke nahi.

Jawaab

well

'sings' verb hai, aur verb ke baare me batane wala shabd adverb hota hai. 'good' ka adverb 'well' hai — isliye 'sings well'.

Exercise 6

This is the ___ day of my life. (superlative of 'happy')

Hint: consonant + y par khatam hone wale shabd ka rule.

Jawaab

happiest

consonant ke baad -y aaye to y hat kar -iest lagta hai: happy → happiest. 'most happy' bolna galat nahi par bhaari lagta hai.

Exercise 7

Is vaakya me kram galat hai — galat jagah wale shabd par tap karo.

He wore a cotton white kurta to the wedding.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: cotton.

Sahi roop: He wore a white cotton kurta to the wedding.

Material (cotton) noun ke sabse paas baithta hai aur colour (white) usse pehle aata hai. Dono ulat gaye the.

Exercise 8

Galat shabd dhoondo.

This phone is more cheaper than that one.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: more.

Sahi roop: This phone is cheaper than that one.

'cheaper' pehle se comparative hai, isliye 'more' extra ho gaya. Hindi ke 'zyada sasta' se ye aadat aati hai.

Exercise 9

Ek shabd galat jagah par hai.

My all relatives came for the function.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: all.

Sahi roop: All my relatives came for the function.

'all' possessive se pehle aata hai — all my, all your, all his. Hindi ka 'mere saare' seedha utaarne se kram ulat jaata hai.

Exercise 10

'I saw the accident with my own eyes.' — yahan 'own' kis prakaar ka adjective hai?

  • Emphasizing
  • Possessive
  • Quality
  • Distributive

Hint: Ye koi nayi jaankari nahi, sirf zor de raha hai.

Jawaab

Emphasizing

'own' aur 'the very' noun par zor dete hain — Emphasizing adjectives. 'my' possessive hai, par 'own' uske upar zor jodta hai.

Exercise 11

This is the ___ book I wanted! (bilkul wahi)

Hint: 'the' ke baad zor dene wala shabd.

Jawaab

very

'the very + noun' = bilkul wahi cheez. Yahan 'very' adjective hai, kyunki noun (book) ke baare me bata raha hai.

Exercise 12

Adjective ke prakaar ko uske sawaal se jodo.

A B Quality Whose? Quantity One at a time Possessive Which one? Distributive What kind? Demonstrative How much? Jawaab

Quality — What kind?; Quantity — How much?; Possessive — Whose?; Distributive — One at a time; Demonstrative — Which one?

Har prakaar ek sawaal ka jawaab hai — kaisa (quality), kitna (quantity), kiska (possessive), ek-ek karke (distributive), kaunsa ishaare se (demonstrative).

Exercise 13

Adjective ko uske kram-number se jodo.

A B lovely 3 — age huge 6 — origin ancient 7 — material Japanese 1 — opinion wooden 2 — size Jawaab

lovely — 1 — opinion; huge — 2 — size; ancient — 3 — age; Japanese — 6 — origin; wooden — 7 — material

Jitna adjective mera apna faisla hai, utna door baithta hai; jitna wo cheez ka asli gun hai, utna noun ke paas. Isi liye opinion pehle aur material aakhir me.

Exercise 14

Adjectives ko sahi kram me lagao.

Shabd: a / bought / round / table / wooden / She / small

Jawaab

She bought a small round wooden table

Kram hai size (small) → shape (round) → material (wooden) → noun (table). Material hamesha noun se chipka rehta hai.

Exercise 15

Ye line bol ke dekho — teen adjectives ek saath, bina ruke.

Jawaab

Bolo: He has a beautiful old Indian painting

Bolte waqt adjectives ke beech koi comma nahi sunai deta, ek bahaav hota hai. Sahi kram me bolne par zubaan khud fisalti hai — galat kram me atakti hai.

Aage kya karein

Aaj ghar ki paanch cheezein chuno aur har ek ko do-teen adjectives ke saath bolo — "a small black plastic chair". Train ka kram pakka ho jaayega. Agla chapter Adverb — adjective ka jodidaar.

docs.title: Chapter 46: Advanced shabd
docs.text:
Advanced shabd — jo padhe-likhe log asal me bolte hain

Advanced shabd ratne ka koi faayda nahi hota — "Hegemony means dominance" yaad karke aap use kabhi theek se nahi bol paayenge. Shabd dimaag me jagah se baithta hai: wo kis tarah ke vaakya me aata hai, kis tarah ke log bolte hain, aur uske saath kaunse shabd chipke rehte hain. Isliye is chapter me har shabd ke saath uski duniya di gayi hai — definition ke bajaye.

Ek line me

Naya shabd tab tak aapka nahi hai jab tak aap uska ek asli vaakya bina soche na bol sakein. Matlab yaad rakhna aadha kaam hai; jagah yaad rakhna poora kaam.

docs.title: nefarious — buraai wala, sochi-samjhi badmaashi
docs.text:
Ye shabd khaali "bura" nahi hai — isme chhupi hui, plan ki hui buraai hai. News, crime story aur film ki baat me aata hai. Mazedaar baat: aaj kal log ise mazaak me bhi bolte hain — "nothing nefarious, I promise". Saath chalne wale shabd: nefarious scheme, nefarious purpose, nefarious activities.

  • The account was being used for something nefarious — fake invoices, mostly. Us account ka istemaal galat kaam ke liye ho raha tha — zyada tar naqli invoices.

docs.title: myriad — ginti se bahar, anek
docs.text:
Matlab "bahut saare", par isme ginna mumkin nahi wala bhaav hai. Sabse badi galti yahi hai ki log "a myriad of" ke baad singular laga dete hain. Dono roop chalte hain: myriad reasons (saaf aur chhota) ya a myriad of reasons. Par uske baad noun hamesha plural.

  • There are myriad reasons why the launch slipped, but three matter most. Launch late hone ki anek wajahein hain, par teen sabse zaroori hain.

docs.title: bucolic — gaon jaisa, shaant aur hara-bhara
docs.text:
Bucolic khet, charaagaah, gaay-bakri aur dheemi zindagi wali tasveer hai — jaise kisi painting ka gaon. Isme hamesha pyaar aur sukoon ka bhaav hota hai, garibi ya pichhdepan ka nahi. Kab use karein: ye literary shabd hai — travel writing, kitaab, review. Bolne me peaceful countryside ya rural zyada natural. Saathi shabd: bucolic setting, bucolic charm, bucolic landscape. Uchchaaran: byoo-KOL-ik.

  • The homestay sits in a bucolic valley of tea gardens and slow rivers. Homestay chaay ke baagon aur dheemi nadiyon wali ek shaant, hari-bhari ghaati me hai.

docs.title: guile — chalaaki, chaalbaazi
docs.text:
Guile noun hai — doosron ko bewakoof banane wali hoshiyari. Dhyan do: iska adjective roop guileful nahi chalta; log cunning bolte hain. Par guileless (bhola, chaalbaazi se khaali) bahut khoobsurat shabd hai aur taareef me aata hai.

  • He won that negotiation with pure guile, not numbers. Wo baat-cheet usne chalaaki se jeeti, aankdon se nahi.

docs.title: onerous — bhaari, thaka dene wala (kaam ya shart)
docs.text:
Kaam mushkil nahi — bojh jaisa. Sabse zyada ye contract, rules, paperwork, duty ke saath aata hai. Office email me ye shabd polite tareeke se shikayat karta hai: aap "ye bakwaas hai" nahi keh rahe, bas "ye bojh hai" keh rahe hain.

  • The reporting requirements are onerous for a team of three. Teen logon ki team ke liye reporting ke niyam bahut bhaari hain.

docs.title: enigmatic — paheli jaisa, samajh me na aane wala
docs.text:
Insaan, muskaan, jawaab, ya kisi ka rawaiya — jab saaf na ho ki andar kya chal raha hai. Isme dilchaspi hai, buraai nahi. Agar koi sirf chup hai to wo reserved hai; enigmatic wo hai jiske baare me aap sochte reh jaate hain.

  • Her reply was enigmatic — a single line that could mean yes or no. Uska jawaab paheli jaisa tha — ek line, jiska matlab haan bhi ho sakta hai aur na bhi.

docs.title: lurid — sansani-khez, bhadkila
docs.text:
Do matlab, dono me "zaroorat se zyada" ka bhaav: (1) kahaani ya khabar jo jaan-boojh kar chaunkane wali, gandi ya khooni detail se bhari ho; (2) rang jo chubhne wale, bhadkile hon. Ye shabd hamesha thodi naapasandgi ke saath aata hai. Kab use karein: news, review, aalochana — sabse aam jodi lurid details. Baat-cheet me kam, par samajh sab lete hain. Uchchaaran: LOOR-id.

  • The tabloid printed every lurid detail of the case. Us akhbaar ne case ki har sansani-khez, chatpati detail chhaap di.

docs.title: hegemony — kisi ek ka dabdaba
docs.text:
Politics, history aur business analysis ka shabd. Matlab: ek desh, company ya group ka itna dabdaba ki baaki sab usi ke hisaab se chalte hain. Rozmarra ki baat me ye shabd mat bolo — bahut bhaari hai. Uchchaaran dhyan se: hi-JEM-uh-nee.

  • Two companies share almost complete hegemony over the search market. Search ke bazaar par lagbhag poora dabdaba do hi companies ka hai.

docs.title: felicity — gehri khushi; ya baat kehne ka sateek, sundar tareeka
docs.text:
Felicity noun hai, aur iske do matlab hain: (1) gehri, sukoon bhari khushi — purani, likhi hui bhasha me; (2) shabdon ka ekdam sahi aur sundar chunaav — felicity of expression. Ulta shabd infelicitous (bedhanga, galat jagah ka) editors aur critics khoob bolte hain. Kab use karein: bahut literary — shaadi ke card, bhaashan, sahitya ki aalochana. Rozmarra me happiness ya joy. Uchchaaran: fuh-LIS-ih-tee.

  • Her essays are admired for their felicity of expression. Uske nibandh apne sateek aur khoobsurat shabd-chunaav ke liye pasand kiye jaate hain.
  • We wish the couple a lifetime of felicity. Hum jode ko umr bhar ki khushiyon ki shubhkaamna dete hain.

docs.title: censure — sarkari ya aupchaarik nindaa
docs.text:
Ye aam naraazgi nahi hai — isme official bhaav hai. Committee, board, parliament, ya institution kisi ko censure karta hai. Dhyan rakho: ye censor (kaat dena, hissa hata dena) se bilkul alag shabd hai, bas aawaz milti hai.

  • The board voted to censure him, though he kept his seat. Board ne uski nindaa ka prastaav paas kiya, halaanki uski kursi bani rahi.

docs.title: jettison — bojh utaar dena, chhod dena
docs.text:
Asli tasveer: jahaaz ya hawai jahaaz se saamaan phenk dena taaki wo halka ho jaaye. Isi se iska aaj ka matlab aaya — kisi plan, feature ya aadat ko majboori me chhod dena. Isme bachne ke liye chhodna ka bhaav hai, isliye business aur project ki baat me khoob chalta hai.

  • We had to jettison half the features to ship on time. Time par release karne ke liye humein aadhe features chhodne pade.

docs.title: disparate — bilkul alag kism ke, mel na khaane wale
docs.text:
Sirf "different" nahi — itne alag ki inhe ek saath rakhna mushkil hai. Isliye ye aksar disparate sources, disparate systems, disparate groups ke roop me aata hai. Uchchaaran: DIS-puh-rut.

  • The report pulls together data from three disparate systems. Ye report teen bilkul alag-alag systems ka data ek jagah laati hai.

docs.title: insidious — dheere-dheere andar se nuksaan karne wala
docs.text:
Sabse zaroori baat: isme dheemi raftaar hai. Jo cheez pehle dikhai nahi deti aur jab dikhti hai tab tak kaafi nuksaan ho chuka hai — wahi insidious hai. Bimari, aadat, afwaah, aur soch — in sabke saath aata hai. Dhamaka insidious nahi hota.

  • The most insidious part is how normal it starts to feel. Sabse khatarnak baat ye hai ki dheere-dheere ye sab normal lagne lagta hai.

docs.title: keen — bahut utsuk; ya tez (nazar, dimaag)
docs.text:
Is list ka sabse kaam ka shabd, aur sabse aasaan. Do matlab: (1) keen to / keen on = kisi cheez ke liye utsuk — interview me sona. (2) a keen eye, a keen sense = tez nazar, paini samajh. Ek aur kaam ki baat: British English me "I'm not keen on it" mana karne ka bahut polite tareeka hai.

  • I'm keen to take on more responsibility this year. Is saal main aur zimmedari lene ke liye utsuk hoon.
  • She has a keen eye for detail — nothing gets past her. Uski nazar bahut paini hai — koi chhoti cheez bachti nahi.

docs.title: auspicious — shubh, achha shagun wala
docs.text:
India me ye shabd roz kaam aata hai — shaadi, griha pravesh, naya kaam. Angrezi bolne wale bahar ise kam bolte hain, par samajhte sab hain. Dhyan do: cheez auspicious occasion / auspicious day hoti hai; insaan nahi. Ulta shabd inauspicious hai.

  • They picked an auspicious date for the opening. Unhone udghaatan ke liye ek shubh din chuna.

docs.title: ubiquitous — har jagah maujood
docs.text:
Technology aur chalan ki baat ka pasandeeda shabd: smartphones are ubiquitous. Isme halka sa "ab to aam baat ho gayi hai" wala bhaav hai. Uchchaaran: yoo-BIK-wi-tus.

  • QR codes were rare five years ago; now they're ubiquitous. Paanch saal pehle QR code kam dikhte the; ab har jagah hain.

docs.title: ephemeral — pal bhar ka, jaldi khatam ho jaane wala
docs.text:
Isme khoobsurti aur thodi udaasi dono hain. Status, story, fashion, mausam, khushi — jo aaya aur gaya. Ye shabd thoda literary hai, isliye likhai me zyada jamta hai. Uchchaaran: ih-FEM-er-ul.

  • Social media fame is ephemeral — gone in a week. Social media ki shohrat pal bhar ki hoti hai — hafte bhar me gayab.

docs.title: pragmatic — vyavhaarik, jo chale wahi theek
docs.text:
Is list ka doosra sabse kaam ka shabd. Iska matlab hai: sidhant ki jagah nateeja dekhna. Interview me apne baare me batane ke liye behtareen — aur taareef ka shabd hai.

  • Let's be pragmatic — ship the simple version now, improve it later. Vyavhaarik banein — abhi aasaan version nikaalein, baad me behtar karein.

docs.title: 46.2 Kahan milenge ye shabd — ek naksha
docs.text:
Shabd ko jagah se jodo. Neeche do cheezein ek saath dikhai gayi hain: shabd kitna formal hai (daayein jitna, utna formal), aur aap use kitni baar sunenge (upar jitna, utna aam). Neeche-daayein kone wale shabd bolne me mat aazmao — wo padhne ke liye hain.

Figure 46.1. Narangi gole = aaj se bol sakte ho. Neele gole = pehle padhne aur pehchaanne ke liye, bolna baad me.

docs.title: 46.3 Ek nazar me — shabd, saathi shabd, uchchaaran
docs.text:
"Saathi shabd" (collocation) sabse kaam ka column hai: ye batata hai ki shabd ke aage-peeche kya aata hai. Native log inhe jodiyon me yaad rakhte hain, akele shabd ki tarah nahi.

Shabd Matlab (Hinglish) Saathi shabd Uchchaaran nefarious sochi-samjhi badmaashi wala scheme, purpose, activities ni-FAIR-ee-us myriad ginti se bahar, anek myriad reasons / ways / forms MIH-ree-ud bucolic gaon jaisa shaant, hara-bhara bucolic setting / charm / landscape byoo-KOL-ik guile chalaaki (noun) with guile, without guile, guileless GY-ul onerous bojh jaisa, bhaari onerous terms / duty / requirements OH-nur-us enigmatic paheli jaisa enigmatic smile / figure / reply eh-nig-MA-tik lurid sansani-khez; bhadkila (rang) lurid details / headlines / colours LOOR-id hegemony ek ka poora dabdaba hegemony over, cultural hegemony hi-JEM-uh-nee felicity gehri khushi; sateek shabd-chunaav felicity of expression, infelicitous fuh-LIS-ih-tee censure aupchaarik nindaa vote to censure, public censure SEN-shur jettison majboori me chhod dena jettison a plan / feature / idea JET-ih-sun disparate mel na khaane wale alag disparate sources / systems / groups DIS-puh-rut insidious dheere-dheere nuksaan karne wala insidious effect / spread / habit in-SID-ee-us keen utsuk; ya tez (nazar) keen to, keen on, a keen eye keen auspicious shubh auspicious day / occasion / start aw-SPISH-us ubiquitous har jagah maujood ubiquitous in, has become ubiquitous yoo-BIK-wi-tus ephemeral pal bhar ka ephemeral fame / beauty / trend ih-FEM-er-ul pragmatic vyavhaarik a pragmatic approach, be pragmatic prag-MA-tik

docs.title: 46.4 Shabdon ke jaal — jo aawaz me milte hain
docs.text:
Ye jodiyan dhyan se

censure (nindaa karna) vs censor (hissa kaat dena) — bilkul alag kaam. ephemeral (pal bhar ka) vs ethereal (halka, swargik) — dono poetic, par matlab alag. disparate (alag kism ke) vs desperate (bechain) — spelling ek akshar ki door hai, matlab kosson door. pragmatic (vyavhaarik) vs dogmatic (apni baat par ada) — ek taareef, doosra ilzaam.

docs.title: 46.5 Galtiyan jo in shabdon ke saath hoti hain
docs.text:
Dhyan do

  • Galat: There are a myriad of reason for this.
  • Sahi: There are myriad reasons for this.

  • Kyun: Myriad ke baad noun hamesha plural. Aur "myriad reasons" zyada saaf hai — "a myriad of" thoda bhaari lagta hai.

  • Galat: The bomb had an insidious effect on the building.

  • Sahi: The bomb had a devastating effect on the building.

  • Kyun: Insidious me dheemi raftaar zaroori hai. Ek jhatke me hone wale nuksaan ke liye devastating.

  • Galat: He is a very auspicious person.

  • Sahi: It was an auspicious day to start.

  • Kyun: Auspicious din, mauka aur shuruaat ke liye hai — insaan ke liye nahi.

  • Galat: The committee decided to censor the minister for his remarks.

  • Sahi: The committee decided to censure the minister for his remarks.

  • Kyun: Censure = nindaa karna. Censor = hissa kaat kar hata dena. Ek akshar, poora alag matlab.

  • Galat: I am keen for learning new tools.

  • Sahi: I am keen to learn new tools.

  • Kyun: Do hi roop hain: keen to + verb, ya keen on + -ing. "Keen for" nahi chalta.

  • Galat: Our team has hegemony in this office.

  • Sahi: Our team has a lot of influence in this office.
  • Kyun: Hegemony desh, bazaar aur sanskriti ke paimane ka shabd hai. Office ke liye bahut bada pad jaata hai.

docs.title: 46.6 Ek paragraph — paanch shabd, apni jagah par
docs.text:
Padh kar dekho, phir zor se bolo

Cheap smartphones are now ubiquitous, and that has created myriad small businesses that did not exist ten years ago. Most are ephemeral — up one month, gone the next. The ones that last are run by pragmatic people who jettison whatever stops working. Dhyan do: paanch bhaari shabd hain par vaakya kahin bhi akda hua nahi lagta, kyunki har shabd apni jagah par hai.

docs.title: 46.7 Practice — Advanced vocabulary
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Ek aadat jo saalon tak chhupi rehti hai aur dheere-dheere nuksaan karti hai. Kaunsa shabd?

  • insidious
  • nefarious
  • ephemeral
  • onerous

Hint: Raftaar dheemi honi chahiye.

Jawaab

insidious

Insidious me dheemi, chhupi hui raftaar zaroori hai. Nefarious me plan ki hui badmaashi hai, aur ephemeral pal bhar ka hai.

Exercise 2

Interview me khud ke baare me batane ke liye sabse behtar shabd?

  • pragmatic
  • enigmatic
  • nefarious
  • onerous
Jawaab

pragmatic

Pragmatic taareef ka shabd hai — nateeja dekhne wala insaan. Enigmatic ka matlab hoga ki aapko koi samajh nahi paata, jo interview me achha nahi.

Exercise 3

Kaunsa vaakya sahi hai?

  • There are myriad reasons for the delay.
  • There are a myriad of reason for the delay.
  • There is myriad reason for the delay.
  • There are myriads reason for the delay.
Jawaab

There are myriad reasons for the delay.

Myriad ke baad noun plural hota hai. 'Myriad reasons' sabse saaf roop hai.

Exercise 4

Project time par nikaalne ke liye aadhe features chhodne pade. Kaunsa verb?

  • jettison
  • censure
  • enhance
  • demonstrate
Jawaab

jettison

Jettison = bachne ke liye bojh utaar dena. Jahaaz se saamaan phenkne wali tasveer isi se aayi hai.

Exercise 5

I'm ___ to take on more responsibility this year.

Hint: Utsuk — interview wala shabd.

Jawaab

keen / eager

Keen to + verb. Dhyan rakho: 'keen for learning' galat hai, 'keen to learn' ya 'keen on learning' sahi.

Exercise 6

The report pulls together data from three ___ systems that were never meant to talk to each other.

Hint: Itne alag ki mel nahi khaate.

Jawaab

disparate

Disparate = bilkul alag kism ke. Sirf 'different' se zyada strong hai — isme 'jodna mushkil hai' ka bhaav hai.

Exercise 7

Ek shabd galat chuna gaya hai — us par tap karo.

The board voted to censor the minister for his remarks.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: censor.

Sahi roop: The board voted to censure the minister for his remarks.

Censure = aupchaarik nindaa. Censor = hissa kaat kar hata dena. Aawaz milti hai, matlab nahi.

Exercise 8

Ye shabd insaan par nahi lagta — use dhoondo.

My uncle is a very auspicious man in our town.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: auspicious.

Sahi roop: My uncle is a well-respected man in our town.

Auspicious din, mauka aur shuruaat ke liye hai. Insaan ke liye 'respected' ya 'well-regarded'.

Exercise 9

Shabd ko uske asli bhaav se jodo.

A B hegemony bojh jaisa bhaari kaam guile pal bhar me khatam onerous ek ka poora dabdaba ephemeral chalaaki se kaam nikaalna Jawaab

hegemony — ek ka poora dabdaba; guile — chalaaki se kaam nikaalna; onerous — bojh jaisa bhaari kaam; ephemeral — pal bhar me khatam

Chaaron bhaari shabd hain — pehle pehchaano aur padho, bolna baad me.

Exercise 10

Shabd ko uske saathi shabd se jodo.

A B keen has become ubiquitous nefarious an enigmatic smile ubiquitous a keen eye for detail enigmatic a nefarious scheme Jawaab

keen — a keen eye for detail; nefarious — a nefarious scheme; ubiquitous — has become ubiquitous; enigmatic — an enigmatic smile

Native log shabd akele yaad nahi rakhte — jodi me rakhte hain. Jodi yaad ho to shabd apne aap sahi jagah girta hai.

Exercise 11

Vaakya banao — technology ke baare me.

Shabd: were / they / five / ago / QR / are / rare / but / years / now / codes / ubiquitous

Jawaab

QR codes were rare five years ago but now they are ubiquitous

Ubiquitous ke saath aksar 'now' aur pehle-baad ka muqabla aata hai — yahi iska natural ghar hai.

Exercise 12

Travel blog me ek shaant, hare-bhare gaon ka varnan karna hai. Kaunsa shabd?

  • bucolic
  • lurid
  • onerous
  • insidious

Hint: Khet, charaagaah, sukoon.

Jawaab

bucolic

Bucolic = gaon jaisa shaant aur sundar. Ye literary shabd hai, isliye blog aur kitaab me jamta hai. Lurid ulta hai — bhadkila aur sansani-khez.

Exercise 13

Ek shabd galat chuna gaya hai — us par tap karo.

The tabloid printed every bucolic detail of the murder.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: bucolic.

Sahi roop: The tabloid printed every lurid detail of the murder.

Chaunkane wali, khooni detail = lurid details. Bucolic gaon ki shaanti ke liye hai.

Exercise 14

Critics praised the poet for the ___ of her expression — every word felt exactly right.

Hint: Sateek, sundar shabd-chunaav — ek noun.

Jawaab

felicity

'Felicity of expression' = shabdon ka ekdam sahi aur sundar chunaav. Bahut literary shabd — rozmarra me nahi.

Exercise 15

Naye shabdon ko unke bhaav se jodo.

A B bucolic gehri khushi ya sateek shabd lurid majboori me chhod dena felicity gaon jaisa shaant jettison sansani-khez, bhadkila Jawaab

bucolic — gaon jaisa shaant; lurid — sansani-khez, bhadkila; felicity — gehri khushi ya sateek shabd; jettison — majboori me chhod dena

Bucolic aur felicity literary hain, lurid news me aam. Teeno pehle padh kar pehchaano, phir likhai me aazmao.

Exercise 16

Naya shabd kab tak aapka nahi hua maana jaata hai?

  • Jab tak uska ek asli vaakya bina soche na bol sako
  • Jab tak uski spelling yaad na ho
  • Jab tak dictionary ki definition yaad na ho
  • Jab tak uska Hindi matlab yaad na ho
Jawaab

Jab tak uska ek asli vaakya bina soche na bol sako

Definition yaad rakhna aadha kaam hai. Shabd tab aata hai jab uski jagah aur jodi yaad ho.

Exercise 17

Ye line bolo. 'Pragmatic' me zor beech me — prag-MA-tik.

Jawaab

Bolo: Let us be pragmatic and ship the simple version now

Office meeting ki asli line hai. 'Let's be pragmatic' bolne se aap samajhdaar lagte hain, zidda nahi.

Aage kya karein

Atharah shabd ek saath mat uthao. Naksha dekho, narangi gole wale paanch chuno — keen, pragmatic, ubiquitous, auspicious, enigmatic — aur is hafte unhe bolo. Neele gole wale shabd padhte waqt pehchaanne ke liye kaafi hain; wo apne waqt par zabaan par aa jaayenge.

docs.title: Chapter 11: Adverb — kaise, kab, kahan
docs.text:
Adverb — kaise, kab, kahan, kitna

Adverb wo shabd hai jo verb, adjective ya doosre adverb ke baare me batata hai. Adjective noun ko chhoota hai; adverb baaki sab ko. Do cheezein isme sabse zyada pakadti hain — pehla, -ly lagana bhool jaana ("she speaks good"), aur doosra, adverb ko galat jagah rakh dena ("I always am late"). Dono is chapter me theek ho jaayengi.

Ek line me

An adverb modifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb. Noun ke alawa jiske baare me bataya jaaye — wo adverb ka kaam hai.

  • He drove carefully. Verb ke baare me — kaise chalaya?
  • The exam was very easy. Adjective ke baare me — kitna aasaan?
  • She sings quite beautifully. Doosre adverb ke baare me — kitni khoobsurti se?
Figure 11.1. Adverb teen cheezein chhoota hai — verb, adjective, doosra adverb. Noun uske daayre me nahi aata.

docs.title: 11.1 Adverb ke prakaar
docs.text: Prakaar Sawaal Examples Vaakya me Manner Kaise? slowly, carefully, well, badly, loudly She writes neatly. Time Kab? now, then, today, yesterday, soon, already, yet He left yesterday. Place Kahan? here, there, outside, upstairs, everywhere, nearby Wait outside. Frequency Kitni baar? always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never I always walk to work. Degree Kitna? very, too, so, quite, almost, enough, hardly It is too hot. Affirmation / negation Haan ya na? certainly, surely, definitely, not, never I certainly agree. Reason Kyun? therefore, hence, thus, consequently He was ill; therefore he stayed home. Interrogative sawaal poochhna when, where, why, how Why are you late? Relative do hisson ko jodna where, when, why This is the place where we met.

docs.title: Interrogative aur Relative adverb — same shabd, alag kaam
docs.text:
where, when, why (aur sawaal me how) do tarah se aate hain. Sawaal ke shuru me ho to interrogative adverb. Kisi noun (place, time, reason) ke turant baad aakar uske baare me poora hissa jode, to relative adverb.

Shabd Interrogative (sawaal) Relative (jodna) where Where do you live? the place where we met when When does the film start? the day when I joined why Why is she crying? the reason why he left how How did you do it? (relative me aksar nahi — "the way" bolo)
  • This is the café where we first met. "where" = jahan — jagah (café) ke baare me poori baat jod raha hai.
  • I still remember the day when I got my first job. "when" = jab — samay (day) ke baad aaya.
  • Tell me the reason why you are upset. "why" = kyun — "reason" ke baad.

Relative adverb ka chhota rule

where = in which / at which (jagah) · when = on which / in which (samay) · why = for which (kaaran). ✓ the house where I was born = the house in which I was born. Relative adverb ke baad poora vaakya (subject + verb) aata hai, aur sawaal wala ulta kram nahi: ✗ "the place where did we meet" → ✓ "the place where we met".

'the way how' — double mat karo

  • Galat: I like the way how she speaks.
  • Sahi: I like the way she speaks. / I like how she speaks.
  • Kyun: "the way" aur "how" ka matlab ek hi hai — dono me se ek lagao.

Frequency ko paimaane par rakho

always (100%) → usually → often → sometimes → occasionally → rarely / seldom → hardly ever → never (0%). Interview me "I sometimes make mistakes" kehna "I never make mistakes" se zyada bharosemand lagta hai.

docs.title: 11.2 Adverb banane ke rule
docs.text:
Adjective kaise khatam hota hai Kya karo Example Normal + ly quick → quickly consonant + y y → ily happy → happily, easy → easily -le e → y simple → simply, gentle → gently -ic + ally basic → basically, tragic → tragically -ll + y full → fully, dull → dully -ue e hatao, + ly true → truly, due → duly

Ye adverb -ly nahi lete — roop wahi rehta hai

Shabd Adjective me Adverb me fast a fast train drives fast hard hard work works hard late a late train came late early an early bus woke up early straight a straight line go straight high a high wall flew high

"fastly" aur "hardly work" dono galat hain — "hardly" ka matlab hai bilkul nahi: He hardly works = wo kaam hi nahi karta!

-ly lagne se matlab badal jaane wale jode

Bina -ly -ly ke saath hard = mehnat se (He works hard.) hardly = bilkul nahi (He hardly works.) late = der se (She came late.) lately = haal hi me (I haven't seen her lately.) near = paas (He lives near.) nearly = lagbhag (I nearly fell.) short = chhota (Cut it short.) shortly = jald hi (He will arrive shortly.) high = ooncha (Birds fly high.) highly = bahut (She is highly qualified.)

docs.title: 11.3 Adverb ki jagah — yahan sabse zyada galti hoti hai
docs.text:
Adverb ki jagah uske prakaar se tay hoti hai. Chaar pakke patterns hain, aur ye chaar yaad ho gaye to bolchaal apne aap sudhar jaati hai.

Figure 11.2. Adverb ki jagah ke chaar rule — frequency, kram, degree, aur object ke beech na aana.

Frequency adverb ka pakka rule

Main verb se pehle — I always wake up early. "be" verb ke baad — She is always busy. Helping verb ke baad — They have never been to Kerala. Ek line me: "be" ke baad, baaki sab se pehle.

Jagah ki galtiyan

  • Galat: I always am ready on time.
  • Sahi: I am always ready on time.

  • Kyun: "be" verb (am) ke baad frequency adverb aata hai — yahi ek apvaad hai.

  • Galat: She speaks fluently English.

  • Sahi: She speaks English fluently.

  • Kyun: Verb aur uske object ke beech me adverb nahi aata. Pehle kaam poora karo (speaks English), phir batao kaise.

  • Galat: He went yesterday to the market.

  • Sahi: He went to the market yesterday.
  • Kyun: Place pehle, time baad me — manner → place → time ka kram.

Shuruaat me adverb — zor dene ke liye

Adverb vaakya ke shuru me bhi rakha ja sakta hai, tab wo poore vaakya par asar daalta hai: Suddenly, the lights went off. / Honestly, I didn't know. Aise waqt comma lagana behtar hai.

docs.title: 11.4 Adverb ka comparative aur superlative
docs.text:
Adjective jaisa hi hai, par ek farq ke saath: -ly wale adverbs me hamesha more / most lagta hai.

Kaise banta hai Positive Comparative Superlative -ly wale → more / most carefully more carefully most carefully -ly wale → more / most quickly more quickly most quickly Chhote (bina -ly) → er / est fast faster fastest Chhote (bina -ly) → er / est hard harder hardest Chhote (bina -ly) → er / est late later latest Irregular well better best Irregular badly worse worst Irregular little less least Irregular much more most Irregular far farther / further farthest / furthest
  • Ravi runs faster than his brother. "fast" chhota hai, isliye -er.
  • She explained it more clearly than the teacher. "clearly" me -ly hai, isliye more.
  • Of all the students, he writes the most neatly. Superlative — teen ya zyada ki tulna.

docs.title: 11.5 Adverb vs Adjective — ek second ka test
docs.text:
Poochho: kiske baare me bata raha hai?

Noun ke baare me → adjective. Verb ke baare me → adverb. a loud noise (noun) · shouted loudly (verb)

Linking verb ke baad adjective aata hai, adverb nahi

✓ The food smells good. ✗ smells well ✓ She looks tired. ✗ looks tiredly Kyunki ye verb subject ke baare me bata rahe hain, kaam ke baare me nahi. Ek apvaad: He looks well = uski sehat theek hai.

docs.title: 11.6 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Adverb ki aam Indian-English galtiyan

  • Galat: She speaks English very good.
  • Sahi: She speaks English very well.

  • Kyun: "speaks" verb hai, isliye adverb chahiye — well. "good" sirf noun ke saath: her English is good. Ye jodi — good/well — sabse zyada pakadti hai.

  • Galat: He is more taller and runs more faster.

  • Sahi: He is taller and runs faster.

  • Kyun: "taller" aur "faster" dono me -er pehle se comparison bana chuka hai. -ly wale adverb me more lagta hai (more slowly), par chhote adverb me -er.

  • Galat: I always am late for meetings.

  • Sahi: I am always late for meetings.

  • Kyun: Frequency adverb "be" verb ke baad aata hai — am always, is never, are usually. Baaki saare verbs se pehle: always come, never eat.

  • Galat: He drives his car fastly.

  • Sahi: He drives his car fast.

  • Kyun: "fastly" English me shabd hi nahi hai. "fast" khud adverb hai. Isi list me: hard, late, early, straight, high — inme -ly nahi lagta.

  • Galat: She explained very nicely the problem.

  • Sahi: She explained the problem very nicely.

  • Kyun: Verb aur object ke beech adverb nahi ghusaate. Pehle "explained the problem", phir batao kaise.

  • Galat: He hardly works, that's why he got promoted.

  • Sahi: He works hard, that's why he got promoted.

  • Kyun: "hardly" ka matlab hai lagbhag nahi — ulta matlab ho gaya! Mehnat batani ho to "works hard" bolo.

  • Galat: I am very much tired today.

  • Sahi: I am very tired today.

  • Kyun: Adjective ke saath sirf "very" aata hai. "very much" verb ke saath chalta hai: I like it very much.

  • Galat: He don't come here never.

  • Sahi: He doesn't come here. / He never comes here.
  • Kyun: Do galtiyan: "he" ke saath doesn't, aur ek vaakya me do negative nahi (doesn't + never). "never" khud negative hai, isliye uske saath normal verb aata hai.

docs.title: 11.7 Chhota naksha
docs.text: Adverb ka prakaar Jagah Example Manner object ke baad, vaakya ke aakhir me She read the letter slowly. Frequency main verb se pehle / "be" ke baad He often calls. · He is often busy. Time aakhir me (ya shuru me zor ke liye) We met yesterday. Place manner ke baad, time se pehle He sat quietly in the corner. Degree jiske baare me bata raha hai, usse turant pehle It is too cold.

docs.title: 11.8 Practice — Adverbs
docs.text:
Exercise 1

She speaks English very ___.

  • well
  • good
  • better
  • goodly

Hint: 'speaks' kaunsa part of speech hai?

Jawaab

well

'speaks' verb hai, aur verb ke baare me batane ke liye adverb chahiye. 'good' ka adverb 'well' hai — 'good' sirf noun ke saath aata: her English is good.

Exercise 2

Kaunsa vaakya sahi hai?

  • She is always on time.
  • She always is on time.
  • Always she is on time.
  • She is on time always.

Hint: Frequency adverb aur 'be' verb ka rule.

Jawaab

She is always on time.

Frequency adverb 'be' verb ke baad aata hai — is always, am never, are usually. Baaki saare verbs se pehle aata hai: always comes, never eats.

Exercise 3

He drives ___ than his father.

  • faster
  • more fast
  • more faster
  • fastly

Hint: 'fast' me -ly hai ya nahi?

Jawaab

faster

'fast' chhota adverb hai aur usme -ly nahi hai, isliye -er lagta hai. -ly wale adverbs me 'more' lagta hai: more carefully, more slowly.

Exercise 4

'He hardly works.' — iska matlab kya hai?

  • Wo kaam hi nahi karta
  • Wo bahut mehnat karta hai
  • Wo kabhi-kabhi kaam karta hai
  • Wo theek kaam karta hai

Hint: hard aur hardly do alag shabd hain.

Jawaab

Wo kaam hi nahi karta

'hardly' ka matlab hai lagbhag nahi — ye 'hard' ka adverb nahi hai. Mehnat batani ho to 'works hard' bolo, bina -ly.

Exercise 5

The child was crying ___. (adverb of 'loud')

Hint: Normal adjective me kya lagta hai?

Jawaab

loudly

Normal adjective me -ly lagane se adverb banta hai — loud se loudly. Yahan 'crying' verb hai, isliye adverb chahiye.

Exercise 6

She solved the puzzle ___ than I did. (comparative of 'easily')

Hint: -ly wale adverb me kya lagta hai?

Jawaab

more easily

-ly par khatam hone wale adverbs me 'more' lagta hai, -er nahi. 'easilier' jaisa koi shabd nahi hota.

Exercise 7

Is vaakya me ek shabd galat jagah par hai — us par tap karo.

She speaks fluently Hindi and Marathi.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: fluently.

Sahi roop: She speaks Hindi and Marathi fluently.

Verb aur uske object ke beech adverb nahi aata. Pehle kaam poora karo — speaks Hindi and Marathi — phir batao kaise.

Exercise 8

Galat shabd dhoondo.

He drives his new car very fastly.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: fastly.

Sahi roop: He drives his new car very fast.

'fastly' English me shabd hi nahi hai — 'fast' khud adverb hai. Isi list me hard, late, early, straight bhi hain.

Exercise 9

Ek shabd galat jagah par hai.

I always am ready before eight.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: always.

Sahi roop: I am always ready before eight.

'be' verb (am) ke baad frequency adverb aata hai — yahi ek apvaad hai. Baaki verbs me adverb pehle: I always wake up early.

Exercise 10

'This is the school where my father studied.' — yahan 'where' kya hai?

  • relative adverb
  • interrogative adverb
  • adverb of place
  • preposition

Hint: Ye sawaal hai ya noun ke baad jod raha hai?

Jawaab

relative adverb

'where' noun 'school' ke baad aakar uske baare me poora hissa jod raha hai — relative adverb. 'Where did he study?' me wo sawaal poochh raha hota — interrogative.

Exercise 11

I will never forget the day ___ we won the cup.

Hint: Samay (day) ke baad kaunsa relative adverb?

Jawaab

when

Samay ke noun (day, year, time) ke baad 'when'. Jagah ke baad 'where', kaaran (reason) ke baad 'why'.

Exercise 12

Ek shabd faltu hai — us par tap karo.

I love the way how my mother cooks.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: how.

Sahi roop: I love the way my mother cooks.
