'the way' aur 'how' ka matlab ek hi hai — dono saath nahi aate. 'the way my mother cooks' ya 'how my mother cooks'.

Exercise 13

Adverb ko uske prakaar se jodo.

A B slowly place — kahan yesterday frequency — kitni baar outside degree — kitna rarely manner — kaise almost time — kab Jawaab

slowly — manner — kaise; yesterday — time — kab; outside — place — kahan; rarely — frequency — kitni baar; almost — degree — kitna

Adverb ka prakaar us sawaal se tay hota hai jiska wo jawaab deta hai. Aur prakaar se hi uski vaakya me jagah tay hoti hai.

Exercise 14

Sahi kram me vaakya banao — manner, place, time ka kram yaad rakho.

Shabd: concert / the / at / last / beautifully / played / He / night

Jawaab

He played beautifully at the concert last night

Kai adverbs ek saath aayein to kram hota hai manner (kaise) → place (kahan) → time (kab). Ye kram todne se vaakya ajeeb lagta hai.

Exercise 15

Ye line bol ke dekho — 'well' saaf bolna hai, 'good' nahi.

Jawaab

Bolo: She speaks English very well

Hum log 'very good' bolne ki aadat me 'well' chhod dete hain. Zor se 'well' bolne ki practice se ye aadat tootti hai.

Aage kya karein

Aaj se jab bhi "good" bolne ka man kare, poochho — "kya main kisi kaam ke baare me bata raha hoon?" Agar haan, to "well" bolo. Agla chapter Preposition hai, aur uske baad Conjunction.

docs.title: Chapter 51: Application aur message
docs.text:
Application aur message — har mauke ka taiyaar namoona

Chhutti chahiye, fridge kharab ho gaya, college se certificate chahiye, naukri ke liye CV bhejna hai, ya boss ko batana hai ki train late hai — zindagi me yahi likhai sabse zyada kaam aati hai. Is chapter me har mauke ka ek poora namoona hai jise aap naam aur taarikh badalkar seedha use kar sakte ho, aur aakhir me ek template jo har jagah chalega.

Ek line me

Every application answers three questions in its first lines: what you want, why, and for which dates or details. Kya chahiye, kyun chahiye, aur kab ya kis cheez ke liye — ye teen baatein shuru me hi saaf ho jaayein.

docs.title: 51.1 Leave application — manager ko
docs.text:
Office me leave application aajkal email hi hota hai. Manager ko sirf "haan" ya "na" kehna hai — to unhe wo sab do jo faisle ke liye chahiye, aur kuch zyada nahi.

Figure 51.1. Chaaron hon to manager ek line me jawaab de sakta hai. Ek bhi chhoota to sawaal-jawaab shuru.

Leave email ki chaar cheezein

Dates (din + taarikh), wajah (ek line, detail nahi), handover (kaam kaun dekhega), aur ek seedha sawaal — "Could you please confirm if these dates are approved?"

Model: Leave application to manager

Subject: Leave request: 18–20 November (sister's wedding)

Dear Ms Iyer,

I would like to request three days of annual leave, from Wednesday, 18 November to Friday, 20 November, for my sister's wedding in Jaipur.

I will finish the monthly GST reconciliation before I leave, and Rohan has agreed to handle any urgent vendor queries while I am away. I will be back at my desk on Monday, 23 November.

Could you please let me know if these dates are approved?

Thank you, Neha Kapoor Accounts Executive

  • I would like to request three days of annual leave… "I want leave" se kahin zyada vinamra, par utna hi seedha. Kitne din + kaunsi leave + kab se kab tak.
  • …and Rohan has agreed to handle… Handover ka naam pehle se tay — manager ki sabse badi chinta khatam.
  • I will be back at my desk on Monday, 23 November. Wapas kab — ye chhoti line manager ko planning me madad karti hai.

docs.title: 51.2 Leave application — school principal ko
docs.text:
School aur college me abhi bhi purana letter format chalta hai — kaagaz par ho ya email me. Teacher yahi format dekhne ki ummeed rakhte hain, isliye yahan uske niyam maanna hi samajhdaari hai.

Figure 51.2. Ye dhaancha school aur college ke liye hai. Office email me ise mat le jaana.

Do duniya, do format

School/college application me purana letter format theek hai: To, taarikh, Subject, "Respected Sir/Madam", "Thanking you". Office email me ye sab hata do — wahan "Dear Ms Iyer" aur "Kind regards" chalta hai.

Model: Leave application to school principal

To The Principal Green Valley Public School Nagpur

10 August

Subject: Application for leave, 6–8 August

Respected Madam,

I am Ananya Joshi, a student of Class 9 B. I was unable to attend school from 6 to 8 August because I had a high fever. The doctor advised me to rest at home, and I have attached a copy of the medical certificate.

I will complete the classwork I missed and submit my pending homework by Friday. Please grant me leave for these three days.

Thanking you, Yours sincerely, Ananya Joshi Class 9 B, Roll No. 14

  • I was unable to attend school from 6 to 8 August… Chhutti ho chuki hai, isliye past tense. Pehle se maang rahe ho to: "I will not be able to attend…"
  • I will complete the classwork I missed… Teacher ki chinta ka jawaab pehle hi de diya — yahi line application ko achha banati hai.
  • Yours sincerely, — "Yours obediently" nahi "Obediently" bahut purana hai. Kai school ab bhi sikhaate hain, par "Yours sincerely" har jagah sahi hai.

docs.title: 51.3 Complaint letter — gussa nahi, saboot
docs.text:
Shikayat likhte waqt gussa aana swabhavik hai. Par company me jo insaan aapka email padhta hai, wo aapki madad tab jaldi karta hai jab use facts, reference number aur saaf maang milti hai — CAPITAL LETTERS nahi.

Figure 51.3. Chaar kadam, ek kram. Gussa is kram me kahin nahi aata — aur zaroorat bhi nahi.

Shikayat ka formula

Kya hua (taarikh aur order number ke saath) + kya chahiye + kab tak. Gussa, CAPITAL LETTERS aur "!!!" se kaam nahi hota; facts aur saboot se hota hai.

Model: Complaint email to customer care

Subject: Complaint: refrigerator not repaired after two visits (Order no. 58213)

Dear Customer Care Team,

I am writing to complain about the refrigerator I bought from your Andheri store on 2 September (Order no. 58213; invoice attached).

Since 20 September, the fridge has not been cooling. Your technician visited on 23 September and again on 30 September, but the problem is still not fixed. As a result, we have had to throw away food twice.

The product is under warranty. I would like you to either repair it fully or replace it by 15 October. Please confirm the next step by replying to this email.

Kind regards, Vikram Singh [Phone number]

  • Subject me order number Customer care ka system order number se hi chalta hai — subject me hoga to email sahi team tak jaldi pahunchega.
  • Since 20 September… visited on 23 and 30 September… Taarikhon ki chhoti si timeline — koi bahas nahi kar sakta.
  • I would like you to either repair it fully or replace it by 15 October. Do saaf option aur ek deadline. Firm hai, par badtameez nahi.

docs.title: 51.4 Request letter — vinamra, par saaf
docs.text:
Request me hum aksar itne vinamra ho jaate hain ki asli baat kho jaati hai — "I humbly request you to kindly please…". Ek please kaafi hai; baaki jagah saaf details do.

Vinamrata ka sahi naap

"Could you please…" ya "I would be grateful if you could…" — bas itna. "Humbly", "kindly" aur "please" teeno ek saath mat jodo. Vinamrata shabdon se nahi, saaf aur poori jaankari dene se aati hai.

Model: Request to college office

Subject: Request for a bonafide certificate — Rohit Kulkarni, TY BCom (Roll No. 2231)

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am a third-year BCom student (Division A, Roll No. 2231), and I need a bonafide certificate to apply for an education loan.

I would be grateful if you could issue the certificate by Wednesday, 21 October, as the bank's deadline is 23 October. I have attached a copy of my college ID card and my fee receipt.

Please let me know if you need any other document from me.

Yours faithfully, Rohit Kulkarni TY BCom, Division A

  • I would be grateful if you could issue the certificate by Wednesday. Vinamra maang + deadline + deadline ki wajah (bank ki taarikh).
  • Dear Sir or Madam → Yours faithfully Naam pata nahi, isliye "faithfully". Naam pata hota (Dear Mrs Patil) to "Yours sincerely".
  • Please let me know if you need any other document. Office ke liye agla kadam aasaan — aage-peeche ke chakkar bachte hain.

docs.title: 51.5 Job application — cover note
docs.text:
CV bhejte waqt email ka body khaali chhodna — ya sirf "PFA my resume" likhna — sabse badi chook hai. Recruiter har application par kuch hi second deta hai; chhota, saaf cover note aapko baaki dher se alag kar deta hai.

Cover note ke teen paragraph

(1) Kaunsi job, kahan dekhi. (2) Ek-do asli uplabdhi, number ke saath. (3) CV attached + baat karne ki ichha. Poora note 150 shabd se kam.

Model: Job application cover note

Subject: Application for Junior Data Analyst (Ref. JDA-24) — Aditya Rao

Dear Ms Fernandes,

I am writing to apply for the Junior Data Analyst role advertised on your careers page.

I recently completed my BSc in Statistics and spent six months as an intern at a retail company, where I built weekly sales dashboards in Excel and Power BI. These dashboards cut the team's reporting time from two days to half a day.

My CV is attached. I would welcome the chance to discuss how I can support your analytics team.

Kind regards, Aditya Rao [Phone number] · [LinkedIn profile link]

  • Subject me role, reference number aur naam HR ek saath kai roles bharta hai — reference number se aapka email sahi folder me jaata hai.
  • …cut the team's reporting time from two days to half a day. "I am hard-working and dedicated" har koi likhta hai. Number wali uplabdhi yaad rehti hai.
  • I would welcome the chance to discuss… Aatmavishwaas bhara ant — "kindly consider my candidature" se zyada aaj ka.

docs.title: 51.6 WhatsApp aur text par professional message
docs.text:
Aaj aadha office kaam WhatsApp par hota hai. Yahan bhi wahi niyam hai jo email me: poori baat ek hi message me. Sirf "Hi sir" bhejkar jawaab ka intezaar karna saamne wale ka samay bhi leta hai aur aapka bhi.

Figure 51.4. Baayein: chaar message, do ghante, phir bhi adhoori baat. Daayein: ek message, poori baat.

Professional message ke chaar niyam

Ek message, poori baat — kaun, kya, kab tak. Pehle message me apna naam aur sandarbh (team, class) batao. Raat 9 baje ke baad sirf zaroori baat. Aur voice note bhejne se pehle poochh lo — har koi meeting me sun nahi sakta.

Model: WhatsApp to your boss

Good morning, Mr Khanna. My train is running about 40 minutes late, so I will reach the office by 10:15. The slides for the 11 am meeting are already in your inbox. — Neha

Model: WhatsApp to a client

Hello Ms Banerjee, this is Arjun from Brightline Interiors. The cabinets for your kitchen have arrived. Would Tuesday at 11 am suit you for the installation? You can reply here or call me on this number.

Model: Message to a teacher

Good evening, Ma'am. This is Ananya Joshi from Class 9 B. I was absent today because of a fever. Could you please tell me which Maths topics were covered, so that I can catch up? Thank you.

  • This is Arjun from Brightline Interiors. Naye number se pehla message — naam + company. "Myself Arjun" nahi.
  • Would Tuesday at 11 am suit you? Client ko ek pakka option do — "aap batao kab free ho" se jawaab dheema aata hai.
  • Good evening, Ma'am. Teacher ke liye "Ma'am / Sir" bilkul theek hai — school ki sanskriti me yahi chalta hai.

docs.title: 51.7 Apna template — khaali jagah bharo
docs.text:
Upar ke saare namoone ek hi dhaanche par bane hain. Ise ek baar apne phone ke notes me save kar lo — har nayi application bas khaali jagah bharne ka kaam reh jaayegi.

Template: application ya formal email

Subject: [Kya chahiye]: [dates / reference number]

Dear [Mr/Ms + surname], — ya naam na pata ho to: Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to [request / inform you about / complain about / apply for] [mukhya baat, ek line me].

\[Wajah ya details — 2–3 line. Taarikh, number, reference.\] \[Aapne kya intezaam kiya hai, ya kya attach kiya hai.\]

Could you please [kya karna hai] by [din, taarikh]?

Kind regards, — ya Dear Sir or Madam ke saath: Yours faithfully, [Poora naam] [Pad / class / roll number] [Phone number]

Template: professional WhatsApp

[Good morning / Hello], [Mr/Ms + surname]. This is [aapka naam] from [team / company / class]. [Kya hua ya kya chahiye — ek line]. [Kab tak / agla kadam]. Thank you.

  • Bhejne se pehle 1: dates me din aur taarikh dono? "Wednesday, 18 November" — aur check karo ki wo sach me Wednesday hai.
  • Bhejne se pehle 2: naam ki spelling sahi? Kisi ka naam galat likhna sabse jaldi pakdi jaane wali galti hai.
  • Bhejne se pehle 3: attachment sach me laga? "Please find attached" likh kar file bhoolna — ye har office me roz hota hai.
  • Bhejne se pehle 4: ek zor se padh liya? Kaan wo galtiyan pakad lete hain jo aankh chhod deti hai.

docs.title: 51.8 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Ye vaakya leave applications aur office messages me itne aam hain ki sahi lagne lagte hain. Inme se zyadatar Hindi ke seedhe anuvaad hain.

Application aur message ki asli galtiyan

  • Galat: I am suffering from fever since two days.
  • Sahi: I have had a fever for two days.

  • Kyun: Duration (do din) ke saath "for", "since" nahi. Aur jo abhi tak chal raha hai uske liye present perfect: have had.

  • Galat: Please grant me leave as my health is not well.

  • Sahi: Please grant me leave as I am unwell.

  • Kyun: "Health is not well" me baat do baar hai. Seedha: I am unwell / I am not well.

  • Galat: I want leave for tomorrow.

  • Sahi: I would like to take leave tomorrow, Friday 20 November.

  • Kyun: "I want" maang jaisa lagta hai. "I would like to" vinamra hai — aur taarikh likhne se confusion nahi hota.

  • Galat: Respected sir, kindly do the needful.

  • Sahi: Good morning, Mr Khanna. Could you please approve my leave for Friday?

  • Kyun: WhatsApp par "Respected sir" bhaari lagta hai, aur "do the needful" batata hi nahi ki kya karna hai.

  • Galat: I am having a doubt in chapter 5.

  • Sahi: I have a question about Chapter 5.
  • Kyun: Bharat ke bahar "doubt" ka matlab shak hai, sawaal nahi. Aur "have" (rakhna) ke saath -ing nahi lagta.

docs.title: 51.9 Practice — Applications
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Manager ko leave email — sabse achhi subject line kaunsi?

  • Leave application
  • Leave request: 18–20 November (sister's wedding)
  • Sir please grant leave
  • Urgent leave needed!!!
Jawaab

Leave request: 18–20 November (sister's wedding)

Topic + exact dates + chhoti si wajah. Manager inbox me hi faisla kar sakta hai, email khole bina bhi.

Exercise 2

School principal ko likhi application me kaunsi greeting abhi bhi chalan me hai?

  • Respected Madam
  • Hey Ma'am
  • Hi Principal
  • Dear Madam ji
Jawaab

Respected Madam

School aur college ki application me purana format chalta hai — 'Respected Sir/Madam'. Office email me iski jagah 'Dear Ms Iyer' likho.

Exercise 3

Boss ko WhatsApp — train late hai. Sabse achha message kaunsa?

  • Hi sir
  • Sir late today
  • Good morning, Mr Khanna. My train is running 40 minutes late, so I will reach by 10:15. The slides for the 11 am meeting are already in your inbox.
  • Sorry sir traffic, coming
Jawaab

Good morning, Mr Khanna. My train is running 40 minutes late, so I will reach by 10:15. The slides for the 11 am meeting are already in your inbox.

Ek hi message me poori baat: kya hua, kab tak pahunchoge, aur kaam ka kya intezaam hai. Boss ko kuch poochhna hi nahi padta.

Exercise 4

Job ke cover note ki sahi lambai kya hai?

  • 150 shabd se kam, teen chhote paragraph
  • Do poore page
  • Sirf ek line: 'PFA my CV'
  • Bachpan se ab tak ki poori kahaani
Jawaab

150 shabd se kam, teen chhote paragraph

Recruiter har application par kuch hi second deta hai. Kaunsi job, ek-do asli uplabdhi number ke saath, aur CV attached — bas.

Exercise 5

Ek galti dhoondo.

I am suffering from fever since two days.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: since.

Sahi roop: I have had a fever for two days.

Duration (do din) ke saath 'for' lagta hai, 'since' nahi — since ke baad shuruaat ka point aata hai (since Monday). Aur 'I have had a fever' zyada natural hai.

Exercise 6

Kaunsa shabd is vaakya ko ajeeb bana raha hai?

I cannot come today because my health is not well.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: health.

Sahi roop: I cannot come today because I am not well.

'Health is not well' me ek hi baat do baar hai. Seedha bolo: I am not well / I am unwell.

Exercise 7

Purana phrase dhoondo jo kuch bhi saaf nahi batata.

Kindly do the needful and approve my leave.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: needful.

Sahi roop: Could you please approve my leave for 18–20 November?

'Do the needful' padhne wale par chhod deta hai ki karna kya hai. Seedha likho kya chahiye — aur kab ke liye.

Exercise 8

I would be ___ if you could issue the certificate by Friday.

Jawaab

grateful / thankful

'I would be grateful if you could…' — vinamra request ka sabse saaf aur professional tareeka. 'Humbly request you to kindly please' ki zaroorat nahi.

Exercise 9

I am writing to ___ for the post of Junior Data Analyst.

Jawaab

apply

apply for a job / apply for a post. Cover note ki pehli line hi bata deti hai ki aap kis kaam ke liye likh rahe ho.

Exercise 10

Mauke ko uski sahi pehli line se jodo.

A B Leave email to manager I am writing to apply for the post of Sales Associate. Complaint Could you please issue me a bonafide certificate? Cover note Good evening, Ma'am. This is Ananya from Class 9 B. Request to college office I would like to request leave from 18 to 20 November. Message to teacher I am writing to complain about a faulty refrigerator. Jawaab

Leave email to manager — I would like to request leave from 18 to 20 November.; Complaint — I am writing to complain about a faulty refrigerator.; Cover note — I am writing to apply for the post of Sales Associate.; Request to college office — Could you please issue me a bonafide certificate?; Message to teacher — Good evening, Ma'am. This is Ananya from Class 9 B.

Har pehli line seedha maqsad batati hai — padhne wale ko shuruaat me hi pata chal jaata hai ki baat kis baare me hai.

Exercise 11

Leave email ki aakhri line sahi kram me banao.

Shabd: whether / approved? / dates / please / confirm / are / you / Could / these

Jawaab

Could you please confirm whether these dates are approved?

Could you please + verb (confirm) + whether-clause. Leave email ka ant isi tarah ek saaf sawaal se karo.

Exercise 12

Ye line bolo — jaise phone par manager ko bata rahe ho.

Jawaab

Bolo: I would like to request two days of leave next week.

'I would like to request' — 'I want leave' se kahin zyada vinamra, aur phir bhi seedha. Bolte waqt 'would like' ko jodkar bolo: wud-laik.

Aage kya karein

Is hafte jo bhi application ya professional message likho, pehle is chapter ka template kholo. Teen baar template se likhoge, to chauthi baar dhaancha apne aap yaad aa jaayega.

docs.title: Chapter 6: a, an, the
docs.text:
a, an, the — teen chhote shabd, bada farq

Hindi me article naam ki koi cheez nahi hoti. "Main doctor hoon" — bas, kaam ho gaya. Isliye jab hum English bolte hain to dimaag wahi aadat dohra deta hai: "I am doctor." Grammar ki kitaab me ye chhoti galti lagti hai, par sunne wale ko turant pata chal jaata hai. Achhi khabar: article ka faisla sirf teen sawaal ka jawaab hai, aur wo teen sawaal is chapter me hamesha ke liye saaf ho jaayenge.

Ek line me

An article is a small word before a noun that tells the listener whether you mean any one of something (a / an) or that particular one (the). Article batata hai — "koi bhi ek" ya "wahi khaas wala".

  • I need a pen. Mujhe ek pen chahiye — koi bhi pen, kaunsa farq nahi padta.
  • I need the pen. Mujhe wo pen chahiye — jo dono jaante hain, wahi khaas pen.
  • I need pens. Mujhe pen chahiye (general baat) — yahan koi article nahi lagta.

docs.title: 6.1 Faisla lene ka flowchart
docs.text:
Har baar jab aapke saamne ek noun aaye, ye teen sawaal poochho — kram se. Jawaab apne-aap mil jaayega. Shuruaat me ye dheema lagega; do hafte me ye apne-aap hone lagega.

Figure 6.1. Sawaal kram se poochhne hain. Pehla sawaal sabse zaroori hai — agar jawaab haan hai, to baaki do sawaal poochhne ki zaroorat hi nahi.

docs.title: 6.2 a ya an — akshar nahi, aawaz dekho
docs.text:
Yahan sabse badi galti ye soch hai ki "vowel se shuru hone wale shabd ke pehle an lagta hai". Rule akshar ka nahi, aawaz ka hai. Bolkar dekho — agar muh se pehli aawaz vowel nikalti hai, to an.

Shabd Pehli aawaz Sahi Kyun hour aa- an hour "h" chup hai — aawaz vowel se shuru honest o- an honest man "h" chup hai university yu- a university "yu" consonant jaisi aawaz hai useful yu- a useful book wahi "yu" aawaz one-rupee coin wa- a one-rupee coin "one" = "wan", consonant aawaz MBA em- an MBA degree M ko "em" bolte hain — vowel aawaz LIC agent el- an LIC agent L = "el" European yu- a European country "yu" aawaz

Short-form ka pakka test

Short form (MBA, SP, FIR, NGO, RTI) ke saath har akshar ki aawaz bolo. Jo aksharon ki aawaz vowel se shuru hoti hai — A, E, F, H, I, L, M, N, O, R, S, X — unke pehle an. Baaki ke pehle a. an FIR · an NGO · an RTI · a BJP leader · a CA · a PhD

docs.title: 6.3 "the" kab lagta hai — saat pakke mauke
docs.text:
Mauka Example Doosri baar zikr (pehli baar "a") I saw a dog. The dog was limping. Duniya me ek hi cheez the sun · the moon · the sky · the earth Superlative aur ordinal the best player · the first bus Nadi, samudra, pahaad ki shrinkhala, registaan the Ganga · the Arabian Sea · the Himalayas · the Thar Baaje (musical instruments) She plays the flute. Akhbaar, kitaab ke naam, imaaratein the Hindu · the Gita · the Taj Mahal Desh jiske naam me plural ya "of" ho the Netherlands · the United States · the Republic of India

Pehla mauka sabse zaroori hai, isliye use ek baar sun lo:

  • Yesterday I met a teacher. The teacher told me about this book. Pehli baar "a teacher" — sunne wala nahi jaanta kaun. Doosri baar "the teacher" — ab jaanta hai.

docs.title: 6.4 Zero article — jahan kuch nahi lagta
docs.text:
Ye list yaad rakhni zaroori hai, kyunki yahan Indian English "the" ghusa deti hai jahan zaroorat nahi hoti.

Shreni Sahi Galat General plural Dogs are loyal. The dogs are loyal. Uncountable (general) Milk is good for health. The milk is good for health. Logon aur jagah ke naam Ravi lives in Jaipur. The Ravi lives in the Jaipur. Bhasha She speaks Marathi. She speaks the Marathi. Khel He plays cricket. He plays the cricket. Khaana We had lunch at two. We had the lunch at two. Sawaari — by + vehicle I came by bus. I came by the bus. Jagah jab kaam ke liye jaayein go to school · go to bed · go to court go to the school (padhne ke liye) Saal, mahina, din in 2026 · on Monday · in June in the 2026

'go to school' vs 'go to the school' — dono sahi, matlab alag

go to school = padhne jaana (kaam ke liye) — My son goes to school. go to the school = us imaarat tak jaana — I went to the school to meet the principal. Yahi farq hospital, college, church, prison, court ke saath bhi chalta hai.

docs.title: 6.5 Ek hi noun, teen roop — farq mehsoos karo
docs.text:
Vaakya Matlab A tiger is dangerous. Koi bhi ek baagh — ek example ke taur par. The tiger is dangerous. Wo khaas baagh, jiski baat ho rahi hai. Tigers are dangerous. Baagh (poori prajaati) khatarnaak hote hain. Ye sabse natural hai.

Ek chhota sa test

Confusion ho to apne-aap se poochho: "Kaunsa?" Agar jawaab aata hai ("wahi jo kal laaya tha") → the. Agar jawaab hai "koi bhi" → a / an. Agar sawaal hi bemaani hai ("Kaunsa doodh?" — poora doodh general me) → kuch nahi.

docs.title: 6.6 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Article ki top galtiyan

  • Galat: I am engineer.
  • Sahi: I am an engineer.

  • Kyun: Kaam-dhandha batate waqt English me article lagta hai — a doctor, an engineer, a teacher. Hindi me "main engineer hoon" kaafi hai, English me nahi.

  • Galat: He is going to the office by the bus.

  • Sahi: He is going to the office by bus.

  • Kyun: "by + vehicle" ke saath article nahi — by bus, by train, by car, by auto, on foot.

  • Galat: She plays the cricket very well.

  • Sahi: She plays cricket very well.

  • Kyun: Khel ke saath article nahi. Par baaje ke saath lagta hai: she plays the guitar.

  • Galat: The honesty is the best policy.

  • Sahi: Honesty is the best policy.

  • Kyun: Bhaav wale uncountable nouns (honesty, love, patience, anger) general baat me bina article aate hain. Par "the best" me "the" zaroori hai — superlative hai.

  • Galat: I have a good news for you.

  • Sahi: I have good news for you.

  • Kyun: "news" uncountable hai — iske pehle "a" nahi lagta. Ek khabar kehni ho to: a piece of good news.

  • Galat: She went to the home early.

  • Sahi: She went home early.

  • Kyun: "home" ke saath na article lagta hai, na "to" — go home, reach home, stay home.

  • Galat: My father is a best cook in our family.

  • Sahi: My father is the best cook in our family.

  • Kyun: Superlative (best, tallest, first) ke pehle hamesha "the" — kyunki wo ek hi ho sakta hai.

  • Galat: He gave me a advice.

  • Sahi: He gave me some advice.
  • Kyun: advice, information, furniture, luggage, equipment, work — ye sab uncountable hain. "a" nahi, "some" ya "a piece of" chalega.

Teen baat jo kaafi hain

1. Kaam-dhandha batao to article lagao — I am a teacher. 2. Pehli baar "a / an", doosri baar "the". 3. General plural aur general uncountable → kuch nahi.

docs.title: 6.7 Practice — Articles
docs.text:
Exercise 1

My brother is ___ MBA student.

  • a
  • an
  • the
  • kuch nahi

Hint: M ko bolkar dekho — kaunsi aawaz nikalti hai?

Jawaab

an

M ki aawaz 'em' hai — vowel se shuru. Isliye 'an MBA'. Akshar M consonant hai, par aawaz vowel hai, aur rule aawaz ka hai.

Exercise 2

She studies at ___ university in Pune.

  • a
  • an
  • the
  • kuch nahi

Hint: University bolkar dekho — yu ya u?

Jawaab

a

'University' ki pehli aawaz 'yu' hai, jo consonant jaisi hai. Isliye 'a university' — 'an university' galat hai.

Exercise 3

___ Himalayas are in the north of India.

  • A
  • An
  • The
  • kuch nahi

Hint: Pahaad ki shrinkhala ka naam hai.

Jawaab

The

Pahaad ki shrinkhala, nadi aur samudra ke naam ke pehle 'the' lagta hai — the Himalayas, the Ganga, the Arabian Sea.

Exercise 4

___ milk is good for children. (general baat)

  • A
  • The
  • An
  • kuch nahi

Hint: General baat hai, koi khaas doodh nahi.

Jawaab

kuch nahi

Uncountable noun jab general matlab me aaye to article nahi lagta. 'The milk' sirf tab jab koi khaas doodh ho — jaise fridge me rakha hua.

Exercise 5

I saw a snake in the garden. ___ snake was bright green.

Hint: Doosri baar zikr ho raha hai.

Jawaab

The

Pehli baar 'a snake', kyunki sunne wala nahi jaanta tha kaunsa. Doosri baar 'the snake' — ab dono jaante hain kis saanp ki baat hai.

Exercise 6

Is vaakya me ek shabd galat hai — us par tap karo.

My uncle is a honest officer in the railways.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: a.

Sahi roop: My uncle is an honest officer in the railways.

'Honest' me h chup hai — aawaz 'o' se shuru hoti hai, isliye 'an honest'. Rule akshar ka nahi, aawaz ka hai. Isi tarah an hour, an heir.

Exercise 7

Rohit is ___ tallest boy in our class.

Hint: Superlative hai.

Jawaab

the

Superlative (tallest, best, first) ke pehle hamesha 'the', kyunki aisa sirf ek hi ho sakta hai.

Exercise 8

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — galat shabd par tap karo.

My brother comes home by the bus every evening.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: the.

Sahi roop: My brother comes home by bus every evening.

'by + vehicle' ke saath article nahi lagta — by bus, by train, by car. 'The' yahan se hatana hai.

Exercise 9

Galat shabd dhoondo.

My sister plays the cricket after school.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: the.

Sahi roop: My sister plays cricket after school.

Khel ke naam ke saath article nahi aata. Baaje ke saath aata hai — 'plays the guitar' bilkul sahi hai.

Exercise 10

Ek shabd galat hai — pakdo.

She gave me a very useful information.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: a.

Sahi roop: She gave me very useful information.

'Information' uncountable hai, isliye 'a' nahi lagta. Ginna ho to 'a piece of information' bolo.

Exercise 11

Vaakya ko uske sahi article se jodo.

A B ___ sun rises in the east a I want ___ apple kuch nahi He is ___ good teacher the ___ children love sweets an Jawaab

___ sun rises in the east — the; I want ___ apple — an; He is ___ good teacher — a; ___ children love sweets — kuch nahi

Duniya me ek hi cheez → the. Vowel aawaz → an. Consonant aawaz → a. General plural → kuch nahi.

Exercise 12

Sahi kram me vaakya banao.

Shabd: a / in / engineer / private / I / am / an / company

Jawaab

I am an engineer in a private company

Kaam-dhandha batate waqt article zaroori hai — 'an engineer'. Aur 'company' pehli baar aayi hai, isliye 'a private company'.

Exercise 13

Ab ye line bol ke dekho — dono article saaf bolne hain.

Jawaab

Bolo: I bought a book and the book was very good

Pehli baar 'a book', doosri baar 'the book'. Bolte waqt 'the' se pehle halka ruk jao — isse sunne wale ko pata chalta hai ki aap usi kitaab ki baat kar rahe ho.

Aage kya karein

Aaj akhbaar ki ek khabar lo aur har a, an, the par pencil se gola lagao. Phir khud se poochho — "ye yahan kyun hai?" Ye ek exercise article ko hamesha ke liye pakka kar deti hai, kisi rule ko ratne se zyada.

docs.title: Chapter 43: Basic se Native
docs.text:
Basic se Native — wahi baat, naya andaaz

Aapki English galat nahi hai. I am very tired poora sahi vaakya hai — grammar perfect, matlab saaf. Phir bhi ek native speaker shayad ye nahi bolega. Wo bolega I'm running on fumes. Is chapter me hum wahi farq seekhenge: sahi English se natural English tak ka chhota safar. Aur sabse zaroori baat — kaunsa phrase kahan bolna hai, kyunki galat jagah par bola gaya natural phrase basic phrase se zyada kharab lagta hai.

Ek line me

Native lagna mushkil shabd se nahi aata — sahi phrase sahi maahaul me rakhne se aata hai. Bade shabd ratne ki zaroorat nahi; thode phrases, par unka sahi istemaal.

docs.title: 43.1 Chaar jodi jo aaj se kaam aayengi
docs.text: Pehle in chaar ko theek se samajh lo. Har ek ke saath tasveer banao dimaag me — phrase ka asli matlab tabhi baithta hai.

docs.title: I'm very tired → I'm running on fumes
docs.text:
"Fumes" matlab petrol ki bhaap — gaadi me petrol khatam, bas dhuaan bacha hai, aur wo phir bhi chal rahi hai. Yahi tasveer hai: energy khatam ho chuki hai par kaam jaari hai. Isliye ye phrase sirf "neend aa rahi hai" ke liye nahi hai; ye tab hai jab aap teen din ki deadline ke baad bhi laptop khole baithe ho.

  • Honestly, I'm running on fumes — can we finish this tomorrow morning? Sach kahun to meri energy bilkul khatam hai — kal subah nipta lein?

Aur bhi options, halke se bhaari ki taraf: I'm beat (casual, dosti me), I'm wiped out (thoda zyada thaka), I'm exhausted (har jagah safe — office, interview, doctor).

docs.title: I don't understand → I'm not following
docs.text:
I don't understand sunne wale ko lagta hai "mujhe samajh nahi aata, main kamzor hoon". I'm not following ka matlab hai "aapki baat ka dhaaga mere haath se chhoot gaya" — ilzaam na aap par, na saamne wale par. Office aur meeting ke liye yahi best hai.

  • Sorry, I'm not following — could you walk me through that part again? Maaf kijiye, main samajh nahi paaya — wo hissa dobara samjha denge?
  • You've lost me. What happens after the payment fails? Main peechhe chhoot gaya. Payment fail hone ke baad kya hota hai?

docs.title: I need to leave → I should get going
docs.text:
I need to leave me majboori hai, jaise koi emergency ho. I should get going narm hai, polite hai, aur jaana apni marzi lagta hai. Kisi ke ghar se nikalte waqt, call khatam karte waqt — yahi line hai.

  • This was lovely, but I should get going — it's a long drive back. Bahut achha laga, par ab mujhe nikalna chahiye — waapsi ka raasta lamba hai.
  • I'd better head out before the traffic starts. Traffic shuru hone se pehle nikal jaata hoon.

docs.title: I made a mistake → I dropped the ball
docs.text:
Yahan dhyan do, kyunki ye jodi barabar nahi hai. I dropped the ball har galti ke liye nahi hai — ye tab hai jab kaam aapke zimme tha aur aapse chhoot gaya. Typo ke liye ye phrase bolna over-dramatic lagega. Client ko follow-up email bhejna bhool gaye — ab theek hai.

  • I dropped the ball on the vendor follow-up. I'm fixing it today. Vendor ka follow-up mere haath se chhoot gaya. Aaj theek kar deta hoon.
  • That one's on me — I misread the deadline. Wo galti meri hai — maine deadline galat padh li.

Galti maanne ka native formula

Maano + theek karne ka plan, safai nahi. "I dropped the ball on this. Here's what I'm doing about it." Native English me galti ke baad "sorry sorry" nahi, aage ka plan aata hai. Yahi professional lagta hai.

docs.title: 43.2 Roz kaam aane wali upgrade table
docs.text:
Baayein taraf wo jo hum bolte hain, daayein taraf wo jo kaan ko natural lagta hai. Teesra column sabse zaroori hai — kab.

Plain Native Kab bolna theek hai I am very busy I'm swamped Office, colleagues, WhatsApp. Boss ko bhi theek hai. Client ke pehle email me nahi. I will think about it Let me sleep on it Jab faisla kal tak tal sakta ho. Meeting aur dosti dono me chalta hai. Tell me about it later Fill me in later Casual aur office. "Fill me in" = chhooti hui baat bata dena. I agree completely Couldn't agree more Har jagah safe — meeting, interview, dost. It is not a problem No worries Casual aur normal office. Formal email me "That's absolutely fine" likho. I am confused I'm a bit lost here Meeting aur class — honest lagta hai, kamzor nahi. Please wait a little Bear with me Jab aap screen share kar rahe ho ya kuch dhoond rahe ho. Bahut natural. I did it very fast, so it is rough It's a first pass Office. Kaam bhejte waqt expectation set karne ke liye. We have very little time We're cutting it close Team ke saath. Client ko "the timeline is tight" kehna behtar. I understood Got it / Makes sense Har roz, har jagah. "Noted with thanks" se bahut behtar. Let us start Let's dive in Presentation aur meeting ki shuruaat. I will do it later I'll circle back on this Sirf office. Doston me ye corporate lagta hai aur hasi aati hai.

docs.title: 43.3 Jazbaat wale upgrades — gussa, dar, khushi, thakaan
docs.text:
Feelings batate waqt I'm very ___ sabse aam aadat hai. Native speaker "very" ki jagah ek tasveer wala phrase uthata hai. Har line par 🔊 dabao aur rhythm suno — ye phrases ek saans me bole jaate hain.

Basic Native Matlab Kab use karein I'm very angry I'm seeing red right now Gusse se aankhon ke aage laal-laal dikh raha hai. Casual, dost aur family. Bahut tez gussa hai — office me bologe to log ghabra jaayenge. Wahan I'm really frustrated. I'm very scared I'm freaking out right now Dar ya ghabrahat se haalat kharab hai. Sirf casual. Dar ke saath-saath "panic" bhi isi me aata hai. Formal me I'm really worried. I'm very confused I'm totally thrown off Kuch achaanak badla aur main patri se utar gaya. Casual aur office dono. Khaas kar jab plan ya jawaab achaanak badal jaaye. I'm very nervous I'm a little worked up Andar se bechaini aur tension chal rahi hai. Casual. Dhyan do — worked up me thoda gussa ya bhadkaav bhi ho sakta hai. Sirf ghabrahat ke liye I've got butterflies bhi bolte hain. I'm very surprised I'm completely caught off guard Bilkul taiyaar nahi tha, baat ne chaunka diya. Har jagah safe — meeting me bhi. Achhi ya buri, dono tarah ki surprise ke liye. I'm very happy I'm feeling great about it Is baat ko lekar man bahut khush aur bharosemand hai. Har jagah safe. Kisi faisle, result ya plan ke baare me khushi — sirf mood ke liye I'm in a great mood. I'm very tired I'm running on fumes Energy khatam, phir bhi kaam chal raha hai. Casual aur team. Poori kahani upar Section 1 me — doctor ke saamne nahi.

Teen phrases jo galat jagah ajeeb lagte hain

seeing red = bahut tez gussa, chhoti chidh ke liye nahi · freaking out = slang, interview ya client ke saamne nahi · worked up = ghabrahat ya bhadkaav — context se saaf karo. Jazbaat wale idioms dost ke saath sabse natural hain; office me neutral roop uthao.

docs.title: 43.4 Kaam aur roz ki baat — 12 aur upgrades
docs.text:
Ye wo lines hain jo din me das baar aati hain — paise, kaam, plan aur mana karna. Inme se zyadatar neutral zone ke hain, yaani office aur dosti dono me chalte hain.

Basic Native Matlab Kab use karein I need to leave I need to get going Ab mujhe nikalna hai. Har jagah safe. I should get going (Section 1) aur narm hai; need to me thodi jaldi hai. I don't understand I'm not catching your drift Aap kehna kya chahte ho, wo pakad nahi paa raha. Casual, thoda purana andaaz. Ishaare wali baat ke liye. Meeting me I'm not following behtar. That's expensive That's gonna cost me big time Isme meri jeb ka bada nuksaan hoga. Sirf bolchaal. Gonna kabhi likhna nahi. Client ko: That's above our budget. I'm very busy I've got a lot on my plate Meri thaali me pehle se bahut kaam pada hai. Har jagah safe — boss ko bhi. I'm swamped se thoda narm. I don't want it I think I'll pass on that Shukriya, par is baar rehne dijiye. Polite mana — khaana, offer, invitation. I don't want it rukha lagta hai. That's very difficult That's a tough nut to crack Sakht akhrot — todna mushkil. Office aur casual. Problem, sawaal ya mushkil insaan ke liye. Idiom fix hai — crack hi aayega. I don't know yet I haven't figured it out yet Abhi tak samajh ya tay nahi kar paaya. Har jagah safe. Isme "koshish jaari hai" ka bhaav hai. I made a mistake I dropped the ball on that Wo kaam mere zimme tha aur chhoot gaya. Team aur manager. Chhoti typo ke liye nahi — Section 1 dekho. Let's talk later Let's touch base later Baad me thodi der ke liye baat kar lete hain. Office ki bhasha. Doston me corporate lagega — wahan Let's catch up later. I'm ready to start I'm ready to get started Main shuru karne ke liye taiyaar hoon. Har jagah safe — meeting, class, interview. That's very annoying That's getting on my nerves Ye cheez dimaag kharab kar rahi hai. Casual. Nerves hamesha plural. Kisi insaan ke muh par bolna rude lagega. I'll handle it I'll take care of it Aap chinta mat karo, main sambhal lunga. Har jagah safe — client ko bhi. I'll handle it bhi sahi hai, bas thoda rukha.

Teen jo har jagah chal jaate hain

Agar is table me se sirf teen uthane hain to ye uthao: I've got a lot on my plate, I'll take care of it, I think I'll pass on that. Teeno neutral hain — dost, manager aur client, sabke saath bina dar ke bolo.

docs.title: 43.5 Register — phrase ki jagah ka naksha
docs.text:
English ke phrases ek line par baithe hote hain: ek sire par bilkul casual, doosre sire par bilkul formal. Beech wala hissa sabse kaam ka hai — wahan ke phrases dost ke saath bhi chalte hain aur manager ke saath bhi. Agar confusion ho, beech se uthao.

Figure 43.1. Ek hi baat, teen jagah ke teen roop. Agar pata na ho ki kahan ho — beech wala column bolo.

Over-correction — asli khatra

Naya phrase seekh kar use har jagah thoos dena sabse aam galti hai. Doctor ke saamne "I'm running on fumes" bolne se wo samajh hi nahi payega ki aapko kitni neend aa rahi hai. Wahan seedha "I've been sleeping badly for a week" bolo. Natural phrase galat jagah = basic phrase se bura. Pehle maahaul dekho, phir shabd chuno.

docs.title: 43.6 Chhoti aadatein jo turant farq laati hain
docs.text:
Phrases ke alawa teen aadatein hain jo aapki English ko ek hi hafte me natural bana deti hain.

a) Contractions bolo

Native log I am, do not, it is pura nahi bolte — I'm, don't, it's bolte hain. Pura roop sirf zor dene ke liye: "I am listening!" Bina contraction wali English kitaabi lagti hai, galat nahi — bas thodi akdi hui.

b) Softener lagao

Native English direct hone se bachti hai. Ek chhota shabd jod do: a bit, kind of, maybe, I think, actually. "This is wrong" → "I think there's a small issue here." Softener se baat kam hamlawar lagti hai — office me ye bahut kaam aata hai.

c) Jawaab lamba karo, do lafz nahi

"How was your weekend?" ka jawaab "Fine" nahi. "Pretty quiet, actually — I just caught up on sleep. You?" Ek chhoti detail + waapis sawaal. Yahi conversation chalti rakhta hai.

docs.title: 43.7 Jo galtiyan native phrases ke saath hoti hain
docs.text:
Phrase theek, istemaal galat

  • Galat: I am running in fumes.
  • Sahi: I'm running on fumes.

  • Kyun: Idiom ke chhote shabd badalne se wo toot jaata hai. Phrase poora, jaisa hai waisa yaad karo — on fumes, kyunki gaadi "petrol par" chalti hai.

  • Galat: I dropped the ball — I made one spelling mistake.

  • Sahi: Sorry, typo. Fixed it.

  • Kyun: Chhoti galti ke liye bada idiom bolna drama lagta hai. "Dropped the ball" tab jab zimmedari ka kaam chhoot gaya ho.

  • Galat: I am not following your.

  • Sahi: I'm not following.

  • Kyun: Ye phrase apne aap me poora hai — object ki zaroorat nahi. Agar jodna hai to: I'm not following your point.

  • Galat: I should get going now itself.

  • Sahi: I should get going right now.

  • Kyun: "Now itself" Indian English ki aadat hai — bahar samajh nahi aati. Sahi roop: right now ya right away.

  • Galat: Let me sleep over it.

  • Sahi: Let me sleep on it.
  • Kyun: "Sleep over" bachchon ka raat ruk jaana hai. Faisla talne ke liye sleep on it.

docs.title: 43.8 Ek chhota script — yahi roz bolna hai
docs.text:
Neeche ek standard office exchange hai, dono roop me. Zor se do baar padho — pehle baayein, phir daayein. Farq kaan se samajh aayega.

Textbook English Jo log asal me bolte hain Good morning. How are you? Morning! How's it going? I have completed the report. I've wrapped up the report. I did not understand the second point. I'm not following the second point. Please give me some time. Bear with me for a minute. I will inform you afterwards. I'll let you know. I am very tired today. I'm running on fumes today. I have to go now. I should get going.

docs.title: 43.9 Practice — Basic se native
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Office meeting me kisi ki baat samajh nahi aayi. Sabse natural line kaunsi hai?

  • Sorry, I'm not following.
  • I am not understanding.
  • I have a doubt in your talk.
  • Please repeat it again.

Hint: Ilzaam kisi par na aaye.

Jawaab

Sorry, I'm not following.

'I'm not following' neutral hai — na aap kamzor lagte ho, na saamne wala galat. 'I am not understanding' grammar se bhi galat hai, aur 'repeat it again' me 'again' bekaar hai.

Exercise 2

Aapne ek bade client ka follow-up email bhejna bhool gaye. Manager ko kya bologe?

  • I dropped the ball on the client follow-up.
  • I am running on fumes.
  • Let me sleep on it.
  • I'm swamped so it is not my fault.
Jawaab

I dropped the ball on the client follow-up.

Zimmedari ka kaam chhoot gaya = dropped the ball. Baaki phrases ka matlab yahan fit nahi baithta, aur aakhri line safai de rahi hai — jo kabhi achha nahi lagta.

Exercise 3

Doctor ke saamne apni thakaan batani hai. Kya bolna chahiye?

  • I've been exhausted for two weeks and sleeping badly.
  • I'm running on fumes, doc.
  • I'm beat.
  • I'm totally wiped.

Hint: Yahan saaf jaankari chahiye, style nahi.

Jawaab

I've been exhausted for two weeks and sleeping badly.

Doctor ko detail chahiye, idiom nahi. Yahi over-correction ka khatra hai — natural phrase galat jagah par ulta nuksaan karta hai.

Exercise 4

This was fun, but I should get ___ — it's getting late.

Hint: Nikalne ka narm tareeka.

Jawaab

going

'I should get going' = mujhe ab nikalna chahiye. 'I need to leave' se zyada polite aur zyada natural hai.

Exercise 5

Give me a minute to find the file — please ___ with me.

Hint: Jaanwar nahi, phrase hai: ___ with me.

Jawaab

bear

'Bear with me' = thoda sabr kijiye. Screen share karte waqt ya kuch dhoondte waqt native log yahi bolte hain.

Exercise 6

Is vaakya me idiom toot gaya hai — galat shabd par tap karo.

After three night shifts I am running in fumes.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: in.

Sahi roop: After three night shifts I'm running on fumes.

Idiom ke chhote shabd fix hote hain — 'on fumes', 'in' nahi. Idiom ke andar ka ek shabd badla to poora phrase ajnabi lagta hai.

Exercise 7

Ek shabd Indian English ki aadat hai aur bahar samajh nahi aata — use dhoondo.

I should get going now itself.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: itself.

Sahi roop: I should get going right now.

'Now itself' sirf India me chalta hai. International call me 'right now' ya 'right away' bolo.

Exercise 8

Plain line ko uske natural roop se jodo.

A B I am very busy Got it I will think about it Couldn't agree more I understood I'm swamped I agree completely Let me sleep on it Jawaab

I am very busy — I'm swamped; I will think about it — Let me sleep on it; I understood — Got it; I agree completely — Couldn't agree more

Chaaron daayein wale roop neutral zone ke hain — office aur dosti, dono me chalte hain.

Exercise 9

Phrase ko uski sahi jagah se jodo.

A B My bad likhit, formal email I dropped the ball sirf office ki bhasha I take full responsibility dost ke saath, bilkul casual I'll circle back on this team ya manager ke saath Jawaab

My bad — dost ke saath, bilkul casual; I dropped the ball — team ya manager ke saath; I take full responsibility — likhit, formal email; I'll circle back on this — sirf office ki bhasha

Register ka naksha yaad rakho: ek hi baat ke teen roop, aur unki jagah alag.

Exercise 10

Sahi kram me lagao — manager ko galti batane wali line.

Shabd: the / today / it / am / this / and / on / I / I / ball / fixing / dropped

Jawaab

I dropped the ball on this and I am fixing it today

Native formula: pehle galti maano, phir aage ka plan batao. Safai beech me nahi aati.

Exercise 11

Kaunsi aadat aapki English ko turant natural banati hai?

  • Contractions bolna — I'm, don't, it's
  • Har vaakya me ek bada shabd daalna
  • Hamesha pura roop bolna — I am, do not
  • Har jawaab do shabd me dena
Jawaab

Contractions bolna — I'm, don't, it's

Contractions rhythm theek karte hain. Pura roop kitaabi lagta hai, aur do-shabd ke jawaab conversation maar dete hain.

Exercise 12

Manager ne naya kaam diya, par aapke paas pehle se bahut kaam hai. Sabse natural aur polite line?

  • I've got a lot on my plate right now.
  • I am having many works today.
  • I'm seeing red right now.
  • That's gonna cost me big time.
Jawaab

I've got a lot on my plate right now.

'A lot on my plate' = thaali me pehle se bahut kaam. Ye manager ke saath bhi safe hai. 'Seeing red' gussa hai aur 'cost me big time' paison ki baat.

Exercise 13

Client ko formal email likh rahe ho. Kaunsi line yahan NAHI likhni chahiye?

  • That's gonna cost me big time.
  • I'll take care of it.
  • I'm ready to get started.
  • I haven't figured it out yet.

Hint: Ek line sirf bolchaal ki hai.

Jawaab

That's gonna cost me big time.

'Gonna' aur 'big time' sirf bolne ki bhasha hai. Client ko 'That's above our budget' likho. Baaki teeno lines har jagah safe hain.

Exercise 14

This bug has taken three days — it's a tough nut to ___.

Hint: Akhrot ke saath kaunsa verb aata hai?

Jawaab

crack

'A tough nut to crack' = mushkil masla. Idiom fix hai — 'break' ya 'open' lagane se toot jaata hai.

Exercise 15

Idiom me ek shabd galat roop me hai — use dhoondo.

The drilling next door is getting on my nerve.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: nerve.

Sahi roop: The drilling next door is getting on my nerves.

'Getting on my nerves' me 'nerves' hamesha plural hai. 'Nerve' akela matlab badal deta hai (himmat).

Exercise 16

Basic feeling ko uske native roop se jodo.

A B I'm very angry I'm caught off guard I'm very scared I'm totally thrown off I'm very surprised I'm seeing red I'm very confused I'm freaking out Jawaab

I'm very angry — I'm seeing red; I'm very scared — I'm freaking out; I'm very surprised — I'm caught off guard; I'm very confused — I'm totally thrown off

Chaaron phrases tasveer wale hain — laal rang, ghabrahat, bina taiyaari, patri se utarna. Pehle teen zyada tar casual hain.

Exercise 17

Ab ye line bol kar dekho. 'I'm' ek hi aawaz me, aur 'not following' me zor 'foll' par.

Jawaab

Bolo: Sorry I'm not following could you walk me through that again

Bolte waqt 'I'm not following' me pause nahi aata — ek saath beh jaata hai. Yahi rhythm native lagta hai.

Aage kya karein

Poori table ratne ki koshish mat karo. Is hafte sirf teen phrases chuno — I'm not following, I should get going, bear with me — aur unhe roz bolo. Teen phrases jo aapke muh me baith gaye, tees ratte phrases se zyada kaam ke hain.

docs.title: Chapter 25: Asar daar vaakya
docs.text:
Grammar sahi ho jaane ke baad agla kadam hai asar. "Maine car theek karwayi", "aisa maine kabhi nahi dekha", "mujhe bas chhutti chahiye" — inhe English me kehne ke khaas tareeke hain jo aapki baat ko vazan dete hain. Is chapter me paanch auzaar hain: causative, inversion, cleft sentences, emphatic do aur chhote jawaab (so do I, I hope not).

Ek line me

get it done = karwana · Never have I… = zor ke liye ulta kram · What I need is… = ek hisse par roshni · I do like it = sach me · So do I = main bhi. Matlab wahi, par vaakya ka dhaancha badal kar zor paida karna.

docs.title: 25.1 Paanch auzaar — ek nazar me
docs.text:
Pehle poora naksha dekh lo. Har auzaar ek saadharan vaakya leta hai aur use zyada saaf, zyada formal ya zyada bhaavuk bana deta hai.

Auzaar Saadharan Asardaar Causative A mechanic repaired my car. I got my car repaired. Inversion I have never seen this. Never have I seen this. Cleft I need a holiday. What I need is a holiday. Emphatic do I like it. I do like it. Ellipsis I like tea too. So do I.
  • Never have I seen such a crowd at Marine Drive. Marine Drive par itni bheed maine kabhi nahi dekhi.
  • What I need is a long holiday. Mujhe to bas ek lambi chhutti chahiye.

docs.title: 25.2 Causative — "karwana" English me
docs.text:
Hindi me banana → banwana, kaatna → katwana, theek karna → theek karwana — ek chhota sa "-wa-" batata hai ki kaam kisi aur ne kiya. English me iske liye have / get + cheez + V3 lagta hai. Ye bahut zaroori hai, kyunki iske bina English bolne wala sochega ki kaam aapne khud kiya.

Figure 25.1. Causative me kaam karne wala beech me chhup jaata hai. Vaakya sirf itna kehta hai: cheez par kaam hua , aur wo maine karwaya .

Causative ka formula

have / get + object + V3 = karwana. get bolchaal me zyada, have thoda formal. Kram pakka: pehle cheez, phir V3 — got my car repaired.

  • I got my car repaired last week. Pichhle hafte maine car theek karwayi.
  • She had her hair cut short. Usne baal chhote katwa liye.
  • We're having the house painted before Diwali. Diwali se pehle hum ghar paint karwa rahe hain.
  • Where do you get your kurtas stitched? Tum apne kurte kahan silwaate ho?
  • You need to get your eyes tested. Tumhe aankhein check karwani chahiye.
  • Don't worry, I'll get it done by Friday. Fikar mat karo, Friday tak ho jaayega (main karwa dunga / kar dunga).

✗

I cut my hair yesterday. (barber ne kaate)

✓

I got my hair cut yesterday.

✗

I got repaired my phone.

✓

I got my phone repaired.

object

docs.title: Jab kuch bura "ho jaaye"
docs.text:
Yahi dhaancha tab bhi chalta hai jab aapke saath kuch bura hua ho — yahan "karwaya" ka matlab nahi, bas "mere saath hua":

  • I had my phone stolen on the local train. Local train me mera phone chori ho gaya.

docs.title: 25.3 have someone do, get someone to do, make, let, help
docs.text:
Kabhi aap insaan ka naam lena chahte ho — "maine Ravi se file bhijwayi", "usne mujhe rukwaya". Yahan har verb ka apna pattern hai: kisi ke baad seedha V1, kisi ke baad to + V1. Yahi galti ka sabse bada adda hai.

Verb Pattern Matlab / Example have have + person + V1 kaam saunpna: I'll have Ravi send it. get get + person + to V1 manana: I got him to sign. make make + person + V1 majboor karna: She made me wait. let let + person + V1 ijaazat dena: Let me go. help help + person + (to) V1 madad: Help me (to) carry this.
  • I'll have my assistant email you the details. Main apne assistant se aapko details email karwa dunga.
  • I finally got the landlord to fix the geyser. Aakhirkaar maine makaan-maalik ko geyser theek karne ke liye mana liya.
  • The teacher made us rewrite the essay. Teacher ne hamse essay dobara likhwaya.
  • My parents didn't let me go on the trip. Mummy-papa ne mujhe trip par jaane nahi diya.
  • Can you help me move this almirah? Ye almari khiskane me meri madad karoge?

✗

He made me to wait for an hour.

✓

He made me wait for an hour.

I was made to wait.

✗

Please let me to explain.

✓

Please let me explain. / Please allow me to explain.

to

Teen chhote shabd, teen alag zor

make = zabardasti · let = chhoot · get … to = samjha-bujha kar. "My boss made me stay" (majboori) vs "My boss let me leave early" (meharbaani) vs "I got my boss to approve it" (meri koshish).

docs.title: 25.4 Inversion — "Never have I…" wala zor
docs.text:
Jab vaakya kisi negative ya seemit shabd se shuru ho (never, rarely, not only, hardly, only then…), to uske baad subject aur helping verb jagah badal lete hain — bilkul sawaal ki tarah. Ye formal, likhit ya speech wali English hai; isse baat me drama aur vazan aata hai.

Figure 25.2. Do kadam: negative shabd aage, phir helping verb + subject — jaise Have I…? sawaal me hota hai.

Inversion ka niyam

Negative/limiting shabd + helping verb + subject + baaki. Helping verb nahi hai to do / does / did lagao: Rarely do we eat out.

Shuruaat Example Suno Never / Rarely / Seldom Rarely do we get such rain in April. Not only … but also Not only did she top the class, but she also won the debate. Hardly / Scarcely … when Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang. No sooner … than No sooner had we reached than it started pouring. Only then / Only after Only then did I realise my mistake. Under no circumstances Under no circumstances should you share your OTP. Little Little did he know what was coming.
  • Not only did she top the class, but she also won the debate. Usne na sirf class me top kiya, balki debate bhi jeeti.
  • Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang. Main baitha hi tha ki phone baj utha.
  • Only after the results came out did he start studying. Result aane ke baad hi usne padhna shuru kiya.

✗

Never I have seen such a crowd.

✓

Never have I seen such a crowd.

I have never seen such a crowd.

✗

No sooner had we reached when it started raining.

✓

No sooner had we reached than it started raining.

No sooner … than

Hardly / Scarcely … when

✗

Not only she sings, but she also dances.

✓

Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

Roz ki baat me kam

Dosto ke saath "Never have I eaten such good pani puri!" thoda natakiya lagega (mazaak me chalega). Inversion ki asli jagah: essay, speech, formal email, IELTS writing. Bolchaal me "I've never eaten such good pani puri!" hi kaafi hai.

docs.title: 25.5 if ke bina if — Should you…, Had I…, Were I…
docs.text:
Formal English me if hata kar helping verb ko aage la dete hain. Matlab bilkul wahi rehta hai jo conditional ka — bas zyada sophisticated (conditionals ki poori kahani If wale vaakya chapter me hai).

if wala roop Inversion If you need any help, … Should you need any help, … If I had known, … Had I known, … If I were you, … Were I in your place, … If it had not rained, … Had it not rained, …
  • Should you need any help, please call me. Agar kabhi madad chahiye ho to mujhe call kijiye. (email ki pasandida line)
  • Had I known about the strike, I would have taken the metro. Agar mujhe hadtaal ka pata hota, to main metro le leta.
  • Were I in your place, I would accept the offer. Aapki jagah main hota to offer maan leta.
  • Had it not rained, we would have won. Agar baarish na hoti to hum jeet jaate.

✗

Hadn't I known, I would have gone.

✓

Had I not known, I would have gone.

docs.title: 25.6 Cleft sentences — ek hisse par spotlight
docs.text: "Cleft" ka matlab hai "do tukde". Ek vaakya ko tod kar do hisson me likhte hain taaki ek khaas cheez par roshni pade — khaas kar jab aap kisi galatfehmi ko sudhaar rahe ho. Hindi me ye kaam "hi" karta hai: Ravi ne hi todi thi.

docs.title: (a) It is / was … who / that …
docs.text:
• It was Ravi who broke the glass, not Amit. Gilaas Ravi ne hi toda tha, Amit ne nahi.
  • It's the price that worries me, not the quality. Mujhe quality nahi, daam pareshaan kar raha hai.
  • It was in Jaipur that they first met. Wo dono pehli baar Jaipur me hi mile the.

docs.title: (b) What … is / All … is / The reason … is
docs.text:
• What I need is a good night's sleep. Mujhe to bas achhi neend chahiye.
  • What she did was call the police immediately. Usne jo kiya wo ye tha — turant police ko phone.
  • All I want is some peace and quiet. Mujhe bas thoda sukoon chahiye — aur kuch nahi.
  • The reason I called is to ask about Saturday. Maine isliye call kiya ki Saturday ke baare me poochh sakoon.

Cleft = 'hi' wala zor

It was X who/that… = X hi. What I need is X = mujhe to X chahiye. All I want is X = bas X, aur kuch nahi.

✗

All what I want is a holiday.

✓

All I want is a holiday. / What I want is a holiday.

✗

It was my sister which found the keys.

✓

It was my sister who (ya that) found the keys.

Chhote se bade vaakya

docs.title: 25.7 Emphatic do aur fronting — "sach me!"
docs.text:
Positive vaakya me do / does / did + V1 daal kar (aur us par zor de kar) aap kehte ho "sach me", "waqai", "maine kiya tha!". Ye tab kaam aata hai jab koi aapki baat par shak kare, ya aap kisi baat ko garmjoshi se kehna chahte ho.

  • I do like your new haircut — honestly! Tumhara naya haircut mujhe sach me pasand hai!
  • I did call you — three times! Maine call kiya tha — teen baar!
  • She does know a lot about cars. Use cars ke baare me waqai bahut pata hai.
  • Do sit down, Uncle — make yourself at home. Baithiye na, Uncle — apna hi ghar samjhiye.

✗

I did called you yesterday!

✓

I did call you yesterday!

Zor aawaz me bhi

Emphatic do likhne se zyada bolne ki cheez hai — "do / did" ko lamba aur zor se bolo: "I DID call you." Is taal ke liye Rhythm aur stress chapter dekho.

docs.title: Fronting — jo zaroori hai, wo pehle
docs.text:
Kabhi object ya koi hissa vaakya ke shuru me le aate hain, taaki contrast dikhe. Kram (subject + verb) waisa hi rehta hai — ye inversion nahi hai.

  • Tea I can live without. Coffee, never. Chai ke bina reh lunga. Coffee ke bina — kabhi nahi.
  • Strange as it may seem, I enjoy Monday mornings. Ajeeb lagega, par mujhe Monday ki subah achhi lagti hai.

docs.title: 25.8 Chhote jawaab — so do I, neither do I, I hope not
docs.text:
Native speaker poora vaakya dohraate nahi. Wo sirf helping verb se jawaab dete hain — isse ellipsis (chhod dena) kehte hain. Hindi me "main bhi", "main bhi nahi" — English me helping verb pichhle vaakya se match karna padta hai.

Doosre ne kaha Main bhi Main bhi nahi I love biryani. So do I. — I can't swim. — Neither can I. I'm tired. So am I. — I didn't go. — Neither / Nor did I. I've been there. So have I. —
  • "I love biryani." — "So do I!" "Mujhe biryani pasand hai." — "Mujhe bhi!"
  • "I didn't sleep well." — "Neither did I." "Mujhe theek se neend nahi aayi." — "Mujhe bhi nahi."
  • Informal: "Me too." / "Me neither." Dosto me chhota roop bilkul theek hai.

✗

"I don't eat meat." — "Me also not." / "I also don't."

✓

"Neither do I." / "Me neither."

docs.title: so / not — poore vaakya ki jagah
docs.text:
think, hope, guess, be afraid ke baad so (haan wala) aur not (na wala) poore clause ki jagah le lete hain.

Sawaal Jawaab Matlab Will it rain? I think so. mujhe lagta hai haan Is the shop open? I don't think so. shayad nahi Will we miss the flight? I hope not. ummeed hai nahi Is it serious, doctor? I'm afraid so. afsos, haan Can you come? I'd love to. zaroor aana chahunga
  • "Will the match be cancelled?" — "I hope not." "Match cancel hoga kya?" — "Ummeed hai nahi hoga."
  • "Are you coming to the wedding?" — "I'd love to, but I can't." "Shaadi me aa rahe ho?" — "Aana to chahta hoon, par nahi aa paunga."

✗

"Is he coming?" — "I think yes." / "I don't think."

✓

"I think so." / "I don't think so."

so

docs.title: 25.9 Asli zindagi me — ek interview jawaab
docs.text:
Interviewer ne poochha: "Tell me about a challenge you faced." Dekho kaise ek hi jawaab me kai auzaar milkar baat ko yaadgaar bana dete hain.

Vaakya Auzaar Suno Last year our biggest client threatened to leave. — What they wanted was a working app in two weeks. Cleft I got the whole team to work in two shifts. get + person + to Not only did we deliver on time, but we also cut costs. Inversion It was that project that taught me to plan backwards. Cleft

Kitna use karein?

Ek jawaab me ek-do auzaar kaafi hain. Har vaakya ulta ya cleft hoga to baat banawati lagegi. Masala ki tarah — thoda sa, sahi jagah.

docs.title: 25.10 Practice — Asar daar vaakya
docs.text:
Exercise 1

My scooter broke down, so I ___ at the garage near my office.

  • got it repaired
  • got repaired it
  • repaired it
  • made it repair

Hint: Mechanic ne theek kiya.

Jawaab

got it repaired

Causative: get + object + V3. Cheez (it) beech me, phir V3.

Exercise 2

You should get your blood pressure ___ (check) regularly.

Hint: get + object + V3

Jawaab

checked

get + your blood pressure + checked = check karwana.

Exercise 3

The teacher made us ___ the whole chapter again.

  • read
  • to read
  • reading
  • reads
Jawaab

read

make + person + V1, bina 'to'. (Passive me: We were made to read…)

Exercise 4

Tap the extra word.

My father did not let me to go on the school trip.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: to.

Sahi roop: My father did not let me go on the school trip.

let + person + V1. 'to' sirf allow ke saath: allow me to go.

Exercise 5

Never ___ such a beautiful sunset.

  • have I seen
  • I have seen
  • I saw
  • seen I have
Jawaab

have I seen

Negative shabd aage = helping verb + subject (sawaal jaisa kram).

Exercise 6

No sooner had we reached the platform ___ the train left.

Hint: 'sooner' ek comparative hai.

Jawaab

than

Pakki jodi: No sooner … than.

Exercise 7

Hardly had I opened the laptop ___ the power went off.

  • when
  • than
  • then
  • that
Jawaab

when

Pakki jodi: Hardly / Scarcely … when.

Exercise 8

Put the words in order.

Shabd: not / she / also / only / the / record / she / did / broke / but / win

Jawaab

not only did she win but she also broke the record

Not only + did + subject + V1, but + subject + also …

Exercise 9

___ I known about the metro strike, I would have left earlier.

Hint: if ke bina third conditional

Jawaab

Had

Had I known = If I had known (formal inversion).

Exercise 10

___ I need right now is a cup of strong chai.

  • What
  • That
  • Which
  • All what
Jawaab

What

Cleft: What I need is … = mujhe to … chahiye.

Exercise 11

Tap the wrong word.

It was my sister which found the lost keys.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: which.

Sahi roop: It was my sister who found the lost keys.

Insaan ke liye who / that, 'which' nahi.

Exercise 12

Match the reply to its meaning.

A B So do I. ummeed hai aisa na ho Neither do I. afsos, haan I hope not. main bhi (haan wali baat par) I'm afraid so. main bhi nahi Jawaab

So do I. — main bhi (haan wali baat par); Neither do I. — main bhi nahi; I hope not. — ummeed hai aisa na ho; I'm afraid so. — afsos, haan

Chhote jawaab me helping verb ya so/not poore vaakya ki jagah le leta hai.

Exercise 13

A: I can't drive. B: Neither ___ I.

Hint: Pehle vaakya ka helping verb.

Jawaab

can

can't → Neither can I. Helping verb match karna padta hai.

Exercise 14

"Will the flight be on time?" — "I think ___."

  • so
  • yes
  • it
  • that
Jawaab

so

think / hope / guess ke baad haan = so. 'I think yes' galat hai.

Exercise 15

Who fixed the AC?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

I didn't fix the AC myself. I had a technician come over on Sunday, and he got it working in ten minutes.

  • a technician
  • the speaker
  • the speaker's father
  • nobody
Jawaab

a technician

'I had a technician come over' = have + person + V1. Kaam technician ne kiya.

Exercise 16

According to the speaker, what saved the project?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Not only did Ananya finish the report early, but she also found two mistakes in the budget. It was her careful checking that saved the project.

  • Ananya's careful checking
  • the early deadline
  • a bigger budget
  • the manager's help
Jawaab

Ananya's careful checking

Cleft 'It was her careful checking that…' isi par spotlight daalta hai.

Exercise 17

Write what you hear.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

Had I known you were coming, I would have cooked something special.

Had I known = If I had known.

Exercise 18

Write what you hear.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

What I need is a long holiday.

Cleft: What I need is …

Exercise 19

Say it with stress on 'do'.

Jawaab

Bolo: I do like your new haircut

Emphatic do = 'sach me'. 'do' ko lamba aur zor se bolo.

Aage kya karein

Apne agle formal email me ek Should you need… aur agli baat-cheet me ek What I need is… zaroor daalo. Aur jab bhi salon ya darzi ke paas jao, man me bolo: I'm getting my hair cut. Bolne ki taraf badhna ho to Rhythm aur stress aur Native speed English dekho.

docs.title: Chapter 20: Chhote se bade vaakya
docs.text:
Clauses — chhote vaakyon se bade vaakya

Agar aapki English me har vaakya chhota-chhota hai — "I have a friend. He lives in Delhi. He is a doctor." — to galat kuch nahi, par baat bachchon jaisi lagti hai. Clauses ko jodna seekh lo, to wahi baat ek saaf, pakke vaakya me aa jaati hai. Ye chapter wahi jodne ka hunar sikhata hai.

Ek line me

A clause is a group of words with its own subject and verb. A sentence can have one clause or many. Sentence structure wala chapter yaad hai? Phrase me subject-verb jodi nahi hoti; clause me hoti hai.

  • I have a friend who lives in Delhi. Do clause: "I have a friend" + "who lives in Delhi".
  • She was tired, so she went to bed early. Do clause, "so" se jude hue.

docs.title: 20.1 Independent aur Dependent clause
docs.text:
Har clause ek jaisa nahi hota. Kuch akele khade ho sakte hain, kuch nahi. Ye farq samajhna zaroori hai, kyunki adhoore clause ko poora vaakya maan lena likhne me sabse badi galti hai.

Figure 20.1. Dependent clause (dashed) ko khada rehne ke liye independent clause (solid) ka sahaara chahiye.

Independent vs dependent

Independent clause akela poora vaakya hai (I stayed at home.). Dependent clause because, when, if, although, who, which jaise shabd se shuru hota hai aur akela adhoora rehta hai — use independent clause se jodo.

Dependent clause shuru karne wale Kaam Example because, since, as kaaran because he was ill when, while, after, before, until samay when the bell rang if, unless shart if you call me although, though, even though virodh although it was late who, which, that, whose, where noun ke baare me who lives next door

docs.title: 20.2 Chaar tarah ke vaakya
docs.text:
Clauses kitne hain aur kaise jude hain — isse vaakya ke chaar prakaar bante hain. Achhi English me chaaron ka mel hota hai; sirf ek tarah ke vaakya likhne se lekh neeras ho jaata hai.

Figure 20.2. Solid dabba = independent clause, dashed = dependent. Prakaar sirf ginti se tay hota hai.

Chaar prakaar

Simple = ek independent clause. Compound = do independent (and, but, so se). Complex = independent + dependent (because, when, who se). Compound-complex = do independent + kam se kam ek dependent.

docs.title: 20.3 Compound — barabar ke do clause jodna
docs.text:
Jab do baatein barabar zaroori hon, to unhe compound sentence me jodo. Iske liye saat chhote shabd hain jinhe yaad karne ki trick hai — FANBOYS.

Shabd Kaam Example For kaaran (formal) He left early, for he was ill. And jodna I cooked, and she cleaned. Nor na ye, na wo He didn't call, nor did he write. But virodh It was cheap, but it was good. Or vikalp Hurry up, or we'll miss the train. Yet phir bhi She was tired, yet she kept working. So natija It was raining, so we stayed in.

Compound ka niyam

Do independent clause jodne ke liye comma + FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so) lagao. Sirf comma se do poore vaakya nahi judte: I was tired, I slept. ✗ → I was tired, so I slept. ✓

Comma kab chhod sakte ho

Dono clause bahut chhote hon to comma zaroori nahi: I cooked and she cleaned. Aur agar doosre hisse me subject hi na ho, to wo clause nahi — comma mat lagao: She opened the door and smiled.

docs.title: 20.4 Complex — kaaran, samay, shart aur virodh
docs.text:
Jab ek baat mukhya ho aur doosri usse kaaran, samay, shart ya virodh batati ho, to complex sentence banta hai. Ye wahi vaakya hain jo aapki English ko sochi-samjhi aur paripakv banate hain.

  • I took an umbrella because it looked cloudy. Mukhya baat: chhaata liya. Kaaran: baadal the.
  • When the guests arrived, we served lunch. Dependent clause pehle aaya, isliye beech me comma.
  • Although the test was hard, she passed. Test mushkil tha, phir bhi wo paas ho gayi. — "but" ki zaroorat nahi.

Complex ka niyam

Dependent clause pehle aaye to beech me comma lagao (When it rained, we stayed in.); baad me aaye to comma nahi. Ek jod ke liye ek hi shabd: although ya but — dono nahi.

Hindi ka 'halaanki… lekin' English me nahi chalta

  • Galat: Although he is rich, but he is not happy.
  • Sahi: Although he is rich, he is not happy. / He is rich, but he is not happy.
  • Kyun: Hindi me "halaanki… lekin" dono lagte hain, English me ek hi. Isi tarah "because… so" bhi saath nahi aate.

docs.title: 20.5 Relative clauses — who, which, that, whose, where
docs.text:
Relative clause kisi noun ke baare me aur jaankari deta hai, bilkul adjective ki tarah — bas ek shabd ki jagah poora clause. Isse do chhote vaakya ek ho jaate hain: I met a man. He speaks six languages. → I met a man who speaks six languages.

Figure 20.3. Relative clause (dashed) apne noun ke theek baad baithta hai, aur who/that us noun ki jagah le leta hai.

Relative clause ka niyam

who — log, which — cheezein, that — dono, whose — kiska, where — jagah. Relative shabd noun ki jagah leta hai, isliye wahi noun ya pronoun dobara mat lagao.

Shabd Kiske liye Example who insaan the girl who won the prize which cheez, jaanwar the bus which goes to Agra that insaan ya cheez (bina comma) the book that I lost whose maalikana — "jiska" the boy whose bike was stolen where jagah the village where I was born when samay the day when we met

Object wala relative chhod bhi sakte ho

Jab who/that clause ka object ho, to use hata sakte ho: the book (that) I lost, the man (who) I met. Bolchaal me ye bahut aam hai. Par subject ho to nahi: the man who called — "who" zaroori hai.

docs.title: 20.6 Defining vs Non-defining — comma ka khel
docs.text:
Do commas vaakya ka matlab badal sakte hain. Sawaal ye hai: kya clause batata hai ki kaunsa noun, ya sirf ek extra jaankari jodta hai jo hata bhi do to farq nahi padta?

Figure 20.4. Commas ke beech wala hissa bonus jaankari hai. Bina comma wala hissa batata hai ki kiski baat ho rahi hai.

Defining vs non-defining

Defining clause batata hai kaunsa noun — bina comma, who/which/that teeno chalte hain. Non-defining sirf extra jaankari deta hai — commas ke saath, aur isme "that" nahi lagta.

  • The Taj Mahal, which is in Agra, attracts millions of visitors. Taj Mahal ek hi hai — "which is in Agra" extra jaankari hai, isliye commas.
  • Students who finish early can leave. Sirf wo students jo jaldi khatam karein — clause zaroori hai, comma nahi.

docs.title: 20.7 Chhote vaakyon ko jodkar behtar vaakya
docs.text:
Ab sab saath laate hain. Likhte waqt pehle chhote vaakya likh lo, phir dekho kaunse jod sakte ho. Ye teen sawaal poochho: kya ye barabar hain (FANBOYS)? kya ek kaaran/samay hai (because, when)? kya ek noun ke baare me hai (who, which)?

Pehle (chhote vaakya) Baad me (jode hue) I have a cousin. She lives in Canada. She is a nurse. I have a cousin who lives in Canada and works as a nurse. The train was late. We missed the meeting. The train was late, so we missed the meeting. It was raining. The match continued. Although it was raining, the match continued. This is the school. My father studied here. This is the school where my father studied. I met a writer. Her books are famous. I met a writer whose books are famous.

Sab kuch ek vaakya me mat thoso

Jodne ka matlab ye nahi ki poora paragraph ek vaakya ban jaaye. Ek vaakya me do-teen clause kaafi hain. Lamba ho jaaye to wapas tod do — saaf baat hamesha lambi baat se behtar hai.

docs.title: 20.8 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Clauses ki sabse aam Indian-English galtiyan

  • Galat: Although I studied hard, but I failed.
  • Sahi: Although I studied hard, I failed.

  • Kyun: "halaanki… lekin" ka seedha anuvaad. English me ek jod ke liye ek hi shabd — although ya but.

  • Galat: This is the man who I told you about him.

  • Sahi: This is the man (who) I told you about.

  • Kyun: "who" pehle hi "the man" ki jagah le chuka hai. "him" lagane se wahi aadmi do baar aa gaya. Isi tarah: the book which I bought it.

  • Galat: I was very tired, I went to bed early.

  • Sahi: I was very tired, so I went to bed early.

  • Kyun: Do independent clause sirf comma se nahi judte. Beech me FANBOYS lagao, ya full stop.

  • Galat: My father, that is a teacher, loves reading.

  • Sahi: My father, who is a teacher, loves reading.

  • Kyun: Commas wale (non-defining) clause me "that" nahi lagta. Insaan ke liye "who", cheez ke liye "which".

  • Galat: Because the shop was closed.

  • Sahi: We came back because the shop was closed.
  • Kyun: "Because" wala clause dependent hai — akela vaakya nahi ban sakta. Jawab me bolna theek hai, par likhte waqt use mukhya clause se jodo.

docs.title: 20.9 Practice — Clauses
docs.text:
Exercise 1

'I called her, but she didn't answer.' — ye kaunsa vaakya hai?

  • Compound
  • Simple
  • Complex
  • Compound-complex

Hint: Kitne independent clause hain?

Jawaab

Compound

Do independent clause hain — 'I called her' aur 'she didn't answer' — jo 'but' (FANBOYS) se jude hain. Dependent clause koi nahi, isliye compound.

Exercise 2

'When the power went off, we lit candles.' — ye kaunsa vaakya hai?

  • Complex
  • Compound
  • Simple
  • Compound-complex
Jawaab

Complex

'When the power went off' dependent clause hai, 'we lit candles' independent. Independent + dependent = complex.

Exercise 3

This is the girl ___ father is a pilot.

  • whose
  • who
  • which
  • where

Hint: 'jiske pita'

Jawaab

whose

Maalikana batana hai — 'jiske pita'. Iske liye 'whose'. 'who father' galat hai.

Exercise 4

Kaunsa vaakya sahi hai?

  • Although it was late, we kept talking.
  • Although it was late, but we kept talking.
  • Although it was late, so we kept talking.
  • It was late, although but we kept talking.
Jawaab

Although it was late, we kept talking.

Ek jod ke liye ek hi shabd. 'Although' lag gaya to 'but' ki zaroorat nahi — Hindi ka 'halaanki… lekin' English me nahi chalta.

Exercise 5

Mumbai, ___ is India's financial capital, is very crowded.

  • which
  • that
  • who
  • where

Hint: Commas ke beech — non-defining.

Jawaab

which

Commas wale clause me 'that' nahi lagta, aur Mumbai cheez/jagah hai (yahan subject), insaan nahi — isliye 'which'. 'where' tab aata jab clause me apna subject hota: where my uncle lives.

Exercise 6

This is the village ___ my grandmother was born.

Hint: Jagah ki baat.

Jawaab

where / in which

Jagah ke liye 'where' — the village where she was born. 'in which' bhi sahi hai, par thoda formal.

Exercise 7

Ek extra shabd hai — us par tap karo.

This is the laptop which I bought it last week.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: it.

Sahi roop: This is the laptop which I bought last week.

'which' pehle hi 'the laptop' ki jagah le chuka hai. 'it' lagaane se wahi cheez do baar aa jaati hai.

Exercise 8

Galat shabd dhoondo.

Although the hotel was expensive, but the food was terrible.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: but.

Sahi roop: Although the hotel was expensive, the food was terrible.

'Although' aur 'but' ek saath nahi aate. Ek hata do — yahan 'but'.

Exercise 9

Relative shabd ko uske kaam se jodo.

A B who jiska / maalikana which jagah whose insaan where cheez Jawaab

who — insaan; which — cheez; whose — jiska / maalikana; where — jagah

who log ke liye, which cheezon ke liye, whose maalikana ke liye, where jagah ke liye. 'that' defining clause me log aur cheez dono ke liye chalta hai.

Exercise 10

Do vaakya ek banao: 'I have a friend. He speaks Japanese.'

Shabd: friend / Japanese / I / who / speaks / a / have

Jawaab

I have a friend who speaks Japanese

'who' ne 'He' ki jagah le li aur clause seedha 'a friend' ke baad baith gaya. Do chhote vaakya ek saaf vaakya ban gaye.

Exercise 11

Complex sentence banao.

Shabd: inside / stayed / We / raining / because / was / heavily / it

Jawaab

We stayed inside because it was raining heavily

Mukhya baat pehle (we stayed inside), kaaran baad me (because…). Dependent clause baad me aaya, isliye comma ki zaroorat nahi.

Exercise 12

Ye vaakya bolo — commas par halka sa ruko.

Jawaab

Bolo: My brother, who lives in Pune, is a doctor

Bolte waqt commas ka matlab hai chhota sa thehraav. Is thehraav se sunne wala samajh jaata hai ki 'who lives in Pune' sirf extra jaankari hai.

Aage kya karein

Apna pichla koi email ya message kholo. Jahan teen chhote vaakya lagaatar hon, unme se do ko who, because ya so se jodo. Har roz ek paragraph — ek mahine me aapki likhai badal jaayegi.

docs.title: Chapter 37: Kaunsa shabd kiske saath
docs.text:
Kaunsa shabd kiske saath — collocations

"I did a mistake" — grammar me koi galti nahi, phir bhi kaan ko chubhta hai. Kyon? Kyonki English me kuch shabd jodi me chalte hain, jaise Hindi me "chai banana" aur "khaana pakaana" — koi "chai pakaana" nahi kehta. In pakki jodiyon ko collocations kehte hain. Inka koi logic nahi, sirf aadat hai — aur yahi aadat aapki English ko "sahi" se "natural" banati hai.

docs.title: 37.1 Collocation kya hai — shabdon ki pakki jodiyan
docs.text:
Collocation galat ho to log samajh to jaate hain, par turant pata chal jaata hai ki aap anuvaad kar rahe ho. Dictionary ka matlab sahi hone se kaam nahi chalta — saathi shabd bhi sahi hona chahiye.

Figure 37.1. Powerful aur strong ka matlab lagbhag ek hai, par chai sirf strong hoti hai. Yahi collocation hai.

Shabd nahi, jodi seekho

Collocation = do shabd jo aadat se saath aate hain: strong tea, heavy rain, make a mistake. Inka logic nahi hota — isliye naya shabd hamesha uske saathi ke saath likho aur bolo. "mistake" mat likho; "make a mistake" likho.

docs.title: 37.2 make ya do?
docs.text:
Hindi me dono "karna" hain, isliye ye sabse badi gadbad hai. Ek mota niyam kaafi kaam aata hai — aur jo niyam me na baithe, wo bas jodi me yaad karne hain.

Figure 37.2. Make ke baad aksar kuch nikalta hai — faisla, paisa, aawaaz, dost. Do ke baad koi kaam hota hai jo nipataana hai.
  • I made a few mistakes, but I did my best. Galti "banti" hai (make); koshish ek kaam hai (do).
  • Could you do me a favour and make a quick call to the bank? Ek hi vaakya me dono — favour = do, phone call = make.

make vs do

make = kuch naya banana ya paida karna (a decision, a mistake, money, a noise, a call). do = kaam, duty ya kriya (homework, the dishes, exercise, a favour, your best). "Do a mistake" sabse aam Indian galti hai — galti hamesha make hoti hai.

docs.title: 37.3 have, take, give, get — chaar chhote verb, saikdon jodiyan
docs.text:
Ye chaar verb itne chhote hain ki inka apna matlab lagbhag kho jaata hai — matlab jodi se aata hai. Isliye inhe akela nahi, hamesha saathi ke saath seekho.

Verb Pakki jodiyan Suno have a meal · a bath · a good time · a look · a party · a chat take a photo · a break · a seat · a bus · a chance · medicine give a speech · advice · an example · a hand · a call · a smile get ready · a job · home · lost · better · married

Exam aur dawai — 'take'

Student exam take karta hai (British: sit) — teacher exam give ya set karta hai. Dawai bhi take hoti hai, "eat" nahi: take your medicine. "I gave my exam" India me sab samajhte hain, par bahar iska matlab ulta lagta hai — jaise aapne exam liya ho.

docs.title: 37.4 Adjective jodiyan — heavy rain, strong tea, high fever
docs.text:
