Shabd Kab Example each do ya zyada, ek-ek par dhyan Each player gets a shirt. every teen ya zyada, poora group I walk every day. both do ke do Both my parents work. either do me se koi ek You can sit on either side. neither do me se koi nahi Neither answer is correct. all teen+ ya uncountable All the shops were closed.

'of' lagaoge to 'the / my / these' bhi lagao

each student ✓ each of the students ✓ each of students ✗ both my hands ✓ both of my hands ✓ neither of them** ✓

docs.title: 7.7 enough, aur my / your / their
docs.text:
Do chhote par roz ke kaam ke determiners. enough batata hai "jitna chahiye utna", aur possessive determiners batate hain "kiska".

enough — noun se pehle, adjective ke baad

enough* money · enough chairs — noun se pehle. old enough · fast *enough — adjective ya adverb ke baad. ✗ He is enough old. ✓ He is old enough to vote.

Pronoun Possessive determiner Example I my my phone you your your idea he / she his / her his car, her office it its The dog wagged its tail. we / they our / their our house, their children

Do baatein jo pakad leti hain

1. Ek noun ke saath ek hi determiner: the my book ✗ → my book ✓. 2. its = uska (possessive), it's = it is. The company changed its name. "his / her" maalik ke gender se tay hota hai, cheez se nahi: Priya's brother = her brother.

docs.title: 7.8 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Determiner ki sabse aam Indian-English galtiyan

  • Galat: I have many works today.
  • Sahi: I have a lot of work today.

  • Kyun: "work" (kaam) uncountable hai — iska plural nahi banta aur "many" nahi lagta. "works" ka matlab kalaakriti hota hai: the works of Premchand.

  • Galat: Each students must bring an ID card.

  • Sahi: Each student must bring an ID card.

  • Kyun: each aur every ke baad noun hamesha singular. Plural chahiye to "each of the students" ya "all students" bolo.

  • Galat: Can you give me some informations?

  • Sahi: Can you give me some information?

  • Kyun: information, advice, furniture, luggage — sab uncountable. Inme -s kabhi nahi lagta.

  • Galat: There are less buses on Sunday.

  • Sahi: There are fewer buses on Sunday.

  • Kyun: Buses gin sakte ho, to "fewer". "less" uncountable ke liye: less traffic, less noise.

  • Galat: I don't have some money.

  • Sahi: I don't have any money.
  • Kyun: Negative vaakya me "any". "some" positive baat aur offer ke liye hai.

docs.title: 7.9 Practice — Determiners
docs.text:
Exercise 1

How ___ sugar do you take in your tea?

  • much
  • many
  • few
  • a few

Hint: Sugar gin sakte ho?

Jawaab

much

Sugar uncountable hai — hum 'do sugar' nahi bolte. Uncountable ke saath 'much', aur 'How much' se maatra poochhte hain.

Exercise 2

Don't worry, we still have ___ time before the train leaves.

  • a little
  • little
  • a few
  • few

Hint: Baat positive hai — thoda samay hai, kaafi hai.

Jawaab

a little

Time uncountable hai, isliye 'little' wala pair. Aur 'don't worry' bata raha hai ki baat positive hai — to 'a' ke saath: a little.

Exercise 3

Look at ___ birds on that far tree!

  • those
  • these
  • this
  • that

Hint: Door hain aur kai hain.

Jawaab

those

'that far tree' — cheezein door hain, aur 'birds' plural hai. Door + kai = those.

Exercise 4

I asked two shopkeepers, but ___ of them had the charger.

  • neither
  • either
  • both
  • none

Hint: Do me se koi nahi.

Jawaab

neither

Do log the aur dono ke paas charger nahi tha — 'do me se koi nahi' = neither. 'none' teen ya zyada ke liye zyada aata hai.

Exercise 5

Is there ___ milk left in the fridge?

Hint: Aam sawaal hai.

Jawaab

any

Aam sawaal aur negative me 'any' lagta hai. 'some' tab aata jab hum kuch offer ya request kar rahe hote.

Exercise 6

Every child ___ a gift at the party. (get — present simple)

Hint: 'every' ke baad singular.

Jawaab

gets

'every child' singular hai, isliye verb bhi singular — gets. Hindi me 'har bachche ko' sunke plural lagta hai, par English me 'every' akela ek ko ginta hai.

Exercise 7

Is vaakya me galat shabd par tap karo.

Sir, I have many works to finish today.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: works.

Sahi roop: Sir, I have a lot of work to finish today.

'work' (kaam) uncountable hai — 'works' nahi banta, aur 'many' bhi nahi lagta. 'a lot of work' ya 'much work' bolo.

Exercise 8

Galat shabd dhoondo.

Each students has a locker.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: students.

Sahi roop: Each student has a locker.

'each' ke baad noun hamesha singular — student. Verb 'has' pehle se singular hai, wo sahi hai.

Exercise 9

Ek galti hai — dhoondo.

She gave me some useful advices about the interview.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: advices.

Sahi roop: She gave me some useful advice about the interview.

'advice' uncountable hai, iska plural nahi hota. Ek salaah ginni ho to 'a piece of advice'.

Exercise 10

Determiner ko sahi noun se jodo.

A B many minutes much patience a few chairs a little furniture Jawaab

many — chairs; much — furniture; a few — minutes; a little — patience

chairs aur minutes gin sakte ho — many, a few. furniture aur patience nahi gin sakte — much, a little.

Exercise 11

Sahi kram me vaakya banao.

Shabd: to / not / is / old / enough / He / drive

Jawaab

He is not old enough to drive

'enough' adjective ke baad aata hai — old enough. 'enough old' galat hai.

Exercise 12

Ye line bolo — 'information' ke aakhir me -s nahi lagana.

Jawaab

Bolo: Could you give me some information about the course

Bol-bol ke 'informations' ki aadat todni padti hai. Request hai, isliye 'some' — aur 'information' bina -s.

Aage kya karein

Apni ek chhoti list banao: work, advice, information, luggage, furniture, news. Har baar inme se koi shabd bolo to ruk ke socho — "gin sakta hoon?" Ek hafte me ye sawaal aadat ban jaayega.

docs.title: Chapter 54: Chhoti kahaniyan
docs.text:
Chhoti kahaniyan — suno, samjho, likho

Grammar padh li, shabd yaad kar liye — par jab koi English bolta hai to sab tez lagta hai. Iska ilaaj ek hi hai: roz thoda sunna. Is chapter me chhe chhoti kahaniyan hain — Priya ka pehla din, train me khoya phone, Sunday ka bazaar, ek surprise party, baarish ka din aur naye padosi. Har kahani pehle suno, phir transcript kholo. Aakhir me quiz me sunkar jawaab doge aur sunkar likhoge (dictation).

docs.title: 54.1 Sunne ka tareeka — pehle, beech me, baad me
docs.text:
Achha listener seedha 🔊 dabakar shuru nahi karta. Wo teen kadam me sunta hai: sunne se pehle andaaza lagata hai, sunte waqt sirf zaroori cheez pakadta hai, aur sunne ke baad transcript se milaata hai.

Figure 54.1. Before → While → After. Sabse zaroori niyam: pehli do baar transcript mat dekho. Dimaag ko aawaz se matlab nikaalne ki aadat daalni hai.

Do baar suno, phir padho

Pehli baar gist (mota-mota kya hua), doosri baar detail (naam, samay, jagah). Transcript sirf teesre kadam me. Har shabd samajhna zaroori nahi — kahani samajhna zaroori hai.

Har kahani ke liye paanch sawaal dimaag me rakho. Ye "story map" har kahani par lagta hai — aur quiz ke zyaadatar sawaal inhi se aate hain.

Figure 54.2. Story map: Who, Where, When, What happened, How did they feel. Pehli baar sunkar inme se teen bhi bhar diye to aap sahi raaste par ho.

docs.title: 54.2 Kahani 1 — Priya's first day
docs.text:
Priya Pune me rehti hai aur uski nayi naukri ka pehla din hai. Kahani past simple me hai (woke, wore, took, was). Suno: Priya subah kaisa mehsoos kar rahi thi, aur lunch par uske saath kaun baitha?

Shabd Matlab nervous ghabraaya hua manager boss, sanchaalak introduced parichay karaaya colleagues saath kaam karne wale wore pehna (wear ka past)

🎧 Poori kahani suno

  • Story 1 — Priya's first day Pehli baar: kya hua? Doosri baar: naam aur samay pakdo.
Transcript

Priya is twenty-three years old, and she lives in Pune. Last Monday was her first day at a new job. She woke up at six o'clock and wore her new blue kurta. She took a bus to the office. She was a little nervous. Her manager, Mr Desai, was very kind. He showed her the office and introduced her to the team. At lunch, two colleagues, Neha and Farhan, sat with her. In the evening, Priya called her mother. She said that she loved her new job.

  • She was a little nervous. Wo thodi ghabraayi hui thi. "a little" = thoda — bahut nahi.
  • He showed her the office and introduced her to the team. Usne use office dikhaaya aur team se milwaaya. "showed her" me "her" bahut halka bolte hain — "sho-der".
  • She said that she loved her new job. Usne kaha ki use nayi naukri bahut pasand hai. Shaam tak ghabraahat khushi me badal gayi.

-ed ki aawaz chhoti hoti hai

Past simple ka -ed teen tarah bola jaata hai: called (d), walked (t), wanted (id). Ye aawaz halki hai — dhyan se suno. Dictation me sabse zyada yahi -ed chhoot jaata hai.

docs.title: 54.3 Kahani 2 — The lost phone
docs.text:
Arjun Mumbai ki local train se office jaata hai. Ek din bheed me uska phone kho jaata hai. Suno: phone kahan mila, aur Arjun ko jab phone nahi mila to kaisa laga?

Shabd Matlab crowded bheed bhara got off utar gaya exit bahar jaane ka raasta explained samjhaaya, bataaya thanked shukriya kaha

🎧 Poori kahani suno

  • Story 2 — The lost phone Dhyan do: kahani present se shuru hoti hai (takes — roz ki aadat), phir past me jaati hai.
Transcript

Arjun takes the local train to work every day. On Friday, the train was very crowded. He got off at Dadar station and walked to the exit. Then he put his hand in his pocket. His phone was not there! He felt terrible. He ran back, but the train was gone. A railway policeman asked him what was wrong, and Arjun explained. The policeman called the next station. An hour later, a kind woman brought the phone to the station office. She found it under a seat. Arjun thanked her again and again.

  • Arjun takes the local train to work every day. Arjun roz local train se kaam par jaata hai. "every day" = roz ki aadat → present simple.
  • His phone was not there! He felt terrible. Phone wahan nahi tha! Use bahut bura laga. "terrible" = bahut bura — yahan dar aur pareshaani.
  • She found it under a seat. Use phone ek seat ke neeche mila. "found it" jud kar "faun-dit" sunai deta hai.

Sunne ki galti — jude hue shabd

  • Galat: He gotto fat Dadar station.
  • Sahi: He got off at Dadar station.
  • Kyun: Bolte waqt "got off at" ek lambi aawaz ban jaati hai — "go-to-fat". Jab ajeeb shabd sunai de, socho: kaunse do-teen chhote shabd jud gaye?

docs.title: 54.4 Kahani 3 — Sunday at the market
docs.text:
Meena har Sunday apne dada ji ke saath sabzi mandi jaati hai. Yahan present simple (aadat) aur past simple (aaj kya hua) dono hain. Suno: wo jaldi kyon jaate hain, aur aaj Meena ne kya khareeda?

Shabd Matlab fresh taaza stalls thele, chhoti dukaanein expensive mehenga instead uski jagah heavy bhaari

🎧 Poori kahani suno

  • Story 3 — Sunday at the market Number par dhyan do: kitne baje nikle, aam kitne ke the?
Transcript

Every Sunday, Meena and her grandfather go to the vegetable market near their house. They leave early, at seven, because the vegetables are fresh in the morning. Grandfather always buys tomatoes, onions and green chillies. Meena likes the fruit stalls. Today she wanted mangoes, but they were very expensive. They cost two hundred rupees a kilo! So she bought bananas instead. Grandfather talked to all the shopkeepers, because he knows everyone. They walked home slowly with two heavy bags.

  • They leave early, because the vegetables are fresh in the morning. Wo jaldi nikalte hain, kyonki subah sabziyan taazi hoti hain. "because" ke baad hamesha kaaran aata hai — "why?" wale sawaal ka jawaab yahin milta hai.
  • So she bought bananas instead. To usne aam ki jagah kele khareede. "instead" sunte hi samjho — plan badal gaya.
  • Grandfather talked to all the shopkeepers, because he knows everyone. Dada ji sab dukaandaron se baat karte rahe, kyonki wo sabko jaante hain. "knows" present me hai — ye hamesha ka sach hai.

because = kaaran ka darwaza

Jab sawaal "Why…?" ho, to kahani me because ya so ka intezaar karo. because ke baad kaaran, so ke baad nateeja. Ye do chhote shabd "why" ke aadhe jawaab khud de dete hain.

docs.title: 54.5 Kahani 4 — The birthday surprise
docs.text:
Rahul ka janmdin hai, par lagta hai sab bhool gaye. Kahani me ek mod (twist) hai — "but" aur "when" par dhyan do. Suno: Rahul dopahar me udaas kyon tha, aur party kahan hui?

Shabd Matlab busy vyast, kaam me laga terrace chhat shouted zor se bole, chillaaye planned yojana banaayi surprise achaanak khushi

🎧 Poori kahani suno

  • Story 4 — The birthday surprise "but" ke baad pareshaani aati hai, "When he opened the door" ke baad twist.
Transcript

Saturday was Rahul's birthday, but his wife, Anjali, said she was busy all day. Rahul was a bit sad. In the evening, she asked him to come up to the terrace for some fresh air. When he opened the door, the lights came on. All his friends were there! They shouted happy birthday and laughed. There was a big chocolate cake on the table. Anjali planned the party for two weeks, and Rahul knew nothing about it. He said it was the best birthday of his life.

  • His wife said she was busy all day. Rahul was a bit sad. Biwi ne kaha wo poore din vyast hai. Rahul thoda udaas tha. Kaaran aur bhaav ek ke baad ek — yahi "why was he sad?" ka jawaab hai.
  • When he opened the door, the lights came on. Jaise hi usne darwaza khola, battiyan jal uthin. "came on" = jal gayi (light/TV ke liye).
  • It was the best birthday of his life. Ye uski zindagi ka sabse achha janmdin tha. Udaasi se khushi tak — kahani ka poora safar.

docs.title: 54.6 Kahani 5 — A rainy day
docs.text:
Kolkata me zor ki baarish — school band, aur ek bachchi ke liye mazedaar din. Is kahani me samay ke shabd hain: on Tuesday morning, in the afternoon, in the evening. Suno: Tara ghar par kyon thi, aur bachchon ne kya banaaya?

Shabd Matlab heavily bahut zor se closed band ho gaye paper boats kaagaz ki naav sailed (naav) chalaayi the power went off bijli chali gayi

🎧 Poori kahani suno

  • Story 5 — A rainy day Samay ke shabd ek naksha banaate hain: subah → dopahar → shaam.
Transcript

On Tuesday morning, it rained very heavily in Kolkata. The streets were full of water, and the schools closed. Ten-year-old Tara was happy. She stayed at home with her little brother, Babu. They made paper boats and sailed them in the water near the gate. Their mother made hot pakoras and tea. In the afternoon, the power went off, so Tara read a story book by the window. In the evening, the rain stopped and the sky turned orange.

  • The streets were full of water, and the schools closed. Sadkein paani se bhari thin, aur school band ho gaye. Isi line me Tara ke ghar rehne ka kaaran hai.
  • Tara read a story book by the window. Tara ne khidki ke paas kahani ki kitaab padhi. Yahan "read" past hai, bola jaata hai "red" — "reed" nahi.

read — likhne me same, bolne me alag

  • Galat: Tara reads a story book. (dictation me galat suna)
  • Sahi: Tara read a story book.
  • Kyun: Past "read" ki aawaz "red" hai. Kahani past me chal rahi hai (rained, stayed, made), isliye yahan "reads" ho hi nahi sakta. Baaki kahani ka tense bhi clue hai.

docs.title: 54.7 Kahani 6 — The new neighbour
docs.text:
Ye kahani "I" (main) bol raha hai — kahani sunaane wala khud kirdaar hai. Suno: naya padosi kaun hai, kya kaam karta hai, aur kya lekar aaya?

Shabd Matlab neighbour padosi moved into rehne aaye doorbell ghanti (darwaze ki) nurse nurse, parichaarika invited bulaaya, nyota diya

🎧 Poori kahani suno

  • Story 6 — The new neighbour Pehle past (moved, saw, rang), phir present (is, works, teaches) — aaj ki sachchai.
Transcript

Last week, a new family moved into the flat next to ours. On the first day, I saw a lot of boxes on the stairs. The next morning, the doorbell rang. It was a young man with a plate of sweets. His name is Joseph, and he is from Kochi. He works at a hospital as a nurse, and his wife teaches music. My mother invited them for dinner on Sunday. Now our children play together every evening.

  • It was a young man with a plate of sweets. Darwaze par ek naujawaan mithai ki plate lekar khada tha. "a plate of" jud kar "uh-PLAY-tuv" sunai deta hai.
  • He works at a hospital as a nurse. Wo hospital me nurse ka kaam karta hai. "as a" = ke roop me. Naukri batane ka sabse aam tareeka.
  • Now our children play together every evening. Ab hamare bachche roz shaam saath khelte hain. Kahani ka ant — dosti ho gayi.

Chhote shabd bhi suno — a, the, of

Fast English me a, the, of, to, and bahut halke bolte hain ("uh", "thuh", "uv"). Dictation me agar vaakya adhoora lage, to inhi ko jodo. a plate of sweets → "uh PLAY-tuv sweets".

docs.title: 54.8 Dictation ki taiyaari — sunne ki paanch galtiyan
docs.text:
Quiz me chaar dictation hain: aap sunoge, aur poora vaakya type karoge. Har shabd alag se check hoga. Ye wo galtiyan hain jo Hindi bolne wale sabse zyada karte hain — pehle se jaan lo.

Dictation me aam galtiyan

  • Galat: He walk to the exit.
  • Sahi: He walked to the exit.

  • Kyun: "walked" ki aakhri "t" aawaz agle "to" me mil jaati hai. Kahani past me hai? To verb par -ed lagao.

  • Galat: They cost two hundred rupee.

  • Sahi: They cost two hundred rupees.

  • Kyun: Ek se zyada = plural -s. "two hundred" sunte hi aage ka noun plural hoga, chahe -s saaf sunaai na de.

  • Galat: Mangoes cost fifteen rupees a kilo.

  • Sahi: Mangoes cost fifty rupees a kilo.

  • Kyun: fif-TEEN me zor aakhri hisse par aur "n" lambi; FIF-ty me zor shuru me, aakhir chhota "tee". Yahi farq 13/30, 14/40, 16/60 me bhi.

  • Galat: She took bus to office.

  • Sahi: She took a bus to the office.

  • Kyun: Hindi me articles nahi hote, isliye kaan unhe "chhod" deta hai. English me noun ke aage aksar a / the hota hai — dictation ke baad har noun ke aage check karo.

  • Galat: The sky turn orange in the evening.

  • Sahi: The sky turned orange in the evening.
  • Kyun: "turned orange" me -ed aur "o" mil jaate hain: "tern-DOR-inj". Do vowel ya consonant milte hi ek shabd ka ant doosre ki shuruaat ban jaata hai.
  • Fifteen. Fifty. Fifteen rupees. Fifty rupees. Farq suno: fif-TEEN vs FIF-ty.
  • Thirteen. Thirty. Fourteen. Forty. Wahi pattern — -teen me zor peeche, -ty me aage.
  • He walked to the exit. He called his mother. "walkt" aur "cawld" — -ed ki do aawazein.

Dictation ka teen-step tareeka

1. Poora suno, kuch mat likho. 2. Dobara suno aur likho. 3. Grammar se check karo: tense, -s, a/the. Kaan + grammar = sahi dictation.

docs.title: 54.9 Practice — Chhoti kahaniyan
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Kahani pehli baar sunte waqt sabse zaroori kya hai?

  • Gist — mota-mota kya hua
  • Har shabd ka matlab
  • Transcript saath me padhna
  • Spelling yaad karna

Hint: Before → While → After yaad karo.

Jawaab

Gist — mota-mota kya hua

Pehli baar gist, doosri baar detail. Transcript sirf aakhir me.

Exercise 2

How did Priya feel in the morning?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Last Monday was Priya's first day at a new job. She woke up at six o'clock and wore her new blue kurta. She took a bus to the office. She was a little nervous.

  • a little nervous
  • very angry
  • bored
  • sick
Jawaab

a little nervous

'She was a little nervous' — nervous = ghabraayi hui.

Exercise 3

Who sat with Priya at lunch?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Her manager, Mr Desai, was very kind. He showed her the office and introduced her to the team. At lunch, two colleagues, Neha and Farhan, sat with her.

  • Neha and Farhan
  • Mr Desai
  • her mother
  • nobody
Jawaab

Neha and Farhan

Mr Desai ne office dikhaaya, par lunch par 'two colleagues, Neha and Farhan, sat with her'.

Exercise 4

Where did the woman find Arjun's phone?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

The policeman called the next station. An hour later, a kind woman brought the phone to the station office. She found it under a seat.

  • under a seat
  • in his pocket
  • at the exit
  • on the platform
Jawaab

under a seat

'She found it under a seat' — under = neeche.

Exercise 5

How did Arjun feel when his phone was not in his pocket?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

He got off at Dadar station and walked to the exit. Then he put his hand in his pocket. His phone was not there! He felt terrible.

  • terrible
  • happy
  • sleepy
  • calm
Jawaab

terrible

'He felt terrible' — bahut bura laga. Phone khone par koi calm nahi rehta.

Exercise 6

Why do Meena and her grandfather go to the market early?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Every Sunday, Meena and her grandfather go to the vegetable market near their house. They leave early, at seven, because the vegetables are fresh in the morning.

  • because the vegetables are fresh
  • because the market closes at eight
  • because it is hot later
  • because Meena has school
Jawaab

because the vegetables are fresh

'because the vegetables are fresh in the morning' — because ke baad kaaran.

Exercise 7

What did Meena buy?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Meena likes the fruit stalls. Today she wanted mangoes, but they were very expensive. They cost two hundred rupees a kilo! So she bought bananas instead.

  • bananas
  • mangoes
  • tomatoes
  • green chillies
Jawaab

bananas

Wo mangoes chahti thi, par mehenge the — 'so she bought bananas instead'.

Exercise 8

Why was Rahul a bit sad?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Saturday was Rahul's birthday, but his wife, Anjali, said she was busy all day. Rahul was a bit sad.

  • His wife said she was busy.
  • He was ill.
  • He lost his job.
  • It was raining.
Jawaab

His wife said she was busy.

Janmdin par biwi ne kaha 'I am busy all day' — isliye wo udaas tha.

Exercise 9

Where was the party?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

In the evening, she asked him to come up to the terrace for some fresh air. When he opened the door, the lights came on. All his friends were there!

  • on the terrace
  • in a restaurant
  • at his office
  • in the garden
Jawaab

on the terrace

'come up to the terrace' — terrace = chhat. Darwaza khulte hi dost wahin the.

Exercise 10

Why did Tara stay at home?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

On Tuesday morning, it rained very heavily in Kolkata. The streets were full of water, and the schools closed. Ten-year-old Tara was happy. She stayed at home with her little brother.

  • The schools closed.
  • She was ill.
  • It was a holiday.
  • Her mother was away.
Jawaab

The schools closed.

Baarish se sadkon par paani — 'the schools closed'.

Exercise 11

What did Tara and Babu make?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

She stayed at home with her little brother, Babu. They made paper boats and sailed them in the water near the gate. Their mother made hot pakoras and tea.

  • paper boats
  • pakoras
  • tea
  • a kite
Jawaab

paper boats

Bachchon ne paper boats banaayin; pakore aur chai maa ne banaaye.

Exercise 12

What is Joseph's job?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

His name is Joseph, and he is from Kochi. He works at a hospital as a nurse, and his wife teaches music.

  • a nurse
  • a music teacher
  • a doctor
  • a shopkeeper
Jawaab

a nurse

'He works at a hospital as a nurse.' Music to unki wife sikhaati hain.

Exercise 13

What did the new neighbour bring?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

The next morning, the doorbell rang. It was a young man with a plate of sweets.

  • a plate of sweets
  • a lot of boxes
  • flowers
  • a cake
Jawaab

a plate of sweets

'a young man with a plate of sweets' — boxes to pehle din seedhiyon par the.

Exercise 14

How much do the mangoes cost?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Those mangoes are very good. They cost fifty rupees a kilo.

  • fifty rupees
  • fifteen rupees
  • five rupees
  • five hundred rupees
Jawaab

fifty rupees

FIF-ty — zor shuru me. fif-TEEN me zor aakhir me hota.

Exercise 15

Kahani ke shabd ko uske matlab se jodo.

A B nervous mehenga crowded padosi expensive ghabraaya hua neighbour bheed bhara Jawaab

nervous — ghabraaya hua; crowded — bheed bhara; expensive — mehenga; neighbour — padosi

Ye chaaron shabd kahaniyon ki chaabi the — Priya nervous, train crowded, aam expensive, Joseph neighbour.

Exercise 16

Suno aur likho.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

She took a bus to the office.

Dhyan do: 'a bus' aur 'the office' — dono articles.

Exercise 17

Suno aur likho.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

His phone was not there.

'was not' — past simple, ek cheez ke liye 'was'.

Exercise 18

Suno aur likho.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

They walked home slowly with two heavy bags.

'walked' ka -ed (t aawaz) aur 'bags' ka -s mat bhoolna.

Exercise 19

Suno aur likho.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

The streets were full of water, and the schools closed.

'were' (plural streets), 'full of', aur 'closed' ka -ed.

Exercise 20

Rahul ki taraf se ye line bolo — jaise aapka hi janmdin ho.

Jawaab

Bolo: It was the best birthday of my life

'best birthday' me dono b saaf bolo; 'of my' jud kar 'uv-my'.

Next step

Roz ek kahani teen baar suno — bina text, phir text ke saath, phir saath-saath bolkar (shadowing). Jab ye sab aasaan lage, aage badho Roz ki kahaniyan par: office ki meeting, customer care call aur dost ka voice note.

docs.title: Chapter 53: Essay aur report
docs.text:
Essay aur report — intro, body, conclusion, IELTS style bhi

School me humne essay "ratte" the — "Since ancient times, man has…" se shuru, teen page lambe. Asli duniya ka essay ulta hai: chhota, saaf, aur ek raay ke saath. Is chapter me poora dhaancha hai — thesis, PEEL paragraph, teen tarah ke essay, essay ke linking words, formal aawaz, IELTS Writing Task 2 ka seedha parichay, ek annotated model essay, aur office wali report ka format.

docs.title: 53.1 Essay ka naksha — intro, body, conclusion
docs.text:
Har essay teen hisson me chalta hai. Intro bade topic se shuru hokar aapki raay (thesis) tak pahunchta hai. Body ke do-teen paragraph us raay ko saboot dete hain. Conclusion raay ko dobara kehkar thoda bada sochta hai.

Figure 53.1. Intro chaude se patla hota hai (topic → thesis), conclusion patle se chauda (raay → badi tasveer). Beech me har body paragraph ek PEEL hai.

Chaar paragraph ka essay

Intro (2–3 line) → Body 1 → Body 2 → Conclusion (2–3 line). 250–300 words ke essay ke liye yahi kaafi hai. Har body paragraph = ek main idea. Paragraph ki buniyaad (topic sentence, ek idea) ke liye Vaakya se paragraph dekho.

docs.title: 53.2 Thesis statement — poore essay ki ek line
docs.text:
Thesis intro ki aakhri line hoti hai. Ye batati hai ki aap kya sochte ho aur aage kya saabit karoge. Kamzor thesis sirf topic dohraata hai; majboot thesis ek saaf raay leta hai — aur aksar wajah bhi bata deta hai.

Kamzor Majboot This essay will discuss online classes. Online classes are a useful addition to school, but they cannot replace a real teacher. Pollution is a big problem. The most effective way to cut urban pollution is to make public transport faster, not just cheaper. There are many advantages and disadvantages. Although working from home saves time, its effect on teamwork outweighs that benefit.
  • While technology has made learning easier, it cannot replace a good teacher. "While…" se doosri taraf ko maano, phir apni raay — ek line me santulan.
  • I firmly believe that cities should invest more in cycling lanes than in flyovers. Opinion essay me "I believe" bilkul theek hai.

✗

Since ancient times, education has been a burning question in today's modern world.

✓

In many Indian cities, students now spend more time on coaching than in school.

asli, aaj ki

docs.title: 53.3 PEEL — body paragraph ka formula
docs.text:
Har body paragraph chaar kadmon me chalta hai. Ye formula yaad ho jaaye to "kya likhun?" wala sawaal khatam.

Kadam Kaam Shuruaat ke shabd Point Paragraph ka ek main idea Firstly, … · One major advantage is … Explain Kyun? Kaise? This is because … · This means that … Evidence Example, data, anubhav For instance, … · A recent survey found … Link Thesis se jodo Therefore, … · This shows that …

Ek PEEL paragraph — tukde pehchano

  • [P] One major benefit of online classes is flexibility. Point — ek idea, saaf.
  • [E] Students can watch lessons at any time, which helps those who work part-time or live far from a college. Explain — ye fayda kaise hai.
  • [E] For instance, a student in a small town can now attend lectures from a university in Delhi without moving there. Evidence — ek thos example.
  • [L] This shows that online learning can widen access to higher education. Link — wapas thesis se jodo.

PEEL ek line me

Kya (Point) → kyun (Explain) → saboot (Evidence) → to kya (Link). Evidence ke bina paragraph sirf raay hai. Exam me data nahi hota? Ek realistic example kaafi hai — "For instance, in my city…".

docs.title: 53.4 Teen tarah ke essay — sawaal pehchano
docs.text:
Essay likhne se pehle sawaal ka type pehchano. Galat type ka jawaab = achhi English ke baad bhi kam marks. Sawaal ki aakhri line me hi type chhupa hota hai.

Type Sawaal kaisa dikhta hai Dhaancha Opinion To what extent do you agree or disagree? Raay intro me → 2 kaaran → raay dobara Discussion Discuss both views and give your opinion. View A → View B → apni raay (intro aur conclusion me) Problem–solution What are the causes? What can be done? Kaaran / samasya → hal Advantages–disadvantages Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages? Fayde → nuksaan → kaun bhaari
  • Some people think that all university education should be free. To what extent do you agree? Opinion — saaf haan/naa/aadha, aur kyun.
  • Some believe children should start school at four, while others think seven is better. Discuss both views. Discussion — dono paksh, phir aapki raay.
  • Many young people in cities feel lonely. Why is this, and what can be done about it? Problem–solution — kaaran + hal, dono.

Sawaal ke har hisse ka jawaab do

"Discuss both views and give your opinion" me raay dena zaroori hai. "Why is this, and what can be done?" me dono sawaal. Ek hissa chhoota = Task Response me seedha nuksaan.

docs.title: 53.5 Linking words — kaam ke hisaab se
docs.text:
Vaakya se paragraph me humne however, therefore, for example dekhe. Essay me thode aur chahiye — khaaskar maanna-phir-kaatna (concession) aur doosron ki raay batana. Har shabd ka grammar alag hai, wahi sabse zaroori hai.

Kaam Shabd Grammar Maano, phir kaato although, while, whereas + poora clause Maano, phir kaato despite, in spite of + noun / -ing Doosron ki raay It could be argued that…, Critics claim that… + clause Natija consequently, as a result, thus vaakya ki shuruaat + comma Zor dena in particular, indeed, above all vaakya me kahin bhi Ant In conclusion, On balance, Overall conclusion ki pehli line
  • Although metro fares are high, the service saves commuters a great deal of time. although + clause (subject + verb).
  • Despite the high fares, many people prefer the metro. despite + noun. ("despite of" nahi!)
  • It could be argued that exams measure memory rather than understanding. Doosri raay ko izzat se rakhna — discussion essay ke liye.
  • Fuel prices rose sharply. Consequently, more people switched to electric scooters. consequently = iske nateeje me (therefore se thoda formal).
  • On balance, the benefits of the scheme outweigh its costs. On balance = sab taul ke — conclusion ki achhi shuruaat.

✗

Although the metro is expensive, but it is fast.

✓

Although the metro is expensive, it is fast. / The metro is expensive, but it is fast.

although

but

✗

Despite of the rain, the match continued.

✓

Despite the rain… / In spite of the rain…

despite

in spite of

docs.title: 53.6 Formal register — essay ki aawaz
docs.text:
Essay me aap dost se baat nahi kar rahe. Contractions nahi (don't → do not), slang nahi, aur bolchaal ke chhote shabdon ki jagah thode formal shabd. Par yaad rakho: formal ka matlab bhaari nahi, saaf hai.

Bolchaal Essay me a lot of / lots of many, a large number of, a great deal of kids children, young people get better improve go up / go down rise / fall, increase / decrease things factors, issues, aspects really bad serious, harmful I think I believe, In my view (opinion essay me)
  • A large number of young people now rely on social media for news. "Lots of kids get news from Insta" ka formal roop.
  • Air quality tends to improve when private vehicles are restricted. "tends to" — har baar nahi, aksar. Essay me hedge karna achha lagta hai.
  • This issue is becoming increasingly serious in smaller cities as well. "really bad" ki jagah "increasingly serious".
  • Several factors contribute to this problem, the most important being cost. "many things" ki jagah "several factors".

Hedge karo — sab pe 'always' mat lagao

tend to, can, may, often, in many cases — ye shabd aapki baat ko imaandaar aur majboot banate hain. "Social media always destroys students" se behtar: "Social media can distract many students."

✗

In my opinion, I think that it doesn't work.

✓

In my view, this approach does not work.

docs.title: 53.7 IELTS Writing Task 2 — ek nazar me
docs.text:
IELTS Writing me do task hote hain. Task 2 ek essay hai — Academic aur General Training dono me lagbhag ek jaisa. Task 1 se iska wazan zyada hai, isliye ispe zyada samay do. (Exam ke format ki poori jaankari IELTS, TOEFL aur aapka level me.)

Figure 53.2. Planning chhodna sabse badi galti hai. Paanch minute ka plan likhte waqt das minute bachata hai.

docs.title: Band kaise milta hai — chaar criteria, seedhi bhasha me
docs.text:
Criterion Seedhi bhasha me Task Response Sawaal ke har hisse ka jawaab diya? Raay saaf hai? Ideas ko samjhaya aur example diya? Coherence & Cohesion Paragraph ka kram theek hai? Ek paragraph = ek idea? Linking words sahi aur zaroorat jitne? Lexical Resource Shabdon me vividhta aur sahi jodi (collocation)? Spelling theek? Grammatical Range & Accuracy Chhote-bade dono tarah ke vaakya? Galtiyan kam?

IELTS Task 2 ke pakke niyam

40 minute, kam se kam 250 words, chaaron criteria ka barabar wazan. 250 se kam = penalty. Rati hui lines aur sawaal ke shabd copy karna = nuksaan. Exam ke niyam badal sakte hain — hamesha official IELTS website par current details dekho.

docs.title: 53.8 Model essay — tukde-tukde samjho
docs.text:
Neeche ek opinion essay hai (lagbhag 270 words). Har paragraph ke neeche likha hai ki wo kya kaam kar raha hai. Pehle 🔊 se suno, phir padho.

Sawaal

  • Some people believe that public transport in cities should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Type: opinion ("To what extent…"). Aapko saaf raay deni hai.

Introduction

  • In many Indian cities, roads are choked with private vehicles, while buses and metro trains often run below capacity. Some argue that the best solution is to make public transport free for all. While this idea has clear benefits, I believe that free travel should be offered only to those who need it most, rather than to everyone. Line 1: background (asli, aaj ki baat). Line 2: sawaal apne shabdon me (paraphrase). Line 3: thesis — "While… I believe…" — santulit par saaf raay.

Body 1 — doosri taraf ko maano

  • Admittedly, free public transport could significantly reduce traffic and pollution. If travel cost nothing, many commuters would leave their cars and motorbikes at home, which would mean cleaner air and shorter journeys. It would also help families on low incomes, who often spend a significant part of their earnings on daily travel. For example, Luxembourg made all public transport free in 2020, partly to tackle congestion. This suggests that, in principle, removing fares is a serious option for crowded cities. P: Admittedly… reduce traffic (maana). E: If travel cost nothing… (second conditional). E: Luxembourg ka example. L: This suggests that…

Body 2 — apni raay ka kaaran

  • However, offering free travel to everyone would be extremely expensive. Ticket sales pay for a large share of maintenance and new routes, so governments would have to raise taxes or cut services. In a country with limited public funds, this money might be better spent on schools or hospitals. As a result, buses might become older and more crowded, which would discourage the very people the policy aims to attract. It would therefore be more sensible to target support at students, senior citizens and low-income workers. P: However… expensive. E: ticket ka paisa kahan jaata hai. E: nateeja — purani, bhari buses. L: It would therefore… — wapas thesis par.

Conclusion

  • In conclusion, although free public transport for all is an attractive idea, its cost would be difficult to sustain. On balance, I believe that free or discounted passes for those in need, combined with more frequent and reliable services, would achieve the same goals far more effectively. Raay dobara, naye shabdon me. Koi naya kaaran nahi — sirf saar aur aage ka raasta.

Model se kya churaayein

Dhaancha churaao, lines nahi: background → paraphrase → thesis, maano → kaato, aur "On balance" wala ant. Rati hui poori lines examiner pakad leta hai — unke marks nahi milte. Sawaal se copy kiye shabd bhi word count me nahi gine jaate.

docs.title: 53.9 Report — headings, findings, recommendations
docs.text:
Essay raay deta hai; report jaankari aur sujhaav deti hai. Office, college project aur kuch exams (jaise Cambridge B2 First) me report likhni padti hai. Report ki pehchaan: headings, chhote paragraph, aur aakhir me saaf recommendations.

Heading Kya jaata hai Taiyaar shuruaat Title Report kis baare me Report on the staff canteen Introduction Maqsad aur tareeka The purpose of this report is to… Findings Kya pata chala (data) It was found that… · The majority of… Conclusion Ek line ka saar Overall, … Recommendations Kya karna chahiye It is recommended that… · The company should…

Mini report — staff canteen

  • Introduction. The purpose of this report is to assess staff satisfaction with the office canteen. It is based on an online survey of 120 employees conducted in March. Maqsad + data kahan se aaya.
  • Findings. The majority of respondents, 68 per cent, said the food was good value. However, nearly half complained about long queues between one and two pm. Only a few mentioned hygiene. Numbers ke shabd: the majority of, nearly half, only a few. Raay nahi — sirf tathya.
  • Recommendations. It is recommended that lunch be served in two shifts and that a pre-order option be added to the office app. "It is recommended that + subject + base verb (be served)" — formal. Aasaan roop: "The company should serve lunch in two shifts."

docs.title: Report ki taiyaar lines
docs.text:
• This report is based on interviews with twenty shop owners. Data kahan se aaya — Introduction me.
  • A significant number of respondents said they would pay more for faster delivery. respondents = jinhone survey ka jawaab diya.
  • Only a small minority were unhappy with the timings. the majority ↔ a small minority — numbers ko shabdon me.
  • The management should consider extending the opening hours. Recommendation ka aasaan roop — should + consider + -ing.

Report ki pehchaan

Headings + tathya + sujhaav. Findings me raay nahi; Recommendations me "should" ya "It is recommended that…". Essay = "I believe…"; report = "It was found that…".

✗

I think the canteen is very bad and people are very angry.

✓

Nearly half of the respondents complained about long queues at lunchtime.

docs.title: 53.10 Practice — Essay aur report
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Thesis statement essay me kahan aata hai?

  • Intro ki aakhri line
  • Conclusion ki aakhri line
  • Body 1 ki pehli line
  • Title me
Jawaab

Intro ki aakhri line

Intro background se shuru hokar thesis par khatam hota hai.

Exercise 2

PEEL ke har akshar ko uske kaam se jodo.

A B Point example ya data Explain thesis se jodna Evidence paragraph ka main idea Link kyun aur kaise Jawaab

Point — paragraph ka main idea; Explain — kyun aur kaise; Evidence — example ya data; Link — thesis se jodna

Kya → kyun → saboot → to kya.

Exercise 3

'Discuss both views and give your opinion.' — ye kaunsa type hai?

  • Discussion
  • Opinion
  • Problem–solution
  • Report
Jawaab

Discussion

Dono paksh + apni raay = discussion essay.

Exercise 4

Ek shabd hatana hai — kaunsa?

Although the metro is expensive, but it is very fast.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: but.

Sahi roop: Although the metro is expensive, it is very fast.

although aur but ek saath nahi — ek hi chuno.

Exercise 5

___ the heavy rain, the match continued. (although nahi)

Hint: Noun ke pehle aane wala concession shabd — 'of' ke bina.

Jawaab

Despite / despite / In spite of / in spite of

despite / in spite of + noun. 'Despite of' galat hai.

Exercise 6

Galat shabd dhoondo.

Despite of the cost, many families buy smartphones.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: of.

Sahi roop: Despite the cost, many families buy smartphones.

despite ke baad 'of' nahi aata.

Exercise 7

Essay ke liye 'lots of kids' ka sabse achha roop?

  • a large number of children
  • plenty kids
  • a lot of kiddos
  • many many kids
Jawaab

a large number of children

Formal register: kids → children, lots of → a large number of.

Exercise 8

IELTS Writing Task 2 me kitne words kam se kam?

  • 250
  • 150
  • 200
  • 350
Jawaab

250

Task 2: kam se kam 250 words, lagbhag 40 minute. (Task 1: 150 words.)

Exercise 9

IELTS ka 'Coherence and Cohesion' kya check karta hai?

  • Paragraph ka kram aur linking
  • Spelling aur shabd
  • Sawaal ka jawaab diya ya nahi
  • Accent
Jawaab

Paragraph ka kram aur linking

Coherence = kram aur saafi; cohesion = linking words aur jodna.

Exercise 10

The purpose of this ___ is to assess staff satisfaction with the canteen.

Hint: Headings, findings, recommendations wala document.

Jawaab

report

'The purpose of this report is to…' — report ki pakki shuruaat.

Exercise 11

Report ke Findings section me kya likhte hain?

  • Survey se kya pata chala
  • Apni bhavnaayein
  • Kya karna chahiye
  • Sawaal dobara
Jawaab

Survey se kya pata chala

Findings = tathya. Kya karna chahiye = Recommendations.

Exercise 12

Ye essay ka kaunsa hissa hai?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

In conclusion, although free public transport is an attractive idea, its cost would be difficult to sustain. On balance, targeted support would work better.

  • Conclusion
  • Introduction
  • Body paragraph
  • Title
Jawaab

Conclusion

'In conclusion… On balance…' — raay dobara, koi naya point nahi.

Exercise 13

Is report ke hisaab se kitne log khaane ko good value maante hain?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

The majority of respondents, sixty-eight per cent, said the food was good value. However, nearly half complained about long queues at lunchtime.

  • 68 per cent
  • Nearly half
  • A few
  • All of them
Jawaab

68 per cent

'The majority of respondents, sixty-eight per cent' — 68%.

Exercise 14

Logon ki sabse badi shikayat kya thi?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

The majority of respondents, sixty-eight per cent, said the food was good value. However, nearly half complained about long queues at lunchtime.

  • Long queues at lunchtime
  • The price
  • Hygiene
  • The taste
Jawaab

Long queues at lunchtime

'nearly half complained about long queues at lunchtime.'

Exercise 15

Suno aur likho.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

Although technology has made learning easier, it cannot replace a good teacher.

Although + clause, phir comma, phir main clause — thesis ka classic roop.

Exercise 16

Report ki line sahi kram me banao.

Shabd: be / It / shifts / served / is / two / recommended / in / that / lunch

Jawaab

It is recommended that lunch be served in two shifts

It is recommended that + subject + base verb (be served).

Exercise 17

Essay ki is line me kya faltu hai?

In my opinion, I think online exams are unfair.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: think.

Sahi roop: In my opinion, online exams are unfair.

'In my opinion' aur 'I think' ek hi baat — ek chuno.

Exercise 18

Ek thesis zor se bolo.

Jawaab

Bolo: I firmly believe that cities need better public transport

Opinion essay me 'I firmly believe that…' saaf raay deta hai.

Aage kya karein

Is hafte ek essay 40 minute me likho — upar ke chaar sawaalon me se koi bhi. Phir model se milao: thesis saaf hai? Har body me PEEL hai? Essay ke shabdon ke liye Kaam aur duniya, aur apna level samajhne ke liye IELTS, TOEFL aur aapka level.

docs.title: Chapter 30: Roz ki baat-cheet
docs.text:
Roz ki baat-cheet — taiyaar jawaab

Is chapter me grammar nahi hai. Isme taiyaar lines hain — wo vaakya jo aap ratte hi kal use kar sakte hain: dukaan par, auto me, doctor ke paas, phone par, restaurant me, aur raasta poochhte waqt. Yahi asli raaz hai: fluent log har vaakya naya nahi banate — unke paas taiyaar tukde hote hain jo turant nikal aate hain. Har line par 🔊 hai. Suno, bolo, rat lo.

Kaise padhein

Ek baithak me poora chapter mat karo. Ek din = ek haalat. Aaj sirf "dukaan" karo — uske paanch line 10 baar bolo. Kal "auto". Chhah din me chhah haalat taiyaar ho jaayengi, aur wo kabhi nahi bhoolengi.

docs.title: 30.1 Dukaan par — khareedna
docs.text:
Figure 30.1. Baayein taraf aapki lines, daayein taraf dukaandaar ki lines jo aapko pehchaanni hain. Sunna aadhi baat-cheet hai — isi liye dono taraf di gayi hain. Kehna hai English line Suno Ye hai aapke paas? Excuse me, do you have this in blue? Kitne ka hai? How much is this? Bas dekh raha hoon I'm just looking, thanks. Chhota/bada size hai? Do you have a smaller size? Pehen kar dekh sakta hoon? Can I try this on? Thoda kam karo Can you do it for a little less? Bahut mehnga hai That's a bit more than I wanted to spend. Le lunga I'll take it. Card chalega? Do you take cards? Bill de dijiye Could I have the receipt, please? Badal sakte hain? Can I exchange it if the size is wrong?

Poora mini-dialogue — dukaan

Dono taraf bolo. Pehle aap, phir dukaandaar ki line bhi — isse kaan taiyaar hota hai.

  • Aap: Excuse me, do you have this shirt in medium? Ye shirt medium me hai?
  • Dukaandaar: Let me check. Yes, here you go. "Here you go" = ye lijiye. Bahut aam line hai.
  • Aap: Thanks. How much is it? Kitne ka hai?
  • Dukaandaar: It's nine hundred and fifty. 950. Note karo: "nine hundred AND fifty" — beech me "and".
  • Aap: Could you do nine hundred? I'll take two. 900 me de denge? Do le lunga. Mol-bhaav ka sabse sharif tareeka.
  • Dukaandaar: All right, nine hundred each. Cash or card? "each" = ek ka. Dhyan do, sirf "nine hundred" nahi.
  • Aap: Card, please. And could I have the receipt? receipt = "ri-SEET", P chup hai.

docs.title: 30.2 Auto aur cab
docs.text:
Kehna hai English line Suno Station chaloge? Will you go to the railway station? Kitna lega? How much will it be? Meter se chalo Could you go by the meter, please? Bahut zyada hai That's too much. Two hundred is fine. Kitni der lagegi? How long will it take? Thoda jaldi chalo Could you go a bit faster? I'm running late. Dheere chalaiye Could you slow down a little, please? Yahan rok dijiye You can stop here, thanks. Agle chowk par baayein Take a left at the next signal. Chhutta nahi hai Sorry, I don't have change. Online se de dun? Can I pay online? AC chala dijiye Could you turn on the AC, please?

Poora mini-dialogue — cab

  • Aap: Hi, are you going towards the airport? Airport ki taraf jaa rahe hain?
  • Driver: Yes, hop in. It'll take about forty minutes. "Hop in" = baith jaiye. "About forty" = lagbhag chaalees.
  • Aap: Perfect. My flight is at six, so I have time. Flight chhah baje hai, isliye waqt hai.
  • Driver: There's some traffic near the bridge, is that okay? Pul ke paas traffic hai, theek hai?
  • Aap: That's fine. Take whichever route is faster. Jo raasta tez ho wahi le lijiye.
  • Aap (pahunchne par): You can drop me at gate three. Thanks a lot. Gate teen par chhod dijiye. "Drop me" = chhod dena.

docs.title: 30.3 Doctor ke paas
docs.text:
Ek saancha jo hamesha kaam karta hai

"I have [takleef] + for [kitne din]." I have a bad headache. It's been two days. Kya hai, aur kab se hai — doctor ko bas yahi do cheezein chahiye.

Takleef English line Suno Bukhaar hai I have a fever. It started last night. Sar dard I've had a headache since yesterday. Khaansi aur zukaam I have a cough and a blocked nose. Pet dard I have a stomach ache, mostly after eating. Chakkar aate hain I feel dizzy when I stand up. Kamzori lagti hai I've been feeling weak and tired all week. Yahan dard hai It hurts here, right below the knee. Neend nahi aati I'm not sleeping well these days. Dawai se allergy hai I'm allergic to penicillin. Ye dawai pehle se le raha hoon I'm already taking a tablet for blood pressure. Doctor jo poochhega Matlab Suno How long have you had this? Kab se hai? Does it hurt when I press here? Yahan dabane se dard hota hai? Are you on any medication? Koi dawai chal rahi hai? Take this twice a day after meals. Din me do baar, khaane ke baad. Come back if it doesn't improve in three days. Teen din me theek na ho to dobara aaiye.

Ye do sawaal hamesha poochho

How many times a day should I take this? Before food or after food?

docs.title: 30.4 Phone call
docs.text:
Phone sabse mushkil lagta hai — chehra nahi dikhta, aawaz katti hai. Isliye yahan lines ratna sabse zyada kaam aata hai.

Kaam English line Suno Call uthana Hello, this is Ravi speaking. Kaun bol raha hai? May I know who's calling? Kisi ko bulana Could I speak to Mr Sharma, please? Thoda rukiye Hold on a second, please. Wo nahi hain He's not at his desk right now. Message le lijiye Can I take a message? Aawaz nahi aa rahi Sorry, you're breaking up. Could you say that again? Network kharaab hai The line is bad. Let me call you back. Galat number I think you have the wrong number. Baad me baat karte hain Can I call you back in ten minutes? Baat khatam karna Thanks for your time. Have a good day.

Phone par teen aam galtiyan

  • Galat: "Hello, myself Ravi."
  • Sahi: Hello, this is Ravi.

  • Kyun: "Myself Ravi" English me vaakya hi nahi banta. Phone par hamesha "This is…".

  • Galat: "Who is this?" (seedha, thoda rukha)

  • Sahi: May I know who's calling?

  • Kyun: "Who is this?" sunne me sakht lagta hai. "May I know…" se wahi baat, par tehzeeb ke saath.

  • Galat: "I didn't get you." (lagta hai aapne insaan hi na pehchaana)

  • Sahi: Sorry, I didn't catch that.
  • Kyun: "Didn't catch that" ka matlab saaf hai: aawaz/baat samajh nahi aayi.

docs.title: 30.5 Restaurant me
docs.text:
Kehna hai English line Suno Do logon ki table A table for two, please. Menu dijiye Could we see the menu, please? Kya achcha hai yahan? What would you recommend? Ye kitna teekha hai? Is this very spicy? Kam teekha banwaiye Could you make it less spicy, please? Main ye lunga I'll have the paneer tikka, please. Veg hai? Is this vegetarian? Thoda paani Could we get some water, please? Order nahi aaya Excuse me, our order hasn't come yet. Ye galat aaya hai Sorry, I think this isn't what I ordered. Pack kar dijiye Could you pack the rest, please? Bill lao Could we have the bill, please?

Poora mini-dialogue — restaurant

  • Waiter: Good evening. How many of you? Kitne log hain?
  • Aap: Three, please. Somewhere away from the AC, if possible. "If possible" = ho sake to. Ye do shabd har request ko narm bana dete hain.
  • Waiter: Sure. Are you ready to order? Order dene ko taiyaar hain?
  • Aap: Give us a couple of minutes. What would you recommend? "A couple of minutes" = do-teen minute.
  • Waiter: The butter chicken is very popular here. Yahan ye sabse chalta hai.
  • Aap: We'll have that, two rotis and a plain rice. And could you make it less spicy? Order dene ka saancha: "We'll have…" + list. Bilkul natural hai.
  • Aap (baad me): That was lovely, thanks. Could we have the bill? Khaana achcha tha. "Lovely" khaane ke liye bahut natural shabd hai.

docs.title: 30.6 Raasta poochhna aur batana
docs.text: Kehna hai English line Suno Maaf kijiye, raasta poochhna hai Excuse me, could you help me with directions? Metro kahan hai? How do I get to the metro station? Kitni door hai? Is it far from here? Paidal ja sakte hain? Can I walk there, or should I take an auto? Main kho gaya hoon I think I'm lost. I'm looking for Lake Road. Dobara bataiye Sorry, could you say that once more, slowly? Jo jawaab milega Matlab Suno Go straight for about five minutes. Paanch minute seedha chalte raho. Take the second left. Doosri baayein galli lo. It's right opposite the bank. Bank ke theek saamne hai. It's next to the chemist. Medical store ke bilkul bagal me. You'll see it on your right. Daayein haath par dikh jaayega. You've come too far — turn around. Aap aage nikal aaye — wapas mudiye.

docs.title: 30.7 Chhote shabd jo har jagah kaam aate hain
docs.text:
Line Kab bolo Suno Excuse me… Kisi ko tokne se pehle — hamesha. Sorry to bother you. Jab kisi ko bich me rok rahe ho. No worries. Koi baat nahi — jab koi maafi maange. That's all right. Theek hai, chhodo. Thanks a lot — that helps. Madad ke liye shukriya. Appreciate it. Chhota, natural shukriya. Take care. Vidaai ke waqt — dost ya jaan-pehchaan ko.

Chaar lines jo hum bolte hain par English me ajeeb lagti hain

  • Galat: What is your good name?
  • Sahi: May I know your name?

  • Kyun: "Good name" Hindi ke "shubh naam" ka seedha anuvaad hai. English me aisa kuch nahi hota.

  • Galat: Please do the needful.

  • Sahi: Could you take care of this, please?

  • Kyun: "Do the needful" se saamne wale ko pata nahi chalta ki karna kya hai. Saaf kaho.

  • Galat: I am having two brothers.

  • Sahi: I have two brothers.

  • Kyun: "Have" ko -ing nahi lagta jab wo "paas hona" ke matlab me ho.

  • Galat: Where you are going?

  • Sahi: Where are you going?
  • Kyun: Sawaal me helping verb subject se pehle aata hai: Where are you…

docs.title: 30.8 Practice — Roz ki baat-cheet
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Dukaan par keemat poochhne ka sabse natural tareeka?

  • How much is this?
  • What is the cost of this?
  • How much price?
  • This is how much rupees?
Jawaab

How much is this?

Chhota, seedha, har jagah chalta hai. 'What is the cost' kitaabi lagta hai.

Exercise 2

Phone uthate waqt apna naam kaise batayein?

  • Hello, this is Ravi speaking.
  • Hello, myself Ravi.
  • Hello, I am Ravi speaking here.
  • Hello, Ravi this side.

Hint: 'Myself' se shuru nahi.

Jawaab

Hello, this is Ravi speaking.

Phone par apna naam hamesha 'This is…' se. 'Myself Ravi' English me vaakya hi nahi banta.

Exercise 3

Doctor ko takleef batane ka saancha kya hai?

  • Kya hai + kab se hai
  • Sirf dawai ka naam
  • Kitna dard hai, 1 se 10 me
  • Pehle apni umar batana
Jawaab

Kya hai + kab se hai

'I have a fever. It started last night.' Doctor ko shuru me bas ye do cheezein chahiye.

Exercise 4

Phone par aawaz kat rahi hai. Kya bolein?

  • Sorry, you're breaking up. Could you say that again?
  • I didn't get you.
  • Your voice is not coming.
  • Speak loudly please.
Jawaab

Sorry, you're breaking up. Could you say that again?

'Breaking up' phone ki network dikkat ke liye sahi shabd hai. 'I didn't get you' se lagta hai aapne insaan hi nahi pehchaana.

Exercise 5

Restaurant me order dene ka natural saancha?

  • I'll have the… / We'll have the…
  • Give me one…
  • I want to eat…
  • Bring me…
Jawaab

I'll have the… / We'll have the…

'I'll have the paneer tikka, please.' Sabse aam aur sabse sharif tareeka.

Exercise 6

Auto me 'meter se chalo' ka sahi English?

  • Could you go by the meter, please?
  • Please put meter on.
  • Meter only please.
  • Go in meter.
Jawaab

Could you go by the meter, please?

'by the meter' sahi phrase hai. 'Could you…, please' se baat request banti hai, order nahi.

Exercise 7

Dukaan me: Do you have this ___ a smaller size?

Hint: Size/rang ke liye kaunsa preposition?

Jawaab

in

Size aur rang ke saath 'in': in blue, in medium, in a smaller size.

Exercise 8

Restaurant: Could we have the ___, please? (jo paisa dene ke liye maangte hain)

Jawaab

bill / cheque / check

India aur UK me 'bill', US me 'check'. Dono chalte hain.

Exercise 9

Raasta: Take the second ___. (doosri baayein galli)

Jawaab

left

'Take the second left' = doosri baayein. 'Take a left at the signal' bhi aam hai.

Exercise 10

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — us shabd par tap karo.

I am having two brothers and one sister.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: having.

Sahi roop: I have two brothers and one sister.

'Have' jab 'paas hona' ke matlab me ho to usme -ing nahi lagti.

Exercise 11

Galat shabd dhoondo.

What is your good name, sir?

Jawaab

Galat shabd: good.

Sahi roop: May I know your name, sir?

'Good name' Hindi ke 'shubh naam' ka seedha anuvaad hai. English me aisa nahi bolte.

Exercise 12

Haalat ko uski taiyaar line se jodo.

A B Dukaan — bas dekh rahe hain It started last night. Cab — yahan rok do Can I call you back in ten minutes? Doctor — kab se hai I'm just looking, thanks. Phone — baad me call karta hoon You can stop here, thanks. Jawaab

Dukaan — bas dekh rahe hain — I'm just looking, thanks.; Cab — yahan rok do — You can stop here, thanks.; Doctor — kab se hai — It started last night.; Phone — baad me call karta hoon — Can I call you back in ten minutes?

Har haalat ke liye ek taiyaar line. Soch kar banane ki zaroorat hi nahi padti.

Exercise 13

Dukaan ki line banao.

Shabd: please / Could / have / I / receipt / the

Jawaab

Could I have the receipt please

'Could I have…' sabse sharif maangne ka saancha hai. receipt = ri-SEET, P chup.

Exercise 14

Dukaan par. Pehli line bolo.

Jawaab

Bolo: Excuse me, do you have this in blue

'Excuse me' se shuruaat. 'in blue' — rang ke saath hamesha 'in'.

Exercise 15

Mol-bhaav sharif tareeke se karo.

Jawaab

Bolo: Could you do it for a little less

Seedha 'Reduce the price' kehne se behtar. 'Could you' se wahi baat narm ho jaati hai.

Exercise 16

Cab me baith kar pehli baat.

Jawaab

Bolo: Are you going towards the airport

'towards' se baat aasaan ho jaati hai. Aakhir me aawaz halki oopar — sawaal hai.

Exercise 17

Cab se utarte waqt.

Jawaab

Bolo: You can drop me at gate three. Thanks a lot

'drop me at' = yahan chhod dijiye. Aakhir me shukriya — chhota aur natural.

Exercise 18

Doctor ko takleef batao — kya aur kab se.

Jawaab

Bolo: I have a bad headache. It's been two days

Takleef + samay. Yahi do cheezein doctor ko shuru me chahiye.

Exercise 19

Dawai ke baare me zaroori sawaal.

Jawaab

Bolo: How many times a day should I take this

Roz kitni baar. Saath me 'Before food or after food?' bhi poochh lo.

Exercise 20

Phone uthao — apna naam batao.

Jawaab

Bolo: Hello, this is Ravi speaking

'This is' + naam. 'Myself' bilkul nahi.

Exercise 21

Phone par samajh nahi aaya. Politely poochho.

Jawaab

Bolo: Sorry, you're breaking up. Could you say that again

Network ki dikkat ke liye 'breaking up'. Phir dobara poochho.

Exercise 22

Restaurant me baithte hi.

Jawaab

Bolo: A table for two please

Bas itna kaafi hai. Lamba vaakya banane ki zaroorat nahi.

Exercise 23

Khaana kam teekha banwao.

Jawaab

Bolo: Could you make it less spicy please

'less spicy' = kam teekha. 'Could you' har request ko sharif bana deta hai.

Exercise 24

Raasta poochho.

Jawaab

Bolo: Excuse me, how do I get to the metro station

'How do I get to…' raasta poochhne ka sabse kaam ka saancha hai — kisi bhi jagah ke liye.

Exercise 25

Kho gaye ho. Madad maango.

Jawaab

Bolo: I think I'm lost. I'm looking for Lake Road

Pehle haalat batao, phir jagah ka naam. Log turant madad karte hain.

Aage kya karein

Aaj ka kaam: ek haalat chuno — jo kal sach me pesh aayegi — aur uski paanch lines 10 baar bolo. Phir kal wahi lines asli jagah par use karo. Pehli baar me dil dhadkega; doosri baar aasaan hoga; teesri baar aadat ban jaayegi. Agla chapter: Interview aur office — apna intro, sawaal-jawaab aur meeting ki bhasha.

docs.title: Chapter 55: Roz ki kahaniyan
docs.text:
Roz ki kahaniyan — office, ghar aur safar ki English

Asli zindagi me English chhoti kahaniyon jaisi saaf nahi hoti. Meeting me log jaldi-jaldi summary dete hain, customer care wala script padhta hai, dost voice note me aadhe shabd kha jaata hai. Is chapter me paanch lambe tukde hain (100–200 shabd). Yahan sirf "kya hua" nahi — kyon hua aur bolne wala kaisa mehsoos kar raha hai, ye bhi pakadna hai. Aur naye shabd? Unka matlab context se nikaalna seekhenge.

docs.title: 55.1 Line ke beech sunna — inference kya hai
docs.text:
Log aksar seedha nahi kehte "I am angry" ya "I am worried". Wo apne shabdon, aawaz ke utaar-chadhaav aur haalat se bata dete hain. In teen clues ko jodkar matlab nikaalna = inference. Intermediate level ke listening sawaal ("How does she feel?", "Why does he say…?") isi par hote hain.

Figure 55.1. Inference = teen clues ka jod. Ek clue galat raah dikha sakta hai; teeno ek hi taraf ishaara karein to jawaab pakka.

Feeling = words + tone + situation

"How does she feel?" ka jawaab ek shabd se nahi, teen clues se aata hai: kya kaha, kaise kaha, aur kis haalat me kaha. Pehle haalat samjho, phir shabd, phir aawaz.

  • Rohit, I know that's frustrating, but it's the safer choice. Rohit, mujhe pata hai ye chidhaane wali baat hai, par ye zyada surakshit faisla hai. Bolne wali samajh rahi hai ki Rohit naraaz hoga — wo usko manaa rahi hai.
  • Honestly, I don't blame her. Sach kahun to main use galat nahi maanta. Matlab: "uska aisa karna theek hai" — galti meri thi.
  • And please don't be late this time, okay? Aur is baar late mat hona. "this time" chhupa sach bata deta hai — pichhli baar wo late thi.

docs.title: 55.2 Team meeting ka summary
docs.text:
Kavita ek software team ki lead hai. Meeting ke aakhir me wo saari baatein jaldi se dohraati hai. Aise summary me signpost words naksha banaate hain: First, Second, Third, And finally. Suno: launch date kyon badli, aur stand-up ab kitne baje hoga?

Phrase Matlab (is context me) sum up saar me batana, nichod dena launch date product shuru hone ki taarikh stand-up roz ki 10–15 minute ki chhoti meeting take over kisi ka kaam apne haath me lena have a think soch lo (British, dostana)

🎧 Poora summary suno (2 hisse)

  • Part 1 — good news aur nayi date Do numbers pakdo: purani date aur nayi date.
  • Part 2 — stand-up aur Sana ka kaam "instead of" sunte hi samjho — kuch badal raha hai.
Transcript

Kavita: Okay, everyone, let me quickly sum up today's meeting. First, the good news: the new billing app is almost ready, and the client loved the demo on Tuesday. Second, we've moved the launch date from the tenth of March to the seventeenth, because the testing team needs one more week. Rohit, I know that's frustrating after all those late nights, but honestly, it's the safer choice.

Third, from next Monday, our daily stand-up will start at nine forty-five instead of ten, so please don't be late. And finally, Sana is moving to the design team next month, so someone will need to take over her weekly reports. Have a think and let me know by Friday. Any questions? No? Great. Thanks, everyone, and well done on the demo.

  • We've moved the launch date from the tenth of March to the seventeenth. Launch 10 March se 17 March kar diya. "from … to …" = purana → naya. Kaaran turant "because" ke baad aata hai.
  • After all those late nights. Itni raaton tak der se kaam karne ke baad. Inference: Rohit ne bahut mehnat ki thi — isliye wo naaraz ho sakta hai.

Signposts = summary ka naksha

First… Second… Third… And finally… sunte hi notes me 1, 2, 3, 4 likh lo. Har number ke aage ek-do shabd — poora vaakya nahi. "And finally" = ab aakhri baat; dhyan wapas laao.

docs.title: 55.3 Customer care call — internet band hai
docs.text:
Mrs Lata Iyer ghar se kaam karti hain aur unka internet kal raat se band hai. Wo BlueRiver Broadband ke customer care ko phone karti hain. Yahan ek hi aawaz dono log padhegi — naam ("Hi, Deepak", "Thank you, Mrs Iyer") aur sawaal-jawaab se pehchaano kaun bol raha hai. Suno: unke liye ye itna urgent kyon hai, aur do baje tak theek na hua to kya milega?

Phrase Matlab (is context me) down (machine, net) band, kaam nahi kar raha fault takneeki kharaabi arrange intezaam karna complaint number shikaayat ka number patience sabr (PAY-shuns)

🎧 Poora call suno (2 hisse)

  • Part 1 — problem kya hai ID ke letters aur digits alag-alag bole jaate hain — B R seven two zero five.
  • Part 2 — kab tak theek hoga "If it isn't…" ke baad shart (condition) aur vaada — ise dhyan se suno.
Transcript

Deepak: Good morning, thank you for calling BlueRiver Broadband. My name is Deepak. How may I help you today?

Mrs Iyer: Hi, Deepak. My internet has been down since last night, and I work from home, so this is really urgent.

Deepak: I'm very sorry to hear that, ma'am. May I have your customer ID, please?

Mrs Iyer: Yes, it's BR7205.

Deepak: Thank you, Mrs Iyer. I can see there's a fault in your area, and our engineers are already working on it.

Mrs Iyer: How long will it take?

Deepak: It should be fixed by 2 p.m. today. If it isn't, I'll arrange a technician visit, and you'll get a 50% discount on this month's bill.

Mrs Iyer: Okay, but please make sure it's done. I have an important client call at three.

Deepak: Absolutely, ma'am. Your complaint number is SR4481. Is there anything else I can help you with?

Mrs Iyer: No, that's all. Thank you.

Deepak: Thank you for your patience. Have a good day.

  • I work from home, so this is really urgent. Main ghar se kaam karti hoon, isliye ye bahut zaroori hai. "so" ke pehle kaaran, baad me nateeja.
  • Okay, but please make sure it's done. Theek hai, par pakka kar dena. "Okay, but…" = maan to liya, par bharosa poora nahi. Inference: wo pareshaan aur thodi be-sabr hain.
  • It should be fixed by two p.m. today. Aaj do baje tak theek ho jaana chahiye. "should" = ummeed hai, guarantee nahi. "by 2" = do baje se pehle kabhi bhi.

Customer care ki English — galat samajhna aasaan hai

  • Galat: "It should be fixed by two" = do baje pakka theek ho jaayega.
  • Sahi: "It should be fixed by two" = ummeed hai, do baje se pehle.
  • Kyun: "should" vaada nahi, andaaza hai. Isiliye Deepak turant plan B deta hai: "If it isn't, …".

docs.title: 55.4 Safar ki gadbad — teen past tenses
docs.text:
Ek bhai apni behan ke saath Jaipur shaadi me jaane ki kahani sunaata hai. Kahani me teen tarah ka past hai — past simple (ek ke baad ek ghatna), past continuous (jab kuch chal raha tha) aur past perfect (usse bhi pehle). Tense samjho to samay ka kram samajh aata hai. (Poora niyam: Saare 12 tenses.)

Figure 55.2. had + V3 sunte hi socho: ye aur bhi pehle hua tha . were + -ing = pardaa (background), aur beech me ek past simple ghatna — kahani ka jhatka. Phrase Matlab (is context me) security queue checking ki line (queue = "kyoo") realised achaanak samajh aaya furious bahut zyada gusse me got through (checking) paar kar li I don't blame her main use galat nahi maanta

🎧 Poori kahani suno (2 hisse)

  • Part 1 — airport par jhatka Behan kuch nahi boli — ye chuppi bhi ek clue hai.
  • Part 2 — ek aur musibat "But the adventure wasn't over" = abhi aur gadbad baaki hai.
Transcript

Last December, my sister and I were travelling to Jaipur for our cousin's wedding. We had booked an early flight from Bengaluru, so we left home at four in the morning. While we were standing in the security queue, I suddenly realised that I had left my ID card at home. I couldn't believe it. My sister was furious, and for a minute she didn't say a word.

Luckily, a staff member told me that I could show a digital copy of my ID on my phone. I downloaded it in five minutes, and we got through just in time. But the adventure wasn't over. When we landed in Jaipur, we discovered that our suitcase had gone to Delhi! We spent the first evening of the wedding in our travel clothes. Now, whenever we travel, my sister checks my bag twice. Honestly, I don't blame her.

  • While we were standing in the security queue, I suddenly realised that I had left my ID card at home. Hum line me khade the, tabhi achaanak yaad aaya ki ID ghar par chhod aaya hoon. Ek vaakya, teen tense — background, ghatna, aur usse pehle ki baat.
  • Luckily, a staff member told me that I could show a digital copy. Kismat se staff ne bataaya ki digital copy chal jaayegi. "Luckily" = kahani ki disha achhi taraf mudi.
  • Now, whenever we travel, my sister checks my bag twice. Ab jab bhi hum safar karte hain, behan mera bag do baar check karti hai. Present simple = nayi aadat, kahani ka sabak.

Kahani ke mod-shabd

suddenly (achaanak jhatka) · luckily (achhi khabar) · but (ulti baat) · when we landed (naya scene). Ye shabd aate hi kahani ki disha badalti hai. Mod-shabd sunte hi agla vaakya aur dhyan se suno.

docs.title: 55.5 Podcast — work from home par baat
docs.text:
"Chai and Careers" naam ke podcast me do host — Nikhil aur Aisha — ghar se kaam karne ke fayde aur nuksaan par baat karte hain. Podcast me log raay dete hain, isliye mostly, but, to be honest, for me jaise shabd sabse zaroori hain. Suno: Nikhil ko kya achha lagta hai, kya bura, aur uska hal kya hai?

Phrase Matlab (is context me) remotely office se door, ghar ya kahin aur se commute roz ghar se office aana-jaana overhear bina iraade ke kaan me padna hidden cost chhupa nuksaan best of both worlds dono taraf ka fayda

🎧 Podcast suno (2 hisse)

  • Part 1 — Nikhil ka anubhav "Mostly, yes" — haan, par poori tarah nahi. Ab "but" ka intezaar karo.
  • Part 2 — listener ki baat aur hal "For me, it's…" = ab apni raay aa rahi hai.
Transcript

Nikhil: Welcome back to Chai and Careers. I'm Nikhil.

Aisha: And I'm Aisha. Today we're talking about working from home. Nikhil, you've been working remotely for three years now. Do you still enjoy it?

Nikhil: Mostly, yes. I save almost two hours a day because I don't have to commute. I cook a proper lunch, and I see much more of my kids. But to be honest, I sometimes feel a bit lonely. There's no chat by the coffee machine, you know?

Aisha: That's interesting, because a lot of our listeners say the same thing. One listener, Pooja from Indore, wrote in to say that she works better at home, but she misses learning from senior colleagues.

Nikhil: Yes, I think that's the hidden cost. You don't overhear how experienced people solve problems.

Aisha: So what's the answer?

Nikhil: For me, it's a hybrid model. Two days in the office for teamwork, and three days at home for focused work.

Aisha: That sounds like the best of both worlds.

  • I see much more of my kids. Main bachchon ke saath bahut zyada samay bitaata hoon. "see more of someone" = zyada milna, saath rehna.
  • But to be honest, I sometimes feel a bit lonely. Par sach kahun to kabhi-kabhi akelapan lagta hai. "to be honest" ke baad aksar wo baat aati hai jo kehna thoda mushkil ho.
  • You don't overhear how experienced people solve problems. Aap ye nahi sun paate ki tajurbekaar log mushkil kaise suljhaate hain. Yahan "you" = koi bhi, aam log — sirf Aisha nahi.

docs.title: 55.6 Dost ka WhatsApp voice note
docs.text:
Tanvi apni dost Riya ko voice note bhejti hai. Ye informal English hai — tez, aadhe vaakya, "kind of", "six-ish", "anyway". Asli zindagi me sabse zyada yahi sunoge. Suno: Karan kyon nahi aa raha, plan kya bana, aur Riya ko kya laana hai?

🎧 Voice note suno

  • Voice note — Tanvi → Riya Teen kaam ki baatein pakdo: kaun nahi aa raha, kahan milna, kya laana.
Transcript

Hey Riya! Sorry, sorry, I know I didn't reply yesterday. It was a crazy day at work. Listen, about Saturday. The plan's changed a bit. Karan can't make it, because his flight got cancelled, so it's just the four of us now. Instead of the movie, how about that new café in Bandra, the one with all the board games? I'm kind of bored of movies anyway. Oh, and can you bring your speaker? Mine's broken. Let's meet at six-ish outside the station. And please don't be late this time, okay? I'm joking. Well, mostly! Anyway, text me when you get this. Bye!

Voice note (informal) Formal roop Matlab Karan can't make it. Karan is unable to attend. Karan nahi aa paayega I'm kind of bored of movies. I'm rather tired of films. thoda bore ho gayi hoon at six-ish at around six o'clock lagbhag chhe baje Mine's broken. Mine is not working. mera kharaab hai Anyway, text me. Please reply when you can. khair, message kar dena
  • Karan can't make it, because his flight got cancelled. Karan nahi aa sakta, uski flight cancel ho gayi. "can't" me "t" lagbhag gaayab — "kaan(t) make it". Matlab "na" hai, ye context (because…cancelled) se pakka hota hai.
  • I'm joking. Well, mostly! Mazaak kar rahi hoon. Khair, zyaadatar! Inference: wo sach me chahti hai ki Riya time par aaye.
  • Let's meet at six-ish outside the station. Station ke bahar lagbhag chhe baje milte hain. "-ish" = lagbhag (six-ish, tallish, greenish).

can vs can't — context se pakdo

Fast speech me can halka "kn" ho jaata hai aur can't lamba "kaant" — par "t" aksar sunaai nahi deta. Agle shabd dekho: because… cancelled = can't. Aawaz + context = sahi matlab.

docs.title: 55.7 Context se matlab — aur sunne ke jaal
docs.text:
Lambi English me har baar koi naya shabd aayega. Rukna mat. Teen sawaal poochho: 1) ye achhi baat hai ya buri? 2) aas-paas ke shabd kya bata rahe hain? 3) kahani ka agla hissa kya kehta hai? Aksar itna kaafi hai. (Phrasal verbs ki poori list: Phrasal verbs chapter.)

Wo phrases jo shabd-dar-shabd galat samajh aate hain

  • Galat: "My internet is down" = internet neeche hai / dheema hai.
  • Sahi: "down" = bilkul band, kaam nahi kar raha.

  • Kyun: Machine, website, server, network ke liye "down" = band. Ulta: "It's up again" = phir chal gaya.

  • Galat: "I don't blame her" = main use dosh deta hoon.

  • Sahi: "I don't blame her" = main use galat nahi maanta, wo sahi hai.

  • Kyun: "don't" chhota sunaai deta hai aur chhoot jaata hai. Ek "not" poora matlab ulat deta hai — hamesha negatives par kaan lagao.

  • Galat: "Karan can't make it" = Karan kuch bana nahi sakta.

  • Sahi: "can't make it" = (party, meeting me) nahi aa paayega.

  • Kyun: "make it" = pahunch paana, aa paana. "Can you make it on Friday?" = kya tum Friday aa sakte ho?

  • Galat: "Take over her reports" = report le jaana.

  • Sahi: "take over" = uska kaam ab aap sambhaaloge.
  • Kyun: Sana design team me ja rahi hai — context hi bata raha hai ki uska kaam kisi aur ko karna padega.

Naya shabd? Rukna mat

Agla vaakya suno — wo aksar pichhle shabd ka matlab khol deta hai. Pehle achha ya bura tay karo, phir context se matlab. furious → "didn't say a word" → bahut gussa.

docs.title: 55.8 Practice — Roz ki kahaniyan
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Why has the launch date been moved?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Second, we've moved the launch date from the tenth of March to the seventeenth, because the testing team needs one more week.

  • The testing team needs more time.
  • The client didn't like the demo.
  • Rohit is on leave.
  • The app is already finished.
Jawaab

The testing team needs more time.

'because the testing team needs one more week' — kaaran 'because' ke baad.

Exercise 2

How does Kavita think Rohit feels about the new date?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Rohit, I know that's frustrating after all those late nights, but honestly, it's the safer choice.

  • frustrated
  • relieved
  • excited
  • bored
Jawaab

frustrated

'I know that's frustrating after all those late nights' — Rohit ne der raat tak kaam kiya, ab date aage badh gayi. Kavita samajh rahi hai ki wo chidha hua hoga.

Exercise 3

What time will the daily stand-up start from next Monday?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Third, from next Monday, our daily stand-up will start at nine forty-five instead of ten, so please don't be late.

  • 9:45
  • 10:00
  • 10:15
  • 9:15
Jawaab

9:45

'nine forty-five instead of ten' — 'instead of' ke baad purana time aata hai, pehle naya.

Exercise 4

Why is the problem really urgent for Mrs Iyer?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Hi, Deepak. My internet has been down since last night, and I work from home, so this is really urgent.

  • She works from home.
  • Her children have online exams.
  • She is moving house.
  • She has already paid twice.
Jawaab

She works from home.

'I work from home, so this is really urgent' — so ke pehle kaaran.

Exercise 5

What will happen if the internet is not fixed by 2 p.m.?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

It should be fixed by two p.m. today. If it isn't, I'll arrange a technician visit, and you'll get a fifty percent discount on this month's bill.

  • a technician visit and a 50% discount
  • a free new router
  • a full refund for the year
  • a call from the manager
Jawaab

a technician visit and a 50% discount

'If it isn't' ke baad do vaade: technician visit + 50% discount.

Exercise 6

How does Mrs Iyer probably feel at the end of the call?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Okay, but please make sure it's done. I have an important client call at three.

  • still worried and a little impatient
  • completely relaxed
  • angry with Deepak personally
  • very happy
Jawaab

still worried and a little impatient

'Okay, but…' + 'please make sure' + client call at three = maan gayi, par fikr abhi bhi hai.

Exercise 7

What had the speaker forgotten?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

While we were standing in the security queue, I suddenly realised that I had left my ID card at home. I couldn't believe it.

  • his ID card
  • his phone
  • the flight tickets
  • his suitcase
Jawaab

his ID card

'I had left my ID card at home' — past perfect: ghar se nikalne se pehle hi chhoot gaya tha.

Exercise 8

How did his sister react?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

I couldn't believe it. My sister was furious, and for a minute she didn't say a word.

  • She was very angry and silent.
  • She laughed at him.
  • She cried loudly.
  • She went home alone.
Jawaab

She was very angry and silent.

furious = bahut gussa; 'didn't say a word' = bilkul chup.

Exercise 9

What does the speaker mean by 'I don't blame her'?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Now, whenever we travel, my sister checks my bag twice. Honestly, I don't blame her.

  • She is right to check his bag.
  • He is angry with his sister.
  • She made the mistake.
  • He doesn't want her help.
Jawaab

She is right to check his bag.

'I don't blame her' = main use galat nahi maanta — galti meri thi, uska check karna theek hai.

Exercise 10

How much time does Nikhil save every day?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Mostly, yes. I save almost two hours a day because I don't have to commute. I cook a proper lunch, and I see much more of my kids.

  • almost two hours
  • about thirty minutes
  • three hours
  • one day a week
Jawaab

almost two hours

'almost two hours a day' — commute nahi karna padta.

Exercise 11

What is Nikhil's solution?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

So what's the answer? For me, it's a hybrid model. Two days in the office for teamwork, and three days at home for focused work.

  • two days in the office, three at home
  • five days at home
  • five days in the office
  • working only at weekends
Jawaab

two days in the office, three at home

'For me, it's a hybrid model' — 2 din office (teamwork), 3 din ghar (focused work).

Exercise 12

Why can't Karan come on Saturday?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Listen, about Saturday. The plan's changed a bit. Karan can't make it, because his flight got cancelled, so it's just the four of us now.

  • His flight got cancelled.
  • He is ill.
  • He has to work.
  • He doesn't like movies.
Jawaab

His flight got cancelled.

'can't make it, because his flight got cancelled' — make it = aa paana.

Exercise 13

What does Tanvi ask Riya to bring?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Oh, and can you bring your speaker? Mine's broken. Let's meet at six-ish outside the station.

  • her speaker
  • board games
  • movie tickets
  • snacks
Jawaab

her speaker
