Koi dikkat nahi — har browser me speech recognition nahi hota. Us soorat me page khud likh dega ki sun kar dohra lo. Mic sirf ek sahayak hai, shart nahi. Aapka khud ka kaan sabse achcha judge hai: 🔊 suno, record karne wale app me khud bolo, dono bajao, farq suno. Yahi professional log karte hain.

docs.title: 1.4 Kahan se shuru karein — apna raasta chuno
docs.text:
Teen tarah ke padhne wale hote hain. Apni line dhoondo:

A. 'Mujhe kuch nahi aata, zero se shuru karna hai'

Seedha kram se chalo. Agla chapter — English ki aawazein — pehle padho, kyunki wahi neev hai. Phir Grammar ki buniyaad, phir Bolna seekho. Rozana ek hissa. Teen mahine me aap pehchaan nahi paayenge khud ko.

B. 'Grammar aati hai, par bolte waqt atak jaata hoon'

Ye sabse aam haalat hai — aur iska ilaaj grammar nahi hai. Seedha "Bolna seekho" hisse par jao: Uchchaaran → Rhythm → Fluency → Roz ki baat-cheet. Grammar wale chapters sirf tab kholo jab koi khaas cheez atke.

C. 'Interview hai / office join kar raha hoon'

Pehle Interview aur office chapter, phir Fluency, phir Indian English ki aadatein (jo galtiyan interview me turant pakdi jaati hain). Baaki kitaab baad me, aaraam se.

Kahin bhi atko to

Sidebar me saari chapters ki list hai — jahan se marzi kholo. Kitaab aapka progress khud yaad rakhti hai: jo quiz aap kar lete hain, unka nishaan contents page par lag jaata hai. Koi login nahi, kuch bharna nahi.

docs.title: 1.5 Jab man kare chhod dene ka
docs.text:
Ek baat seedhi keh deta hoon, kyunki koi kitaab ye nahi kehti: do-teen hafte baad aapko lagega ki kuch sudhaar nahi ho raha. Ye bilkul normal hai. Bhasha seekhna seedhi chadhaai nahi, seedhiyan hain — kai din ek jaisa lagta hai, phir achaanak ek din aap ek poora vaakya bina soche bol dete hain.

  • It is normal to feel stuck. I will speak anyway. Atakna normal hai. Phir bhi bolunga. Jis din man na kare, ye line bol do aur 5 minute kar lo.
  • Sorry, my English is improving. Please bear with me. Asli duniya me jab atko to yahi bolo — "thoda sambhaal lijiye". Log hamesha madad karte hain.

Teen aadatein jo sab se zyada nuksaan karti hain

  • Galat: "Pehle grammar perfect karunga, phir bolunga."
  • Sahi: Aaj se galat-salat bolo, grammar saath-saath theek hoti jaayegi.

  • Kyun: Jo log bolne se pehle perfect hone ka intezaar karte hain, wo kabhi shuru hi nahi karte.

  • Galat: Hindi me soch kar, dimaag me translate karke bolna.

  • Sahi: Chhote ready-made vaakye ratna, aur unhe seedha bolna.

  • Kyun: Translate karne me 3-4 second lagte hain — isi gap me confidence toot jaata hai. Isliye is kitaab me taiyaar lines di gayi hain.

  • Galat: Sirf aankhon se padhte rehna, kabhi aawaz nahi nikaalna.

  • Sahi: Har line kam se kam ek baar zor se bolna.
  • Kyun: Yahi is kitaab aur baaki sab kitaabon ka farq hai. Chup-chaap padhoge to natija bhi chup rahega.

docs.title: 1.6 Chhota sa pehla kadam — abhi
docs.text: Neeche ka quiz choti si shuruaat hai. Isme kuch sawaal bol kar dene hain. Kamre ka darwaza band karo, aur shuru karo. Paanch minute, bas.

docs.title: 1.7 Practice — Shuruaat
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Is kitaab ka sabse bada niyam kya hai?

  • Har English line zor se bolna
  • Roz ek poora chapter khatam karna
  • Pehle saari grammar yaad karna
  • Sirf dhyan se padhna

Hint: Chaar hisson me sabse bada hissa kaunsa tha?

Jawaab

Har English line zor se bolna

Padhna samajh deta hai, bolna fluency deta hai. Zubaan ki muscle sirf dohraav se seekhti hai.

Exercise 2

Roz kitna waqt dena sabse behtar hai?

  • 15 minute, roz
  • 2 ghante, hafte me ek din
  • 45 minute, hafte me do din
  • Jab man kare, jitna man kare
Jawaab

15 minute, roz

Dimaag bhasha dohraav se seekhta hai, lambai se nahi. Roz thoda > kabhi-kabhi bahut.

Exercise 3

15 minute me sabse zyada waqt kis par jaata hai?

  • Zor se bolna (6 minute)
  • Padhna (4 minute)
  • Quiz (3 minute)
  • Dohraav (2 minute)
Jawaab

Zor se bolna (6 minute)

Diagram me narangi hissa sabse bada tha — bolna. Padhna sirf 4 minute.

Exercise 4

Quiz me galat jawaab aaye to?

  • Explanation dhyan se padho — wahi seekhna hai
  • Quiz chhod do
  • Chapter dobara poora ratna padega
  • Aage ke quiz skip kar do

Hint: Galti ka sabse bada faayda kya hai?

Jawaab

Explanation dhyan se padho — wahi seekhna hai

Sahi jawaab sirf confirm karta hai. Galat jawaab ke baad wala 'kyun' asli seekh hai.

Exercise 5

Agar aapki grammar theek hai par bolte waqt atakte hain, to kahan se shuru karein?

  • Seedha Bolna seekho hisse se
  • Shabd ke 8 prakaar se
  • Idioms se
  • Final test se
Jawaab

Seedha Bolna seekho hisse se

Atakna grammar ki kami nahi, practice ki kami hai. Uchchaaran, rhythm aur fluency se shuru karo.

Exercise 6

It is ___ to feel stuck.

Hint: Atakna 'aam baat' hai — English me?

Jawaab

normal

'It is normal to…' ek bahut kaam ka saancha hai: It is normal to feel nervous. It is normal to make mistakes.

Exercise 7

I make mistakes, ___ I keep speaking.

Hint: Do ulti baatein jodne wala shabd.

Jawaab

but

'but' do ulti baaton ko jodta hai. Is poore vaakye ko apna niyam bana lo.

Exercise 8

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — us shabd par tap karo.

I am learning English since two months.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: since.

Sahi roop: I have been learning English for two months.

Kitne samay se = 'for'. 'since' tab aata hai jab shuruaat ka point ho — since June.

Exercise 9

Shuruaat ki pehli line. Zor se bolo — dheere, saaf.

Jawaab

Bolo: I am learning English

Chhoti line se shuru karo. 'learning' me 'ning' ko puri tarah bolo, 'learnin' nahi.

Exercise 10

Ab apna niyam bolo.

Jawaab

Bolo: I make mistakes but I keep speaking

Bolte waqt 'mistakes' aur 'speaking' par halka zor aata hai — yahi baat ka matlab hai.

Exercise 11

Samajh na aaye to ye poochhna hai. Politely bolo.

Jawaab

Bolo: Could you say that again please

'Could you' se shuruaat sabse polite hai. Aawaz aakhir me halki oopar jaati hai — ye sawaal hai.

Exercise 12

Aaj ka vaada. Bol kar khatam karo.

Jawaab

Bolo: I will practise for fifteen minutes every day

'fifteen' me zor doosre hisse par — fif-TEEN. 'fifty' me pehle par — FIF-ty. Yahi farq hai.

Aage kya karein

Agar aap zero se shuru kar rahe hain, agla chapter chhodna mat — English ki aawazein. Wahi neev hai jiske bina baaki sab kuch thoda-thoda galat sunai deta rahega. Aur haan: darwaza band, aawaz zor se. 🔊

docs.title: Chapter 41: Idioms
docs.text:
Idioms — jo dictionary se samajh nahi aate

Idiom wo phrase hai jiske shabd alag matlab dete hain aur poora phrase bilkul alag. It's not rocket science me na rocket hai na science — matlab hai "koi mushkil kaam nahi hai". Idioms seekhne ka asli faayda samajhne me hai, bolne me nahi. Jab tak aap dus idioms theek se pehchaante nahi, meeting ki aadhi baat sir ke upar se nikal jaati hai. Aur bolne ke liye? Paanch-chhe kaafi hain — par sahi jagah par.

Ek line me

Idioms pehchaanne ke liye bees seekho, bolne ke liye paanch. Zyada idiom bolne wala native nahi lagta — rata hua lagta hai.

docs.title: 41.1 Idiom ka pehla niyam — wo badalta nahi
docs.text:
Idiom ek jama hua saancha hai. Uske andar ka ek shabd badal do, aur wo toot jaata hai — sunne wale ko lagega aapne galti ki hai, naya andaaz nahi.

Toote hue idioms

  • Galat: It's not rocket technology.
  • Sahi: It's not rocket science.

  • Kyun: Idiom ke shabd fix hote hain — samaanaarthi shabd nahi chalte.

  • Galat: Let's play it from ear.

  • Sahi: Let's play it by ear.

  • Kyun: Chhote shabd bhi fix hote hain. Ek preposition badla, idiom gaya.

  • Galat: He is on the same boat.

  • Sahi: He is in the same boat.
  • Kyun: Naav ke "andar" hote hain, "upar" nahi — isliye in the same boat.

docs.title: 41.2 Teen signal — kaunsa idiom kahan
docs.text:
Sabse zaroori hissa yahi hai. Idioms ko teen dabbon me baanto: har jagah safe, office me theek par likhai me nahi, aur formal jagah par bilkul nahi. Interview, client call aur likhit email — yahan teesra dabba poora band hai.

Figure 41.1. Teen dabbe, teen signal. Agar yaad na rahe, hara dabba hamesha surakshit hai.

docs.title: 41.3 Kaam aur faisle ke idioms
docs.text:
Idiom Matlab Signal on the same page ek hi samajh par hona Hara — email me bhi theek in the long run aage chalkar, lambe samay me Hara play it by ear maahaul dekh kar tay karna Peela back to the drawing board shuru se phir sochna Peela the ball is in their court ab faisla unka hai Peela on the back burner filhaal side me rakha hua Peela cut corners shortcut maar kar quality girana Peela call it a day aaj ka kaam band karna Peela bite the bullet mushkil kaam himmat kar ke karna Laal — bahut casual
  • Before we start, let's make sure we're all on the same page. Shuru karne se pehle pakka kar lein ki hum sab ek hi samajh par hain.
  • We don't have the numbers yet, so let's play it by ear. Aankde abhi nahi aaye, to maahaul dekh kar tay karenge.
  • I've sent the proposal — the ball is in their court now. Proposal bhej diya — ab faisla unka hai.
  • It's seven already — shall we call it a day? Saat baj gaye — aaj ka kaam band kar dein?

docs.title: 41.4 Logon aur rishton ke idioms
docs.text:
Idiom Matlab Signal see eye to eye raay milna Hara in the same boat ek hi halat me hona Peela a safe pair of hands bharosemand insaan Hara — taareef ke liye rub someone the wrong way kisi ko chubhna, bura lagna Peela pull someone's leg mazaak me chidhana Laal — sirf doston me let someone off the hook chhod dena, maaf kar dena Peela get cold feet aakhri waqt par ghabra jaana Peela
  • We don't always see eye to eye, but we work well together. Humari raay hamesha nahi milti, par hum achhe se kaam karte hain.
  • Put her on the project — she's a safe pair of hands. Use project par rakho — wo bharosemand hai.
  • Everyone's waiting on the same approval — we're all in the same boat. Sab ek hi approval ka intezaar kar rahe hain — halat sabki ek hai.

docs.title: 41.5 Paisa, waqt aur mushkil
docs.text:
Idiom Matlab Signal in the pipeline banne ki prakriya me hai Hara a long shot ummeed kam, par koshish karni hai Peela down to the wire aakhri pal tak khinchna Peela cost an arm and a leg bahut mehnga Laal — casual tighten one's belt kharcha kam karna Peela a drop in the ocean itna kam ki farq hi na pade Hara round the clock chauvees ghante Hara a piece of cake bahut aasaan Laal — bachkana lagta hai
  • Two more features are in the pipeline for next quarter. Agle quarter ke liye do aur features banne ki prakriya me hain.
  • It's a long shot, but it costs us nothing to ask. Ummeed kam hai, par poochhne me kuch nahi jaata.
  • The approval came through right down to the wire. Approval bilkul aakhri pal par aayi.

docs.title: 41.6 Jo idioms formal jagah par nahi bolne chahiye
docs.text:
Teen alag wajah hoti hain — aur teeno ka ilaaj alag hai.

a) Bahut casual — bachkana lagte hain

a piece of cake, hit the sack, spill the beans, under the weather, pull someone's leg, cost an arm and a leg. Interview me "The test was a piece of cake" ghamandi aur bachkana dono lagta hai. Isi ki jagah: "The test was straightforward." Formal jagah par idiom hata kar seedha shabd rakho — baat aur saaf ho jaati hai.

b) Bahut ghise hue — cliché

think outside the box, give 110 percent, at the end of the day (baar baar), touch base, hit the ground running, low-hanging fruit. Ye galat nahi hain — bas itne istemaal ho chuke hain ki sunne wale ka dhyan hat jaata hai. Interview me "I always give 110 percent" ka asar zero hai. Uski jagah ek asli udaharan do.

c) Jo India ke bahar samajh nahi aate

Kuch idioms India me bilkul aam hain par international call me chehre khaali reh jaate hain: "Do the needful" → "Please go ahead and process it." "Same to same" → "Exactly the same." "What is your good name?" → "May I have your name?" "Hats off to him" → theek hai, par "Full credit to him" zyada aam hai. Cricket ke idioms bhi dhyan se — "He was on a sticky wicket" ya "clean bowled" America me koi nahi samjhega. In phrases me koi galti nahi hai — ye India ki English ka hissa hain. Baat sirf ye hai ki saamne wale ko samajh aaye ya nahi.

docs.title: 41.7 Idiom ke bina kaam kaise chalayein
docs.text:
Sabse kaam ki skill ye hai: idiom ki jagah seedha matlab bolna. Isse aap kabhi nahi phansoge.

Casual idiom Formal roop It was a piece of cake. It was straightforward. Let's play it by ear. Let's decide once we have more information. We're back to the drawing board. We're revisiting the approach. It cost an arm and a leg. It was extremely expensive. I'm under the weather. I'm not keeping well today. Let's call it a day. Let's stop here and continue tomorrow. The ball is in their court. We're waiting for their decision. It's on the back burner. It's been deprioritised for now.

Ek nuskha jo hamesha chalta hai

Agar idiom bolne me shaq ho, to usse pehle ek saaf line bol do, phir idiom jod do: "We're waiting on their decision — the ball's in their court." Matlab pehle se saaf hai, isliye idiom samajh na aaye to bhi baat ruk nahi rahi.

docs.title: 41.8 Jo galtiyan idioms ke saath hoti hain
docs.text:
Dhyan do

  • Galat: We are on the same page with this.
  • Sahi: We're on the same page about this.

  • Kyun: Idiom ke baad "about" aata hai: on the same page about the plan.

  • Galat: Please do the needful and revert back.

  • Sahi: Please go ahead and let me know once it's done.

  • Kyun: Ye India me bilkul normal hai, par bahar dono phrases ajnabi lagte hain — aur "revert back" me "back" bekaar hai.

  • Galat: In the interview I said the test was a piece of cake.

  • Sahi: I said the test was straightforward.

  • Kyun: Interview me casual idiom ghamandi lagta hai. Seedha shabd zyada confident lagta hai.

  • Galat: I will touch base you tomorrow.

  • Sahi: I'll touch base with you tomorrow.

  • Kyun: "With" zaroori hai. Waise bhi ye idiom ghisa hua hai — seedha "I'll check in with you" behtar.

  • Galat: Every point he made was same to same.

  • Sahi: Every point he made was exactly the same.

  • Kyun: "Same to same" bahar samajh nahi aata. India me chalta hai, international call me nahi.

  • Galat: She spilled the beans in the client presentation.

  • Sahi: She shared the details early in the client presentation.
  • Kyun: Idiom theek hai par jagah galat. Client ke saamne idiom ka matlab halka pad jaata hai.

docs.title: 41.9 Practice — Idioms
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Interview me test ke baare me kya bolna behtar hai?

  • The test was straightforward.
  • The test was a piece of cake.
  • The test was child's play.
  • The test was nothing for me.

Hint: Casual idiom ghamandi lagta hai.

Jawaab

The test was straightforward.

Formal jagah par idiom hata kar seedha shabd rakho. 'A piece of cake' bachkana aur ghamandi dono lagta hai.

Exercise 2

'The ball is in their court' ka matlab?

  • Ab faisla unka hai
  • Wo khel rahe hain
  • Unki galti hai
  • Hum jeet gaye hain
Jawaab

Ab faisla unka hai

Agla kadam saamne wale ka hai. Office me intezaar batane ka polite tareeka hai.

Exercise 3

Kaunsa idiom email aur client call me bhi bilkul safe hai?

  • in the long run
  • hit the sack
  • spill the beans
  • pull my leg
Jawaab

in the long run

'In the long run' hare dabbe ka hai — formal likhai me bhi chalta hai. Baaki teeno bahut casual hain.

Exercise 4

International call me 'Please do the needful' ki jagah kya bolna chahiye?

  • Please go ahead and process it.
  • Please do the necessary.
  • Kindly do the needful immediately.
  • Please needful it.
Jawaab

Please go ahead and process it.

'Do the needful' India me saaf samajh aata hai par bahar ajnabi lagta hai. Seedha bolo ki kya karna hai.

Exercise 5

Let's make sure we're all on the same ___ before we start.

Hint: Ek hi samajh par hona.

Jawaab

page

'On the same page' = ek hi samajh par. Iske baad 'about' aata hai: on the same page about the plan.

Exercise 6

We don't have the numbers yet, so let's play it by ___.

Hint: Jism ka ek hissa.

Jawaab

ear

'Play it by ear' = maahaul dekh kar tay karna. Dhyan rakho: 'by ear', 'from ear' nahi.

Exercise 7

Idiom toot gaya hai — galat shabd par tap karo.

We are all on the same boat this month.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: on.

Sahi roop: We are all in the same boat this month.

Naav ke andar hote hain — 'in the same boat'. Idiom ke chhote shabd fix hote hain.

Exercise 8

Ek shabd bekaar hai — use dhoondo.

Please do the needful and revert back to me.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: back.

Sahi roop: Please go ahead and let me know once it's done.

'Revert' ka matlab hi 'waapas aana' hai, isliye 'back' bekaar hai. Aur poora vaakya seedha likhna behtar hai.

Exercise 9

Idiom ko uske matlab se jodo.

A B call it a day aakhri waqt par ghabra jaana cut corners bharosemand insaan get cold feet aaj ka kaam band karna a safe pair of hands shortcut maar kar quality girana Jawaab

call it a day — aaj ka kaam band karna; cut corners — shortcut maar kar quality girana; get cold feet — aakhri waqt par ghabra jaana; a safe pair of hands — bharosemand insaan

Ye chaaron office me roz sunai dete hain — pehchaanna zaroori hai, bolna optional.

Exercise 10

Casual idiom ko uske formal roop se jodo.

A B It was a piece of cake I'm not keeping well It cost an arm and a leg It's been deprioritised I'm under the weather It was straightforward It's on the back burner It was extremely expensive Jawaab

It was a piece of cake — It was straightforward; It cost an arm and a leg — It was extremely expensive; I'm under the weather — I'm not keeping well; It's on the back burner — It's been deprioritised

Ye skill sabse kaam ki hai: idiom ki jagah seedha matlab bolna. Isse aap kabhi nahi phansoge.

Exercise 11

Kitne idioms bolne ke liye kaafi hain?

  • Paanch-chhe, par sahi jagah par
  • Jitne zyada utna achha
  • Kam se kam pachaas
  • Ek bhi nahi — idioms galat hote hain
Jawaab

Paanch-chhe, par sahi jagah par

Pehchaanne ke liye bees seekho, bolne ke liye paanch. Zyada idiom bolne wala rata hua lagta hai, native nahi.

Exercise 12

Sahi kram banao — office wali line.

Shabd: are / the / ball / court / in / decision / We / waiting / is / their / for / so / their

Jawaab

We are waiting for their decision so the ball is in their court

Yahi nuskha hai: pehle saaf matlab, phir idiom. Agar idiom samajh na aaye to bhi baat poori rehti hai.

Exercise 13

Ye line bolo. 'Same page' me dono shabd barabar zor lete hain.

Jawaab

Bolo: Before we start let us make sure we are on the same page

Meeting shuru karne ki sabse aam line hai. Email me bhi likh sakte ho — ye hare dabbe ka idiom hai.

Aage kya karein

Ek kaagaz par teen column banao — hara, peela, laal. Jab bhi koi naya idiom sunai de, use turant kisi ek column me daal do. Do mahine me aapke paas apni list hogi, aur ye kisi kitaab ki list se zyada kaam aayegi — kyunki ye aapke maahaul ki hogi.

docs.title: Chapter 57: Indian English ki aadatein
docs.text:
Pehle ek baat saaf kar dein: is chapter ki ek bhi cheez "ganwaarpan" nahi hai. Indian English ek asli, poori tarah vikasit English hai — iski apni lay hai, apne shabd hain, aur ise bolne wale karoron log hain. Prepone ek hoshiyaar shabd hai: postpone ka ulta, bilkul taarkik. Out of station angrezi raaj ke zamaane se seedha chala aa raha hai. Ye aadatein hain — kami nahi, aur bewakoofi to bilkul nahi.

To phir ye chapter kyun? Kyunki ek khaas kamre me — international call, videsh ka interview, bahar ke client ko email — saamne wale ko ye phrases samajh nahi aate. Wahan "galat-sahi" ki baat nahi hoti; sirf samajh na aane ki baat hoti hai. Aur jab aapki baat samajh nahi aati, to aapki kaabiliyat bhi kam dikhne lagti hai — jo bilkul na-insaafi hai. Isliye maqsad apni English badalna nahi hai. Maqsad hai ek doosra gear seekhna, jo zaroorat padne par daal sakein.

Is chapter ka asli sawaal

"Ye galat hai ya sahi?" nahi — balki "ye kamra kaunsa hai?" Dilli ke office me "out of station" bilkul theek hai. London ke client ke saath "out of town" bolna behtar hai. Dono sahi — jagah alag.

docs.title: 57.1 Asli dikkat kahan hoti hai — ek naksha
docs.text:
Neeche beech ka column sabse zaroori hai. Wo batata hai ki jab aap ye phrase bolte ho, to saamne wale ke dimaag me kya chalta hai. Wo naraz nahi hota — wo confuse hota hai, aur ruk kar sochne lagta hai. Bas us ek pal ka rukna aapki baat ka asar kam kar deta hai.

Figure 57.1. Beech ka column yaad rakho. Saamne wala naraz nahi hota — wo ruk kar sochta hai, aur wahi ek pal ka rukna aapki baat ka asar kam karta hai.

docs.title: 57.2 Apna parichay — "Myself Ravi"
docs.text:
Ye Hindi ki seedhi chhaap hai: "Main Ravi" — bilkul poora vaakya, bina verb ke. English me myself reflexive pronoun hai (I hurt myself), subject nahi ban sakta. Isliye "Myself Ravi" sunkar saamne wala ruk jaata hai.

Parichay ke teen roop

  • Galat: Myself Ravi, I am from Pune.
  • Sahi: I'm Ravi, and I'm from Pune.

  • Kyun: Casual aur normal — phone par, meeting me, naye log se milte waqt. Sabse aam roop yahi hai.

  • Galat: I am Ravi this side.

  • Sahi: Hi, this is Ravi.

  • Kyun: Phone aur video call par "this is" hi natural hai. "This side" sirf India me chalta hai.

  • Galat: What is your good name?

  • Sahi: May I have your name?
  • Kyun: "Good name" Hindi ke "shubh naam" ka seedha tarjuma hai — pyaara hai, par bahar samajh nahi aata.
  • Hi, I'm Ravi — I handle the vendor side of things. Namaste, main Ravi — vendor ka kaam main dekhta hoon.

docs.title: "Please revert back"
docs.text:
Do cheezein hain yahan. Pehli: revert ka asli matlab hai purani haalat me laut jaana — "The file reverted to its old version." Jawaab dene ke matlab me ye sirf Indian English me chalta hai. Doosri: revert me "waapas" pehle se shaamil hai, isliye back dobara bekaar hai. Yahi return back aur reply back me bhi hota hai.

Jawaab maangne ke saaf tareeke

  • Galat: Kindly revert back at the earliest.
  • Sahi: Please get back to me by Thursday.

  • Kyun: Do sudhaar: "revert back" → "get back to me", aur "at the earliest" → asli taarikh. Taarikh dene se kaam asal me hota hai.

  • Galat: Please reply back soon.

  • Sahi: Please reply when you can.
  • Kyun: Reply, return, revert — teeno me "waapas" shaamil hai. Inke saath "back" kabhi nahi.

docs.title: "Kindly do the needful"
docs.text:
Ye phrase purani sarkari English se aaya hai, aur India me iska matlab sab samajhte hain: "jo karna chahiye wo kar dijiye". Par bahar ke padhne wale ke liye ye sabse bada sawaal chhod deta hai — needful kya hai? Email ka maqsad hi ye hai ki saamne wale ko pata chale ki use kya karna hai. "Do the needful" wo jaankari chhupa deta hai.

Saaf maang likhna seekho

  • Galat: Kindly do the needful and revert back.
  • Sahi: Could you approve the invoice and forward it to accounts? Let me know once it's done.

  • Kyun: Saamne wale ko do cheezein chahiye: kya karna hai, aur kab tak. Dono likho — email aadhi lambi aur dus guna zyada kaam ki ho jaati hai.

  • Galat: Kindly share the file.

  • Sahi: Could you share the file?
  • Kyun: "Kindly" galat nahi hai, par bahar ye bahut purane zamaane ka ya thoda akda hua lagta hai. "Could you" sabse safe hai.

Email ka ek-line formula

Kaam + kaun + kab tak. "Could you approve the PO by Friday so we can release payment?" Teen cheezein ek line me. Isme "kindly", "needful" aur "at the earliest" ki zaroorat hi nahi padti.

docs.title: 57.4 "Prepone" — ek achha shabd, jo bahar nahi pahuncha
docs.text:
Imaandaari se: prepone bahut samajhdaar shabd hai. Post ka ulta pre hai, to postpone ka ulta prepone kyun nahi? Logic bilkul theek hai, aur kuch dictionaries ab ise "Indian English" ke tag ke saath rakhti bhi hain. Par American ya British colleague ne ye shabd zindagi me suna hi nahi hoga.

Jo kehna hai India me Bahar ke liye Pehle kar dena prepone the meeting move the meeting up / bring it forward Baad me kar dena postpone the meeting push the meeting back / postpone it Bilkul radd karna cancel call it off / cancel
  • Could we move Thursday's call up to Tuesday? Thursday ki call Tuesday par le aa sakte hain?

Dhyan do — 'postpone' bilkul sahi hai

Sirf "prepone" ka jodi-shabd bahar nahi hai. Postpone poori duniya me chalta hai, isliye use chhodne ki zaroorat nahi.

docs.title: 57.5 Padhai, parivaar aur safar ke shabd
docs.text:
'Passed out from college'

  • Galat: I passed out from college in 2019.
  • Sahi: I graduated in 2019.

  • Kyun: Pass out ka matlab bahar hai "behosh ho jaana"! Ye line sunkar log hairan ho jaate hain. Sahi roop: graduated from Pune University in 2019, ya finished college in 2019.

  • Galat: I am doing my graduation.

  • Sahi: I'm doing my bachelor's degree. / I'm an undergraduate.

  • Kyun: Bahar "graduation" ka matlab hai degree milne ka samaroh (convocation), padhai nahi.

  • Galat: I gave my twelfth standard exam.

  • Sahi: I took my final school exams. / I finished high school.
  • Kyun: Do cheezein: exam "give" nahi karte, take karte hain (teacher give karta hai). Aur "standard" ki jagah "grade" ya "class" zyada samajh aata hai.

'Cousin brother' aur rishton ke naam

  • Galat: He is my cousin brother.
  • Sahi: He's my cousin.

  • Kyun: English me "cousin" me ladka-ladki ka farq nahi hota, isliye brother/sister jodna ajeeb lagta hai. Agar farq batana zaroori hai: "my cousin — my uncle's son".

  • Galat: My real brother lives in Indore.

  • Sahi: My brother lives in Indore.

  • Kyun: "Real brother" se lagta hai ki baaki bhai naqli hain. English me "brother" ka matlab seedha sagaa bhai hota hai.

  • Galat: She is my co-brother's wife.

  • Sahi: She's my wife's sister. / My sister-in-law.
  • Kyun: Hindi me rishton ke naam bahut zyada aur bahut saaf hain; English me nahi. Isliye rishta seedha samjha do — "my wife's brother", "my mother's cousin".

'Out of station'

  • Galat: I will be out of station next week.
  • Sahi: I'll be out of town next week. / I'm travelling next week.
  • Kyun: Ye phrase angrezi raaj ke "posting station" se aaya hai — India me saaf hai, bahar nahi. Email ke liye sabse saaf: "I'm away from the office until the 14th."

docs.title: 57.6 "I have a doubt" — chhota shabd, bada farq
docs.text:
Class me "Sir, I have a doubt" bolna India me bilkul normal hai. Par English me doubt = shaq, bharosa na hona. "I doubt it" ka matlab hai "mujhe nahi lagta". Isliye international class ya meeting me ye line sunkar teacher ko lagta hai ki aap unki baat par shaq kar rahe ho.

Jo kehna hai Sahi roop Sawaal poochhna hai I have a question. Ek hissa samajh nahi aaya I'm not clear on the second step. Thoda confusion hai Could you clarify that bit? Sach me shaq hai I doubt that will work. (yahan doubt sahi hai)
  • I have a question about the second step — should it run before or after the backup? Doosre step ke baare me ek sawaal hai — wo backup se pehle chalega ya baad me?

docs.title: 57.7 Chaar chhoti aadatein
docs.text:
'Same to same'

  • Galat: Both reports are same to same.
  • Sahi: Both reports are exactly the same. / They're identical.
  • Kyun: "Same to same" bahut hi expressive hai, par ye sirf India ka roop hai. Ek shabd me kaam ho jaata hai: identical.

'Discuss about'

  • Galat: Let's discuss about the budget.
  • Sahi: Let's discuss the budget. / Let's talk about the budget.
  • Kyun: Discuss ke andar hi "about" ka matlab hai. Isi family ke aur shabd: enter the room (not "enter into"), reach Delhi (not "reach at"), marry her (not "marry with"), consider it (not "consider about").

'Order for'

  • Galat: I ordered for two coffees.
  • Sahi: I ordered two coffees.

  • Kyun: Order ke baad seedha cheez aati hai. "For" tab aata hai jab insaan ke liye ho: "I ordered a coffee for you."

  • Galat: Let me request for a copy.

  • Sahi: Let me request a copy. / Let me ask for a copy.
  • Kyun: Request ke baad bhi "for" nahi. Par "ask" ke saath "for" zaroori hai. Yahi jodiyan yaad rakhni padti hain.

Teen aur jo roz dikhti hain

  • Galat: I will do it now itself.
  • Sahi: I'll do it right now.

  • Kyun: "Itself" ko zor dene ke liye lagana Hindi ke "hi" se aaya hai (abhi hi). English me "right" lagao: right now, right there, right away.

  • Galat: What all did he say?

  • Sahi: What exactly did he say? / What did he say?

  • Kyun: "What all", "where all", "who all" — Hindi ke "kya kya" se aaye hain. Pyaare hain, par bahar nahi chalte.

  • Galat: He is my batchmate only.

  • Sahi: We were in the same class. / He's a classmate of mine.
  • Kyun: "Batchmate" aur vaakya ke aakhir me "only" dono Indian English ke hain. "Only" ka ye istemaal bahar bilkul samajh nahi aata.

docs.title: 57.8 Ek nazar me — poori list
docs.text: India me aam International roop Kyun Myself Ravi I'm Ravi "Myself" subject nahi ban sakta Please revert back Please get back to me Revert = purani haalat me jaana; "back" bekaar Kindly do the needful Could you approve and forward it? Saamne wale ko kaam saaf nahi pata chalta Prepone Move it up / bring it forward Shabd bahar maujood nahi hai Passed out from college Graduated in 2019 "Pass out" = behosh ho jaana Cousin brother Cousin Cousin me ling ka farq nahi hota Out of station Out of town / away "Station" ka matlab saaf nahi hota I have a doubt I have a question Doubt = shaq, sawaal nahi Same to same Exactly the same / identical Sirf India ka roop Discuss about Discuss Discuss me "about" shaamil hai Order for two teas Order two teas Order ke baad preposition nahi Now itself Right now Zor dene ka English tareeka "right" hai What all did she say? What exactly did she say? "Kya kya" ka seedha tarjuma I am having a car I have a car Maalikana haq me "have" continuous nahi hota She is in my good books only She's in my good books Aakhir me "only" bahar samajh nahi aata

docs.title: 57.9 Aakhir me — do gear wali English
docs.text:
Duniya ke har bhasha-bolne wale ke paas do gear hote hain: ghar ka roop aur bahar ka roop. Ek Scotsman apne gaon me jo bolta hai, wo New York ki meeting me nahi bolta. Ek Texan London me apna lehja dheema kar leta hai. Isme koi sharm nahi — ye hunar hai.

Ye yaad rakho

Apni Indian English chhodne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Wo aapki hai, aur wo poori tarah theek hai. Bas doosra gear paas rakho — international call, bahar ka interview, videsh ka client. Gear badalna seekh gaye, to aap kahin bhi baat kar sakte ho. Do gear = do taakat. Ek gear chhod kar doosra lena nuksaan hai.

docs.title: 57.10 Practice — Indian English ki aadatein
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Videsh ke interview me apna parichay kaise dein?

  • Hi, I'm Ravi.
  • Myself Ravi.
  • I am Ravi this side.
  • Myself is Ravi.

Hint: Myself subject nahi ban sakta.

Jawaab

Hi, I'm Ravi.

'Myself' reflexive pronoun hai, subject nahi. 'This side' sirf India me chalta hai — phone par bahar 'this is Ravi' bolte hain.

Exercise 2

'I passed out from college in 2019' sunkar bahar ka insaan kya samajhta hai?

  • Aap college me behosh ho gaye the
  • Aapne degree li
  • Aap college chhod aaye
  • Aap exam me fail ho gaye
Jawaab

Aap college me behosh ho gaye the

'Pass out' ka matlab hai behosh ho jaana. Degree lene ke liye 'graduated' bolo.

Exercise 3

In sab me se kaunsi baat sach hai?

  • Indian English ek asli roop hai; dikkat sirf tab hoti hai jab saamne wala use na samjhe
  • Indian English galat English hai
  • Indian English sirf gaon me boli jaati hai
  • Indian English ko poori tarah chhod dena chahiye
Jawaab

Indian English ek asli roop hai; dikkat sirf tab hoti hai jab saamne wala use na samjhe

Sawaal 'galat ya sahi' ka nahi, 'kaunsa kamra' ka hai. Do gear rakho — ek chhod kar doosra lena nuksaan hai.

Exercise 4

'Kindly do the needful and revert back' me sabse badi dikkat kya hai?

  • Saamne wale ko pata hi nahi chalta ki karna kya hai
  • Vaakya bahut chhota hai
  • 'Kindly' bahut rude hai
  • Isme koi verb nahi hai

Hint: Email ka maqsad kya hota hai?

Jawaab

Saamne wale ko pata hi nahi chalta ki karna kya hai

Email ka kaam hai kaam saaf batana. 'Do the needful' wahi jaankari chhupa deta hai. Formula: kaam + kaun + kab tak.

Exercise 5

I'll be out of ___ next week, so let's meet after the 14th.

Hint: Station nahi.

Jawaab

town

'Out of station' India me saaf hai par bahar confusion banata hai. 'Out of town' ya 'away from the office' bolo.

Exercise 6

I have a ___ about the second step — does it run before the backup?

Hint: Doubt matlab shaq hota hai.

Jawaab

question / query

Doubt = shaq. Sawaal poochhne ke liye 'question'. Agar samajh nahi aa raha to 'I'm not clear on…' bolo.

Exercise 7

Could we move the Thursday call ___ to Tuesday?

Hint: Prepone ki jagah kaunsa particle?

Jawaab

up / forward

Pehle laana = move it up / bring it forward. 'Prepone' logical shabd hai par bahar maujood nahi.

Exercise 8

Ek shabd bekaar hai — us par tap karo.

Please revert back to me by Thursday.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: back.

Sahi roop: Please get back to me by Thursday.

Revert, reply aur return — teeno me 'waapas' pehle se hai, isliye 'back' bekaar hai. Aur 'revert' ka matlab bahar purani haalat me jaana hota hai.

Exercise 9

Ek shabd hata dena chahiye — use dhoondo.

Let us discuss about the budget tomorrow.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: about.

Sahi roop: Let's discuss the budget tomorrow.

Discuss ke andar hi 'about' shaamil hai. Isi family me: enter the room, reach Delhi, order two teas, consider my request.

Exercise 10

Ek shabd ajeeb lagta hai — us par tap karo.

He is my cousin brother from Indore.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: brother.

Sahi roop: He's my cousin from Indore.

English me 'cousin' me ladka-ladki ka farq nahi hota, isliye brother jodna ajeeb lagta hai. Zaroori ho to: 'my cousin — my uncle's son'.

Exercise 11

Aadat ko uske international roop se jodo.

A B Myself Ravi exactly the same I have a doubt right now same to same I'm Ravi now itself I have a question Jawaab

Myself Ravi — I'm Ravi; I have a doubt — I have a question; same to same — exactly the same; now itself — right now

Chaaron India me poori tarah saaf hain — bas bahar ke kaan ke liye doosra roop chahiye.

Exercise 12

Phrase ko uski dikkat se jodo.

A B prepone kaunsa station, saaf nahi hota pass out from college 'back' bekaar hai out of station ye shabd bahar maujood nahi hai revert back matlab behosh hona ban jaata hai Jawaab

prepone — ye shabd bahar maujood nahi hai; pass out from college — matlab behosh hona ban jaata hai; out of station — kaunsa station, saaf nahi hota; revert back — 'back' bekaar hai

Har aadat ki dikkat alag hai — kahin shabd hi nahi hai, kahin matlab badal jaata hai, kahin ek shabd bekaar hai.

Exercise 13

Email ki ek saaf line banao — kaam, kaun aur kab tak.

Shabd: approve / by / the / release / payment / you / so / we / can / invoice / Could / Friday

Jawaab

Could you approve the invoice by Friday so we can release payment

Yahi formula hai: kya karna hai, kisko, kab tak. Isme 'kindly', 'needful' aur 'at the earliest' ki zaroorat hi nahi padti.

Exercise 14

Apna parichay bol kar dekho. Shuru me 'I'm' ek hi aawaz me nikalna chahiye.

Jawaab

Bolo: Hi I am Ravi and I graduated in 2019

Interview ki pehli do line hi sabse zyada yaad rehti hain. 'I'm' aur 'graduated' — dono yahan hain, aur dono safe hain.

Aage kya karein

Apni pichhli paanch bheji hui emails kholo aur sirf teen shabd dhoondo: kindly, revert, needful. Jahan milein, wahan seedha likho ki kya karna hai aur kab tak. Ek baar me aapki likhit English do kadam aage chali jaayegi — aur wo bhi bina kuch "seekhe".

docs.title: Chapter 14: Interjection — bhaav wale shabd
docs.text:
Interjection wo shabd hai jo achaanak koi bhaav bahar nikaal deta hai — khushi, dard, hairani, afsos. Ye vaakya ka hissa nahi hota; baaki vaakya se alag khada rehta hai, aur hata do to vaakya ka matlab bilkul nahi badalta — sirf uski aawaz chali jaati hai. Aath parts of speech me ye sabse chhota hissa hai, par bolchaal me sabse zyada kaam aata hai.

Ek line me

An interjection is a word or short phrase that expresses sudden feeling and stands apart from the rest of the sentence. Hindi me "arre, waah, haaye, achha, ohho" — bilkul wahi kaam.

  • Wow! That was a brilliant catch. Waah! Kya shaandaar catch thi.
  • Ouch! That hurt. Aah! Dard hua. (Hindi me hum "ssss" ya "aai" bolte hain.)
  • Oh, I forgot my wallet at home. Halka bhaav hai, isliye comma — exclamation mark nahi.

docs.title: 14.1 Interjection vaakya me kahan baithta hai
docs.text:
Interjection ka baaki vaakya se koi grammar ka rishta nahi hota. Wo na subject hai, na verb, na object. Isliye use hata do, vaakya tootta nahi.

Figure 14.1. Interjection vaakya ke bahar khada hota hai, aur bhaav ki teevrata punctuation tay karti hai.

Interjection ki paanch pehchaan (Features)

1. Strong / sudden emotion — achaanak, tez bhaav batata hai: khushi, dard, dar, hairani. 2. Stands apart — baaki vaakya se alag khada rehta hai, aksar shuru me. 3. Usually "!" — aksar iske baad exclamation mark lagta hai (halka bhaav ho to comma). 4. No grammatical link — subject, verb ya object se koi grammar ka rishta nahi; hata do, vaakya theek rehta hai. 5. Same word, different feelings — ek hi shabd alag mauke par alag bhaav deta hai.

  • Oh! What a lovely surprise. "Oh" = hairani / khushi (Surprise).
  • Oh! My knee hurts. Wahi "Oh" = dard (Pain).
  • Oh! I am so sorry to hear that. Wahi "Oh" = afsos (Sorrow). Bhaav shabd se nahi, mauke aur aawaz se pata chalta hai.

docs.title: 14.2 Prakaar — bhaav ke hisaab se
docs.text:
School ki kitaabon me interjection ke das (10) prakaar padhaaye jaate hain. Har prakaar ka English naam bhi saath me hai, taaki textbook se seedha milaan ho sake.

Type (bhaav) Typical shabd Example Hindi me 1. Joy (khushi) Hurrah! Hurray! Yippee! Hurray! We won the match. Waah! Jeet gaye! 2. Sorrow (dukh / afsos) Alas! Oh! Ah! Alas! He could not make it. Haaye! Afsos! 3. Surprise (hairani) Oh! Wow! What! Ah! What! You passed already? Arre! Sach me? 4. Pain (dard) Ouch! Ah! Oh! Ouch! The tea is hot. Aai! Ssss! 5. Approval / Appreciation (taareef) Bravo! Well done! Excellent! Bravo! What a performance. Shabaash! Kya baat hai! 6. Anger / Irritation (gussa, jhunjhalahat) Pooh! Bah! Bah! Another traffic jam. Uff! Hadd hai! 7. Greeting (abhivaadan) Hello! Hi! Hey! Hello! How are you? Namaste! Kaise ho? 8. Attention (dhyan khinchna) Hey! Look! Listen! Look! The train is coming. Arre! Dekho! 9. Calling (bulaana) O! Ho! Hey! Hey, Ravi! Come here. Aye Ravi! Idhar aao. 10. Fear (dar) Help! Oh! Ah! Help! There is a snake! Bachao!
  • Yippee! School is closed tomorrow. Joy — bachchon wali uchhalti khushi.
  • Well done! You topped the class. Approval — do shabd, par kaam ek interjection ka.
  • O God, please help us! Calling — "O" aaj prarthana aur kavita me hi bacha hai; hamesha capital, aur turant naam ke saath.

'Damn!' — gusse ka shabd, par rude

Filmon me "Damn!" bahut sunai deta hai, par ye rude / asabhya maana jaata hai. Class, office, bade logon ke saamne kabhi mat bolo. Jhunjhalahat batani ho to "Oh no!", "Ugh!" ya "Come on!" kaafi hai.

docs.title: Bolchaal ke aur bhi bhaav
docs.text: Bhaav Shabd Example Hindi me Sehmati Yes! Sure! Indeed! Right! Indeed, that was clever. Bilkul! Sahi! Nafrat / ghin Ugh! Yuck! Eww! Yuck! This milk has gone bad. Chhee! Thoo! Rukna / sochna Well… Um… Hmm… Er… Hmm, let me check. Hmm… Achha… Galti Oops! Whoops! My bad! Oops! I sent the wrong file. Oho! Galti ho gayi. Rahat Phew! Thank goodness! Phew! That was close. Uff! Bach gaye.

docs.title: Common interjections aur unka use
docs.text: Interjection Kab bolte hain Example Oh! hairani, dard, afsos — teeno Oh! I didn't know that. Ah! samajh aana, sukoon, halka dard Ah, now I understand. Wow! hairani + taareef Wow! What a view. Ouch! achaanak apna dard Ouch! I cut my finger. Hurray! jeet ki khushi Hurray! We are on holiday. Bravo! kisi ke kaam ki taareef Bravo! Great speech. Hello! / Hi! milna, phone uthaana Hi! Good to see you. Hey! dhyan khinchna, bulaana (barabar walon ko) Hey! Wait for me. Help! dar, musibat Help! I can't swim. Oops! chhoti galti Oops! I dropped it. Phew! rahat Phew! We made it. Alas! gehra dukh (kitaabi) Alas! The king was dead.

docs.title: 14.3 Punctuation — teen pakke rule
docs.text:
Kahan comma, kahan exclamation mark

1. Tez bhaav → exclamation mark, aur agla shabd capital se: Wow! That is amazing. 2. Halka bhaav → comma, aur agla shabd small se: Oh, it's you. 3. Beech me aaye to dono taraf comma: The result, alas, was disappointing.

Ek hi shabd, do punctuation — matlab badal jaata hai

Oh! You came. — hairani, lagta hai umeed nahi thi. Oh, you came. — halki pehchaan, lagta hai pata tha. Punctuation yahan bhaav ka volume control hai.

Exclamation mark ek se zyada nahi

Chat me "Wow!!!" chalta hai. Email, exam ya kisi bhi likhe kaam me ek hi exclamation mark lagao. Teen lagane se baat zyada nahi, kam gambhir lagti hai.

docs.title: 14.4 Interjection ya kuch aur — ek shabd ke do kaam
docs.text:
Kai shabd interjection ke roop me bhi aate hain aur normal part of speech ke roop me bhi. Faisla ye dekh kar hota hai ki wo vaakya ke andar hai ya bahar.

Shabd Interjection ke roop me Normal roop me well Well, I am not sure. She sings well. (adverb) what What! You are leaving? What is your name? (pronoun) right Right, let's begin. Your answer is right. (adjective) indeed Indeed! I never expected that. It was indeed difficult. (adverb) my My! How you have grown. This is my bag. (possessive)

Pehchaanne ka test

Shabd hata ke baaki vaakya padho. Agar vaakya poora aur theek hai → wo interjection tha. Agar vaakya adhoora ho gaya → wo vaakya ka hissa tha. "Well, I am not sure" → "I am not sure" poora hai. ✓ interjection. "She sings well" → "She sings" ka matlab badal gaya. ✗ interjection nahi.

docs.title: 14.5 Hindi se English — asli bolchaal ke jode
docs.text:
Hum log Hindi interjections ko seedha English me le jaate hain — "Arre, where were you?" Ye samajh aa jaata hai par English nahi lagta. Neeche kaam ke jode hain:

Hum bolte hain English me Kab Arre! Hey! / Oh! / Come on! dhyan khinchna ya halki hairani Achha? Really? / Is that so? nayi baat sunkar Achha, theek hai Right. / Okay then. baat maan lena Waah! Wow! / Brilliant! taareef Haaye! Oh no! / Alas! (purana) dukh Uff / Chalo bach gaye Phew! rahat Chhee! Yuck! / Ugh! ghin Hmm… dekhte hain Well… let me see. sochte waqt Oho, galti ho gayi Oops! My bad. chhoti galti Arre nahi! Oh no! / No way! buri khabar sunkar

'Alas', 'Hurrah', 'Pooh' ka sach — purane shabd

School ki kitaabon me Alas!, Hurrah! aur Pooh! bahut aate hain, par aaj ki bolchaal me ye lagbhag nahi bole jaate — old-fashioned aur naatakiya lagte hain. Exam aur kahani me likhna theek hai; baat-cheet me neeche wale aaj ke shabd bolo.

Purana (kitaabi) Aaj bolo Bhaav Alas! Oh no! / That's so sad. dukh Hurrah! Yay! / Yes! / Woo-hoo! khushi Pooh! / Bah! Ugh! / Come on! / Seriously? jhunjhalahat O! / Ho! Hey! / Excuse me! bulaana

docs.title: 14.6 Office aur formal jagah — kahan rukna hai
docs.text:
Jagah Chalta hai Nahi chalta Dost ke saath chat Wow! Oops! Yay! Ugh! — Office email Well, Right, Indeed (comma ke saath) Yay! Yuck! Oops! Interview Well, … (sochne ka waqt lene ke liye) Hmm… bahut baar Exam ki writing kahani / dialogue me essay ya report me

Interview ki ek kaam ki baat

Sawaal sunkar turant bolne ki jagah "Well, that's an interesting question…" bolna bilkul theek hai — isse do second sochne ka waqt mil jaata hai aur aap taiyaar lagte hain. Par ek hi interview me teen baar ye na bolein.

docs.title: 14.7 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Interjection ke saath hone wali galtiyan

  • Galat: Myself Ravi. Wow, nice to meet you!
  • Sahi: Hello! I am Ravi. Nice to meet you.

  • Kyun: Do baatein: "Myself Ravi" galat hai — subject ke liye "I" chahiye. Aur milte waqt "Wow" ajeeb lagta hai; wo taareef ke liye hai. Greeting me "Hello" ya "Hi" bolo.

  • Galat: Oh! i forgot to call her.

  • Sahi: Oh! I forgot to call her.

  • Kyun: Exclamation mark ke baad naya vaakya shuru hota hai, isliye agla shabd capital se. Comma lagate to small letter chalta: Oh, I forgot…

  • Galat: Dear Sir, Wow!!! Thank you for the offer.

  • Sahi: Dear Sir, Thank you very much for the offer.

  • Kyun: Formal email me interjection aur teen exclamation mark dono bhaari padte hain. Khushi batani ho to shabdon se batao: I am delighted to accept.

  • Galat: Alas the news was bad.

  • Sahi: Alas, the news was bad.

  • Kyun: Interjection ke baad punctuation zaroori hai — comma ya exclamation mark. Bina kuch lagaye wo vaakya me ghul jaata hai aur padhne me atakta hai.

  • Galat: Ouch, she don't know the answer.

  • Sahi: Oh no, she doesn't know the answer.

  • Kyun: "Ouch" sirf apne dard ke liye hai, kisi aur ki musibat ke liye nahi — uske liye "Oh no". Aur "she" ke saath "doesn't" lagta hai, "don't" nahi.

  • Galat: Hey! Sir, can you discuss about my marks?

  • Sahi: Excuse me, Sir, could we discuss my marks?

  • Kyun: "Hey!" barabar walon ke liye hai; kisi bade ya teacher ke liye "Excuse me" bolo. Aur "discuss" ke baad "about" nahi lagta.

  • Galat: Yuck! This is my cousin brother's cooking.

  • Sahi: Hmm, this is my cousin's cooking — not my favourite.
  • Kyun: "Yuck" kaafi kathor hai, kisi ke saamne uske khane par bolna rukhaai hai. Aur "cousin" apne aap me poora shabd hai — brother jodne ki zaroorat nahi.

docs.title: 14.8 Chhota naksha
docs.text:
Chaar cheezein yaad rakho

1. Interjection vaakya ke bahar hota hai — hata do, vaakya tootta nahi. 2. Tez bhaav → ! aur agla shabd capital. Halka bhaav → , aur agla shabd small. 3. Formal likhne me na use karo — wahan shabdon se bhaav batao. 4. Ek exclamation mark kaafi hai.

docs.title: 14.9 Practice — Interjections
docs.text:
Exercise 1

___! We finally won the trophy.

  • Hurray
  • Alas
  • Ouch
  • Yuck

Hint: Khushi ka bhaav chahiye.

Jawaab

Hurray

Jeet par khushi hai, aur khushi ke liye Hurray / Yay / Wow aate hain. Alas dukh ke liye, ouch dard ke liye, aur yuck ghin ke liye hai.

Exercise 2

Kaunsa vaakya punctuation ke hisaab se sahi hai?

  • Oh! I forgot my keys.
  • Oh! i forgot my keys.
  • Oh i forgot my keys.
  • Oh. i forgot my keys!

Hint: Exclamation mark ke baad kya hota hai?

Jawaab

Oh! I forgot my keys.

Exclamation mark ke baad naya vaakya shuru hota hai, isliye agla shabd capital se. Comma lagate to small letter chalta — 'Oh, I forgot'.

Exercise 3

'Well, I am not sure about that.' — yahan 'Well' kya hai?

  • interjection
  • adverb
  • adjective
  • conjunction

Hint: Shabd hata ke vaakya padho.

Jawaab

interjection

'Well' hataane ke baad bhi 'I am not sure about that' poora vaakya hai, isliye wo bahar khada tha — interjection. 'She sings well' me hataao to matlab badal jaata, wahan wo adverb hai.

Exercise 4

Office email me kaunsa roop sabse theek hai?

  • I am delighted to accept the offer.
  • Wow!!! Thanks for the offer.
  • Yay! I accept.
  • Oops, I accept.

Hint: Formal jagah me bhaav shabdon se batate hain.

Jawaab

I am delighted to accept the offer.

Formal likhne me interjection aur multiple exclamation marks bhaari lagte hain. Khushi shabdon se batana zyada professional lagta hai.

Exercise 5

___! That water is boiling hot. (dard ka shabd)

Hint: Apne dard par kya bolte hain?

Jawaab

Ouch

Achaanak dard ke liye Ouch / Ow aata hai. Dhyan rakho — ye sirf apne dard ke liye hai; kisi aur ki musibat par 'Oh no' bolte hain.

Exercise 6

___, that was a close call. (rahat ka shabd)

Hint: Bach jaane par ek saans chhodte hain.

Jawaab

Phew

Rahat ke liye 'Phew' aata hai — Hindi ka 'uff' ya 'chalo bach gaye'. Ye saans chhodne ki aawaz se bana hai.

Exercise 7

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — galat shabd par tap karo.

Hey Sir can you discuss about my result?

Jawaab

Galat shabd: about.

Sahi roop: Excuse me, Sir, could we discuss my result?

'Discuss' ke baad 'about' nahi lagta. Aur 'Hey' barabar walon ke liye hai — teacher ya kisi bade ke liye 'Excuse me' bolo.

Exercise 8

Galat shabd dhoondo.

Oh no she don't know about the meeting.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: don't.

Sahi roop: Oh no, she doesn't know about the meeting.

'she' third person singular hai, isliye 'doesn't' lagta hai. Aur interjection ke baad comma bhi chahiye tha.

Exercise 9

Ek galti hai — dhoondo.

Myself Ravi and wow I am happy to be here.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: Myself.

Sahi roop: Hello! I am Ravi, and I am happy to be here.

Reflexive pronoun 'myself' subject nahi ban sakta — 'I am' chahiye. Aur milte waqt 'wow' ajeeb lagta hai; greeting me 'Hello' bolo.

Exercise 10

'Bravo! That was a brilliant speech.' — 'Bravo' kis type ka interjection hai?

  • Approval / Appreciation
  • Joy
  • Surprise
  • Calling

Hint: Kisi ke kaam ki taareef ho rahi hai.

Jawaab

Approval / Appreciation

Bravo!, Well done!, Excellent! — ye kisi ke kaam ki taareef (Approval / Appreciation) ke shabd hain. Apni khushi ke liye Hurray! ya Yippee! (Joy) aata hai.

Exercise 11

___! There is a snake under the bed! (dar ka shabd)

Hint: Musibat me madad maangte hain.

Jawaab

Help

Fear (dar) ke liye 'Help!' sabse saaf interjection hai. 'Oh!' aur 'Ah!' bhi dar me aate hain, par 'Help!' turant musibat bata deta hai.

Exercise 12

Dost ke saath baat-cheet me 'Hurrah!' ki jagah aaj kya bolna zyada natural hai?

  • Yay!
  • Alas!
  • Pooh!
  • Damn!

Hint: Hurrah purana, kitaabi shabd hai.

Jawaab

Yay!

'Hurrah!', 'Alas!', 'Pooh!' aaj old-fashioned lagte hain. Khushi ke liye aaj 'Yay!' ya 'Yes!' bolte hain. 'Damn!' rude hai — use mat karo.

Exercise 13

Interjection ki pehchaan me kaunsi baat GALAT hai?

  • Ye vaakya ka subject banta hai
  • Ye achaanak bhaav batata hai
  • Iske baad aksar '!' lagta hai
  • Ek hi shabd alag bhaav de sakta hai

Hint: Paanch features yaad karo.

Jawaab

Ye vaakya ka subject banta hai

Interjection ka vaakya se koi grammatical rishta nahi hota — na subject, na object. Baaki teeno baatein uske features hain.

Exercise 14

Interjection ko uske bhaav se jodo.

A B Hurray! dard Alas! rahat Ouch! ghin Phew! khushi Yuck! dukh Jawaab

Hurray! — khushi; Alas! — dukh; Ouch! — dard; Phew! — rahat; Yuck! — ghin

Interjection ka chunaav bhaav se hota hai, grammar se nahi. Galat bhaav ka shabd chunne se baat ajeeb lagti hai — jaise taareef me 'Alas' bol dena.

Exercise 15

Sahi kram me vaakya banao — interjection pehle aayega.

Shabd: painting / is / beautiful / this / Wow

Jawaab

Wow this painting is beautiful

Interjection lagbhag hamesha vaakya ke shuru me aata hai, kyunki bhaav pehle nikalta hai aur baat baad me. Likhte waqt uske baad comma ya exclamation mark lagta hai.

Exercise 16

Ye line bol ke dekho — 'Oh no' ko thoda kheench kar bolna hai, jaise sach me afsos ho.

Jawaab

Bolo: Oh no I have missed the train

Interjection ka asar shabd se zyada aawaz se aata hai. Flat bol do to natak lagta hai; bhaav ke saath bolne par natural lagta hai.

Aage kya karein

Interjection ratne ki cheez nahi, sunne ki cheez hai. Koi English show dekhte waqt dhyan do ki log hairani aur rahat me kya bolte hain — aur agle din ek naya shabd try karo. Isi ke saath aath parts of speech poore hue; aage vaakya banane ka hissa shuru hota hai.

docs.title: Chapter 34: Interview aur office
docs.text:
Interview aur office English

Interview me English se zyada dhaancha maayne rakhta hai. Jo log atak jaate hain, unki English kharaab nahi hoti — unke paas jawaab ka saancha nahi hota, isliye wo soch-soch kar bolte hain aur ghabra jaate hain. Is chapter me aapko taiyaar saanche milenge: apna introduction, aam sawaalon ke jawaab, meeting me bolne ki bhasha, aur email ke phrase. Sab bol kar practise karne layak.

Interview ka ek hi asli niyam

Jawaab 30 se 60 second ka ho. Isse chhota = taiyaari nahi lagti. Isse lamba = aap bhatakne lagte hain aur English ulajhne lagti hai. Teen-chaar vaakya. Bas. Phir chup ho jao aur agla sawaal aane do.

docs.title: 34.1 Apna introduction — teen hisson ka saancha
docs.text:
"Tell me about yourself" sabse pehla aur sabse zyada bigadne wala sawaal hai. Log yahan apni poori zindagi suna dete hain — paida kahan hue, kitne bhai-behen. Interviewer ko wo nahi chahiye. Use sirf teen cheezein chahiye: aaj aap kya karte hain → pehle kya kiya → aage kya chahte hain.

Figure 34.1. Yahi saancha har interview me chalta hai — fresher ho ya 10 saal ka anubhav. Sirf andar ka maal badalta hai, dhaancha wahi rehta hai.

Taiyaar introduction — anubhav wale ke liye

  • Thanks for having me. I'm Ravi, and I currently work as a support engineer at a telecom company in Pune. Hissa 1 — abhi. "Thanks for having me" ek sharif shuruaat hai.
  • I've been there for about three years, mostly handling customer issues and billing problems. Hissa 2 — pehle. "for about three years" — "about" se aawaz natural lagti hai.
  • Last year I also trained two new team members, which I really enjoyed. Ek thos example — ye line aapko baaki sabse alag karti hai.
  • Now I'm looking for a role where I can work more directly with clients, and that's why this job caught my eye. Hissa 3 — aage, aur yahan kyun. "caught my eye" = nazar me aaya.

Taiyaar introduction — fresher ke liye

  • Good morning. I'm Priya, and I finished my B.Com from Pune University this year. Fresher ke liye "abhi" ka matlab padhai hai.
  • During my final year I did a three-month internship at a small accounting firm, where I worked on GST filings. Internship, project, part-time kaam — jo bhi ho, ek thos cheez batao.
  • I'm comfortable with Excel and I'm learning Tally at the moment. "I'm comfortable with…" — "I know" se behtar aur imaandaar lagta hai.
  • I'm looking for my first full-time role, and I'd like to start in a team where I can learn quickly. Fresher ke liye "seekhna" sabse imaandaar aur sabse achcha jawaab hai.

Introduction ki paanch galtiyan

  • Galat: Myself Ravi Kumar.
  • Sahi: I'm Ravi Kumar.

  • Kyun: "Myself" ek pronoun hai, vaakya nahi. Ye sabse jaldi pakdi jaane wali galti hai.

  • Galat: I am belonging to Jaipur.

  • Sahi: I'm from Jaipur.

  • Kyun: "Belong" me -ing nahi lagti. Aur "I'm from…" chhota aur natural hai.

  • Galat: I have did my graduation in 2021.

  • Sahi: I graduated in 2021.

  • Kyun: "Graduation" ek event hai, "graduate" verb hai. Seedha verb use karo.

  • Galat: I am having 4 years experience.

  • Sahi: I have four years of experience.

  • Kyun: "have", na ki "am having". Aur beech me "of" lagta hai.

  • Galat: My father is a businessman and I have two sisters…

  • Sahi: Introduction me parivaar ki baat bilkul nahi.
  • Kyun: Interviewer ko aapke kaam ka introduction chahiye, zindagi ka nahi. Poochhein to batana.

docs.title: 34.2 Aam interview sawaal — taiyaar jawaab
docs.text:
Kahani ka saancha — har 'example wale' sawaal ke liye

Haalat → aapka kaam → jo aapne kiya → natija. Chaar vaakya, usi kram me. Jab bhi poochha jaaye "tell me about a time when…", bas is saanche me bhar do. Natija bhoolna nahi — wahi jawaab ko poora karta hai.

Sawaal Taiyaar jawaab Suno Why do you want to leave your current job? I've learnt a lot where I am, but the work has become quite repetitive. I'm looking for something with more responsibility. What are your strengths? I'm patient with people, which helps a lot in support work. I also stay calm when things go wrong. What is your weakness? I used to take on too much and then struggle with deadlines. I've started saying no more often, and planning my week on Monday. Why should we hire you? You need someone who can handle angry customers without losing patience. That's exactly what I've been doing for three years. Where do you see yourself in five years? I'd like to be leading a small team by then. For now my focus is on getting really good at the work itself. Tell me about a difficult situation at work. Last Diwali two people were on leave and our tickets doubled. I rearranged the queue by urgency and asked a colleague to help with calls. We cleared everything in two days. What are your salary expectations? Based on my experience and the market, I'm looking at somewhere between eight and ten lakhs. But I'm open to discussing it. Do you have any questions for us? Yes — could you tell me what a typical week looks like in this role? And how is the team structured?

'Weakness' ka jaal

"I have no weakness" ya "I am a perfectionist" — dono jawaab har interviewer ne hazaar baar sune hain, aur dono se lagta hai aapne sach nahi bola. Sahi saancha: ek asli kami + usse theek karne ke liye jo aap kar rahe hain. Yahi imaandaar aur samajhdaar dono lagta hai.

Aakhir me sawaal poochhna zaroori hai

"Do you have any questions?" ka jawaab kabhi "No" nahi hona chahiye — isse lagta hai aapko dilchaspi nahi. Do sawaal pehle se taiyaar rakho: What does a typical week look like in this role? What would you want me to achieve in the first three months?

docs.title: 34.3 Interview me atak gaye to
docs.text:
Ye hoga — har kisi ke saath hota hai. Ghabraane ki zaroorat nahi, bas taiyaar line nikal jaaye.

Haalat Line Suno Sawaal samajh nahi aaya Sorry, could you rephrase that? Thoda waqt chahiye That's a good question. Let me think for a second. Jawaab nahi aata I haven't worked on that, but I'd be happy to learn it. Vaakya ulajh gaya Sorry, let me start that again. Sahi samjha ya nahi, confirm karna Just to make sure I understood — you're asking about…? Interview khatam Thank you for your time. I enjoyed talking to you.

'Nahi aata' kehna nuksaan nahi karta

Jhoot bolne se bahut zyada nuksaan hota hai. "I haven't worked on that, but I'd be happy to learn it" ek pakka, professional jawaab hai — aur zyadatar interviewer ise pasand karte hain.

docs.title: 34.4 Office aur meeting ki bhasha
docs.text:
Kaam Line Suno Meeting me bolna shuru Can I add something here? Sorry to interrupt, but I think there's an issue with the timeline. If I could just jump in for a second… Sehmat / asehmat That makes sense to me. I see your point, but I'd do it slightly differently. I'm not sure that will work. Can I explain why? Samay aur kaam I'll have it ready by Thursday. I'm a bit stretched this week — could we push it to Monday? Let me check and get back to you in an hour. Madad aur saaf karna Could you walk me through it once? Just to confirm — you want the report before the call, right? I'll need a bit of help with this part. Galti aur maafi That was my mistake. I'll fix it today. Sorry for the delay — I got held up in another call. Let me look into it and come back with an answer. Meeting khatam karna So, to sum up — I'll send the draft and you'll review it by Friday. Shall we take this offline and discuss it after?

Poora mini-dialogue — team meeting

  • Manager: So, where are we on the client report? "Where are we on…" = us kaam ka kya haal hai?
  • Aap: I've finished the first half. The numbers for March are still pending from finance. Pehle jo ho gaya, phir jo ruka hai — aur kiske paas ruka hai.
  • Manager: Can you have it done by Thursday? Guruwaar tak ho jaayega?
  • Aap: If I get the numbers by tomorrow, yes. Otherwise Friday would be safer. Shart ke saath haan kehna — "Friday would be safer" bahut professional hai.
  • Manager: Fair enough. I'll chase finance today. "Fair enough" = theek hai, baat sahi hai. "Chase" = peeche padna.
  • Aap: Thanks. Just to confirm — you want the full report, not just the summary? "Just to confirm" aapko dhyan rakhne wala dikhata hai. Ye line roz kaam aati hai.

docs.title: 34.5 Email ke taiyaar phrase
docs.text:
Kaam Phrase Shuruaat (jaan-pehchaan) Hi Anita,Hope you're doing well. Shuruaat (official) Dear Mr Sharma,I hope this email finds you well. Kaaran batana I'm writing to ask about… / I'm following up on my last email. Kuch bhej rahe hain Please find the report attached. / I've attached the file below. Kuch maangna Could you please share the figures for March? / Would you be able to review this by Friday? Yaad dilana (narmi se) Just a gentle reminder about the pending approval. Deri ki maafi Apologies for the delay in replying. Kaam ki pushti Noted, I'll take care of it. / Thanks, that's clear now. Samay maangna Would it be possible to extend the deadline to Monday? Ant (jaan-pehchaan) Thanks,Ravi Ant (official) Best regards,Ravi Kumar

Email ki wo lines jo hata deni chahiye

  • Galat: Please do the needful and revert back at the earliest.
  • Sahi: Could you review this and let me know by Friday?

  • Kyun: Teen dikkat: "do the needful" se pata nahi chalta karna kya hai; "revert" ka matlab wapas lautna hota hai, jawaab dena nahi; "at the earliest" ki jagah asli tareekh do.

  • Galat: Respected Sir, I beg to state that…

  • Sahi: Dear Mr Sharma, I'm writing to…

  • Kyun: Ye bahut purani, school ki chitthi wali bhasha hai. Aaj ke office me ajeeb lagti hai.

  • Galat: Kindly intimate me the same.

  • Sahi: Please let me know.

  • Kyun: "Intimate" aur "the same" dafter ki purani bhasha hai. Chhote shabd zyada professional lagte hain.

  • Galat: Thanking you in advance for the same.

  • Sahi: Thanks in advance. / Thanks for your help.
  • Kyun: "For the same" kaatna hi hai. Email me chhoti lines sabse achchi lagti hain.

docs.title: 34.6 Interview se pehle ki aakhri taiyaari
docs.text:
Ek din pehle — paanch kaam

1. Apna 45-second introduction zor se 10 baar bolo. Aaine ke saamne. 2. Teen sawaalon ke jawaab taiyaar karo: kyun chhod rahe ho, kamzori, aur ek mushkil haalat. 3. Do sawaal taiyaar karo jo aap poochhoge. 4. Phone par apna introduction record karo aur sun lo — jo ulajha lage, use chhota karo. 5. Interview ke din rozmarra se bhi dheere bolo. Ghabraahat me tezi aati hai, aur tezi me English ulajhti hai.

docs.title: 34.7 Practice — Interview aur office
docs.text:
Exercise 1

'Tell me about yourself' ka sahi dhaancha kya hai?

  • Abhi kya karte hain → pehle kya kiya → aage kya chahte hain
  • Paida kahan hue → padhai → parivaar
  • Parivaar → hobby → naukri
  • Sirf apni degree aur marks

Hint: Teen hisse, teen waqt.

Jawaab

Abhi kya karte hain → pehle kya kiya → aage kya chahte hain

Teen hisse, lagbhag 15 second har ek. Parivaar aur gaon tab batana jab poochha jaaye.

Exercise 2

Interview ka jawaab kitna lamba hona chahiye?

  • 30 se 60 second
  • 5 se 10 second
  • 3 se 4 minute
  • Jitna lamba ho sake
Jawaab

30 se 60 second

Chhota jawaab taiyaari ki kami dikhata hai; lamba jawaab me aap bhatakne lagte hain aur English ulajhti hai.

Exercise 3

'What is your weakness?' ka sahi saancha?

  • Ek asli kami + usse theek karne ki koshish
  • I have no weakness
  • I am a perfectionist
  • Ek kami jo asal me taarif ho
Jawaab

Ek asli kami + usse theek karne ki koshish

Imaandaari + samajhdaari. 'No weakness' aur 'perfectionist' har interviewer hazaar baar sun chuka hai.

Exercise 4

Koi technical cheez poochhi gayi jo aapko nahi aati. Kya karein?

  • I haven't worked on that, but I'd be happy to learn it
  • Jhoot bol do ki aati hai
  • Chup ho jao
  • Baat badal do
Jawaab

I haven't worked on that, but I'd be happy to learn it

Jhoot aage jaa kar pakda jaata hai. Imaandaar jawaab zyadatar interviewer ko pasand aata hai.

Exercise 5

'Do you have any questions for us?' ka sabse kharaab jawaab?

  • No, everything is clear
  • Ek sawaal role ke baare me
  • Ek sawaal team ke baare me
  • Pehle teen mahine ke lakshya ke baare me
Jawaab

No, everything is clear

'No' se lagta hai aapko dilchaspi nahi. Do sawaal pehle se taiyaar rakho.

Exercise 6

'Tell me about a difficult situation' ka saancha?

  • Haalat → aapka kaam → jo kiya → natija
  • Sirf natija
  • Kis par ilzaam tha wo batana
  • Haalat → kis ki galti thi

Hint: Chaar hisse.

Jawaab

Haalat → aapka kaam → jo kiya → natija

Chaar vaakya usi kram me. Natija bataana bhoolo nahi — wahi jawaab poora karta hai.

Exercise 7

Theek karo: I have ___ years of experience. (chaar saal)

Hint: Sankhya shabdon me, aur 'am having' nahi.

Jawaab

four / 4

'I have four years of experience' — 'am having' galat hai, aur beech me 'of' lagta hai.

Exercise 8

Meeting me pushti karna: ___ to confirm — you want the full report?

Hint: Do shabd ka shuruaati phrase, 'J' se.

Jawaab

Just / just

'Just to confirm…' office me roz kaam aane wali line hai — aapko dhyan rakhne wala dikhati hai.

Exercise 9

Email: Please find the report ___.

Hint: File saath bheji hai.

Jawaab

attached

'Please find the report attached' ya 'I've attached the report'. Dono theek.

Exercise 10

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — us shabd par tap karo.

Myself Ravi Kumar from Jaipur.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: Myself.

Sahi roop: I'm Ravi Kumar, from Jaipur.

'Myself' pronoun hai, vaakya shuru karne wala shabd nahi. Interview me ye sabse jaldi pakdi jaati hai.

Exercise 11

Galat shabd dhoondo.

I am belonging to a small town near Nashik.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: belonging.

Sahi roop: I'm from a small town near Nashik.

'Belong' me -ing nahi lagti. Aur 'I'm from…' chhota aur natural hai.

Exercise 12

Email me jo shabd hata dena chahiye, us par tap karo.

Please review this and revert at the earliest.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: revert.

Sahi roop: Please review this and let me know by Friday.

'Revert' ka matlab wapas purani haalat me jaana hai, jawaab dena nahi. Aur 'at the earliest' ki jagah asli tareekh do.

Exercise 13

Office ki haalat ko uski line se jodo.

A B Meeting me bolna shuru I'm a bit stretched this week. Asehmat, par sharifi se That was my mistake. I'll fix it today. Zyada kaam hai Can I add something here? Galti maanna I see your point, but I'd do it differently. Jawaab

Meeting me bolna shuru — Can I add something here?; Asehmat, par sharifi se — I see your point, but I'd do it differently.; Zyada kaam hai — I'm a bit stretched this week.; Galti maanna — That was my mistake. I'll fix it today.

Har haalat ki ek taiyaar line. Meeting me sochne ka waqt nahi hota — isi liye ratna kaam aata hai.

Exercise 14

Interview ki shuruaati line banao.

Shabd: for / Thanks / having / me

Jawaab

Thanks for having me

Chhoti, sharif shuruaat. Iske baad seedha hissa 1 — abhi aap kya karte hain.

Exercise 15

Introduction, hissa 1 — abhi aap kya karte hain.

Jawaab

Bolo: I currently work as a support engineer at a telecom company

'currently' se saaf hota hai ki ye aaj ki baat hai. Dheere bolo — ye pehla impression hai.

Exercise 16

Introduction, hissa 2 — anubhav.

Jawaab

Bolo: I've been there for about three years, mostly handling customer issues

'for about three years' — 'about' se aawaz natural lagti hai, ratt hui nahi.

Exercise 17

Introduction, hissa 3 — aage kya chahte hain.

Jawaab

Bolo: Now I'm looking for a role where I can work more directly with clients

Yahi hissa batata hai ki aap yahan kyun baithe hain. Ise chhodna sabse badi galti hai.

Exercise 18

Apni taqat batao — bina bade-bade shabdon ke.

Jawaab

Bolo: I'm patient with people and I stay calm when things go wrong

Thos aur sach lagta hai. 'I am a hard worker' se bahut behtar.

Exercise 19

Naukri chhodne ki wajah — bina purani company ko bura kehne.

Jawaab

Bolo: I've learnt a lot where I am but I'm looking for more responsibility

Purani jagah ki buraai bilkul nahi karni. Aage ki baat karo, peeche ki nahi.

Exercise 20

Sawaal samajh nahi aaya. Politely poochho.

Jawaab

Bolo: Sorry, could you rephrase that

'Rephrase' = dobara dusre shabdon me kahiye. Interview me ye bilkul theek hai.

Exercise 21

Technical sawaal jo nahi aata. Imaandaar jawaab do.

Jawaab

Bolo: I haven't worked on that but I'd be happy to learn it

Saaf, professional aur sach. Jhoot se bahut behtar.

Exercise 22

Aakhir me aap jo sawaal poochhenge.

Jawaab

Bolo: What does a typical week look like in this role

Ye sawaal aapko gambhir dikhata hai, aur aapko asli jaankari bhi deta hai.

Exercise 23

Interview khatam. Vidaai ki line.

Jawaab

Bolo: Thank you for your time. I enjoyed talking to you

Chhota, garmjoshi se. Aakhri impression bhi yaad rehta hai.

Exercise 24

Meeting me shart ke saath haan kehna.

Jawaab

Bolo: If I get the numbers by tomorrow yes. Otherwise Friday would be safer

Jhoothi haan se behtar hai shart ke saath haan. 'Would be safer' bahut professional lagta hai.

Exercise 25

Office me zyada kaam hai. Samay maango.

Jawaab

Bolo: I'm a bit stretched this week. Could we push it to Monday

'A bit stretched' = thoda dabaav me hoon. 'Push it to' = aage badhana.

Exercise 26

Galti maano — bina safai dene.

Jawaab

Bolo: That was my mistake. I'll fix it today

Do chhote vaakye: galti maani, aur ilaaj bataya. Lambi safai se bahut behtar.

Aage kya karein

Apna 45-second introduction aaj likho — paanch vaakya se zyada nahi — aur phone par record kar ke sun lo. Jo vaakya bolte waqt ulajha, use chhota karo. Phir 10 baar bolo. Interview se pehle sabse zyada faayda do chapters se hoga: Fluency aur filler words (atakne ka ilaaj) aur Indian English ki aadatein (jo galtiyan turant pakdi jaati hain).

docs.title: Chapter 16: can, could, should, must
docs.text:
Modals — kar sakna, karna chahiye, karna padega

Hindi me hum verb ke saath "sakna", "chahiye", "padega", "shayad" jod kar apna mood batate hain. English me ye kaam chhote helping verbs karte hain jinhe modals kehte hain. Ye roz ki baatcheet ki jaan hain — vinamrata se kuch maangna ho, salaah deni ho, ya andaaza lagana ho, modal ke bina kaam nahi chalta.

Ek line me

A modal verb is a helping verb that adds ability, permission, advice, obligation or possibility to the main verb. Main verb kaam batata hai; modal batata hai ki kaam ke baare me hum kya soch rahe hain.

  • I can swim. Main tair sakta hoon. — kshamta
  • You should drink more water. Tumhe zyada paani peena chahiye. — salaah
  • It might rain in the evening. Shaam ko shayad baarish ho. — sambhavna

docs.title: 16.1 Modal kaise kaam karta hai — teen pakke niyam
docs.text:
Achhi baat ye hai ki saare modals ek hi tarah se chalte hain. Ye teen niyam ek baar pakke ho gaye, to aadhi galtiyan apne aap band ho jaayengi — chahe modal koi bhi ho.

Figure 16.1. Modal khud negative aur question bana leta hai — do ko bulaane ki zaroorat nahi.

Modal ke teen niyam

1. Modal ke baad verb ka pehla roop (V1) — bina -s, bina -ing, bina "to". 2. Modal khud nahi badalta — "cans" ya "musted" nahi hota. 3. Negative aur sawaal modal khud banata hai: can't go, Can you go?

Teen modal 'to' ke saath aate hain

ought to, have to, used to — inme "to" unka hissa hai: You ought to apologise. Baaki kisi modal ke baad "to" nahi: You must to go.

docs.title: 16.2 Ability — can, could, be able to
docs.text:
"Main ye kar sakta hoon" — ye roz ki baat hai: naukri ke interview me, form bharte waqt, dosto ke saath. Time badalne par sahi shabd chunna zaroori hai.

Samay Shabd Example Abhi (present) can She can speak Tamil. Pehle, aam taur par could I could run fast when I was young. Pehle, ek khaas mauke par was / were able to We were able to catch the last bus. Aage (future) will be able to You will be able to drive in a month. Perfect tense me have been able to I haven't been able to sleep.

Kshamta (ability)

Abhi ke liye can, beete samay ke liye could. Jahan "can" fit nahi hota — future, perfect, ya doosre modal ke baad — wahan be able to lagao: will be able to.

Do modal ek saath nahi

You will can come. ✗ → You will be able to come. ✓ Ek vaakya me ek hi modal. Doosri zaroorat ho to "be able to" ya "have to" jaisa roop lo.

docs.title: 16.3 Permission aur Request — kitni vinamrata chahiye?
docs.text:
Kuch maangte waqt shabd ka chunaav batata hai ki aap saamne wale ki kitni izzat kar rahe ho. Dost se "Can I…?" theek hai, par boss ya anjaan se "Could you…?" zyada achha lagta hai.

Figure 16.2. Seedhi jitni upar, baat utni vinamra. Office aur anjaan logon ke saath beech ki seedhiyan sabse surakshit hain.

Anumati aur request

Permission: Can I (casual) → Could I → May I (formal). Request: Can you → Could you → Would you mind + -ing. "May" sirf apne liye permission maangne me — "May you…?" nahi hota.

  • Could you send me the file by evening? Kya aap shaam tak file bhej sakte hain? — office me perfect.
  • Would you mind closing the window? Agar bura na lage to khidki band kar denge? — jawaab "No, not at all" matlab "haan, kar deta hoon".

docs.title: 16.4 Advice aur Obligation — should, must, have to
docs.text:
"Karna chahiye" aur "karna padega" me bada farq hai — ek salaah hai, doosra majboori. English me bhi ye farq saaf hai, aur galat shabd chunne se aapki baat ya to bahut kadak lagti hai ya bahut halki.

Figure 16.3. Upar: zaroorat badhti jaati hai. Neeche: negative me must aur have to ka matlab bilkul alag ho jaata hai.

Salaah aur majboori

should / ought to = salaah. have to = niyam ya halaat ki majboori. must = pakki zaroorat. Dhyan: mustn't = mana hai, par don't have to = zaroori nahi.

  • You should see a doctor. Doctor ko dikhana chahiye — salaah hai, faisla aapka.
  • I have to wear a uniform at work. Company ka niyam hai — majboori bahar se aayi.
  • Past me: I had to wait for two hours. "must" ka past nahi hota — "had to" lagao.

docs.title: 16.5 Possibility — might se must tak, kitna yakeen?
docs.text:
Andaaza lagate waqt modal batata hai ki aapko kitna yakeen hai. "Wo shayad ghar par ho" aur "wo pakka ghar par hoga" — dono ke liye alag modal hai. Isse aapki English sochi-samjhi lagti hai.

Figure 16.4. Baayein se daayein yakeen badhta hai. can't aur must dono pakke andaaze hain — ek nahi ka, ek haan ka.

Yakeen ka meter

might / could (shayad) → may (ho sakta hai) → should (hona chahiye) → must (pakka hoga). Ulta pakka andaaza: can't — He can't be at home; I just saw him at the station.

Andaaze wale 'must' ka ulta 'mustn't' nahi

She must be at work. (pakka hai ki office me hai) → ulta: She can't be at work. "She mustn't be at work" ka matlab ho jaayega — use office me hona mana hai!

docs.title: 16.6 will, would, shall, need, used to
docs.text:
Ye paanch modal (ya modal jaise shabd) roz aate hain, par har ek ka apna khaas kaam hai. Ek jagah dekh lo, to alag-alag yaad rakhne ki zaroorat nahi.

Shabd Kaam Example will future, vaada, turant faisla I will call you tonight. would vinamra iccha, kalpana I would like a cup of tea. would purani aadat (kaam) Dadi would tell us stories every night. shall I / we ke saath offer, sujhaav Shall I open the window? need zaroorat You need to sign here. / You needn't worry. used to pehle hota tha, ab nahi I used to live in Patna.

used to vs be used to — do alag cheezein

used to + V1 = pehle karta tha: I used to wake up at 9. (ab nahi) be used to + -ing = aadat pad gayi hai: I am used to waking up early. Doosre me "to" preposition hai, isliye -ing. Sawaal me: Did you use to…? (bina -d)

docs.title: 16.7 Past modals — should have, could have, must have
docs.text:
Beeti baat par afsos, chhoota hua mauka, ya pichli ghatna ka andaaza — ye sab modal + have + V3 se bolte hain. Ye pattern sunne me mushkil lagta hai, par roz ki baatcheet me bahut aata hai.

Figure 16.5. Teeno teer aaj se peeche jaate hain — hum abhi khade hokar beete hue kal ke baare me bol rahe hain.

Past modals

modal + have + V3: should have done = karna chahiye tha (afsos), could have done = kar sakte the (mauka chhoota), must have done = kiya hoga (pakka andaaza). "have" kabhi "has" nahi banta.

  • I should have studied harder. Mujhe aur mehnat se padhna chahiye tha. (nahi padha — afsos)
  • The roads are wet. It must have rained last night. Raat ko baarish hui hogi — sadak geeli dekh kar pakka andaaza.

Bolne me 'should've'

Baatcheet me should have "should've" (shud-uv) sunai deta hai. Isliye kai log "should of" likh dete hain — wo galat hai. Likhte waqt hamesha have.

docs.title: 16.8 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Modal ki sabse aam Indian-English galtiyan

  • Galat: Can you able to come tomorrow?
  • Sahi: Can you come tomorrow? / Will you be able to come?

  • Kyun: "can" aur "able to" ka matlab ek hi hai — dono saath lagaana dohraav hai. Ek chuno.

  • Galat: You must to submit the form today.

  • Sahi: You must submit the form today.

  • Kyun: Modal ke baad seedha V1, beech me "to" nahi. Sirf ought to, have to, used to me "to" hota hai.

  • Galat: May you help me with this?

  • Sahi: Could you help me with this?

  • Kyun: "May" se sirf apne liye permission maangte hain (May I…?). Kisi se kaam karwana ho to Could you / Would you.

  • Galat: I could not able to attend the meeting.

  • Sahi: I couldn't attend / I wasn't able to attend the meeting.

  • Kyun: Wahi dohraav — "could" aur "able" saath nahi. Ek khaas mauke ki baat ho to "wasn't able to" sabse natural hai.

  • Galat: You should have went to the doctor.

  • Sahi: You should have gone to the doctor.
  • Kyun: "have" ke baad hamesha V3 — gone, seen, done. "went" V2 hai, wo yahan nahi aata.

docs.title: 16.9 Practice — Modals
docs.text:
Exercise 1

She ___ speak four languages.

  • can
  • cans
  • can to
  • is can

Hint: Modal ke baad verb ka kaunsa roop?

Jawaab

can

Modal khud kabhi nahi badalta — na -s, na 'to', na 'is' ke saath. Bas 'She can speak'.

Exercise 2

Boss se vinamrata se poochhna hai: '___ you check my report, please?'

  • Could
  • May
  • Must
  • Shall
Jawaab

Could

Kisi se kaam karwane ki vinamra request = Could you…? 'May you' galat hai — may sirf apne liye permission ke liye (May I…?).

Exercise 3

Tomorrow is a holiday, so you ___ come to the office.

  • don't have to
  • mustn't
  • can't
  • shouldn't have

Hint: Mana nahi hai — bas zaroorat nahi.

Jawaab

don't have to

Chhutti hai to aana zaroori nahi — 'don't have to'. 'mustn't' ka matlab hota ki aana mana hai, jo yahan matlab nahi.

Exercise 4

He has been working for 14 hours. He ___ be very tired.

  • must
  • might
  • can't
  • should have

Hint: Pakka andaaza.

Jawaab

must

14 ghante kaam — iske baad thakna lagbhag pakka hai. Pakke andaaze ke liye 'must'.

Exercise 5

When I was a child, I ___ climb trees easily.

  • could
  • can
  • am able to
  • will be able to
Jawaab

could

Bachpan ki aam kshamta — beeta samay — isliye 'can' ka past 'could'.

Exercise 6

I missed the bus. I should have ___ earlier. (leave)

Hint: have + V3

Jawaab

left

Past modal ka formula: should + have + V3. 'leave' ka V3 'left' hai. Matlab: jaldi nikalna chahiye tha (par nahi nikla).

Exercise 7

Next year I will ___ able to vote.

Hint: Do modal ek saath nahi aate.

Jawaab

be

'will can' galat hai, kyunki do modal saath nahi lagte. Future ki kshamta = will be able to.

Exercise 8

Galat shabd par tap karo.

Can you able to send the document today?

Jawaab

Galat shabd: able.

Sahi roop: Can you send the document today?

'Can' aur 'able to' dono ka matlab 'sakna' hai — saath me dohraav ho jaata hai. 'able to' hata do, ya bolo 'Will you be able to…?'

Exercise 9

Ek extra shabd hai — dhoondo.

You must to wear a helmet on the bike.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: to.

Sahi roop: You must wear a helmet on the bike.

'must' ke baad seedha V1 aata hai, 'to' nahi. 'to' sirf ought to, have to, used to me hota hai.

Exercise 10

Modal ko uske kaam se jodo.

A B should shayad, kam yakeen mustn't pehle hota tha, ab nahi might salaah used to mana hai Jawaab

should — salaah; mustn't — mana hai; might — shayad, kam yakeen; used to — pehle hota tha, ab nahi

should = chahiye, mustn't = mat karo, might = shayad, used to = purani aadat jo ab chhoot gayi.

Exercise 11

Vinamra request banao.

Shabd: mind / door / Would / the / opening / you

Jawaab

Would you mind opening the door

'Would you mind' ke baad verb -ing me aata hai — opening. Ye sabse vinamra tareeka hai kisi se kaam karwane ka.

Exercise 12

Ye line bolo — 'should have' ko 'should've' jaisa jod kar.

Jawaab

Bolo: I should have called you yesterday

Native speakers 'should have' ko 'shud-uv' bolte hain. Ise jod kar bolne ki aadat se sunna bhi aasaan ho jaata hai, aur formula (modal + have + V3) bhi pakka hota hai.

Aage kya karein

Kal office ya college me jab bhi kuch maango, "Can you" ki jagah "Could you" bolo. Aur din ke aakhir me ek "should have" wala vaakya apne baare me likho — kya karna chahiye tha jo nahi kiya.

docs.title: Chapter 44: Verb upgrade
docs.text:
Verb upgrade — teen shabd ki jagah ek

English me verb vaakya ka engine hai. Jab engine kamzor ho — make better, get rid of, give permission — to poora vaakya dheela lagta hai, chahe grammar bilkul theek ho. Ek sahi verb do-teen shabd ka kaam akela kar deta hai, aur vaakya turant saaf aur padha-likha lagta hai.
