Exercise 4

___ broke this glass?

  • Who did
  • Whom did
  • Who
  • Who does

Hint: Yahan WH-word khud subject hai.

Jawaab

Who

Jab WH-word hi subject ho to do/does/did nahi lagta — 'Who broke this glass?' Seedha verb aata hai.

Exercise 5

___ you like some tea?

Hint: Shisht offer karne wala shabd.

Jawaab

Would / would

'Would you like…?' kuch offer karne ka shisht tareeka hai. 'Do you want' se zyada polite lagta hai.

Exercise 6

How ___ brothers do you have?

Hint: Bhai ginne layak hain ya nahi?

Jawaab

many

Countable cheezon ke liye 'how many', uncountable ke liye 'how much'. Brothers gine jaa sakte hain.

Exercise 7

Let's start the meeting, ___ we?

Hint: Ye khaas tag hai.

Jawaab

shall

'Let's' ke saath hamesha 'shall we?' tag aata hai — ye yaad rakhne wali cheez hai.

Exercise 8

Is sawaal me ek galti hai — galat shabd par tap karo.

Does your sister knows my address?

Jawaab

Galat shabd: knows.

Sahi roop: Does your sister know my address?

'Does' ne -s apne andar le liya hai, isliye main verb saada rehta hai — 'know', not 'knows'.

Exercise 9

Galat shabd dhoondo.

Please tell me where is the railway station.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: is.

Sahi roop: Please tell me where the railway station is.

Indirect question ke andar kram seedha rehta hai. 'is' ko subject ke baad bhejna padega.

Exercise 10

Tag me ek galti hai — use pakdo.

She writes poems, isn't she?

Jawaab

Galat shabd: isn't.

Sahi roop: She writes poems, doesn't she?

Vaakya Present Simple me hai, usme chhipa helping verb 'does' hai — isliye tag 'doesn't she' banega. 'isn't' tab aata jab vaakya me 'is' hota.

Exercise 11

Sahi kram me sawaal banao.

Shabd: been / city / in / have / you / this / long / How / living

Jawaab

How long have you been living in this city

How long + helping verbs (have been) + subject (you) + main verb (living). 'How long you are living' galat kram hai.

Exercise 12

Sawaal ko sahi WH-word se jodo.

A B Kitni doori hai? Whose Kitni baar? Which Kiska hai? How much Diye gaye options me se kaunsa? How far Kitna cheeni? How often Jawaab

Kitni doori hai? — How far; Kitni baar? — How often; Kiska hai? — Whose; Diye gaye options me se kaunsa? — Which; Kitna cheeni? — How much

How far = doori, how often = baar, whose = kiska, which = options me se chunna, how much = uncountable ki maatra.

Exercise 13

Ab ye sawaal bol ke dekho — aakhir me aawaz uthaani hai.

Jawaab

Bolo: Could you please tell me where the bus stop is

Ye station, dukaan, kahin bhi kaam aane wala sabse kaam ka vaakya hai. Yaad rakho — 'where the bus stop is', 'where is the bus stop' nahi, kyunki ye indirect sawaal hai.

Aage kya karein

Aaj se jab bhi koi sawaal poochhna ho, bolne se pehle man me ek second ruk kar helping verb dhoondo aur use aage rakho. Shuru me ye dheema lagega — par yahi ek aadat aapki English ko turant saaf kar deti hai.

docs.title: Chapter 56: Asli duniya ki English
docs.text:
Asli duniya ki English — announcement se interview tak

Station par announcement ek baar hota hai. News reader rukta nahi. Lecture me professor 40 minute bolta hai, aur ad me sabse zaroori baat sabse tez bolte hain. Asli duniya ki listening me aap sab kuch nahi pakad sakte — aur zaroorat bhi nahi. Zaroorat hai strategy ki: pehle se andaaza, key words, signposts, numbers, aur achhe notes. Is chapter me chhe asli formats hain (sab kalpanik, par bilkul asli jaise) — har ek ke apne niyam ke saath.

docs.title: 56.1 Sunne ki chaar strategies
docs.text:
Advanced listener zyada tez nahi sunta — wo smart sunta hai. Wo jaanta hai kis cheez ka intezaar karna hai. Ye chakra har format par lagta hai:

Figure 56.1. Predict → Gist → Detail → Check. Har naye audio par chakra phir se ghoomta hai. Beech wale teen cheezein har kadam par kaam aati hain.

Pehle andaaza, phir sunna

Sunne se pehle 10 second socho: ye kaun bol raha hai, kis liye, aur kaunse shabd aayenge? Announcement = train, platform, minutes. Forecast = degrees, rain, wind. Jo dimaag pehle se intezaar kar raha ho, wo tez English bhi pakad leta hai.

docs.title: Signposts — baat ki disha batane wale shabd
docs.text: Signpost Kya batata hai However / But ulti baat aa rahi hai — dhyan do! On the other hand doosra pehlu, tulna For example udaharan — main baat pehle hi aa chuki In other words wahi baat, aasaan shabdon me So / As a result nateeja Finally / To sum up aakhri point / saar

docs.title: Numbers aur names
docs.text:
• Gate thirteen, not gate thirty. thir-TEEN (zor peeche, lamba "n") vs THIR-ty (zor aage). Galat gate = chhooti flight.
  • That's Varghese, V-A-R-G-H-E-S-E. Naam aksar spell karke bolte hain. Letters ki aawaz pakki karo: G (jee) vs J (jay), E (ee) vs I (aai).
  • The fourteen thirty train — that's 2:30 p.m. Station aur airport par 24-ghante ki ghadi: fourteen thirty = dopahar 2:30. (Dekho: Number, date, time, paise.)

docs.title: 56.2 Notes kaise lein
docs.text:
Lecture, interview ya news — notes me poore vaakya kabhi nahi. Sirf key words, numbers aur nishaan. Ek page ko teen hisson me baanto:

Figure 56.2. Baayein: signposts aur sawaal (dhaancha). Daayein: tathya aur numbers. Neeche: ek line ka saar — sunne ke baad likho. Nishaan Matlab ↑ / ↓ badhna / ghatna (prices ↑, temp ↓) → nateeja, ki taraf, badalna = / ≠ matlab hai / alag hai b/c · w/ · w/o because · with · without ~ · approx. lagbhag

Notes = shabd + number + nishaan

Poora vaakya likhoge to agla vaakya chhoot jaayega. Noun aur number likho, verb ki jagah ↑ ↓ → lagao. "Fuel costs will be cut by nearly 40%" → fuel cost ↓ ~40%.

docs.title: 56.3 Railway aur airport announcements
docs.text:
Announcements ka dhaancha hamesha ek jaisa hai: dhyan kheencho → kaun si train/flight → kya badla → aapko kya karna hai. Bhasha bahut formal hoti hai (passengers are requested to…), aur echo ki wajah se shabd dhundhle ho jaate hain. Isliye predict karo: number, platform/gate, time.

Phrase Matlab scheduled to depart chhootne ka tay samay running late by itni der se chal rahi hai foot overbridge paidal pul (FOB) final boarding call flight me chadhne ki aakhri pukaar proceed to (formal) ki taraf jaayein

🎧 Do announcements suno

  • Railway station — Pune Junction Do badlaav hain — dono pakdo.
  • Airport — final boarding call "immediately" do baar — matlab samay khatam ho raha hai.
Transcript

Railway: Attention, please. Train number 12794, the Deccan Pearl Express from Pune to Hyderabad, scheduled to depart at 14:30, is running late by approximately 45 minutes. This train will now depart from platform number 6, instead of platform number 2. Passengers are requested to use the foot overbridge to reach platform 6. Please do not cross the railway tracks. We regret the inconvenience caused.

Airport: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. This is the final boarding call for SkyIndus flight SI 712 to Kochi. Passengers on this flight are requested to proceed immediately to gate number 23, where boarding is about to close. Passenger Shalini Varghese, travelling to Kochi, please report to gate 23 immediately. Thank you.

  • This train will now depart from platform number six, instead of platform number two. Ab train platform 6 se chhootegi, 2 se nahi. "instead of" ke baad purani jaankari — naya number pehle aata hai.
  • We regret the inconvenience caused. Asuvidha ke liye khed hai. Ye line aate hi samjho — announcement khatam, ab koi nayi jaankari nahi.

Announcement ki aam galti

  • Galat: "…platform six, instead of platform two" → main platform 2 par jaata hoon (aakhri number yaad raha).
  • Sahi: Naya platform = 6. "instead of" ke baad wala number purana hai.
  • Kyun: Kaan aakhri shabd yaad rakhta hai. Isliye "instead of / not / no longer" jaise shabdon par ruk kar socho: kaunsa naya, kaunsa purana?

docs.title: 56.4 Mausam ki khabar (weather forecast)
docs.text:
Forecast me teen cheezein hamesha hoti hain: kya hoga (rain, sun, wind), kab (tonight, by tomorrow morning, the weekend) aur kitna (degrees, km per hour). Aakhir me aksar ek salaah hoti hai. Suno: taapmaan kitna girega, aur machhuaaron ko kya kaha gaya?

Phrase Matlab humid umas bhara (HYOO-mid) relief is on the way raahat aane wali hai showers halki, thodi der ki baarish are advised not to salaah: na jaayein (chetaavni)

🎧 Forecast suno

  • Weather — Mumbai aur Konkan coast Notes ke liye: aaj → kal → weekend. Har ek ke aage ek-do shabd.
Transcript

Here's the weather for Mumbai and the Konkan coast. After two very hot and humid days, relief is finally on the way. Light showers are expected in the city tonight, and by tomorrow morning the rain will become heavier, especially in the northern suburbs. Temperatures will drop from 34 degrees to around 29. Winds from the south-west may reach 50 km per hour along the coast, so fishermen are advised not to go out to sea until Thursday. However, the weekend looks brighter, with sunshine returning on Saturday. If you're commuting tomorrow, leave a little early and carry an umbrella.

  • Winds may reach fifty kilometres per hour, so fishermen are advised not to go out to sea. Hawa 50 km/h tak pahunch sakti hai, isliye machhuaare samundar me na jaayein. Kaaran (tez hawa) → "so" → salaah.
  • However, the weekend looks brighter. Lekin weekend behtar dikh raha hai. "However" = mausam ki kahani ulti disha me mud gayi — baarish ke baad dhoop.

docs.title: 56.5 News bulletin
docs.text:
News me sabse zaroori baat pehle vaakya me hoti hai (kaun, kya, kab) — baaki vaakya detail dete hain. Har nayi khabar "In other news…" ya "And finally…" se shuru hoti hai. Ye bulletin kalpanik hai — shahar aur ghatnaayein banaayi hui hain. Suno: pehli khabar kis baare me hai, aur kis baat par log khush nahi hain?

Phrase Matlab announced ghoshna ki officials say adhikaariyon ka kehna hai (srot) commuter groups roz safar karne walon ke sangathan rice husk dhaan ki bhoosi represent pratinidhitva karna

🎧 Bulletin suno (2 khabrein)

  • Story 1 — electric buses "However" ke baad doosra paksh — aalochna.
  • Story 2 — science prize "proud, but not surprised" — teacher ko bachchon par pehle se bharosa tha.
Transcript

Good evening, and here are tonight's main stories. The city of Ambarpur will get 200 new electric buses by the end of this year, the transport department announced today. Officials say the buses will cut fuel costs by nearly 40% and reduce air pollution on the busiest routes. However, some commuter groups have asked why ticket prices are not coming down as well. The first 50 buses are expected on the roads in August.

In other news, four students from a government school in Ranchi have won first prize at a national science fair. Their project, a low-cost water filter made from clay and rice husk, costs less than ₹300 to build. The students will now represent India at an international competition next spring. Speaking to reporters, their teacher said she was proud, but not surprised.

  • The buses will cut fuel costs by nearly forty percent. Buses se fuel ka kharcha lagbhag 40% kam hoga. "nearly" = thoda kam (38–39%), "over" hota to zyada. Notes: fuel ↓ ~40%.
  • Some commuter groups have asked why ticket prices are not coming down as well. Kuch yaatri sangathan pooch rahe hain ki ticket bhi sasta kyon nahi ho raha. News "shikaayat" ko aksar aise sawaal ke roop me batata hai.

News ka pehla vaakya = poori khabar

Gist ke liye har khabar ka pehla vaakya dhyan se suno — kaun, kya, kab wahin hai. Baaki vaakya numbers aur raay jodte hain. "In other news" = naya topic, naya notes ka block.

docs.title: 56.6 Lecture ka hissa — PIN code ki kahani
docs.text:
Lecture lamba hota hai, isliye lecturer (yahan kalpanik Dr Meenakshi Rao) khud naksha deti hai: Today I want to talk about… So, how does it work? For example… Finally… In other words…. Ye signposts aapke notes ke headings ban jaate hain (upar wala template dekho). Suno: PIN code kyon aaya, aur pehla digit kya batata hai?

Phrase Matlab stands for poora naam hai (abbreviation) digit ank (0–9) narrows it down daayra chhota karta hai sorting district dak chhaantne wala zila I'd argue that meri raay hai ki (tark ke saath)

🎧 Lecture suno (2 hisse)

  • Part 1 — kyon? "Why? Well, …" — lecturer khud sawaal poochh kar jawaab deta hai. Jawaab = key point.
  • Part 2 — kaise? Aakhri sawaal agle hisse ka trailer hai — notes me "GPS? → next" likh do.
Transcript

Good morning, everyone. Today I want to talk about something you write almost every week, but probably never think about: the PIN code. PIN stands for Postal Index Number, and it was introduced in India in 1972. Before that, letters were often delayed or lost. Why? Well, many towns had similar names, and letters were addressed in many different languages. So the postal department needed a system that worked in numbers, not words.

So, how does it work? A PIN code has six digits, and each part has a job. The first digit tells you the region. For example, 1 covers Delhi and much of the north, while 6 covers Tamil Nadu and Kerala. The second digit narrows it down to a sub-region, and the third shows the sorting district. Finally, the last three digits point to the individual post office. In other words, the number moves from big to small, just like an address. Now, you might ask: do we still need PIN codes in the age of GPS? I'd argue that we do, and here's why.

  • One covers Delhi and much of the north, while six covers Tamil Nadu and Kerala. 1 Delhi aur uttar ke bade hisse ke liye, jabki 6 Tamil Nadu aur Kerala ke liye. "while" yahan samay nahi, tulna hai (jabki).
  • In other words, the number moves from big to small, just like an address. Yaani number bade se chhote ki taraf jaata hai, address ki tarah. "In other words" = saar — ye line summary me jaani chahiye.

Lecture notes ki galti

  • Galat: Notes: "For example, one covers Delhi and much of the north…" (poora vaakya likhte rahe, agla point chhoot gaya)
  • Sahi: Notes: "1st = region (eg 1 = N, 6 = TN/KL)"
  • Kyun: "For example" ke baad wali baat udaharan hai, main point nahi. Udaharan chhota likho, main point (first digit = region) pakka likho.

docs.title: 56.7 Interview — sawaal aur jawaab
docs.text:
Radio interview me host sawaal poochhta hai aur mehmaan kahani ke saath jawaab deta hai. Asli jawaab aksar shuru me nahi, aakhir me hota hai — "That's when I realised…", "For me, that was the moment…". Ye interview kalpanik hai: Kamla ji ek gaanv me chalta-phirta pustakaalaya (mobile library) chalaati hain. Suno: shuruaat kaise hui, aur unhe kab laga ki kaam ho raha hai?

Phrase Matlab by accident bina soche, sanyog se access pahunch, milne ka mauka convincing manaana, yakeen dilaana a waste of time samay ki barbaadi

🎧 Interview suno (2 hisse)

  • Part 1 — shuruaat Sawaal "?" ke saath khatam hote hain — wahin se jawaab shuru.
  • Part 2 — mushkilein aur safalta "But the bigger challenge…" — pehla jawaab (paisa) asli jawaab nahi tha.
Transcript

Host: Kamla ji, thank you for joining us. Your mobile library now visits forty villages. How did it all start?

Kamla: Thank you for having me. Honestly, it started by accident. In 2019, I gave my old books to a school near my village, and within a week, the children had read all of them. They kept asking for more. That's when I realised the problem wasn't interest. It was access.

Host: And the library is actually a bus, isn't it?

Kamla: Yes, an old school bus. We removed the seats, added shelves, and painted it bright yellow, so children can see it coming from far away.

Host: What has been the biggest challenge?

Kamla: Money, of course. Fuel is expensive, and books get damaged. But the bigger challenge was convincing some parents that story books are not a waste of time.

Host: And has that changed?

Kamla: Slowly, yes. Last year, three mothers asked if they could borrow books for themselves. For me, that was the moment I knew it was working.

  • The problem wasn't interest. It was access. Dikkat ruchi ki nahi thi, kitaabon tak pahunch ki thi. Inference: bachche padhna chahte the, bas kitaabein nahi thin.
  • Three mothers asked if they could borrow books for themselves. Teen maaon ne apne liye kitaabein maangi. Jo parents pehle kitaabon ko "time waste" maante the, wahi ab padhna chahte hain — yahi safalta hai.

docs.title: 56.8 Advertisement — bechne wali bhasha
docs.text:
Ad sunna ek alag hunar hai: yahan aapko sirf samajhna nahi, parakhna bhi hai. Ad me sawaal (Tired of…?), sabse badhiya wale shabd (quietest), hukm (Order today), jaldi ka dabaav (before Sunday) aur "sab le rahe hain" (thousands of families) hota hai. Aur sabse zaroori baat — terms and conditions — sabse aakhir me, sabse tez. Ye product kalpanik hai.

Tareeka Ad me Asar Rhetorical question Tired of sleepless nights? dard yaad dilaana Superlative the quietest fan we have ever made sabse achha lagna "up to" save up to 50% zyada se zyada — pakka nahi Urgency Order before Sunday jaldi faisla Social proof Thousands of families… sab le rahe hain

🎧 Ad suno

  • Radio ad — CoolNest Breeze fan Gin ke dekho: kitne hukm (imperatives) aur kitne sawaal?
Transcript

Tired of sleepless summer nights? Meet the new CoolNest Breeze, the quietest ceiling fan we have ever made. Its smart sensor adjusts the speed automatically, so you sleep better and save up to 50% on electricity. Imagine coming home to a cool, calm room every single night. And that's not all! Order before Sunday and get free installation, plus a five-year warranty. Thousands of families have already made the switch. Why wait? Visit your nearest store or order online today. CoolNest Breeze. Feel the difference. Terms and conditions apply. Savings compared with a standard 75-watt fan.

Ad ki chaal pakdo

  • Galat: "Save up to 50%" = bill aadha ho jaayega.
  • Sahi: "up to 50%" = zyada se zyada 50% — shayad 10% hi bache.
  • Kyun: Aur fine print kehta hai: tulna ek purane 75-watt fan se hai. Jis ghar me pehle se naya fan ho, wahan bachat aur kam hogi.

Ad = vaada + dabaav + fine print

Har ad me teen cheezein suno: kya vaada hai (up to?), kya dabaav hai (before Sunday), aur aakhri tez line me kya chhupa hai. Sabse dheemi bolne wali line bechti hai; sabse tez wali sach batati hai.

docs.title: 56.9 Practice — Asli duniya ki English
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Announcement sunne se pehle sabse achhi strategy kya hai?

  • Predict — number, platform, time ka intezaar
  • Har shabd likhne ki koshish
  • Sirf aakhri line sunna
  • Aankhein band karke kuch na sochna

Hint: Chakra ka pehla kadam.

Jawaab

Predict — number, platform, time ka intezaar

Predict → Gist → Detail → Check. Jo dimaag intezaar kar raha ho, wo numbers jaldi pakadta hai.

Exercise 2

Signpost ko uske kaam se jodo.

A B However wahi baat, aasaan shabdon me For example aakhri point In other words ulti baat Finally udaharan Jawaab

However — ulti baat; For example — udaharan; In other words — wahi baat, aasaan shabdon me; Finally — aakhri point

Signposts baat ka naksha hain — inhe sunte hi notes me naya block shuru karo.

Exercise 3

What has changed for the Deccan Pearl Express? (gist)

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Attention, please. Train number one two seven nine four, the Deccan Pearl Express from Pune to Hyderabad, scheduled to depart at fourteen thirty, is running late by approximately forty-five minutes. This train will now depart from platform number six, instead of platform number two.

  • It is late and the platform has changed.
  • It has been cancelled.
  • It will leave early.
  • It now goes to Mumbai.
Jawaab

It is late and the platform has changed.

Do badlaav: 'running late by approximately forty-five minutes' aur 'platform number six, instead of platform number two'.

Exercise 4

Which platform should passengers go to?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

This train will now depart from platform number six, instead of platform number two. Passengers are requested to use the foot overbridge to reach platform six. Please do not cross the railway tracks.

  • platform 6
  • platform 2
  • platform 4
  • platform 12
Jawaab

platform 6

'instead of' ke baad purana platform (2). Naya = 6.

Exercise 5

What should Shalini Varghese do?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

This is the final boarding call for SkyIndus flight S I seven one two to Kochi. Passengers on this flight are requested to proceed immediately to gate number twenty-three, where boarding is about to close. Passenger Shalini Varghese, travelling to Kochi, please report to gate twenty-three immediately.

  • Go to gate 23 immediately.
  • Go to gate 33 after dinner.
  • Collect her bag at gate 13.
  • Wait for the next flight.
Jawaab

Go to gate 23 immediately.

'please report to gate twenty-three immediately' — final boarding call = aakhri mauka.

Exercise 6

What will the temperature drop to?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Light showers are expected in the city tonight, and by tomorrow morning the rain will become heavier, especially in the northern suburbs. Temperatures will drop from thirty-four degrees to around twenty-nine.

  • around 29 degrees
  • 34 degrees
  • around 24 degrees
  • 39 degrees
Jawaab

around 29 degrees

'from thirty-four … to around twenty-nine' — from = abhi, to = naya.

Exercise 7

Why are fishermen told not to go out to sea?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Winds from the south-west may reach fifty kilometres per hour along the coast, so fishermen are advised not to go out to sea until Thursday. However, the weekend looks brighter, with sunshine returning on Saturday.

  • because of strong winds
  • because of very hot weather
  • because it is a holiday
  • because of fog
Jawaab

because of strong winds

Kaaran 'so' se pehle: hawa 50 km/h tak. 'are advised not to' = chetaavni.

Exercise 8

What is the first news story mainly about?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Good evening, and here are tonight's main stories. The city of Ambarpur will get two hundred new electric buses by the end of this year, the transport department announced today. Officials say the buses will cut fuel costs by nearly forty percent.

  • new electric buses for a city
  • higher bus ticket prices
  • a new metro line
  • a fuel shortage
Jawaab

new electric buses for a city

News ka pehla vaakya = poori khabar: Ambarpur ko 200 electric buses.

Exercise 9

What are some commuter groups unhappy about?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Officials say the buses will cut fuel costs by nearly forty percent and reduce air pollution on the busiest routes. However, some commuter groups have asked why ticket prices are not coming down as well.

  • Ticket prices are not going down.
  • The buses are too noisy.
  • There are too few routes.
  • The buses are arriving late.
Jawaab

Ticket prices are not going down.

'However' ke baad aalochna: kharcha sarkaar ka ghata, par ticket sasta nahi hua.

Exercise 10

How much does the students' water filter cost to build?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Their project, a low-cost water filter made from clay and rice husk, costs less than three hundred rupees to build.

  • less than 300 rupees
  • about 3,000 rupees
  • exactly 30 rupees
  • more than 300 rupees
Jawaab

less than 300 rupees

'less than three hundred rupees' — 'less than' bhi jawaab ka hissa hai.

Exercise 11

Why were letters often delayed before 1972?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Before that, letters were often delayed or lost. Why? Well, many towns had similar names, and letters were addressed in many different languages.

  • Towns had similar names and addresses were in many languages.
  • There were not enough postmen.
  • Trains were very slow.
  • Stamps were too expensive.
Jawaab

Towns had similar names and addresses were in many languages.

Lecturer ne khud 'Why? Well, …' poochha aur do kaaran diye.

Exercise 12

What does the first digit of a PIN code show?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

A PIN code has six digits, and each part has a job. The first digit tells you the region. For example, one covers Delhi and much of the north, while six covers Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

  • the region
  • the post office
  • the sorting district
  • the state capital
Jawaab

the region

'The first digit tells you the region.' 'For example' ke baad sirf udaharan hai.

Exercise 13

What does the lecturer do after saying 'In other words'?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Finally, the last three digits point to the individual post office. In other words, the number moves from big to small, just like an address.

  • She repeats the idea in a simpler way.
  • She gives the opposite view.
  • She starts a new topic.
  • She asks the students a question.
Jawaab

She repeats the idea in a simpler way.

'In other words' = wahi baat, aasaan shabdon me — summary ke liye sabse achhi line.

Exercise 14

What does Kamla mean by 'the problem wasn't interest, it was access'?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

I gave my old books to a school near my village, and within a week, the children had read all of them. They kept asking for more. That's when I realised the problem wasn't interest. It was access.

  • The children wanted to read but had no books.
  • The children were not interested in books.
  • The school did not allow books.
  • The books were too difficult.
Jawaab

The children wanted to read but had no books.

Ek hafte me saari kitaabein padh li aur aur maangi — ruchi thi, kitaabein nahi thin.

Exercise 15

Why did they paint the bus bright yellow?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Yes, an old school bus. We removed the seats, added shelves, and painted it bright yellow, so children can see it coming from far away.

  • so children can see it from far away
  • because yellow paint is cheap
  • because it was a school bus
  • to protect the books from the sun
Jawaab

so children can see it from far away

'so children can see it coming from far away' — 'so' ke baad maqsad.

Exercise 16

What does 'save up to fifty percent' really promise?

Ise zor se padho, ya kisi se padhwao:

Its smart sensor adjusts the speed automatically, so you sleep better and save up to fifty percent on electricity.

  • You may save less than 50%.
  • You will always save exactly 50%.
  • You will save more than 50%.
  • The fan costs 50% less.
Jawaab

You may save less than 50%.

'up to' = zyada se zyada. Asli bachat kam bhi ho sakti hai — ad ki sabse purani chaal.

Exercise 17

Suno aur likho.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

Passengers are requested to use the foot overbridge.

'are requested to' = formal 'please'. 'overbridge' ek shabd.

Exercise 18

Suno aur likho (numbers ank me bhi likh sakte ho).

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

Temperatures will drop from thirty-four degrees to around twenty-nine.

thir-ty-FOUR aur twen-ty-NINE — -ty wale numbers; 'from … to' ka dhaancha.

Exercise 19

Suno aur likho.

Dictation. Kisi se ye vaakya zor se padhwao, phir likh lo.

Jawaab

The problem wasn't interest. It was access.

'wasn't' me 't' halka hai — par wahi poora matlab palat deta hai.

Exercise 20

Station announcer ki tarah saaf aur dheere bolo.

Jawaab

Bolo: Please do not cross the railway tracks

Announcement me 'do not' poora bolte hain (don't nahi) — zor dene ke liye. 'tracks' ka -s saaf.

Next step

Is hafte ek asli cheez roz suno — station ka announcement, radio ka mausam, ya ek chhota podcast — aur upar wale template me 5 line ke notes banao. Exam ki taiyaari ho to dekho IELTS, TOEFL aur aapka level.

docs.title: Chapter 22: Kisi ki baat aage batana
docs.text:
Kisi ki baat aage batana — reported speech

Din bhar hum yahi karte hain: "Mummy ne kaha ki khaana khaa lo", "Boss bola ki kal aa jana". English me ise reported speech kehte hain, aur isme ek hi bada rule hai — tense ek kadam peeche chala jaata hai. Jaise kisi ne jo kaha, wo ab purani baat ban gayi, to uski tense bhi ek seedhi peeche ki seedhi utar jaati hai. Is chapter me wo seedhi (ladder) aapko tasveer me dikhegi.

Ek line me

If the reporting verb is in the past (said, told, asked), move the tense inside one step back. Bahar wala verb past me hai, to andar wala tense ek kadam peeche — present → past, past → past perfect.

docs.title: 22.1 Paanch cheezein badalti hain
docs.text: # Kya badalta hai Direct Reported 1 Quotes aur comma hat jaate hain, "that" aa jaata hai He said, "I am tired." He said that he was tired. 2 Pronoun badalte hain "I am tired." … he was tired. 3 Tense ek kadam peeche "I am tired." … he was tired. 4 Samay ke shabd badalte hain "I will come tomorrow." … he would come the next day. 5 Jagah ke shabd badalte hain "Sit here." … to sit there.

docs.title: 22.2 Tense ki seedhi — ek kadam peeche
docs.text:
Yahi is poore chapter ka dil hai. Bayein taraf wo tense hai jo bolne wale ne use kiya, aur dayein taraf wo tense jo report karte waqt aata hai. Dhyaan do — sab kuch ek kadam neeche utar raha hai.

Figure 22.1. Hara dabba = jo bola gaya. Narangi dabba = report karte waqt ka roop. Past Perfect aakhri seedhi hai — usse aage peeche jaane ki jagah nahi hai.

docs.title: 22.3 Pronoun kaise badalte hain
docs.text:
Rule aasaan hai: pronoun report karne wale ke nazariye se badalta hai. "Main" bolne wale ka tha — ab wo "wo" ban jaata hai.

Direct Reported Example I, me, my he/she, him/her, his/her He said, "I lost my pen." → He said he had lost his pen. we, us, our they, them, their They said, "We are busy." → They said they were busy. you, your me/him/her (kisse kaha, uske hisaab se) She told me, "You are late." → She told me I was late. he, she, it, they wahi rehte hain She said, "He is away." → She said he was away.

docs.title: 22.4 Samay aur jagah ke shabd
docs.text:
Direct Reported now then today that day tonight that night tomorrow the next day / the following day yesterday the previous day / the day before last night the previous night next week the following week two days ago two days before here there this / these that / those come go
  • Direct: She said, "I am going to Delhi tomorrow."
  • Reported: She said that she was going to Delhi the next day. Teen badlaav: I → she, am → was, tomorrow → the next day.

docs.title: 22.5 Jab tense nahi badalti
docs.text:
Har baar tense peeche nahi jaati. Chaar mauke aise hain jahan tense waisi hi rehti hai — aur ye jaanna bahut zaroori hai, warna English banaawati lagti hai.

Mauka Example Reporting verb present me hai He says that he is busy. Hamesha sach rehne wali baat The teacher said that the sun rises in the east. Baat abhi bhi sach hai She said she works in a bank. (aaj bhi karti hai) Pehle se Past Perfect hai He said, "I had finished." → He said he had finished.

docs.title: 22.6 Sawaal ko report karna
docs.text: Yahan do cheezein hoti hain: "that" nahi aata, aur kram seedha ho jaata hai — helping verb wapas subject ke peeche chala jaata hai. Question mark bhi hat jaata hai.

docs.title: WH wale sawaal — WH-word hi joint banta hai
docs.text: Direct Reported He asked, "Where do you live?" He asked where I lived. She asked, "What is your name?" She asked what my name was. They asked, "Why did he leave?" They asked why he had left.

docs.title: Yes/No sawaal — "if" ya "whether" lagao
docs.text:
Direct Reported He asked, "Are you ready?" He asked if I was ready. She asked, "Did you call him?" She asked whether I had called him. Mother asked, "Have you eaten?" Mother asked if I had eaten.

Sawaal reported hone ke baad sawaal nahi rehta

  • Galat: He asked me where was I going?
  • Sahi: He asked me where I was going.
  • Kyun: Reported sawaal ab ek bayaan (statement) hai. Isliye kram seedha, aur aakhir me full stop — question mark nahi.

docs.title: 22.7 Hukm, request aur salaah
docs.text:
In sab me ek hi trick hai: "to" + V1. Negative ho to "not to" + V1. Aur reporting verb baat ke suroor ke hisaab se badalta hai.

Kism Reporting verb Direct Reported Hukm ordered / told "Stand up!" He ordered me to stand up. Request requested / asked "Please help me." She requested me to help her. Salaah advised "You should rest." He advised me to rest. Mana karna forbade / told… not to "Don't touch it." She told me not to touch it. Sujhaav suggested "Let's go out." He suggested going out. Prarthna / dua prayed / wished "May you succeed!" He wished that I might succeed.

docs.title: 22.8 say, tell, ask — teen shabd, teen aadat
docs.text:
Ye teen shabd Indian English ki sabse badi reported-speech galti banate hain. Farq sirf itna hai ki kaun kisko leta hai.

Verb Kaise aata hai Sahi say insaan seedha nahi aata — "to" lagta hai He said to me… / He said that… tell insaan seedha aata hai — "to" nahi He told me that… ask insaan seedha aata hai He asked me if…

'She said me' — sabse aam galti

  • Galat: She said me that the shop was closed.
  • Sahi: She told me that the shop was closed.

  • Kyun: "Say" ke baad insaan seedha nahi aata. Do raaste hain: She told me… ya She said to me…. Aasaan tareeka — insaan ka naam lena ho to hamesha tell use karo.

  • Galat: He told that he would come.

  • Sahi: He said that he would come. / He told me that he would come.
  • Kyun: "Tell" ke baad kisko bataya — ye batana padta hai. Akela "told that" adhoora hai.

docs.title: 22.9 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Reported speech ki top galtiyan

  • Galat: She said that she is coming tomorrow.
  • Sahi: She said that she was coming the next day.

  • Kyun: "said" past me hai, to andar ka tense ek kadam peeche — is → was, aur tomorrow → the next day.

  • Galat: He asked me that where I live.

  • Sahi: He asked me where I lived.

  • Kyun: Sawaal me "that" nahi aata. WH-word khud jodne ka kaam karta hai.

  • Galat: My father told me that study hard.

  • Sahi: My father told me to study hard.

  • Kyun: Hukm aur salaah ke liye "to + V1" — "that" nahi.

  • Galat: She asked me do I know the way.

  • Sahi: She asked me if I knew the way.

  • Kyun: Yes/no sawaal ke liye "if" ya "whether", aur kram seedha. "do/does/did" gayab ho jaate hain.

  • Galat: He said that he will help me.

  • Sahi: He said that he would help me.

  • Kyun: will → would. Isi tarah can → could, may → might, must → had to.

  • Galat: The teacher said that water boiled at 100 degrees.

  • Sahi: The teacher said that water boils at 100 degrees.

  • Kyun: Hamesha sach rehne wali baat me tense peeche nahi jaati.

  • Galat: He told me that don't go there.

  • Sahi: He told me not to go there.
  • Kyun: Mana karne ke liye "not to + V1" — chhota aur seedha roop.

Chaar kadam, har baar

1. Kism pehchaano — bayaan, sawaal, ya hukm? 2. Sahi joint lagao — that / if-whether / WH-word / to. 3. Pronoun badlo. 4. Tense ek kadam peeche, aur samay-jagah ke shabd badlo.

docs.title: 22.10 Practice — Reported speech
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Report karo: She said, "I am very tired."

  • She said that she is very tired.
  • She said that she was very tired.
  • She said that I was very tired.
  • She told that she was very tired.

Hint: said past me hai, to andar kya hoga?

Jawaab

She said that she was very tired.

Do badlaav hue: pronoun I → she, aur tense am → was. 'said' past me hai isliye tense ek kadam peeche jaati hai.

Exercise 2

Report karo: He asked, "Where is the bank?"

  • He asked where is the bank.
  • He asked that where was the bank.
  • He asked where the bank was.
  • He asked where was the bank?

Hint: Sawaal reported hone par kram seedha ho jaata hai.

Jawaab

He asked where the bank was.

Reported sawaal ab bayaan hai — isliye 'the bank was', aur aakhir me full stop. 'That' bhi nahi aata.

Exercise 3

Report karo: Mother said, "Don't play in the sun."

  • Mother said that don't play in the sun.
  • Mother told not to play in the sun.
  • Mother told me not to play in the sun.
  • Mother said me not to play in the sun.

Hint: Mana karna hai.

Jawaab

Mother told me not to play in the sun.

Mana karne ke liye 'not to + V1'. Aur 'tell' ke baad kisko kaha — ye batana zaroori hai, isliye 'told me'.

Exercise 4

Kis vaakya me tense peeche NAHI jaayegi?

  • He said, "I am ill."
  • She said, "The earth moves round the sun."
  • They said, "We are leaving."
  • He said, "I will call you."

Hint: Kaunsi baat hamesha sach hai?

Jawaab

She said, "The earth moves round the sun."

Hamesha sach rehne wali baat (universal truth) me tense waisi hi rehti hai — 'She said that the earth moves round the sun.'

Exercise 5

He said, "I will come tomorrow." → He said that he ___ come the next day.

Hint: will ka reported roop?

Jawaab

would

will → would. Isi tarah can → could, may → might, shall → should.

Exercise 6

She asked, "Are you coming?" → She asked ___ I was coming.

Hint: Yes/no sawaal ka joint.

Jawaab

if / whether

Yes/no sawaal report karte waqt 'if' ya 'whether' lagta hai. Dono sahi hain — 'whether' thoda zyada formal hai.

Exercise 7

Ravi ___ me that the train was late.

Hint: Insaan ('me') seedha aa raha hai — to kaunsa verb?

Jawaab

told

'Tell' ke baad insaan seedha aata hai — told me. 'Said me' galat hai; 'said to me' chalta hai.

Exercise 8

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — galat shabd par tap karo.

My sister said me that she would help.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: said.

Sahi roop: My sister told me that she would help.

'Say' ke baad insaan seedha nahi aata. 'Told me' bolna hai, ya 'said to me'.

Exercise 9

Galat shabd dhoondo.

He asked me that where I was going.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: that.

Sahi roop: He asked me where I was going.

Sawaal report karte waqt 'that' nahi lagta. WH-word khud dono hisson ko jod deta hai.

Exercise 10

Ek shabd galat hai — pakdo.

The doctor advised him that rest for a week.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: that.

Sahi roop: The doctor advised him to rest for a week.

Salaah aur hukm ke liye 'to + V1' aata hai — 'to rest'. 'That' yahan nahi chalta.

Exercise 11

Sahi kram me reported vaakya banao.

Shabd: she / work / finished / me / that / her / told / She / had

Jawaab

She told me that she had finished her work

'Tell' ke baad insaan (me), phir 'that', phir tense ek kadam peeche — 'has finished' ban gaya 'had finished'.

Exercise 12

Direct roop ko uske reported roop se jodo.

A B I write he would write I wrote he could write I will write he had to write I can write he wrote I must write he had written Jawaab

I write — he wrote; I wrote — he had written; I will write — he would write; I can write — he could write; I must write — he had to write

Present → past, past → past perfect, will → would, can → could, must → had to. Seedhi ka har kadam ek hi disha me utarta hai.

Exercise 13

Ab ye line bol ke dekho — roz kaam aane wali reported speech.

Jawaab

Bolo: He told me that he would call me the next day

Teen cheezein ek saath sahi karni hain: 'told me' (said me nahi), 'would' (will nahi), aur 'the next day' (tomorrow nahi). Bolkar practice karne se ye teeno saath aane lagte hain.

Aage kya karein

Aaj raat sone se pehle, din bhar ki teen baatein kisi ko report karke bolo — "My boss told me that…", "My friend asked me if…", "Mummy told me to…". Teen vaakya, roz. Ek hafte me ye seedhi apne-aap dimaag me baith jaayegi.

docs.title: Chapter 27: Rhythm aur stress
docs.text:
Rhythm aur stress — kaunsa shabd zor se

Aapki saari aawazein theek ho sakti hain, grammar bhi theek ho sakti hai, aur phir bhi English robotic lag sakti hai. Wajah ek hi hoti hai: hum har shabd ko barabar zor se bolte hain. English ek asamaan bhasha hai — kuch shabd chamakte hain, baaki shabd peeche chale jaate hain, lagbhag gayab. Jo log is ek cheez par kaam kar lete hain, wo turant "fluent" lagne lagte hain — chahe unka vocabulary wahi purana ho.

Ek line me

Hindi lagbhag samaan taal wali bhasha hai — har akshar ko lagbhag barabar waqt milta hai. English zor ki taal wali bhasha hai — zor wale hisse lambe aur tez hote hain, baaki hisse dabe aur chhote. Isliye seedha Hindi ki taal me English bolna "flat" lagta hai.

docs.title: 27.1 Word stress — ek shabd me ek hi hissa chamakta hai
docs.text:
English ke har bade shabd me ek hissa (syllable) zor wala hota hai: wo lamba, zor se, aur thoda oonchi awaaz me bolte hain. Baaki hisse dheele aur chhote. Galat hisse par zor dene se shabd kabhi-kabhi samajh me hi nahi aata.

Figure 27.1. Narangi ooncha khamba = zor wala hissa. Dhyan do — shabd ka roop badalte hi zor jagah badal deta hai . Yaad rakhne layak baat: ek shabd = ek chamakta hissa.
  • He is a photographer, and this is his photograph. Dono shabd ek line me — zor ki jagah ka farq saaf sunai dega.

docs.title: Zor badalne se matlab badal jaata hai
docs.text:
Angrezi me kai shabd noun aur verb dono hote hain, aur farq sirf zor ka hota hai: noun me zor pehle hisse par, verb me doosre hisse par.

Shabd Noun (naam) Verb (kaam) Suno record RE-cord — rikaard, lekha re-CORD — rikaard karna present PRE-sent — tohfa pre-SENT — pesh karna increase IN-crease — badhotri in-CREASE — badhana object OB-ject — vastu ob-JECT — virodh karna contract CON-tract — samjhauta con-TRACT — sikudna conduct CON-duct — vyavhaar con-DUCT — karwana

Yaad rakhne ka chhota naksha

Naam = aage zor. Kaam = peeche zor. Noun pehle, verb baad me — jaise shabd me bhi wahi kram ho.

docs.title: Kuch pakke patterns
docs.text:
Ant me Zor kahan Examples Suno -tion / -sion usse theek pehle wale hisse par inforMAtion, deciSIon, educAtion -ity usse theek pehle aBIlity, opporTUnity, uNIversity -ic usse theek pehle ecoNOmic, fanTAStic, speCIfic -ate (verb) teesre hisse par peeche se CElebrate, EDUcate, comMUnicate -ee aakhir wale hisse par employEE, trainEE, agrEE Do hisson wale naam lagbhag hamesha pehle par TAble, WINdow, DOCtor, TEAcher

Jo zor hum sabse zyada galat lagate hain

  • Galat: de-VE-lop-MENT me do zor
  • Sahi: de-VEL-op-ment — sirf ek zor

  • Kyun: Ek shabd me ek hi zor hota hai. Do jagah zor dene se shabd do shabd jaisa lagta hai.

  • Galat: hos-pi-TAL

  • Sahi: HOS-pi-tal

  • Kyun: Aakhri hissa "tul" ban jaata hai, dabi aawaz me. Hum use poora "TAL" bol dete hain.

  • Galat: in-ter-es-TING

  • Sahi: IN-tres-ting — teen hisse, chaar nahi

  • Kyun: Beech wali "e" lagbhag gayab ho jaati hai. Yahi schwa ka kamaal hai.

  • Galat: com-FOR-TA-BLE (chaar barabar hisse)

  • Sahi: KUMF-tuh-bul
  • Kyun: Angrez log beech ka "or" nigal jaate hain. Teen hisse, pehle par zor.

docs.title: 27.2 Sentence stress — vaakya me kaunse shabd chamakte hain
docs.text:
Yahi asli raaz hai. Ek poore vaakya me sirf kaam ki baat wale shabd zor se bolte hain. Baaki shabd — jo sirf vaakya jodne ke liye hain — dabi aawaz me, tezi se, lagbhag nigal kar bolte hain.

Content words — zor se Function words — dabe hue Kaun Noun, main verb, adjective, adverb, question words a/an/the, is/am/are/was, can/will/have (helper), of/to/in/at, and/but, I/he/she/it, that/this (jab zor na ho) Kyun Inme asli jaankari hai. Inhe kaat do, baat samajh nahi aayegi. Ye sirf dhaancha hain. Inhe kaat do, baat phir bhi samajh aa jaayegi. Test Telegram bhejna ho to kaunse shabd rakhoge? Wahi content words hain. Figure 27.2. Pehle sirf narangi shabd bolo — WANT · BUY · TICKet · MORNing · TRAIN . Phir beech wale chhote shabd bina zor ke bhar do. Poora vaakya apne aap sahi taal me aa jaayega.
  • I want to buy a ticket for the morning train. Paanch beat. Pehle sirf paanch bade shabd thaap ki tarah bolo, phir poora vaakya.
  • She was waiting for me at the bus stop. Beat: WAIT-ing · BUS · STOP. "was, for, at, the" sab dabe hue.
  • Can you send me the file before the meeting? Beat: SEND · FILE · be-FORE · MEET-ing. "Can you" lagbhag "kuhnyuh" jaisa sunai deta hai.

docs.title: 27.3 Dabe shabd — asal me kaise sunai dete hain
docs.text:
Jab function words par zor nahi hota, to unki vowel schwa ban jaati hai aur wo bilkul chhote ho jaate hain. Ye "aalsi" English nahi hai — yahi sahi English hai.

Likha hai Bola jaata hai Vaakya me Suno to tuh I want tuh go. of uhv a cup uhv tea and un / n bread n butter for fuh waiting fuh you can kuhn I kuhn do it. at uht look uht this are uh What uh you doing? have (helper) uhv I uhv finished.

Ek zaroori apwaad

Jab function word par khaas zor dena ho, to wo poora bolte hain: "I said I can do it, not I can't." Matlab dabana niyam hai, par zor dene ki chhoot hamesha hai.

docs.title: 27.4 Ek hi vaakya, paanch matlab — sirf zor badal kar
docs.text:
Ye drill aapke kaan ko hamesha ke liye khol degi. Ek hi vaakya hai — "I didn't say she stole my bag." Zor jahan padega, matlab wahin badal jaayega.

Zor is shabd par Matlab Suno I didn't say she stole my bag. Maine nahi kaha — kisi aur ne kaha hoga. I didn't say she stole my bag. Maine ye baat kahi hi nahi — aap galat samjhe. I didn't say she stole my bag. Chori kisi aur ne ki — usne nahi. I didn't say she stole my bag. Usne li thi, par chori nahi ki — udhaar liya hoga. I didn't say she stole my bag. Bag kisi aur ka tha, mera nahi.

Isse kaise practise karein

Paanch baar bolo, har baar alag shabd par zor. Zor dene ka matlab hai: wo shabd thoda lamba, thoda zor se, aur thodi oonchi aawaz me. Jab aap paanchon farq khud sun paayein — samajh lo kaan taiyaar ho gaya.

docs.title: 27.5 Jude hue shabd — English "chipakti" hai
docs.text:
Native log shabdon ke beech rukte nahi. Ek shabd ka ant agle shabd ke shuru se chipak jaata hai. Isi liye sunte waqt lagta hai "bahut tez bol rahe hain" — asal me tez nahi, juda hua hai.

Likha hua Sunai deta hai Suno What is your name? Wot-sure-naim Do you want to go? Juh-wanna-go I am going to call him. Aim-gonna-call-im Did you eat? Dijoo-eet Can I help you? Kun-ai-help-yoo Let me know. Lem-me-no

Dhyan rahe

Ye sunne ke liye seekhna hai, bolne ke liye zaroori nahi. Aap poora "What is your name?" bolein — bilkul theek hai, saaf hai, sahi hai. Par jab koi "Wot-sure-naim" bole, to aap atkein nahi — yahi faayda hai.

docs.title: 27.6 Aawaz ka chadhna-utarna (intonation)
docs.text:
Kis tarah ka vaakya Aawaz Example Suno Saadharan baat Aakhir me neeche ↘ I live in Pune. Haan/nahi wala sawaal Aakhir me oopar ↗ Do you live in Pune? WH- sawaal Aakhir me neeche ↘ Where do you live? List ginna Beech me oopar ↗, aakhri par neeche ↘ I need pens, books and a bag. Politely poochhna Halka oopar ↗ — zyada seedha sakht lagta hai Could you help me, please?

Ek aadat jo sakht lagti hai

  • Galat: "Give me the file." — sapaat, neeche girti aawaz
  • Sahi: "Could you give me the file?" — halki oopar jaati aawaz
  • Kyun: Shabd hi nahi, aawaz ka rukh bhi tehzeeb banata hai. Girti aawaz me poochha gaya sawaal order jaisa lagta hai.

docs.title: 27.7 Roz ki taal wali drill
docs.text:
Ye drill 2 minute ki hai. Har vaakya me pehle sirf bade shabd taali bajate hue bolo, phir poora vaakya bhar do.

  • I NEED to FINish this WORK by TOmorrow. Chaar thaap. "to, this, by" bilkul dabe hue.
  • Could you TELL me where the STAtion IS? Teen thaap. Aakhir me aawaz halki oopar — ye sawaal hai.
  • The MEEting has been POSTponed to NEXT WEEK. Chaar thaap. "has been" ko nigal jao — "uhz-bin".
  • I'm SORry, I didn't CATCH that LAST part. Teen thaap. Ye line roz kaam aati hai — "samajh nahi aaya" ka sabse natural roop.

docs.title: 27.8 Practice — Rhythm aur stress
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Hindi aur English ki taal me buniyadi farq kya hai?

  • Hindi lagbhag samaan taal wali hai, English zor ki taal wali
  • English me har akshar barabar hota hai
  • Dono bilkul ek jaisi hain
  • Hindi me zor hota hai, English me nahi

Hint: Kis bhasha me har akshar ko barabar waqt milta hai?

Jawaab

Hindi lagbhag samaan taal wali hai, English zor ki taal wali

Isi liye Hindi ki taal me boli gayi English sapaat lagti hai. English me kuch shabd chamakte hain, baaki dab jaate hain.

Exercise 2

'photographer' me zor kis hisse par hai?

  • TOG (doosra hissa)
  • PHO (pehla hissa)
  • ra (teesra hissa)
  • pher (chautha hissa)
Jawaab

TOG (doosra hissa)

pho-TOG-ra-pher. Dhyan do: 'photograph' me zor PHO par, par roop badalne se zor jagah badal deta hai.

Exercise 3

Noun aur verb ka stress niyam kya hai? (record, present, increase)

  • Noun me pehle hisse par, verb me doosre hisse par
  • Noun me doosre hisse par, verb me pehle par
  • Dono me pehle hisse par
  • Koi niyam nahi hai

Hint: Naam pehle, kaam baad me.

Jawaab

Noun me pehle hisse par, verb me doosre hisse par

RE-cord (cheez) / re-CORD (karna). PRE-sent (tohfa) / pre-SENT (pesh karna).

Exercise 4

Vaakya me kaunse shabd zor se bolte hain?

  • Content words — noun, main verb, adjective, adverb
  • Articles aur prepositions
  • Sirf pehla aur aakhri shabd
  • Saare shabd barabar
Jawaab

Content words — noun, main verb, adjective, adverb

Jinme asli jaankari hai wo chamakte hain. a/the/of/to/is jaise shabd sirf dhaancha hain — wo dab jaate hain.

Exercise 5

'information' me zor kahan hai?

  • MA — infor-MA-tion
  • IN — IN-formation
  • for — in-FOR-mation
  • tion — informa-TION

Hint: -tion se theek pehle wala hissa.

Jawaab

MA — infor-MA-tion

-tion aur -sion wale shabdon me zor hamesha usse theek pehle wale hisse par: deci-SI-on, educ-A-tion.

Exercise 6

'I didn't say SHE stole my bag' ka matlab kya hai?

  • Chori kisi aur ne ki, usne nahi
  • Maine kuch nahi kaha
  • Bag mera nahi tha
  • Usne chori nahi, udhaar liya
Jawaab

Chori kisi aur ne ki, usne nahi

Zor 'she' par hai, isliye vaakya usko hata kar kisi aur par ishaara karta hai. Zor badlo, matlab badal jaata hai.

Exercise 7

Ek shabd me kitne zor wale hisse hote hain? ___

Hint: Sankhya likho.

Jawaab

ek / 1 / one

Ek shabd = ek chamakta hissa. Do jagah zor dena (de-VE-lop-MENT) sabse aam galti hai.

Exercise 8

Vaakya me 'to' par zor nahi hota — wo bol kar ___ jaisa sunai deta hai.

Hint: Schwa wali dheeli aawaz.

Jawaab

tuh / tu / ta

I want tuh go. Bina zor wale function words ki vowel schwa ban jaati hai.

Exercise 9

Is vaakya ke kis shabd par zor NAHI hona chahiye? Us par tap karo.

I want to buy a ticket.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: a.

Sahi roop: I WANT to BUY a TICKet — 'a' bilkul dabi hui 'uh' hai.

Article 'a' function word hai — sabse dabne wala shabd. 'ay' nahi, 'uh'.

Exercise 10

Vaakya ke prakaar ko uski aawaz ke rukh se jodo.

A B I live in Pune. WH- sawaal, neeche Do you live in Pune? polite, halka oopar Where do you live? aakhir me neeche Could you help me? aakhir me oopar Jawaab

I live in Pune. — aakhir me neeche; Do you live in Pune? — aakhir me oopar; Where do you live? — WH- sawaal, neeche; Could you help me? — polite, halka oopar

Haan/nahi wale sawaal oopar jaate hain; baat aur WH- sawaal neeche. Girti aawaz me sawaal order jaisa lagta hai.

Exercise 11

Sahi kram me vaakya banao, phir thaap ke saath bolo.

Shabd: to / need / I / by / finish / work / tomorrow / this

Jawaab

I need to finish this work by tomorrow

Thaap: NEED · FIN-ish · WORK · TO-morrow. Beech ke 'to, this, by' dabe hue.

Exercise 12

Paanch thaap wala vaakya. Pehle sirf bade shabd taali ke saath, phir poora.

Jawaab

Bolo: I want to buy a ticket for the morning train

WANT · BUY · TICK-et · MOR-ning · TRAIN. 'to, a, for, the' lagbhag gayab.

Exercise 13

Noun-verb stress. Dono roop ek saath bolo.

Jawaab

Bolo: This is a record. Please record it.

RE-cord (noun) phir re-CORD (verb). Farq saaf sunai dena chahiye.

Exercise 14

-tion wala zor. Sahi hisse par chamkao.

Jawaab

Bolo: I need more information about the decision

infor-MA-tion, deci-SI-on. Dono me zor -tion/-sion se theek pehle.

Exercise 15

Polite sawaal — aakhir me aawaz halki oopar le jao.

Jawaab

Bolo: Could you tell me where the station is

TELL · STA-tion · IS par thaap. Aawaz girne se ye order jaisa lagega, sawaal jaisa nahi.

Exercise 16

Ab zor badal kar bolo — 'she' par zor dena hai.

Jawaab

Bolo: I didn't say she stole my bag

'she' ko lamba, zor se, thoda oonchi aawaz me. Baaki shabd dabe rakho — tab farq sunai dega.

Exercise 17

Roz kaam aane wali line. Teen thaap ke saath.

Jawaab

Bolo: I'm sorry I didn't catch that last part

SOR-ry · CATCH · LAST. 'I didn't' ko tezi se nigal jao — aidunt.

Aage kya karein

Ek hafte tak ek hi kaam karo: koi bhi English sunte waqt sirf ye dhyan do ki kaunse shabd zor se aa rahe hain. Matlab samajhne ki koshish bhi mat karo — sirf taal suno. Saat din me aapka kaan badal jaayega. Agla chapter: Fluency aur filler words — bolte waqt atakne ka asli ilaaj.

docs.title: Chapter 4: Vaakya ki banawat
docs.text:
Sentence structure — vaakya ki banawat

Parts of speech se humne eent pehchaani — noun, verb, adjective. Ab dekhenge ki in eenton se deewar kaise banti hai. English me shabdon ka kram lagbhag pakka hota hai, aur jaise hi aap ye kram samajh lete ho, lambe se lamba vaakya bhi aasaan lagne lagta hai. Aage ke saare chapters — tenses, modals, clauses — isi naqshe par chalte hain.

Ek line me

A sentence is a group of words with a subject and a verb that expresses a complete thought. Subject + verb + poora matlab — teeno ho, tabhi vaakya bana.

  • Birds fly. Sirf do shabd, phir bhi poora vaakya — subject bhi hai, verb bhi.
  • My sister teaches maths. Meri behen maths padhaati hai.
  • In the morning. (vaakya nahi) Na subject, na verb — ye sirf ek tukda hai, matlab adhoora hai.

docs.title: 4.1 Subject aur Predicate — vaakya ke do hisse
docs.text:
Har vaakya ko beech se do hisson me kaata ja sakta hai. Jab ye kaat aapko dikhne lagti hai, to verb ka sahi roop chunna (is ya are, go ya goes) apne aap aasaan ho jaata hai — kyunki verb hamesha subject ki sunta hai.

Figure 4.1. Subject = jiske baare me baat ho rahi hai. Predicate = verb se shuru hokar baaki poora hissa.

Subject aur predicate

Subject = jiske baare me baat hai. Predicate = verb aur uske baad ka sab kuch. Subject dhoondhna ho to verb se poochho "kaun?" ya "kya?". Verb ka roop (is/are, go/goes) hamesha subject tay karta hai.

  • The children in the park | are playing cricket. Kaun khel rahe hain? "The children in the park" — poora group subject hai, isliye "are".
  • Learning English | is not difficult. Subject ek kaam bhi ho sakta hai — "English seekhna" mushkil nahi hai.

Chhupa hua subject

Hukm ya request wale vaakyon me subject dikhta nahi, par hota hai — you. Sit down. = (You) sit down. Please close the door. = (You) please close the door.

docs.title: 4.2 Hindi SOV hai, English SVO — kram pakka kyun hai
docs.text:
Hindi me hum kehte hain "Ram ne Shyam ko maara" ya "Shyam ko Ram ne maara" — matlab wahi rehta hai, kyunki "ne" aur "ko" batate hain kisne kya kiya. English me aise chhote marker nahi hote. Wahan kaun kaam kar raha hai, ye sirf jagah se pata chalta hai.

Figure 4.2. Hindi me ne / ko kaam batate hain, isliye kram khula hai. English me jagah hi sab kuch batati hai.

English ka pakka kram

English me kram hi matlab hai: Subject → Verb → Object. Verb hamesha subject ke turant baad aata hai, aakhir me nahi. Shabdon ki jagah badli, to matlab badal gaya.

Hindi kram (S O V) English kram (S V O) Main chai peeta hoon. I drink tea. Wo roz akhbaar padhti hai. She reads the newspaper daily. Bachchon ne khana kha liya. The children have eaten the food. Hum kal Jaipur jaayenge. We will go to Jaipur tomorrow.

Dimaag me translate karte waqt

Hindi se English banate waqt sabse pehle verb uthao aur subject ke paas rakho. "Main roz subah park me chalta hoon" → I walk in the park every morning. Baaki shabd (kahan, kab) verb ke baad, aakhir me aate hain.

docs.title: 4.3 Paanch building blocks — S, V, O, C, A
docs.text:
Har English vaakya in paanch eenton se banta hai. Inke naam yaad rakhna zaroori hai, kyunki aage dictionary, grammar books aur yahi kitaab inhi naamon se baat karegi.

Block Kaam Sawaal Example S — Subject jiske baare me baat hai Kaun? Kya? Ravi plays. V — Verb kaam ya hona Kya karta / kya hai? Ravi plays. O — Object jis par kaam padta hai Kya? Kisko? Ravi plays cricket. C — Complement subject ki pehchaan ya haalat Kaun hai? Kaisa hai? Ravi is the captain. A — Adverbial jagah, samay, tareeka Kahan? Kab? Kaise? Ravi plays in the evening.

Object ya complement? '=' laga ke dekho

Vaakya ke paanch block hain: S, V, O, C, A. Object aur complement me farq karne ke liye "=" lagao: She became a doctor → she = doctor (complement). She met a doctor → she ≠ doctor (object).

  • The tea tastes sweet. tea = sweet → "sweet" complement hai. Complement adjective bhi ho sakta hai.
  • The boy broke the glass. boy ≠ glass → "the glass" object hai, kaam us par pada.

docs.title: 4.4 Paanch core patterns
docs.text:
Achhi khabar ye hai ki English ke hazaaron vaakya asal me sirf paanch dhaanchon par bane hote hain. Kaunsa dhaancha lagega, ye verb tay karta hai — kuch verb akele chal jaate hain, kuch ko object chahiye, kuch ko do.

Figure 4.3. Har rang ek kaam: subject, verb, object, complement, adverbial. Pattern verb tay karta hai.

Paanch dhaanche

Lagbhag har vaakya in paanch me se ek hai: SV, SVO, SVC, SVOO, SVOA. Kaunsa lagega, ye verb tay karta hai. Kab, kahan, kaise wale extra shabd inke upar jud jaate hain.

Pattern Aise verb Example SV arrive, sleep, cry, laugh, fall The guests arrived. SVO eat, buy, love, read, make We bought a scooter. SVC be, become, seem, look, feel The room looks clean. SVOO give, send, show, tell, teach, buy She sent me a photo. SVOA put, keep, place, leave (kahan?) He put the milk in the fridge.

Extra shabd pattern nahi badalte

The baby slept peacefully in the cradle after lunch. — ye abhi bhi SV hai. Kaise, kahan, kab wale hisse sajawat hain; unhe hata do to bhi vaakya poora rehta hai. Par SVOA me A zaroori hai: "He put the milk." adhoora lagta hai — kahan rakha?

docs.title: 4.5 Do objects wale vaakya — kisko aur kya
docs.text:
Give, send, show, tell jaise verbs ke saath ek insaan hota hai aur ek cheez. Inhe do tareekon se lagaya ja sakta hai, aur dono sahi hain — bas chhota sa "to" dhyan se lagana hai.

Figure 4.4. Insaan pehle aaye to to nahi lagta. Cheez pehle aaye to insaan se pehle to (ya for ) lagao.
  • He told us a story. / He told a story to us. Usne humein ek kahaani sunaayi.
  • Papa bought me a cycle. / Papa bought a cycle for me. buy, make, cook ke saath "for" lagta hai, "to" nahi.

explain, describe, suggest — inme insaan pehle nahi aata

  • Galat: Please explain me the rule.
  • Sahi: Please explain the rule to me.
  • Kyun: explain, describe, suggest, say SVOO pattern nahi lete. Pehle cheez, phir "to" + insaan.

docs.title: 4.6 Phrase aur Clause — farq sirf ek jodi ka
docs.text:
Lambe vaakya ko samajhne ke liye usse tukdon me todna padta hai. Tukde do tarah ke hote hain, aur pehchaan ka tareeka ek hi hai: dekho ki tukde ke andar subject + verb ki jodi hai ya nahi.

Figure 4.5. Vaakya ke andar clause, clause ke andar phrase — jaise dabbe ke andar chhote dabbe.

Phrase vs clause

Phrase = shabdon ka group jisme subject + verb ki jodi nahi hoti (in the morning). Clause = group jisme apna subject aur verb ho (when the rain stopped). Ek vaakya me ek ya zyada clause hote hain.

Phrase ka prakaar Kiske aas-paas Example Noun phrase noun a very old temple Verb phrase main verb + helping she has been waiting Prepositional phrase preposition se shuru under the bridge Adjective phrase adjective The film was really boring. Adverb phrase adverb He spoke very slowly.

Ye vocabulary aage kaam aayegi

Clauses ke chapter me hum dekhenge ki do clause kaise jodte hain — and, but, because, who, which se. Abhi bas itna pakka kar lo: clause me verb hota hai, phrase me nahi.

docs.title: 4.7 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Kram aur dhaanche ki aam galtiyan

  • Galat: Yesterday I market went.
  • Sahi: Yesterday I went to the market.

  • Kyun: Ye seedha Hindi ka SOV kram hai ("main market gaya"). English me verb subject ke turant baad aata hai, aur "go" ke baad jagah se pehle "to" lagta hai.

  • Galat: This movie very good.

  • Sahi: This movie is very good.

  • Kyun: Hindi me "ye film bahut achhi" bol dete hain, par English me bina verb vaakya nahi banta. SVC pattern me "is" jaisa linking verb zaroori hai.

  • Galat: Myself Rahul.

  • Sahi: I am Rahul. / My name is Rahul.

  • Kyun: "Myself Rahul" me na sahi subject hai, na verb. "Myself" kabhi subject nahi banta — wo sirf object ki jagah aata hai: I hurt myself.

  • Galat: My brother he works in Pune.

  • Sahi: My brother works in Pune.

  • Kyun: Ek clause me ek hi subject. "My brother" subject hai, to "he" dohraav hai — use hata do.

  • Galat: Why you are late?

  • Sahi: Why are you late?
  • Kyun: Sawaal me helping verb subject se pehle aa jaata hai. Ye English ka ek pakka kram-badlaav hai, Hindi me aisa nahi hota.

docs.title: 4.8 Kisi bhi vaakya ko todne ka tareeka
docs.text:
Jab koi lamba vaakya samajh na aaye, ghabraao mat. Ye chaar sawaal kram se poochho — har vaakya khul jaayega.

Kadam Kya poochho Kya milega 1 Kaam ya hona kya hai? Verb (V) 2 Verb se "kaun? / kya?" Subject (S) 3 Verb ke baad "kya? / kisko?" — aur "=" test Object (O) ya Complement (C) 4 "Kahan? Kab? Kaise?" Adverbial (A)
  • My grandmother makes pickles every summer. V = makes · S = my grandmother · O = pickles · A = every summer → SVO + extra.

docs.title: 4.9 Practice — Sentence structure
docs.text:
Exercise 1

'The baby is sleeping.' — ye kaunsa pattern hai?

  • SV
  • SVO
  • SVC
  • SVOA

Hint: Verb ke baad kuch aur zaroori hai kya?

Jawaab

SV

'is sleeping' poora verb hai, aur uske baad kuch chahiye hi nahi. Na object, na complement — isliye SV.

Exercise 2

'My uncle became a pilot.' — yahan 'a pilot' kya hai?

  • Complement
  • Object
  • Adverbial
  • Subject

Hint: '=' test lagao.

Jawaab

Complement

uncle = pilot — dono ek hi insaan hain. Jab '=' lag jaaye to wo complement hota hai, object nahi.

Exercise 3

'She gave her friend a book.' — kaunsa pattern?

  • SVOO
  • SVO
  • SVOA
  • SVC
Jawaab

SVOO

Do objects hain — 'her friend' (kisko diya) aur 'a book' (kya diya). Isliye S V O O.

Exercise 4

Inme se kaunsa clause hai, phrase nahi?

  • because she was tired
  • in the morning
  • a very tall boy
  • under the old bridge

Hint: Subject + verb ki jodi dhoondho.

Jawaab

because she was tired

'she was' — yahan subject (she) aur verb (was) dono hain, isliye ye clause hai. Baaki teeno me ye jodi nahi, wo phrases hain.

Exercise 5

'Every morning, my grandfather walks in the park.' — subject kya hai?

  • my grandfather
  • Every morning
  • the park
  • walks

Hint: Verb se poochho: kaun chalta hai?

Jawaab

my grandfather

Verb 'walks' hai. Kaun chalta hai? — my grandfather. 'Every morning' vaakya ki shuruaat me hai, par wo samay batata hai, subject nahi.

Exercise 6

This tea ___ very hot.

Hint: Bina verb vaakya adhoora hai.

Jawaab

is

Ye SVC pattern hai — tea = hot. Subject ko complement se jodne ke liye linking verb 'is' chahiye. Hindi me 'chai bahut garam' chal jaata hai, English me nahi.

Exercise 7

Is vaakya me ek extra shabd hai — us par tap karo.

My sister she teaches English in Delhi.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: she.

Sahi roop: My sister teaches English in Delhi.

'My sister' pehle se subject hai. Ek clause me doosra subject 'she' dohraav hai, use hata do.

Exercise 8

Galat shabd dhoondo.

Please explain me this sentence.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: me.

Sahi roop: Please explain this sentence to me.

'explain' do objects wala pattern nahi leta. Pehle cheez aati hai, phir 'to me'.

Exercise 9

Sahi English kram me lagao.

Shabd: drink / every / morning / I / tea

Jawaab

I drink tea every morning

Subject (I) → verb (drink) → object (tea) → samay (every morning). Hindi ki tarah verb aakhir me nahi jaata.

Exercise 10

SVOA pattern me vaakya banao.

Shabd: keys / table / She / on / the / the / put

Jawaab

She put the keys on the table

S (She) + V (put) + O (the keys) + A (on the table). 'put' ke saath 'kahan' zaroori hai, isliye A hata nahi sakte.

Exercise 11

Pattern ko uske example se jodo.

A B SV The soup is hot. SVO He told us a story. SVC The bus arrived. SVOO Ravi plays cricket. Jawaab

SV — The bus arrived.; SVO — Ravi plays cricket.; SVC — The soup is hot.; SVOO — He told us a story.

arrive ko kuch nahi chahiye (SV), play ko object (SVO), is ke baad pehchaan/haalat (SVC), aur tell ke saath insaan + cheez (SVOO).

Exercise 12

Ab ye line bolo — verb 'went' ko subject ke turant baad rakhna hai.

Jawaab

Bolo: Yesterday I went to the market

Zor se bolne se SVO kram zubaan par baith jaata hai. Jitni baar sahi bologe, utni jaldi 'I market went' wali aadat chhootegi.

Aage kya karein

Aaj kisi bhi English akhbaar ki teen lines uthao aur har ek me S, V, O dhoondho. Paanch din ye karoge to lambe vaakya padhte waqt dimaag apne aap unhe tod dega.

docs.title: Chapter 49: Vaakya se paragraph
docs.text:
Vaakya se paragraph — ek baat, saaf tareeke se

Grammar sahi ho, spelling sahi ho, phir bhi kai baar likha hua padhne me thakaata hai. Wajah aksar ek hi hoti hai: vaakya ya to bahut chhote aur jhatkedaar hote hain, ya ek lambi rail-gaadi jo "and… and… so…" par chalti rehti hai. Is chapter me hum seekhenge ki vaakyon ko kaise jodein, aur unhe ek paragraph me kaise sajaayein jise padhne wala ek baar me samajh jaaye.

Ek line me

A paragraph is a group of sentences about one idea: the first sentence states it, the middle sentences support it, and the last sentence closes it. Ek paragraph = ek idea. Pehli line batati hai, beech wali saboot deti hain, aakhri line baat band karti hai.

docs.title: 49.1 Chhote tukdon se behte vaakya tak
docs.text:
Bahut chhote vaakya padhne me robot jaise lagte hain; bahut lambe vaakya me padhne wala saans lene ki jagah dhoondta reh jaata hai. Achhi likhai in dono ke beech chalti hai.

Figure 49.1. Peela = jhatkedaar, hara = behta hua, laal = kabhi na khatam hone wala.

Jodo ya todo

Do chhote vaakya ek hi baat ke hain → jodo (and, but, because, when, which). Ek vaakya 25 shabd se lamba ho gaya, ya usme do "and" aa gaye → todo aur full stop lagao.

  • ✗ I reached the station. The train was late. I waited. I had tea. Chaar tukde — sab sahi, par padhne me jhatka.
  • ✓ When I reached the station, the train was late, so I waited and had a cup of tea. when + so ne chaaron tukdon ko ek behte vaakya me jod diya.
  • ✓ The new manager, who joined last week, has already cut our meeting time in half. "The manager joined last week" ko who se andar fit kar diya.

docs.title: 49.2 Paragraph ka burger — topic, support, closing
docs.text:
Har achhe paragraph ki ek hi banawat hoti hai, chahe wo college ka essay ho ya office ki report. Ise ek burger ki tarah socho: upar aur neeche bun, beech me bharpoor masala.

Figure 49.2. Bun ke bina burger bikhar jaata hai, masale ke bina wo khaali roti hai.

Burger ka formula

1 topic sentence (kya baat + aapki raay) → 2–4 support sentences (wajah, udaharan, number) → 1 closing sentence (baat ko band karo ya agla kadam batao). Office email ho ya essay — yahi dhaancha.

Model: ek poora paragraph

Walking to work is the easiest way to stay fit. Topic sentence — vishay (walking) + raay (easiest way to stay fit).

It needs no gym fee and no extra time, because you are travelling anyway. For example, a twenty-minute walk each way adds up to more than three hours a week. That is more than the 150 minutes of activity that doctors usually suggest. Teen support — wajah (because), udaharan (for example), saboot (150 minutes).

So if your office is close, leave the bike at home. Closing — padhne wale ko ek kaam de diya.

docs.title: 49.3 Topic sentence — pehli line me poori baat
docs.text:
Manager, teacher, examiner — sab jaldi me padhte hain, aur aksar sirf har paragraph ki pehli line. Agar pehli line kuch nahi batati, to baaki paragraph bhi nahi padha jaata.

Achhe topic sentence ka test

Topic sentence me do cheezein hon: vishay + us par aapki raay ya point. "Online classes" sirf vishay hai; "Online classes save time but make it harder to ask questions" poora topic sentence hai.

Kamzor shuruaat Mazboot topic sentence In this paragraph I will tell about my city. Pune is a city where old wadas and new IT parks stand side by side. As we all know, technology is very important. UPI has made it possible for a street vendor to accept payment from anyone. Exercise is a thing which is good. Even ten minutes of exercise a day can lift your mood. I want to say something about our project. Our project is two weeks behind because the vendor delivered late. Since ancient times, man has used water. Most Indian cities lose a large share of their water to leaking pipes.
  • Our project is two weeks behind because the vendor delivered late. Pehli hi line me kya hua (two weeks behind) aur kyun (vendor late) — manager ko aage padhne ka kaaran mil gaya.

docs.title: 49.4 Ek paragraph, ek idea
docs.text:
Jab ek paragraph me do-teen alag baatein aa jaati hain, to padhne wala bhool jaata hai ki shuru kis baat se hua tha. Har line ko topic sentence ke saamne khada karke dekho.

Figure 49.3. Canteen ki baat sach ho sakti hai — par wo library wale paragraph ki nahi hai.

Har line se ek sawaal

"Kya ye line topic sentence ko support karti hai?" Haan → rakho. Nahi → ya hata do, ya naya paragraph shuru karo. Naya paragraph tab bhi: jab samay, jagah ya bolne wala badle, ya ulti baat shuru ho.

docs.title: 49.5 Jodne wale shabd — however, therefore, for example
docs.text:
Linking words sadak ke signboard jaise hain: padhne wale ko pehle hi bata dete hain ki agli line kis taraf mudegi — aur baat, ulti baat, natija ya udaharan.

Figure 49.4. Signboard dekhte hi padhne wala jaan leta hai ki baat kis taraf ja rahi hai.

Linking word ka sahi istemaal

Pehle kaam pehchano (jodna, ulta, natija, udaharan), phir shabd chuno. Vaakya ki shuruaat me ho to uske baad comma: "However, the cost is high." Har line me mat lagao — ek paragraph me do-teen kaafi hain.

Kaam Shabd Example Aur ek baat moreover, in addition, also The flat is cheap. Moreover, it is near the metro. Ulti baat however, on the other hand The flat is cheap. However, it has no lift. Natija therefore, as a result The road was closed. As a result, we were late. Udaharan for example, for instance Some apps save time. For example, UPI. Kram first, then, finally First, fill the form. Then, pay the fee. Wajah because, since, due to + noun We stayed in because it rained. · due to the rain Saar in short, overall Overall, the trip was worth it.
  • The flat is cheap. However, it is on the fifth floor and has no lift. However ke baad halka sa ruko — sunne wala samajh jaata hai ki ab kami aa rahi hai.

docs.title: 49.6 Pehle aur baad — ek kamzor paragraph ki marammat
docs.text:
Ab sab kuch ek saath lagaate hain. Neeche ek college student ka asli jaisa paragraph hai — grammar ki galtiyan kam hain, par dhaancha nahi hai. Dekho ki kaise wahi baat saaf ho jaati hai.

Pehle — kamzor paragraph

Library is important. Our library closes at 5 pm. Many students are working in day time. And they come in evening and library is closed and they go back and they cannot study. Also canteen food is very bad. So library should open late.

Baad — sudhra hua paragraph

Our college library should stay open until 9 pm. At present it closes at 5 pm, which is exactly when many students finish their part-time jobs. For example, in my class of sixty, at least fifteen students work during the day and can study only in the evening. As a result, they either crowd into small rented rooms or do not study at all. Keeping the library open for four more hours would cost little, but it would give these students a fair chance.

  • Topic sentence aa gaya "Library is important" ki jagah saaf maang: open until 9 pm.
  • and… and… and… wali rail tooti Ek lamba vaakya teen saaf vaakyon me badla, which aur either… or ki madad se.
  • Saboot aur number jode "Many students" ki jagah "fifteen out of sixty" — ab baat me wazan hai.
  • Canteen wali line hata di Wo alag idea tha — uska apna paragraph banega.
  • Linking words aur closing sentence For example aur As a result ne lines ko joda; aakhri line ne baat band ki.

docs.title: 49.7 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Ye galtiyan grammar ki kitaab me kam dikhti hain, par emails, reports aur exam ke answers me roz milti hain — aksar isliye ki hum Hindi ka dhaancha seedha English me utaar dete hain.

Paragraph aur vaakya jodne ki asli galtiyan

  • Galat: I reached the office at nine, my manager was not there, I waited for one hour.
  • Sahi: I reached the office at nine, but my manager was not there. I waited for an hour.

  • Kyun: Teen poore vaakya sirf comma se nahi jud sakte. Jodne wala shabd lao (but) ya full stop lagao.

  • Galat: Although it was raining, but we went out.

  • Sahi: Although it was raining, we went out.

  • Kyun: Hindi me "haalaanki… lekin" dono lagte hain; English me although ke saath but nahi aata. Ek hi rakho.

  • Galat: Due to I was ill, I could not submit the assignment.

  • Sahi: Because I was ill, I could not submit the assignment.

  • Kyun: "Due to" ke baad noun aata hai (due to my illness). Poora vaakya (I was ill) aaye to "because".

  • Galat: The hotel was clean. Moreover, it was very expensive.

  • Sahi: The hotel was clean. However, it was very expensive.

  • Kyun: Moreover usi disha me ek aur baat jodta hai. Achhi baat ke baad kami aaye to ulti baat hai — however.

  • Galat: In this paragraph I am going to tell about my city. As we all know, Pune is a nice city.

  • Sahi: Pune is a city where old wadas and new IT parks stand side by side.
  • Kyun: Paragraph ke baare me baat mat karo — seedha baat karo. "As we all know" bhi kuch nahi jodta; use hata do.

Linking words namak jaise hain

Har vaakya "Moreover…", "Furthermore…", "Also…" se shuru karoge to likhai bhaari aur banawati lagegi. Zyadatar vaakyon ko linking word ki zaroorat hi nahi — sahi kram apne aap jodta hai.

docs.title: 49.8 Practice — Paragraphs
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Cycling ke fayde wale paragraph ke liye sabse achha topic sentence kaunsa hai?

  • In this paragraph I will tell about cycling.
  • Cycling to work saves money, keeps you fit and cuts traffic.
  • Cycling is a thing.
  • As we all know, cycling is very very good.
Jawaab

Cycling to work saves money, keeps you fit and cuts traffic.

Achha topic sentence vishay + raay dono batata hai, aur aage aane wale teen support points ka ishaara bhi deta hai. 'In this paragraph I will tell' kuch nahi batata.

Exercise 2

It rained heavily all night. ___, the match was cancelled.

  • As a result
  • However
  • For example
  • Moreover
Jawaab

As a result

Baarish wajah hai aur match cancel hona uska natija — isliye 'As a result' (ya Therefore).

Exercise 3

The flat is quite small. ___, it is only ten minutes from my office.

  • However
  • Therefore
  • For example
  • As a result
Jawaab

However

Pehli line kami batati hai, doosri fayda — ulti baat ke liye 'However'.

Exercise 4

'Ghar me paani bachana' wale paragraph me kaunsi line fit NAHI hoti?

  • Fix leaking taps as soon as you notice them.
  • Use a bucket instead of a hose to wash the car.
  • Our society also needs a new gym.
  • Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
Jawaab

Our society also needs a new gym.

Gym ek alag idea hai. Ek paragraph = ek idea — baaki teen lines paani bachane ko support karti hain.

Exercise 5

The ___ sentence tells the reader what the whole paragraph is about.

Jawaab

topic

Topic sentence paragraph ki pehli line hoti hai — poori baat ka saar, ek vaakya me.

Exercise 6

A good paragraph talks about only one main ___.

Jawaab

idea / point

Ek paragraph, ek idea. Naya idea aaye to naya paragraph — isse padhne wala raasta nahi bhatakta.

Exercise 7

Many students work during the day. ___ example, fifteen students in my class have part-time jobs.

Jawaab

For

'For example' udaharan laata hai, aur vaakya ki shuruaat me ho to uske baad comma lagta hai.

Exercise 8

Is vaakya me ek shabd faltu hai — us par tap karo.

Although the train was late, but we reached the meeting on time.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: but.

Sahi roop: Although the train was late, we reached the meeting on time.

Hindi me 'haalaanki… lekin' dono lagte hain, English me nahi. 'Although' ke saath 'but' kabhi nahi — ek hi rakho.

Exercise 9

Galat shabd dhoondo.

Due to I was unwell, I missed the class.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: Due.

Sahi roop: Because I was unwell, I missed the class.

'Due to' ke baad noun aata hai (due to my illness). Poora vaakya (I was unwell) aaye to 'Because' lagao.

Exercise 10

Jodne wale shabd ko uske kaam se jodo.

A B however udaharan therefore ek aur baat jodna for example aakhri point moreover ulti baat finally natija Jawaab

however — ulti baat; therefore — natija; for example — udaharan; moreover — ek aur baat jodna; finally — aakhri point

however = contrast, therefore = result, for example = udaharan, moreover = addition, finally = kram ka ant.

Exercise 11

Sahi kram me vaakya banao.

Shabd: saves / money. / time / new / plan / and / the / However, / both

Jawaab

However, the new plan saves both time and money.

'However' vaakya ki shuruaat me aaye to uske baad comma. Phir seedha subject + verb + object.

Exercise 12

Ye line bolo — 'As a result' ke baad halka sa ruko.

Jawaab

Bolo: As a result, the project was finished on time.

Linking word ke baad comma = bolte waqt chhota sa viraam. Sunne wale ko pata chal jaata hai ki ab natija aa raha hai.

Aage kya karein

Apna aakhri lamba email ya assignment kholo. Har paragraph ki sirf pehli line padho — kya unse poori baat samajh aati hai? Nahi aati, to wahi pehli lines dobara likho. Ye ek aadat aapki likhai badal degi.

docs.title: Chapter 32: Small talk aur raay dena
docs.text:
Small talk aur raay dena — baat shuru karna, chalana, khatam karna

Office ki lift, shaadi ka buffet, conference ka chai break — yahi do-teen minute ki baatein rishte banati hain. Hum me se bahut log yahan chup ho jaate hain, kyonki dimaag me ek hi sawaal ghoomta hai: "kya bolun?" Sach ye hai ki small talk me koi gehri baat nahi chahiye — bas ek dhaancha chahiye: shuru kaise karein, aage kaise badhaayein, apni raay kaise rakhein, aur izzat se kaise niklein. Har line par 🔊 hai. Suno, saath me bolo, aur kal kisi se try karo.

docs.title: 32.1 Small talk ka naksha — chaar kadam
docs.text:
Jab dimaag me raasta saaf ho, to ghabraahat aadhi ho jaati hai. Har achhi chhoti baat-cheet in chaar kadmon se guzarti hai — aur beech ke do kadam baar-baar ghoomte hain.

Figure 32.1. Kadam 2 aur 3 ek jhoola hain — aap sawaal poochhte ho, wo batate hain, aap apni baat jodte ho, phir naya sawaal. Jab baat thandi pade, kadam 4.

Chaar kadam

Open → Follow up → Share → Close. Beech ke do kadam (sawaal aur apni baat) baar-baar ghoomte hain — yahi baat-cheet ko zinda rakhta hai. Small talk ka maqsad jaankari lena nahi, judna hai.

Pehli mulaqat me ye topics mat chhedo

Safe: mausam, traffic, jis event par aap ho, khaana, kaam, travel, movies, cricket. Avoid: salary, "shaadi kab kar rahe ho?", weight, dharm, politics. Hamare yahan ye sawaal pyaar se poochhe jaate hain, par English bolne wale maahaul me ye bahut personal lagte hain.

docs.title: 32.2 Baat shuru karna — mausam, kaam, aur jahan aap dono hain
docs.text:
Sabse aasaan opener wo hai jo aap dono ke saamne hai — wahi jagah, wahi mausam, wahi khaana. Ek chhota statement, phir ek sawaal. Bas itna.

Kahan English line Suno Shaadi / party So, how do you know the bride and groom? Conference Is this your first time at this conference? Mausam It's so hot today, isn't it? Baarish Looks like the rain's finally here. Kaam What kind of work do you do? Office How's your week going so far? Khaana Have you tried the paneer? It's really good. Naya chehra Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Kavya.

Opener ka formula

Statement + sawaal: "Great music tonight. Do you know the band?" Statement se maahaul banta hai, sawaal se saamne wale ko bolne ka mauka milta hai. Akela statement ("Hot day.") ya akela sawaal ("Your name?") adhoora lagta hai.

Mini-dialogue — conference ka chai break

Haalat: conference me chai break hai. Aap akele khade ho, bagal me ek aur insaan bhi akela hai. Pehle Aap bolo, phir Meera ki line bhi.

  • Aap: Hi! Is this your first time at this conference? Shuruaat — jagah ke baare me sawaal.
  • Meera: No, second time, actually. Last year's was in Bengaluru. "actually" = asal me. Usne extra detail di — achha signal hai.
