  • Aap: Oh, nice. I'm Rohan, by the way. I work in logistics. "by the way" se naam beech me aaram se aa jaata hai.
  • Meera: Nice to meet you, Rohan. I'm Meera. I'm a data analyst. Naam ke saath kaam — ab follow-up ka raasta khul gaya.
  • Aap: So what brings you here this year? "Is saal yahan kaise?" — bahut natural follow-up.
  • Meera: Mostly the AI sessions. My team wants to try some new tools. Ab aap poochh sakte ho: "Oh, which tools?" — baat chal padi.

docs.title: 32.3 Baat aage badhana — follow-up sawaal
docs.text:
Baat-cheet aksar yahin mar jaati hai: sawaal aaya, ek shabd ka jawaab gaya, phir chuppi. Isse bachne ke do hathiyaar hain — ping-pong wala jawaab, aur achhe follow-up sawaal.

Figure 32.2. Detail saamne wale ko naya topic deti hai, aur sawaal ball unke paale me wapas bhejta hai.

Ping-pong jawaab

Jawaab + ek extra detail + sawaal wapas. "Pune. I moved here for work last year. What about you?" Ek shabd ka jawaab ball ko zameen par gira deta hai — phir dono khade rehte hain.

  • Oh, really? How did you get into that? Us kaam me kaise aaye? — kisi ke kaam ke baare me sabse achha sawaal.
  • What's that like? Wo kaisa hai? — naya shehar, naya kaam, kuch bhi.
  • That sounds interesting. What do you enjoy most about it? Isme sabse achha kya lagta hai? — log apni pasand ke baare me khushi se bolte hain.
  • How long have you been doing that? Kab se kar rahe ho?
  • And what about you? Aur aap? — ball wapas bhejne ki sabse chhoti line.

Band sawaal ko khula banao

Band: "Do you like Pune?" → jawaab sirf haan ya na. Khula: "What do you like about Pune?" → jawaab me kahani aati hai. What, how, why se shuru hone wale sawaal baat ko lamba chalaate hain.

docs.title: 32.4 Apni raay dena — I think, In my view, To be honest
docs.text:
Raay dene se baat me jaan aati hai. Par Hindi se seedha anuvaad karne par raay aksar zyada sakht sunai deti hai. English me raay ko thoda naram karke rakha jaata hai — aur kitna naram, ye aap phrase se tay karte ho.

Figure 32.3. Roz ki baat-cheet me beech ki seedhi ( I think ) sabse safe hai. Sabse upar wala step tab, jab aapke paas pakki wajah ho. Line Kab Suno I think the new metro has really helped. Roz ki, normal raay In my view, the second half of the film was better. Soch-samajh wali, thodi formal To be honest, I didn't enjoy the food much. Sach jo shayad pasand na aaye Personally, I prefer working from the office. Apni pasand — doosron par thopna nahi I might be wrong, but I think it's going to rain. Bahut naram, pakka nahi pata If you ask me, cricket is more fun in the stadium. Casual, doston ke beech

Raay + wajah

Raay akeli kamzor lagti hai — use because ke saath do: "I think remote work is great because I save two hours a day." Aur "According to me" ki jagah "I think" ya "In my view" bolo.

docs.title: 32.5 Sehmat aur asehmat — bina jhagde ke
docs.text:
Asehmat hona bura nahi hai; tareeka bura ho sakta hai. Seedha "No, you are wrong" bolne se baat wahin band ho jaati hai. English bolne wale pehle saamne wale ki baat ko maante hain, phir apni rakhte hain.

Figure 32.4. Daayein taraf jaate hue bhi aawaaz naram rehti hai. Asehmati ka sabse sakht roop bhi I see it differently hai — you are wrong nahi.

Asehmat hone ka formula

Maan lo + but + apni baat. "That's a fair point, but I think traffic is the bigger problem." Pehla hissa izzat deta hai, doosra aapki raay. Dono zaroori hain.

Mini-dialogue — work from home par behas

Haalat: lunch par colleague Aman kehta hai ki ghar se kaam behtar hai. Aap aadhe sehmat ho, aadhe nahi.

  • Aman: I think working from home is so much better. Raay — "I think" ke saath.
  • Aap: I know what you mean. No traffic, right? Pehle maano — "main samajh raha hoon".
  • Aman: Exactly! I save almost two hours a day. Raay + wajah.
  • Aap: That's true. But to be honest, I find it harder to focus at home. Maan lo + but + apni baat. Bina jhagde ke asehmati.
  • Aman: Fair enough. I guess it depends on the person. "Fair enough" = theek hai, baat me dum hai.
  • Aap: Yeah, I suppose it does. Dono khush — behas khatam, dosti baaki.

docs.title: 32.6 Baat khatam karna — izzat se
docs.text:
Achhi baat-cheet ka ant bhi achha hona chahiye. Bina kuch kahe mud jaana, ya achaanak "OK, bye" bol dena rude lagta hai. Teen chhote kadam — aur aap ek achhi yaad chhod kar jaate ho.

Figure 32.5. Signal saamne wale ko taiyaar karta hai, wajah se wo bura nahi maanta, aur garam line yaad reh jaati hai.
  • Well, it was really nice talking to you. "Well…" — sabse chhota aur sabse saaf signal.
  • I should let you get back to your friends. "Main aapko roke nahi rakhta" — wajah unki taraf se, bahut sharif tareeka.
  • I'm going to grab some food before it's all gone. Halki-fulki wajah — party me kaam aati hai.
  • I need to catch up with a colleague, but let's talk later. "catch up with" = kisi se milkar haal-chaal lena.
  • Let's stay in touch. Are you on LinkedIn? Agar rishta aage badhana hai.
  • Enjoy the rest of the evening! Aakhri garam line.

Teen kadam ka ant

Signal ("Well…") + wajah ("I should go and say hi to my boss") + garam line ("It was lovely meeting you"). Wajah chhoti aur sachchi rakho. Bina bole gaayab hona ya seedha "OK, bye" — dono rude lagte hain.

docs.title: 32.7 Ek poori baat-cheet — shuru se ant tak
docs.text:
Ab sab kuch ek saath — opener, follow-up, ping-pong, raay, sehmati aur ant. Dono roles bolo; doosre ki line bolne se aapka kaan bhi taiyaar hota hai.

Mini-dialogue — shaadi ka buffet

Haalat: reception me buffet ki lambi line. Aage Priya khadi hai, aap use nahi jaante.

  • Aap: This queue is moving so slowly! Everything looks delicious, though. Opener — jo saamne hai uske baare me statement.
  • Priya: I know! Someone told me the biryani is the best thing here. Usne baat pakdi aur detail di.
  • Aap: Good to know. So, are you from the bride's side or the groom's? Shaadi ka sabse aasaan follow-up.
  • Priya: The bride's. We went to college together. And you? Ping-pong: jawaab + detail + sawaal wapas.
  • Aap: I work with the groom. I'm Vikram, by the way. Naam "by the way" ke saath.
  • Priya: I'm Priya. Nice to meet you. What do you two work on? Khula sawaal — "kis cheez par kaam karte ho?"
  • Aap: We build apps for hospitals. It's busy, but I really enjoy it. Jawaab + feeling. Ab Priya ke paas bolne ko kuch hai.
  • Priya: That sounds interesting. I think technology in healthcare is the future. Raay — "I think" ke saath.
  • Aap: I couldn't agree more. Well, I'll let you get your food. It was lovely talking to you. Sehmati, phir signal + wajah + garam line.
  • Priya: You too, Vikram. Enjoy the biryani! Achha ant — dono muskura ke alag.

docs.title: 32.8 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Ye galtiyan grammar ki kam, anuvaad ki zyada hain — Hindi ka saancha English me utaar dene se aati hain. Sunne wala samajh to jaata hai, par baat ajeeb lagti hai.

Small talk ki aam galtiyan

  • Galat: What is your good name?
  • Sahi: What's your name? / Sorry, I didn't catch your name.

  • Kyun: "Good name" = "shubh naam" ka seedha anuvaad. Hamare yahan izzat hai, English me ajeeb lagta hai.

  • Galat: Myself Rahul, from Pune.

  • Sahi: I'm Rahul. I'm from Pune.

  • Kyun: "Myself" se introduction shuru nahi hota. Seedha "I'm…" — chhota aur natural.

  • Galat: I am agree with you.

  • Sahi: I agree with you.

  • Kyun: "Agree" khud verb hai — "am" ki zaroorat nahi. Ulta bhi: "I don't agree", "I am not agree" nahi.

  • Galat: According to me, the film was boring.

  • Sahi: I thought the film was boring. / In my view, it was boring.

  • Kyun: "According to" doosron ke liye hai — according to the news, according to my doctor. Apni raay = "I think".

  • Galat: So, how much do you earn? When are you getting married?

  • Sahi: So, what do you enjoy most about your job?
  • Kyun: Salary aur shaadi pehli mulaqat me bahut personal maane jaate hain. Kaam ke baare me poochho, kamaai ke baare me nahi.

docs.title: 32.9 Practice — Small talk
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Conference ke chai break me kisi anjaan se baat shuru karni hai. Sabse natural opener kaunsa hai?

  • Is this your first time at this conference?
  • What is your good name?
  • How much salary do you get?
  • Myself Rohan, tell me about you.
Jawaab

Is this your first time at this conference?

Jo jagah aap dono share kar rahe ho, uske baare me sawaal — sabse safe aur sabse natural. Baaki teeno ya to anuvaad hain ya bahut personal.

Exercise 2

Apni raay ko mazboot banane ke liye uske saath kya jodna chahiye?

  • a reason with 'because'
  • the word 'definitely' twice
  • 'according to me' at the start
  • a louder voice
Jawaab

a reason with 'because'

Raay + wajah = mazboot raay. 'I think X because Y' — sunne wala asehmat ho sakta hai, par aapko halke me nahi lega.

Exercise 3

Colleague ki baat se aap asehmat ho. Sabse polite jawaab kaunsa hai?

  • You are wrong.
  • That's a fair point, but I see it differently.
  • No, no, that is not correct.
  • I am not agree.
Jawaab

That's a fair point, but I see it differently.

Formula: maan lo + but + apni baat. Pehla hissa izzat deta hai. 'I am not agree' to grammar ke hisaab se bhi galat hai.

Exercise 4

I ___ with you. The traffic is terrible these days.

Hint: 'am' lagane ki zaroorat nahi.

Jawaab

agree / totally agree / completely agree

'Agree' khud verb hai — 'I agree', 'I am agree' nahi.

Exercise 5

Well, it was really nice ___ to you.

Hint: Baat khatam karne ki line — verb + ing.

Jawaab

talking / speaking

'It was nice talking to you' — baat-cheet ke ant ki sabse garam line.

Exercise 6

Is introduction me ek shabd ajeeb hai — us par tap karo.

Myself Anjali and I work in a bank.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: Myself.

Sahi roop: I'm Anjali and I work in a bank.

Introduction 'Myself…' se nahi, 'I'm…' se shuru hota hai.

Exercise 7

Shabdon ko sahi kram me lagao — ek khula follow-up sawaal banao.

Shabd: do / What / most / job / you / your / about / enjoy

Jawaab

What do you enjoy most about your job

Wh-word + do + you + verb — ye khula sawaal hai, iska jawaab haan/na me nahi aata.

Exercise 8

Line ko uske kaam se jodo.

A B How did you get into that? politely asehmat hona To be honest, I didn't like it. baat khatam karna I see your point, but… follow-up sawaal I'll let you get back to it. sach wali raay Jawaab

How did you get into that? — follow-up sawaal; To be honest, I didn't like it. — sach wali raay; I see your point, but… — politely asehmat hona; I'll let you get back to it. — baat khatam karna

Har line ka ek kaam hai — sawaal, raay, asehmati, ant. Yahi kadam small talk ko chalaate hain.

Exercise 9

Party se nikalne ki line bolo — garam aur saaf.

Jawaab

Bolo: It was really nice talking to you

'talking to you' ko jodkar bolo — 'tawking-tu-yu'. Aakhri 'you' par aawaaz neeche.

Exercise 10

Ab politely asehmat ho kar dikhao.

Jawaab

Bolo: That's a fair point, but I see it differently

'but' ke baad zara ruko — isse lagta hai aapne unki baat sach me suni.

Exercise 11

Ek opener bolo — sawaal ke ant me aawaaz upar.

Jawaab

Bolo: Is this your first time here

Haan/na wale sawaal me aakhri shabd par aawaaz upar jaati hai — 'here?'

Aage kya karein

Is hafte ek naye insaan se chaar kadam wali baat karo — chahe wo society ka guard ho ya office ka naya intern. Pehli baar ajeeb lagega, teesri baar aadat ban jaayegi.

docs.title: Chapter 48: Spelling ke niyam
docs.text:
Spelling ke niyam — ratna kam, samajhna zyada

Email me ek galat spelling — recieve, seperate, definately — aur padhne wala turant soch leta hai ki likhne wale ne dhyan nahi diya. Achhi khabar ye hai ki English spelling jitni ulti-pulti lagti hai, utni hai nahi. Kuch gine-chune niyam zyadatar shabd sambhaal lete hain; bache hue apvaad hum ek list me yaad kar lenge.

Ek line me

Most English spelling follows a few rules about adding endings — double the consonant, drop the e, change y to i. Learn the rules first, then memorise the exceptions. Pehle niyam samjho, phir sirf apvaad yaad karo — poori dictionary nahi.

docs.title: 48.1 Consonant kab double hota hai
docs.text:
stopped ya stoped? beginning ya begining? Ye sawaal roz office ke email me aata hai. Iska jawaab teen chhote sawaalon me chhupa hai — neeche ka naksha ek baar follow kar lo.

Figure 48.1. Teeno sawaalon ka jawaab haan ho, tabhi double. Ek bhi nahi — to single hi rehne do.

1-1-1 ka niyam

Ek syllable, ek vowel, ek aakhri consonant + vowel wala suffix = consonant double: stop → stopped, big → bigger. Lambe shabd me sirf tab, jab zor aakhri hisse par ho: begin → beginning, par visit → visited.

  • We stopped the meeting at five. stop = ek syllable, ek vowel (o), ek consonant (p) → stopped.
  • This is only the beginning. be-GIN — zor aakhri hisse par, isliye n double: beginning.
  • She visited her parents on Sunday. VI-sit — zor pehle hisse par, isliye t single: visited.

British twist — travel, cancel, label

British English me aakhri l hamesha double hota hai, chahe zor kahin bhi ho: travelled, cancelled, labelled, modelling. American me single: traveled, canceled. Bharat me British chalti hai, isliye school aur office me travelled likho.

docs.title: 48.2 Silent e kab girta hai
docs.text:
make ka aakhri e bola nahi jaata — aur yahi e suffix lagate waqt sabse zyada galtiyan karwata hai. Niyam bas itna hai: suffix ka pehla akshar dekho.

Figure 48.2. Ek hi shabd, do raaste. Suffix ka pehla akshar tay karta hai ki e rahega ya jaayega.

Silent e ka faisla

Suffix vowel se shuru ho (-ing, -able, -ed) → e girao: make → making, use → usable. Suffix consonant se shuru ho (-ful, -ment, -ly) → e rakho: care → careful, move → movement.

Shabd Vowel suffix (e gira) Consonant suffix (e raha) make making — hope hoping hopeful care caring careful move moving movement use usable useful manage managing management achieve achieving achievement

Apvaad jo yaad karne padenge

c / g wale shabd e rakhte hain taaki aawaz naram rahe: noticeable, manageable, courageous. Bina wajah e girta hai: truly, argument, ninth, awful. ee wale shabd e nahi girate: seeing, agreeing, fleeing.

docs.title: 48.3 y kab i ban jaata hai
docs.text:
happyness ya happiness? studys ya studies? Bas y se theek pehle wala akshar dekho — wahi jawaab hai.

Figure 48.3. Sirf ek akshar dekhna hai — y ka padosi.

y ka niyam

Consonant + y → i: happy → happiness, study → studied. Vowel + y → y rehta: play → played. Aur -ing se pehle y kabhi nahi badalta: studying, carrying.

  • She studies late and still looks happier than all of us. stud-y → studies (d consonant hai); happ-y → happier.
  • The children enjoyed the play. enjo-y → o vowel hai, isliye y bacha raha: enjoyed.

Chaar puraane apvaad

day → daily, pay → paid, say → said, lay → laid. Inme vowel + y hai, phir bhi i ban gaya — bas yaad kar lo.

docs.title: 48.4 i before e — aur uske apvaad
docs.text:
receive ya recieve, believe ya beleive — ie aur ei ka confusion Indian writers ki sabse aam spelling galti hai. Purani tukbandi aaj bhi kaam aati hai, bas uska poora roop yaad rakho.

ie ya ei — teen line ki trick

"ee" ki aawaz → ie: believe, piece, achieve. c ke turant baad → ei: receive, ceiling, receipt. "ay" ki aawaz → ei: eight, weigh, neighbour.

Kab Spelling Examples "ee" ki aawaz ie believe, achieve, piece, field, chief, niece, brief c ke baad, "ee" ki aawaz ei receive, receipt, ceiling, deceive, perceive "ay" ki aawaz ei eight, weight, neighbour, vein, reign Apvaad — rat lo ei seize, weird, either, neither, protein, foreign, leisure, their c ke baad bhi ie (aawaz "ee" nahi) ie science, ancient, efficient, society
  • I received the receipt from my neighbour. receive, receipt — c ke baad ei. neighbour — "ay" ki aawaz, isliye ei.

docs.title: 48.5 -able ya -ible
docs.text:
acceptable ya acceptible? Dono ki aawaz ek jaisi hai, isliye kaan madad nahi karte. Par ek seedha test hai jo zyadatar shabdon par kaam karta hai.

Figure 48.4. Kainchi chalao: suffix kaato aur dekho ki peeche kya bacha.

-able / -ible ka test

Suffix hatane par poora shabd bache → -able (acceptable, comfortable). Adhoora tukda bache → -ible (possible, visible, terrible). Zyadatar shabdon par ye test sahi baithta hai.

Kuch shabd test todte hain

responsible, flexible, accessible, sensible — inke andar poore shabd chhupe hain, phir bhi -ible lagta hai. Aur noticeable, changeable me e isliye bacha hai taaki c/g ki aawaz naram rahe. Ye chhe shabd alag se yaad kar lo.

docs.title: 48.6 British ya American — colour ya color
docs.text:
Do spelling systems hain, aur dono sahi hain. Par Bharat me school, board exam, sarkari kaam aur zyadatar akhbaar British spelling follow karte hain. Dikkat tab hoti hai jab software chupchaap American spelling laga deta hai.

Pattern British (Bharat) American -our / -or colour, favour, behaviour color, favor, behavior -re / -er centre, metre, theatre center, meter, theater -ise / -ize organise, realise, apologise organize, realize, apologize -ll / -l travelled, cancelled, jewellery traveled, canceled, jewelry -ogue / -og catalogue, dialogue catalog, dialog -ce / -se licence (noun), defence license, defense -yse / -yze analyse, paralyse analyze, paralyze Alag shabd programme, cheque, tyre, grey program, check, tire, gray

Asli galti mix karna hai

"color" likhna galti nahi — galti hai ek hi email me colour aur color dono likhna. Word ya Google Docs me language English (India) ya English (UK) set kar lo. Computer ke liye program dono systems me chalta hai, aur -ize British me bhi galat nahi — bas ek chuno aur poore document me wahi rakho.

docs.title: 48.7 30 shabd jo hum sabse zyada galat likhte hain
docs.text: Ye list Indian offices, colleges aur job applications me sach me dikhne wali galtiyon se bani hai. Har shabd ke saath ek chhoti si trick hai — trick yaad rahegi to spelling bhi.

docs.title: Double letters ka khel
docs.text: Sahi Aam galti Yaad kaise rakhein accommodation accomodation Do c, do m — kamra itna bada ki dono double fit ho jaayein. occurrence occurence Do c, do r, aur ant me -ence. recommend reccomend re + commend: ek c, do m. necessary neccessary Shirt me ek Collar, do Sleeves — ek c, do s. committee commitee Sab double: mm, tt, ee. embarrass embarass Itni sharam ki do r aur do s. beginning begining be-GIN + n + ing — 1-1-1 ka niyam. tomorrow tommorow to + morrow: ek m, do r.

docs.title: Vowel ki gadbad
docs.text: Sahi Aam galti Yaad kaise rakhein separate seperate "There is a rat in separate." definitely definately Andar "finite" chhupa hai: de-FINITE-ly. privilege priviledge Na d, na a: pri-vi-lege. grammar grammer Ant me -ar; poore shabd me do a. calendar calender Ant me -ar, bilkul grammar jaisa. independent independant Ant me -ent: in-de-pen-dent. existence existance exist + ence — teeno vowel e. maintenance maintainance maintain se bana, par "ai" gir gaya: main-te-nance.

docs.title: ie/ei aur chhupe hue akshar
docs.text: Sahi Aam galti Yaad kaise rakhein receive recieve c ke turant baad e-i. achieve acheive "ee" ki aawaz, aur c nahi — to i-e. believe beleive "Never believe a lie." foreign foriegn Apvaad hai — ei. Ise rat lo. government goverment govern + ment — n mat chhodo. environment enviroment environ + ment — yahan bhi n. Wednesday Wensday Likhte waqt mann me bolo: Wed-nes-day.

docs.title: Indian English ke khaas
docs.text:
Sahi Aam galti Yaad kaise rakhein until untill till me do l, until me sirf ek. across accross a + cross — ek hi c. truly truely true ka e gir jaata hai (apvaad). pronunciation pronounciation pronounce me "ou", par pronunciation me sirf "u". argument arguement argue ka e gir jaata hai. colleague collegue col + league — cricket league wali spelling. guarantee gaurantee g-u-a: pehle u, phir a.

Ek hafte me paanch shabd

Poori list ek din me mat rato. Har hafte paanch shabd chuno, unhe haath se paanch-paanch baar bolte hue likho, aur us hafte ke har email me kam se kam ek baar use karo. Chhe hafte me list khatam.

docs.title: 48.8 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Ye vaakya asli office emails aur applications jaise hain. Har ek me spelling ki galti hai — aur har galti ke peeche ek niyam hai jo hum upar padh chuke hain.

Office aur college ki asli spelling galtiyan

  • Galat: I am writting to inform you about the delay.
  • Sahi: I am writing to inform you about the delay.

  • Kyun: write ka silent e girta hai → writing (ek t). written me do t hain — wo alag shabd hai.

  • Galat: We will definately recieve the payment by Monday.

  • Sahi: We will definitely receive the payment by Monday.

  • Kyun: de-FINITE-ly. Aur c ke baad hamesha e-i: receive.

  • Galat: Kindly accomodate my request for a seperate room.

  • Sahi: Please accommodate my request for a separate room.

  • Kyun: accommodate me do c, do m. separate me "a rat" chhupa hai.

  • Galat: It was a priviledge to work with such a commited team.

  • Sahi: It was a privilege to work with such a committed team.

  • Kyun: privilege me d nahi hota. com-MIT — zor aakhri hisse par, isliye t double: committed.

  • Galat: I do not want to loose this oppurtunity.

  • Sahi: I do not want to lose this opportunity.
  • Kyun: lose = khona, loose = dheela. op-por-tu-ni-ty — "port" ki tarah do p ke saath shuru.

Spell-check sab nahi pakadta

loose/lose, their/there, its/it's, then/than, affect/effect — ye sab asli shabd hain, isliye laal line nahi aati. Email bhejne se pehle ek baar zor se padho; kaan wo pakad lete hain jo aankh chhod deti hai.

docs.title: 48.9 Practice — Spelling
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Is vaakya me ek spelling galat hai — us shabd par tap karo.

We will definately send the report today.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: definately.

Sahi roop: We will definitely send the report today.

Andar 'finite' chhupa hai: de-FINITE-ly. Is shabd me 'a' kahin nahi hai.

Exercise 2

Galat spelling wala shabd dhoondo.

I have made a seperate folder for each client.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: seperate.

Sahi roop: I have made a separate folder for each client.

'There is a rat in separate' — sep-A-rate. Beech me a hai, e nahi.

Exercise 3

Ek shabd ki spelling galat hai — dhoondo.

The hotel could not give accomodation to all the guests.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: accomodation.

Sahi roop: The hotel could not give accommodation to all the guests.

accommodation me do c aur do m. Ek m chhod dena sabse aam galti hai.

Exercise 4

Galat shabd par tap karo.

Did you recieve my email about the meeting?

Jawaab

Galat shabd: recieve.

Sahi roop: Did you receive my email about the meeting?

c ke turant baad e-i aata hai: receive, receipt, ceiling.

Exercise 5

-ing lagaane par kis shabd ka aakhri consonant double hoga?

  • begin
  • visit
  • open
  • happen

Hint: Har shabd bolke dekho — zor kahan padta hai?

Jawaab

begin

be-GIN me zor aakhri hisse par hai, isliye beginning. VI-sit, O-pen, HAP-pen me zor pehle hisse par hai — isliye visiting, opening, happening, single consonant ke saath.

Exercise 6

Kaunsi spelling sahi hai?

  • comfortible
  • visible
  • acceptible
  • dependible
Jawaab

visible

'vis' akela koi shabd nahi, isliye -ible. comfort, accept, depend poore shabd hain — unke saath -able lagta hai: comfortable, acceptable, dependable.

Exercise 7

Indian school, board exam aur sarkari kaam me kaunsi spelling system chalti hai?

  • British
  • American
  • Dono ek hi document me mix karke
  • Koi niyam nahi
Jawaab

British

Bharat me British spelling chalti hai — colour, centre, organise, travelled. American galat nahi hai, par ek document me ek hi system rakho.

Exercise 8

American English me 'centre' ko ___ likhte hain.

Jawaab

center

British -re, American -er: centre/center, metre/meter, theatre/theater.

Exercise 9

Silent e tab girta hai jab suffix ek ___ se shuru ho — jaise make + ing = making.

Hint: Consonant ya vowel?

Jawaab

vowel

Vowel se shuru suffix (-ing, -able, -ed) aaye to e girta hai: making, usable. Consonant se shuru suffix (-ful, -ment) aaye to e rehta hai: careful, movement.

Exercise 10

Shabd + suffix ko uske sahi roop se jodo.

A B happy + ness stopped make + ing careful stop + ed played care + ful happiness play + ed making Jawaab

happy + ness — happiness; make + ing — making; stop + ed — stopped; care + ful — careful; play + ed — played

happy: consonant + y, to y → i. make: vowel suffix, to e gira. stop: 1-1-1, to double. care: consonant suffix, to e raha. play: vowel + y, to y raha.

Exercise 11

Sahi kram me vaakya banao.

Shabd: this / colleagues / to / definitely / recommend / my / would / I / hotel

Jawaab

I would definitely recommend this hotel to my colleagues

Subject (I) + would + adverb (definitely) + verb (recommend) + object. Spelling bhi dekho: definitely, recommend (ek c, do m), colleagues.

Exercise 12

Ab ye line bolo — har mushkil shabd ko saaf, hisson me.

Jawaab

Bolo: It is necessary to separate the old receipts

Hisse yaad rakho: NE-ces-sa-ry, SEP-a-rate, re-CEIPT (p silent hai). Hisson me bolne se spelling bhi pakki hoti hai.

Aage kya karein

Apne phone ke notes me ek "meri spelling" list banao. Jab bhi koi shabd galat likho aur spell-check pakde, use list me daal do. Mahine ke ant me wahi list aapki sabse kaam ki dictionary hogi.

docs.title: Chapter 17: Subject-verb agreement
docs.text:
Subject-verb agreement — "He go" ya "He goes"?

Agreement ka matlab hai mel — subject aur verb ka mel. Hindi me ye mel hota hai lekin alag tareeke se (ladka jaata hai / ladke jaate hain), isliye hum ye cheez jaante hain. Dikkat sirf do jagah hoti hai: pehla, English me -s singular ke saath lagta hai (ulta lagta hai!), aur doosra, kabhi-kabhi asli subject chhup jaata hai beech ke shabdon ke peeche. Dono cheezein is chapter me hamesha ke liye saaf.

Ek line me

A singular subject takes a singular verb; a plural subject takes a plural verb. Ek subject → ek wala verb. Kai subject → kai wala verb. Aur yaad rakho — verb me -s matlab singular.

docs.title: 17.1 Buniyaadi naksha
docs.text:
Subject Present Simple be (present) be (past) have I go am was have You go are were have He / She / It goes is was has We go are were have They go are were have

-s ki dohri gadbad

Noun me -s lagne se wo plural banta hai: boy → boys. Verb me -s lagne se wo singular banta hai: go → goes. Yani ek vaakya me -s ya noun par hoga ya verb par — dono par nahi. The boy runs ✓ The boys run ✓ The boys runs ✗

docs.title: 17.2 Asli subject dhoondo — beech ke shabd gin-tee me nahi
docs.text:
Sabse zyada galti yahan hoti hai. Subject aur verb ke beech koi lamba phrase aa jaata hai, aur dimaag us phrase ke aakhri shabd ko subject samajh leta hai. Trick ye hai: us beech wale hisse par kaalpanik kaanch laga do aur bhool jao.

Figure 17.1. Neela shabd = asli subject. Gulabi dotted dabba = wo hissa jo verb par koi asar nahi daalta. Hara teer = kiska mel kisse hai.

Ye sab beech wale shabd verb nahi badalte

of, with, along with, together with, as well as, including, besides, in addition to, accompanied by The minister, along with his officers, has arrived. Subject "the minister" hai — ek insaan. "Officers" se koi farq nahi padta.

docs.title: 17.3 Hamesha singular — ye yaad rakhna hai
docs.text:
Subject Sahi Galat each Each boy has a book. Each boy have… every Every student was present. Every student were… everyone / everybody Everyone knows it. Everyone know it. someone / somebody Somebody is at the door. Somebody are… nobody / no one Nobody came. — anyone / anybody Does anybody know him? Do anybody know… either / neither (akele) Neither is correct. Neither are correct. one of + plural One of my friends is a doctor. One of my friend is… the number of The number of cases is rising. The number of cases are… each of / every one of Each of the girls sings well. Each of the girls sing…

'one of my friend' — do galtiyan ek saath

  • Galat: One of my friend are coming today.
  • Sahi: One of my friends is coming today.
  • Kyun: Socho: "mere doston me se ek". "Doston" plural hai (friends), par baat ek ki ho rahi hai — isliye verb singular (is). Yahi rule "one of the best players", "one of my sisters" sab par chalta hai.

docs.title: 17.4 "A number of" vs "The number of"
docs.text: Phrase Matlab Verb Example a number of kai, bahut se plural A number of students are absent. the number of ginti, sankhya singular The number of students is falling. a lot of / plenty of noun par depend noun dekho A lot of water is wasted. · A lot of people are waiting. 50% of / half of noun par depend noun dekho Half of the cake is gone. · Half of the boys are here.

docs.title: 17.5 Do subject jude hain — tab kya?
docs.text:
Jodne wala shabd Rule Example and plural Ravi and Sita are friends. and (ek hi cheez) singular Bread and butter is my breakfast. or / nor paas wale se mel Ravi or his brothers are coming. either… or paas wale se mel Either the boys or the teacher is wrong. neither… nor paas wale se mel Neither the teacher nor the boys are wrong. not only… but also paas wale se mel Not only the players but also the coach was blamed.

Chalaaki ki salaah

either/or aur neither/nor wale vaakya me, agar ho sake to plural subject ko aakhir me rakho. Tab verb plural ho jaata hai aur vaakya kaan ko zyada natural lagta hai. Neither the manager nor the workers were happy.

docs.title: 17.6 Collective nouns — ek ya kai?
docs.text:
Team, family, class, committee, government, jury, staff — ye ek group hain. Jab group ek ikaai ki tarah kaam kar raha ho to singular; jab group ke log alag-alag kaam kar rahe hon to plural.

  • The team is playing well today. Poori team ek ikaai ki tarah — singular.
  • The team are arguing among themselves. Team ke log aapas me — alag-alag log, isliye plural.

Teen shabd jo hamesha plural hain

police, people, cattle — inke saath verb hamesha plural. The police have arrested him. ✓ The police has arrested him. ✗ Many people were waiting. ✓

docs.title: 17.7 Dikhne me plural, par singular
docs.text:
Kism Shabd Example Vishay ke naam mathematics, physics, economics, politics, statistics Mathematics is my favourite subject. Bimaari measles, mumps, diabetes Measles is contagious. Khabar news The news is good. Uncountable information, advice, furniture, luggage, work, money This information is useful. Doori, paisa, samay — ek ikaai — Ten kilometres is a long walk. · Five hundred rupees is too much. Kitaab / film ka naam — "Three Idiots" is a great film.

Aur inka ulta — dikhne me ek, par plural

scissors, trousers, jeans, spectacles, pliers, scales — do hisson wali cheezein plural hoti hain: My spectacles are broken. Par "a pair of" lagate ho to singular ho jaata hai: A pair of scissors is missing.

docs.title: 17.8 There is / There are
docs.text:
"There" subject nahi hota — subject uske baad aata hai. Isliye verb baad wale noun se mel khaata hai.

  • There is a problem with the laptop. Ek problem — singular.
  • There are three problems in this file. Teen problems — plural.

docs.title: 17.9 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Agreement ki top galtiyan

  • Galat: He don't know my name.
  • Sahi: He doesn't know my name.

  • Kyun: He/she/it ke saath "does" aata hai. "don't" sirf I, you, we, they ke saath.

  • Galat: My parents is very supportive.

  • Sahi: My parents are very supportive.

  • Kyun: "Parents" plural hai — are. Ek ki baat ho to "My father is".

  • Galat: Everyone have their own problems.

  • Sahi: Everyone has their own problems.

  • Kyun: "Everyone" dikhne me sab lagta hai, par grammar me singular hai — has. (Aage "their" chalta hai, ye aaj normal English hai.)

  • Galat: The police is looking for him.

  • Sahi: The police are looking for him.

  • Kyun: "Police" hamesha plural. Ek pulisvaale ki baat ho to "a policeman is".

  • Galat: Mathematics are difficult for me.

  • Sahi: Mathematics is difficult for me.

  • Kyun: -s se khatam hone wale vishay (mathematics, physics, economics) singular hain.

  • Galat: One of my cousin works in Dubai.

  • Sahi: One of my cousins works in Dubai.

  • Kyun: "One of" ke baad noun plural hota hai, par verb singular. Dono ek saath yaad rakho.

  • Galat: The list of items are on the table.

  • Sahi: The list of items is on the table.

  • Kyun: Subject "the list" hai — ek list. "of items" beech ka phrase hai, use hata do.

  • Galat: My brother and I is going to Goa.

  • Sahi: My brother and I are going to Goa.
  • Kyun: "and" se jude do subject = plural. Aur kram bhi dhyaan rakho — "My brother and I", not "I and my brother".

Chaar kadam, har baar

1. Verb dhoondo. 2. Poochho "kaun/kya?" — jawaab hi subject hai. 3. Subject aur verb ke beech ka sab kuch hata do. 4. Ab dekho subject ek hai ya kai — aur usi hisaab se verb chuno.

docs.title: 17.10 Practice — Subject-verb agreement
docs.text:
Exercise 1

One of my cousins ___ in Canada.

  • live
  • lives
  • are living
  • have lived

Hint: Baat kitne logon ki ho rahi hai?

Jawaab

lives

'One of my cousins' ka matlab hai 'mere cousins me se EK'. Baat ek ki hai, isliye verb singular — lives.

Exercise 2

The box of chocolates ___ on the fridge.

  • are
  • is
  • were
  • have

Hint: Asli subject kaun hai — box ya chocolates?

Jawaab

is

Subject 'the box' hai — ek dabba. 'of chocolates' beech ka phrase hai, use hata do, to 'The box is' bachta hai.

Exercise 3

Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ present.

  • was
  • were
  • is
  • has

Hint: Verb ke sabse paas kaun hai?

Jawaab

were

neither…nor me verb sabse paas wale subject se mel khaata hai. Paas me 'the teachers' hai — plural, isliye 'were'.

Exercise 4

The police ___ already caught the thief.

  • has
  • have
  • is
  • was

Hint: 'Police' singular hai ya plural?

Jawaab

have

'Police' English me hamesha plural hai — have. Ek pulisvaale ke liye 'a policeman has' bolte hain.

Exercise 5

Every student ___ (have) a separate roll number.

Hint: 'Every' ke baad kaunsa roop?

Jawaab

has

'Every' aur 'each' hamesha singular hote hain, chahe baad me kitne bhi log hon — isliye 'has'.

Exercise 6

There ___ two pens and a pencil in my bag.

Hint: 'There' ke baad kya aa raha hai?

Jawaab

are

'There' subject nahi hota — baad wala noun subject hai. 'Two pens' plural hai, isliye 'are'.

Exercise 7

Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.

Hint: -s dikhne se plural nahi ho jaata.

Jawaab

is

Mathematics, physics, economics, politics — ye -s par khatam hote hain par singular hain, isliye 'is'.

Exercise 8

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — galat shabd par tap karo.

My younger brother don't like sweets.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: don't.

Sahi roop: My younger brother doesn't like sweets.

Subject 'my younger brother' = he. He/she/it ke saath 'doesn't' aata hai, 'don't' nahi.

Exercise 9

Galat shabd dhoondo.

One of my friend works in a bank.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: friend.

Sahi roop: One of my friends works in a bank.

'One of' ke baad noun hamesha plural hota hai — friends. Verb phir bhi singular rehta hai — works.

Exercise 10

Ek shabd galat hai — pakdo.

The quality of these mangoes are very poor.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: are.

Sahi roop: The quality of these mangoes is very poor.

Subject 'the quality' hai, ek cheez. 'of these mangoes' hata do to 'The quality is' bachta hai.

Exercise 11

Subject ko sahi verb se jodo.

A B Everyone is My parents are The news were My spectacles knows A number of boys know Jawaab

Everyone — knows; My parents — know; The news — is; My spectacles — are; A number of boys — were

Everyone singular → knows. Parents plural → know. News singular → is. Spectacles plural → are. 'A number of' plural → were.

Exercise 12

Sahi kram me vaakya banao.

Shabd: this / thirty / number / class / is / of / in / The / students

Jawaab

The number of students in this class is thirty

'The number of' hamesha singular leta hai — is. Agar 'A number of students' hota to 'are' aata.

Exercise 13

Ab ye line bol ke dekho — teen jagah agreement sambhaalni hai.

Jawaab

Bolo: One of my friends has a shop and his brothers work there

'One of my friends' singular → has. 'His brothers' plural → work. Ek hi vaakya me dono tarah ka mel — bolkar practice karne se ye aadat ban jaata hai.

Aage kya karein

Jab likho, ek baar sirf verbs par ungli rakh kar poora padho — har verb par ruk kar poochho "iska subject kaun hai?". Ye ek minute ka check aapki 90% agreement galtiyan khud pakad lega.

docs.title: Chapter 3: Shabd ke 8 prakaar
docs.text:
Shabd ke 8 prakaar — poora naksha

English me lakhon shabd hain, par kaam sirf aath tarah ke hain. Har ek shabd in aath me se kisi ek dibbe me jaata hai. Jis din ye aath dibbe samajh aa gaye, us din se grammar ratna band ho jaata hai — dikhna shuru ho jaata hai. Ye chapter poori kitaab ka naksha hai; baaki saare chapters inhi aath me se ek-ek ko kholte hain.

Ek line me

A part of speech is the job a word does in a sentence. Shabd kya hai — ye nahi; shabd vaakya me kya kaam kar raha hai — ye.

docs.title: 3.1 Pehle ek vaakya, saare aath kaam ke saath
docs.text:
Neeche ek chhota vaakya hai jisme aath me se saat kaam ek saath dikh rahe hain. Rango par dhyan do — poori kitaab me yahi rang isi kaam ke liye use honge, isliye aankh ko aadat pad jaayegi.

Noun

Pronoun

Verb

Adjective

Adverb

Preposition

Conjunction

Interjection

  • Wow! She quickly opened the old box under the bed, and we laughed. Waah! Usne phataphat palang ke neeche rakha purana dabba khola, aur hum hans pade.
Figure 3.1. Poori kitaab ka naksha. Beech me vaakya, chaaron taraf aath kaam — aur har kaam ka apna rang.

docs.title: 3.2 Aath dibbe, ek-ek line me
docs.text:
Prakaar Kaam kya hai Sawaal jo poochho Example Noun Kisi cheez, insaan, jagah ya bhaav ka naam Kaun? Kya? My sister lives in Pune. Pronoun Noun ki jagah lene wala shabd Kiski baat ho rahi hai? She called me. Verb Kaam, hona, ya haalat Kya ho raha hai? Ravi reads every night. Adjective Noun ke baare me kuch batata hai Kaisa? Kitna? Kaunsa? A heavy bag. Adverb Verb, adjective ya doosre adverb ke baare me Kaise? Kab? Kahan? Kitna? He walks slowly. Preposition Noun ka doosre shabd se rishta Kahan? Kab? Kaise? The pen is on the desk. Conjunction Do shabd ya do vaakya jodta hai Kis se jud raha hai? Tea or coffee? Interjection Achaanak aaya bhaav Kya feeling hai? Oh! I forgot.

Aath ko do hisson me baant lo

Pehle chaar bade khiladi hain — noun, pronoun, verb, adjective — inke bina vaakya banta hi nahi. Baaki chaar jodne-sajane wale hain — adverb, preposition, conjunction, interjection — ye vaakya ko behtar banate hain. Pehle chaar deewarein, baaki chaar paint aur parde.

docs.title: 3.3 Ek shabd, do kaam — yahi asli khel hai
docs.text:
Sabse badi galatfehmi ye hai ki log sochte hain ek shabd hamesha ek hi prakaar ka hota hai. Aisa nahi hai. Kaam vaakya tay karta hai, shabd nahi. Dekho — ek hi shabd "water" kabhi noun hai, kabhi verb:

  • The water is cold. Yahan "water" ek cheez ka naam hai — noun.
  • Please water the plants. Yahan "water" kaam hai — paani dena — isliye verb.
Shabd Ek kaam me Doosre kaam me book noun — I lost my book. verb — Let's book the tickets. fast adjective — a fast car adverb — He runs fast. light noun — Switch on the light. adjective — This bag is light. before preposition — before lunch conjunction — Call me before you leave. that pronoun — That is mine. conjunction — I know that he came.

Pehchaanne ka teen-step tareeka

1. Shabd hata ke dekho — kya vaakya tootta hai? Agar haan, to wo zaroori hai (noun / verb). 2. Poochho ki wo kiske baare me bata raha hai — noun ke? to adjective. verb ke? to adverb. 3. Uske turant baad koi noun aa raha hai aur wo jagah/samay bata raha hai? to preposition.

docs.title: 3.4 Noun aur Pronoun — naam aur naam ka shortcut
docs.text:
Noun har vaakya ki buniyaad hai. Pronoun uska shortcut hai, taaki baar-baar wahi naam na bolna pade.

  • Dohraav: Meera said Meera would bring Meera's books. Kaan ko chubhta hai, na? Isi liye pronoun bane.
  • Saaf: Meera said she would bring her books. Ek baar naam, phir pronoun — yahi natural English hai.

docs.title: 3.5 Verb — vaakya ka dil
docs.text:
Agar ek bhi cheez chunni ho to verb chuno. Verb ke bina koi poora vaakya nahi banta. Verb teen tarah ka kaam karta hai:

Verb kya bata raha hai Example Action — kuch ho raha hai She writes poems. Hona — astitva He is a teacher. Haalat — sthiti The soup tastes salty.

docs.title: 3.6 Adjective aur Adverb — do jodidaar
docs.text:
In dono me gadbad bahut hoti hai, par farq ek line ka hai: adjective noun ko chhoota hai, adverb verb ko.

  • She is a careful driver. "careful" bata raha hai driver kaisi hai — noun ke baare me, isliye adjective.
  • She drives carefully. "carefully" bata raha hai chalati kaise hai — verb ke baare me, isliye adverb.

Dhyan do — -ly hamesha adverb nahi hota

friendly, lovely, costly, silly — ye sab adjectives hain, -ly hone ke baavjood. Aur fast, hard, late, early adverb hote hain bina -ly ke. Isliye pehchaan rang-roop se nahi, kaam se karo.

docs.title: 3.7 Preposition, Conjunction, Interjection — teen chhote madadgaar
docs.text:
Preposition — rishta

Noun se pehle aata hai aur jagah/samay/tareeka batata hai. The keys are inside the drawer.

Conjunction — gond

Do hisse jodta hai. I wanted tea, but there was no milk.

Interjection — achaanak bhaav

Baaki vaakya se alag khada rehta hai, aur aksar ! leta hai. Arre! Bus nikal gayi.

Article ka kya? (a, an, the)

Kuch kitaabein a / an / the ko nauva prakaar — "determiner" — maanti hain. Is kitaab me hum inhe adjective ke parivaar me rakh rahe hain, kyunki ye bhi noun ke baare me hi batate hain. Inka poora chapter alag hai.

docs.title: 3.8 Ek vaakya khud tod ke dekho
docs.text:
Neeche wale vaakya me har shabd ka kaam likha hai. Pehle khud sochkar dekho, phir rang milao.

Figure 3.2. Ek normal vaakya ko tod kar dekhna — yahi grammar dikhne ki shuruaat hai.

docs.title: 3.9 Wo galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Part of speech galat chunne se banti galtiyan

  • Galat: Myself Ravi.
  • Sahi: I am Ravi. / My name is Ravi.

  • Kyun: "Myself" ek reflexive pronoun hai — wo subject ki jagah kabhi nahi le sakta. Intro dete waqt subject chahiye: I. Hindi ka "main Ravi" seedha translate karne se ye galti aati hai.

  • Galat: She drives very careful.

  • Sahi: She drives very carefully.

  • Kyun: "drives" ek verb hai, aur verb ko adverb chahiye. Adjective (careful) sirf noun ke saath chalega — a careful driver.

  • Galat: He don't know the answer.

  • Sahi: He doesn't know the answer.

  • Kyun: "He" third person singular hai, isliye helping verb bhi singular — does. Verb ko subject ke saath milana padta hai; Hindi me ye milan itna sakht nahi hota, isliye chhoot jaata hai.

  • Galat: I need some informations.

  • Sahi: I need some information.

  • Kyun: "Information" uncountable noun hai — uska plural hota hi nahi. Ginti karni ho to two pieces of information bolo.

  • Galat: Let us discuss about this topic.

  • Sahi: Let us discuss this topic.

  • Kyun: "Discuss" ko preposition ki zaroorat nahi — uske baad seedha object aata hai. Hindi me "iske baare me baat karein" hota hai, isliye "about" ghus jaata hai.

  • Galat: She is my cousin brother.

  • Sahi: He is my cousin.
  • Kyun: "Cousin" apne aap me ek poora noun hai — uske saath brother/sister jodne ki zaroorat nahi. English me cousin ladka bhi ho sakta hai, ladki bhi.

docs.title: 3.10 Do minute ka abhyaas
docs.text: Aaj ek kaam karo: koi bhi ek English vaakya lo — newspaper se, YouTube caption se, kahin se — aur uske har shabd par ungli rakh ke bolo "noun… verb… adjective…". Shuru me dheere hoga. Ek hafte baad apne aap hone lagega, aur phir apni galtiyan likhte waqt khud dikhne lagengi.

docs.title: 3.11 Practice — Parts of speech
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Is vaakya me 'quickly' kaunsa part of speech hai? — 'He quickly finished his homework.'

  • adverb
  • adjective
  • verb
  • noun

Hint: Poochho: ye kiske baare me bata raha hai?

Jawaab

adverb

'quickly' bata raha hai ki finish karne ka tareeka kya tha — matlab verb ke baare me. Verb ke baare me batane wala shabd adverb hota hai.

Exercise 2

'Please book two tickets.' — yahan 'book' kya hai?

  • verb
  • noun
  • adjective
  • preposition

Hint: Shabd ko bhoolo, kaam dekho.

Jawaab

verb

Yahan 'book' ek kaam hai — reserve karna. Wahi shabd 'I lost my book' me noun ban jaata hai, kyunki part of speech vaakya tay karta hai, shabd nahi.

Exercise 3

Kaunsa shabd noun ki jagah leta hai?

  • pronoun
  • adverb
  • conjunction
  • interjection
Jawaab

pronoun

Pro + noun ka matlab hi hai 'noun ke badle me'. Isi liye Meera ko dobara 'she' keh dete hain.

Exercise 4

'I waited, but she never came.' — 'but' kya hai?

  • conjunction
  • preposition
  • adverb
  • pronoun
Jawaab

conjunction

'but' do poore vaakyon ko jod raha hai, aur jodne ka kaam conjunction ka hai. Preposition hota to uske turant baad ek noun aata.

Exercise 5

She is a ___ singer. (adjective form of 'beauty')

Hint: Noun 'singer' ke baare me batana hai, isliye adjective chahiye.

Jawaab

beautiful

Noun ke saath adjective lagta hai — beautiful singer. 'beautifully' adverb hai, wo verb ke saath aata: she sings beautifully.

Exercise 6

He sings ___. (adverb form of 'beauty')

Hint: Ab verb 'sings' ke baare me batana hai.

Jawaab

beautifully

Verb ke baare me batane ke liye adverb chahiye. Isi liye yahan beautifully, aur singer ke saath beautiful.

Exercise 7

Is vaakya me ek shabd galat part of speech ka hai — us par tap karo.

She speaks English very fluent.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: fluent.

Sahi roop: She speaks English very fluently.

'speaks' verb hai, to uske baare me batane ke liye adverb chahiye — fluently. 'fluent' adjective hai, wo noun ke saath aata: fluent English.

Exercise 8

Galat shabd dhoondo.

Myself Ravi from Jaipur.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: Myself.

Sahi roop: I am Ravi from Jaipur.

Reflexive pronoun 'myself' subject nahi ban sakta — uske liye 'I' chahiye. Hindi ka 'main Ravi' seedha utaarne se ye galti hoti hai.

Exercise 9

Har part of speech ko uske kaam se jodo.

A B Noun noun ke baare me batata hai Verb noun ka rishta dikhata hai Adjective achaanak aaya bhaav Preposition kisi cheez ya insaan ka naam Interjection kaam ya hona Jawaab

Noun — kisi cheez ya insaan ka naam; Verb — kaam ya hona; Adjective — noun ke baare me batata hai; Preposition — noun ka rishta dikhata hai; Interjection — achaanak aaya bhaav

Har shabd ek hi kaam karta hai, aur wahi kaam uska part of speech hai. Rangon ki aadat pad jaayegi to ye khud dikhne lagega.

Exercise 10

Sahi kram me vaakya banao — article, adjective, noun, verb, adverb ka normal kram.

Shabd: The / old / walked / slowly / man

Jawaab

The old man walked slowly

English ka seedha kram hai: article + adjective + noun (subject), phir verb, phir adverb. Adverb verb ke baad aane se vaakya natural lagta hai.

Exercise 11

Kaunsa shabd -ly hone ke baavjood adjective hai?

  • friendly
  • quickly
  • slowly
  • loudly

Hint: Poochho: kya ye noun ke saath aata hai?

Jawaab

friendly

'friendly' noun ke baare me batata hai — a friendly dog — isliye adjective. Yahi wajah hai ki pehchaan -ly se nahi, kaam se karni chahiye.

Exercise 12

Ab ye vaakya bol ke dekho. Dhyan rakho — 'carefully' me dono -l saaf bolne hain.

Jawaab

Bolo: She drives carefully every day

Bolte waqt adverb verb ke baad aata hai, isliye 'drives carefully' ek saath bahta hai. 'careful' bol dene se English ajeeb lagti hai.

Aage kya karein

Ye naksha yaad rakho — agle aath chapters me hum ek-ek dibba khol kar dekhenge. Agla chapter Noun hai, kyunki har vaakya wahin se shuru hota hai.

docs.title: Chapter 2: English ki aawazein
docs.text:
English ki aawazein — jo Hindi me nahi hain

English me 26 akshar hain, par lagbhag 44 aawazein. Yahi se saari gadbad shuru hoti hai: hum akshar padhte hain, aur maan lete hain ki jo likha hai wahi bolna hai. Hindi me ye maan lena kaam karta hai — Devanagari me jo likha hai, wahi bolte hain. English me nahi. Is chapter me hum unn aawazon par kaam karenge jo aapki zubaan ne aaj tak banayi hi nahi hain — kyunki Hindi me unki zaroorat hi nahi padi.

Ek line me

Uchchaaran galat hone ki wajah aapki "kami" nahi hai — wajah ye hai ki aapke muh ne aaj tak sirf Hindi ki positions seekhi hain. Nayi position seekh lo, aawaz khud aa jaayegi. Ye hunar hai, qismat nahi. Muscle ko sikhana padta hai, bas.

docs.title: 2.1 Likha hua ≠ bola hua
docs.text:
Pehle ye teen jodiyan sun lo. Dono shabd dikhte ek jaise hain, par bilkul alag bolte hain:

Shabd Suno Jo log galti se bolte hain Sahi me kya hai put / but dono "ut" put = "puut", but = "bat" come / home dono "ome" come = "kum", home = "hoam" though / through / tough teeno "ough" ek jaisa tho, throo, taf — teen alag

Isliye ek niyam

Naya shabd dikhe to pehle suno, phir bolo. Spelling se andaaza mat lagao. Is kitaab me har line par 🔊 isi liye hai.

docs.title: 2.2 Aath aawazein jo Hindi me nahi hain
docs.text:
Yahi aath hain jo poora ucchaaran banati ya bigaadti hain. Har ek ke saath muh ki position likhi hai — padho aur usi waqt karke dekho. Aaina saamne ho to behtar.

Aawaz Shabd Muh kahan rakhna hai Suno /θ/ bina aawaz ki TH think, three, mouth Zubaan ki nok upar ke do daanton ke beech se zara bahar nikalo. Hawa bahar phenko, gale se aawaz nahi nikalni. Hindi ka "थ" nahi hai — usme zubaan daanton ke peeche rehti hai. /ð/ aawaz wali TH this, they, mother Zubaan wahi — daanton ke beech. Par ab gale me kampan do. Gale par ungli rakho, hilna chahiye. /v/ very, van, love Upar ke daant neeche ke hoth par rakho, aur gale se aawaz nikalo. Hoth gol nahi hote. Daant lagna zaroori hai. /f/ fan, phone, laugh Bilkul /v/ jaisi position — upar ke daant neeche ke hoth par — par gale se aawaz nahi, sirf hawa. Hindi ka "फ" nahi; usme dono hoth lagte hain. /z/ zoo, buzz, is, was /s/ hi banao — zubaan upar ke daanton ke peeche, patli hawa — par saath me gale ka kampan jodo. Bhanware jaisi bhanbhanaahat. /æ/ cat, man, bad Muh chaudaa kholo, jabda neeche, jaise doctor ko gala dikhana ho. "अ" aur "ऐ" ke beech ki aawaz. Ye "कैट" nahi hai. /ə/ schwa about, doctor, sofa Muh ko bilkul dheela chhod do aur halki si "uh" nikalo. Koi mehnat nahi. English ki sabse aam aawaz yahi hai — aur sabse zyada ignore ki jaati hai. /ʒ/ vision, measure, usual "sh" banao, phir usi position me gale ki aawaz jodo. "zh" — jaise "झ" nahi, balki lambi bhinbhinaati "sh".

docs.title: 2.3 Zubaan kahan hai — teen positions ka naksha
docs.text:
Hindi me "त" ke liye zubaan daanton ke peeche, aur "ट" ke liye talu (mooh ki chhat) se lagti hai. English ka T in dono ke beech hai — daanton ke peeche wali ubhri hui jagah par. Aur TH to daanton ke beech se bahar jaati hai. Ye naksha dekho:

Figure 2.1. English ka T Hindi ke त aur ट ke beech padta hai. Isi liye ट se bola gaya T videshi kaan ko bhaari lagta hai, aur त se bola gaya T thoda narm.

Abhi karo — 10 second

"टाइम" bolo. Phir zubaan ko zara peeche sarka kar "time" bolo. Farq saaf sunai dega.

docs.title: 2.4 Chhoti aur lambi vowel — ek hi galti, sau shabd
docs.text:
Hindi me "इ" aur "ई" ka farq hum जानते hain. English me wahi farq hai, par likhayi me nahi dikhta — isliye hum chhod dete hain. Natija: "ship" aur "sheep" ek jaisa bolte hain. Lambi vowel sirf lambi nahi hoti, uska muh bhi thoda alag hota hai.

Figure 2.2. Neeli patti = chhoti aawaz (jhatke se khatam). Narangi patti = lambi aawaz (kheenchi hui). Ek hi akshar, par lambai se matlab badal jaata hai.
  • The ship is big. / The sheep is big. Jahaaz bada hai / bhed badi hai. Ek hi galti, aur baat badal gayi.
  • My glass is full. / He is a fool. Mera glass bhara hai / wo bewkoof hai. "full" ko kheench kar bolna khatarnaak hai!

docs.title: 2.5 Schwa — English ka sabse bada raaz
docs.text:
English ki sabse zyada boli jaane wali aawaz koi a-e-i-o-u nahi hai — wo hai /ə/ schwa: ek bilkul dheeli, bina mehnat wali "uh". Jo akshar par zor nahi hota, wo English me lagbhag gayab ho jaata hai aur schwa ban jaata hai. Hum Indian speakers har akshar poora bolte hain — isi liye hamari English "sapaat" aur thodi robotic lagti hai.

Shabd Hum bolte hain Asal me Suno doctor dok-TOR DOK-tuh (aakhir dheela) about E-BAUT uh-BOWT (shuru dheela) computer KOM-PYU-TAR kuhm-PYOO-tuh banana BA-NA-NA buh-NAA-nuh support SUP-PORT suh-PORT

Schwa ka niyam

Jis hisse par zor nahi, use poora mat bolo — nigal jao. Ek shabd me sirf ek hissa chamakta hai; baaki hisse peeche rehte hain. Isi par poora "Rhythm aur stress" chapter hai — par shuruaat yahan se karo.

docs.title: 2.6 Hindi ki aadatein jo English me saaf pakdi jaati hain
docs.text:
Paanch aadatein, paanch ilaaj

  • Galat: "iskool", "istation", "ispeak"
  • Sahi: school, station, speak — seedha "s" se

  • Kyun: Hindi me do consonant se shabd shuru nahi hote, isliye hum aage "i" jod dete hain. Ilaaj: pehle sirf "sssss" bolo, phir usi saans me "kool" jodo — "sss-kool".

  • Galat: "filim" (film), "homewark" ke andar extra aawaz

  • Sahi: film — "l" aur "m" ek saath, beech me kuch nahi

  • Kyun: Do consonant ke beech hum anjaane me chhoti "i" ghusa dete hain. Dheere bolo: "fi—lm".

  • Galat: "wery" ya "vindow" — V aur W ki milawat

  • Sahi: very (daant-hoth) / window (gol hoth)

  • Kyun: Hindi me ek hi "व" hai, English me do alag aawazein. Poora ilaaj agle wale chapter me hai.

  • Galat: "iz" ki jagah "is" — buzz ko "bus"

  • Sahi: is, was, buzz — gale me kampan ke saath

  • Kyun: /z/ Hindi me nahi hai, isliye hum /s/ par chale jaate hain. Gale par ungli rakh kar "zzzz" karo — hilna chahiye.

  • Galat: Har shabd ko barabar zor dena — "I AM GO-ING TO MAR-KET"

  • Sahi: I'm GOing to the MARket — do shabd chamakte hain, baaki dheele
  • Kyun: English ka rhythm asamaan hota hai. Sapaat bolna sabse bada "accent" hai jo pakda jaata hai.

docs.title: 2.7 Chup akshar — jo likhe hain par bolte nahi
docs.text:
Chup akshar Shabd Bolo Suno K (kn-) know, knife, knee no, naif, nee W (wr-) write, wrong, wrist rait, rong, rist B (-mb) comb, climb, thumb koam, klaim, tham L talk, walk, half, could tok, wok, haaf, kud T listen, castle, often lisun, kaasul, ofun H hour, honest, honour aawar, onist, onar

Ek chhota sa pakka faayda

Sirf ye chhah lines yaad kar lene se aapke bolne me turant farq aayega — kyunki ye shabd roz aate hain. "I don't know" me ek bhi K nahi bolna.

docs.title: 2.8 Roz ki 5-minute drill
docs.text:
Ye paanch line roz ek baar bolo. Inme saari nayi aawazein ek saath aati hain:

  • I think these three things are true. TH wali drill — "think/these/three/things" me do tarah ki TH hain.
  • Very few of my friends have a van. V aur F — dono me upar ke daant neeche ke hoth par.
  • The zoo was closed because of the rain. /z/ ki drill — zoo, was, closed, because: chaaron me gale ka kampan.
  • The school bus stops at the station. "s" se shuru hone wali drill — iskool, istop, istation bilkul nahi.
  • The doctor asked about my computer. Schwa ki drill — DOK-tuh, uh-BOWT, kuhm-PYOO-tuh. Bina zor wale hisse dheele.

docs.title: 2.9 Practice — English ki aawazein
docs.text:
Exercise 1

English me kitni aawazein hain?

  • Lagbhag 44
  • Theek 26
  • Lagbhag 33
  • Theek 52

Hint: Akshar 26 hain — aawazein usse zyada.

Jawaab

Lagbhag 44

26 akshar, par lagbhag 44 aawazein. Isi liye spelling se uchchaaran ka andaaza lagana galat hai.

Exercise 2

/v/ bolte waqt muh me kya hota hai?

  • Upar ke daant neeche ke hoth par, gale me kampan
  • Dono hoth mil kar gol
  • Zubaan daanton ke beech
  • Zubaan talu se chipki

Hint: Daant kahan hain?

Jawaab

Upar ke daant neeche ke hoth par, gale me kampan

/v/ me daant-hoth ka milna zaroori hai. Hoth gol karne par wo /w/ ban jaata hai.

Exercise 3

'think' aur 'this' ki TH me kya farq hai?

  • 'this' me gale ka kampan hota hai, 'think' me nahi
  • 'this' me zubaan peeche rehti hai
  • 'think' me dono hoth lagte hain
  • Koi farq nahi, dono ek hi aawaz hain
Jawaab

'this' me gale ka kampan hota hai, 'think' me nahi

Zubaan ki position dono me ek — daanton ke beech. Farq sirf aawaz ka: think = sirf hawa, this = kampan.

Exercise 4

English ki sabse zyada boli jaane wali aawaz kaunsi hai?

  • Schwa /ə/ — dheeli 'uh'
  • Lambi /iː/ jaise 'sheep' me
  • /t/
  • /æ/ jaise 'cat' me

Hint: Jisme muh ko koi mehnat nahi karni padti.

Jawaab

Schwa /ə/ — dheeli 'uh'

Bina zor wale hisse schwa ban jaate hain: DOK-tuh, kuhm-PYOO-tuh. Har akshar poora bolna hi 'flat' accent banata hai.

Exercise 5

Hum 'school' ko 'iskool' kyun bol dete hain?

  • Hindi me shabd do consonant se shuru nahi hote
  • 'sch' ka matlab 'isk' hota hai
  • Angrez bhi aisa hi bolte hain
  • 's' chup akshar hai
Jawaab

Hindi me shabd do consonant se shuru nahi hote

Zubaan aaram ke liye aage ek vowel jod deti hai. Ilaaj: pehle 'sss' kheencho, phir usi saans me 'kool'.

Exercise 6

Chup akshar hatao — 'know' me kaunsa akshar bilkul nahi bolte? ___

Hint: Shuruaat ka akshar.

Jawaab

k / K

kn- me K hamesha chup: know = no, knife = naif, knee = nee.

Exercise 7

'listen' me kaunsa akshar chup hai? ___

Jawaab

t / T

listen = li-sun. Isi tarah castle = kaa-sul, often me bhi T lagbhag chup.

Exercise 8

Aawaz ko uski muh-position se jodo.

A B /θ/ think dono hoth gol, daant nahi lagte /v/ very /s/ ki position + gale ka kampan /w/ wet zubaan daanton ke beech, sirf hawa /z/ zoo upar ke daant neeche ke hoth par Jawaab

/θ/ think — zubaan daanton ke beech, sirf hawa; /v/ very — upar ke daant neeche ke hoth par; /w/ wet — dono hoth gol, daant nahi lagte; /z/ zoo — /s/ ki position + gale ka kampan

Har aawaz ek position hai. Position theek, aawaz apne aap theek.

Exercise 9

Is vaakya me ek shabd galat tareeke se likha hai — us par tap karo.

I go to iskool every morning.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: iskool.

Sahi roop: I go to school every morning.

'school' — seedha s se. Aage 'i' ki aawaz Hindi ki aadat hai, English me nahi.

Exercise 10

TH wali drill — dheere, zubaan daanton ke beech se.

Jawaab

Bolo: I think these three things are true

think aur three me sirf hawa; these me gale ka kampan. Dono TH ek hi vaakya me.

Exercise 11

V aur F ki drill. Daant neeche ke hoth par hone chahiye.

Jawaab

Bolo: Very few of my friends have a van

very, few, friends, have, van — paanch baar wahi daant-hoth position.

Exercise 12

's' se shuru — 'i' nahi lagana.

Jawaab

Bolo: The school bus stops at the station

school, stops, station — teeno seedha s se. Pehle 'sss' kheench kar practise karo.

Exercise 13

/z/ ki drill — gale me bhanbhanaahat.

Jawaab

Bolo: The zoo was closed because of the rain

zoo, was, closed, because — chaaron me /z/. Gale par ungli rakho, hilna chahiye.

Exercise 14

Schwa ki drill — bina zor wale hisse dheele chhod do.

Jawaab

Bolo: The doctor asked about my computer

DOK-tuh, uh-BOWT, kuhm-PYOO-tuh. Har akshar poora bolne ki koshish mat karo.

Aage kya karein

Ye chapter neev hai — isse ek baar me "khatam" nahi karna. Hafte me do baar wapas aao aur table ki aawazein dohrao. Ab agla kadam: Uchchaaran theek karo chapter, jahan har aawaz par alag-alag drill aur minimal pairs milenge.

docs.title: Chapter 15: Saare 12 tenses
docs.text:
Saare 12 tenses — ek hi naksha

Log kehte hain "English me 12 tenses hain" aur sunne me lagta hai 12 alag-alag cheezein ratni padengi. Sach ye hai ki 12 tenses 12 cheezein nahi hain — wo sirf 3 × 4 hai. Teen samay (past, present, future) aur chaar haalat (simple, continuous, perfect, perfect continuous). Bas itna. Jis din ye 3 × 4 wali table dimaag me baith gayi, us din tense ki tension khatam.

Ek line me

A tense tells you when the action happens and in what state it is — finished, going on, or completed before some point. Tense do baatein batata hai: kaam kab hua, aur us waqt uski haalat kya thi.

docs.title: 15.1 Pehle ye samajh lo: 3 samay × 4 haalat
docs.text:
Koi bhi kaam kisi ek samay me hota hai — beeta hua (past), abhi (present), ya aage (future). Ye teen column ban gaye.

Aur har samay me kaam ki chaar haalat ho sakti hai. Yahi chaar row hain, aur yahi asli jaadu hai:

Haalat (aspect) Matlab Hindi feel Simple Bas hua / hota hai / hoga. Ek point, ya ek aadat. "main gaya", "main jaata hoon" Continuous Us waqt chal raha tha / chal raha hai / chal raha hoga. "main jaa raha tha" Perfect Kisi point se pehle poora ho chuka tha / hai / hoga. "main jaa chuka tha" Perfect Continuous Kuch der se lagaataar chal raha hai, aur kitni der se — ye bhi batata hai. "main do ghante se jaa raha hoon"

Naam padhne ka tareeka

Tense ka naam hi uska formula hai. "Past Perfect Continuous" ko ulta padho: Continuous hai to -ing lagega, Perfect hai to had/have aayega, Past hai to woh helping verb past form me hoga → had been + -ing. Naam se formula nikaalna seekh gaye, to ratne ki zaroorat hi nahi.

docs.title: 15.2 Poora naksha — timeline par 12 tenses
docs.text:
Neeche wali tasveer is poore chapter ka nichod hai. Ek baar dhyaan se dekho: left se right waqt chalta hai, beech wali narangi lakeer ABHI hai. Har dabbe me chhoti timeline par dekho kaam kahan baitha hai — point par, lakeer ki tarah phaila hua, ya kisi point se pehle khatam.

Figure 15.1. Bhara hua gola = kaam ka point. Moti lakeer = kaam chal raha hai. Khaali gola = wo doosra point jiske pehle kaam khatam hua. Narangi dotted lakeer = ABHI.

Past

Present

Future

docs.title: 15.3 Verb ke chaar roop — poori machine ka petrol
docs.text:
Tense banane ke liye sirf chaar cheezein chahiye hoti hain. Inhe V1, V2, V3 aur V-ing kehte hain. Agar ye chaar roop pata hain, to 12 tenses apne-aap ban jaate hain.

Roop Naam write go eat play V1 base form write go eat play V1-s he/she/it form writes goes eats plays V2 past form wrote went ate played V3 past participle written gone eaten played V-ing present participle writing going eating playing Figure 15.2. BE, HAVE aur WILL — teen helping verbs. Inhe jis kram me jodoge, wahi tense banega. Kram hamesha ye hi rehta hai: will → have → been → V-ing .

docs.title: 15.4 Baaras formula, ek table me
docs.text:
Yahan sab kuch ek jagah hai. Isko ek baar likh kar deewar par chipka do — do hafte me yaad ho jaayega.

Tense Formula Example Hindi Present Simple V1 / V1-s She writes letters. Wo chitthi likhti hai. Present Continuous am/is/are + V-ing She is writing a letter. Wo chitthi likh rahi hai. Present Perfect have/has + V3 She has written the letter. Wo chitthi likh chuki hai. Present Perfect Cont. have/has been + V-ing She has been writing for an hour. Wo ek ghante se likh rahi hai. Past Simple V2 She wrote a letter. Wo chitthi likhi. Past Continuous was/were + V-ing She was writing a letter. Wo chitthi likh rahi thi. Past Perfect had + V3 She had written it before I came. Mere aane se pehle likh chuki thi. Past Perfect Cont. had been + V-ing She had been writing since morning. Subah se likh rahi thi. Future Simple will + V1 She will write a letter. Wo chitthi likhegi. Future Continuous will be + V-ing She will be writing at 5 pm. 5 baje likh rahi hogi. Future Perfect will have + V3 She will have written it by Monday. Somwaar tak likh chuki hogi. Future Perfect Cont. will have been + V-ing She will have been writing for two hours. Do ghante se likh rahi hogi.

docs.title: 15.5 Present ke chaar tenses — paas se
Present Simple — aadat aur sach
docs.text:
Ye tense "abhi is waqt" ke liye nahi hai. Ye aadat, routine, aur hamesha sach rehne wali baat ke liye hai. Yahi sabse bada confusion hai.

  • I catch the 8 o'clock bus every day. Main roz aath baje ki bus pakadta hoon. — roz ki aadat.
  • Water boils at 100 degrees. Paani 100 degree par ubalta hai. — hamesha sach.
  • He does not like coffee. Usse coffee pasand nahi. — negative me "does not + V1", yahan "likes" nahi.

-s sirf he / she / it ke saath

I write · you write · he writes · we write · they write. Aur jaise hi do/does ya koi modal aa jaaye, -s hat jaata hai: He does not write**, not "does not writes".

docs.title: Present Continuous — abhi, is waqt
docs.text:
• I am reading this chapter right now. Main abhi ye chapter padh raha hoon.
  • We are moving to Pune next month. Agle mahine Pune shift ho rahe hain. — pakka plan ho to future ke liye bhi chalta hai.

Kuch verbs -ing me nahi jaate

  • Galat: I am having a car.
  • Sahi: I have a car.

  • Kyun: Jab have ka matlab "paas hona" hai, to -ing nahi lagta. Par jab iska matlab "khaana/karna" ho to lagta hai: I am having lunch — ye bilkul theek hai. Aise hi verbs: know, understand, like, want, need, believe, belong, see (dekhna).

  • Galat: I am knowing him since childhood.

  • Sahi: I have known him since childhood.
  • Kyun: "Know" ek haalat hai, kaam nahi — isliye -ing nahi.

docs.title: Present Perfect — ho chuka, par waqt nahi bataya
docs.text:
Present Perfect ka sabse bada rule: iske saath past ka waqt nahi aata. Agar aap "yesterday", "last week", "in 2019" bol rahe ho, to Past Simple chahiye.

  • I have finished my homework. Main homework kar chuka hoon. — kab kiya, ye matlab ka hissa nahi.
  • She has just left. Wo abhi gayi hai. — abhi-abhi hua, asar taaza hai.
  • I have never seen snow. Maine kabhi barf nahi dekhi. — zindagi bhar ka anubhav.

docs.title: Present Perfect Continuous — "kitni der se"
docs.text:
Jab batana ho ki kaam kitni der se chal raha hai, ye tense use hota hai. Aur yahi wo tense hai jahan Indian speakers sabse badi galti karte hain.

'since three years' — sabse aam galti

  • Galat: I am working here since three years.
  • Sahi: I have been working here for three years.
  • Kyun: Do galtiyan ek saath thi. (1) Jab kaam past me shuru hua aur abhi tak chal raha hai, to have been + -ing chahiye, am working nahi. (2) for = kitni der (three years), since = kab se (2022, Monday, morning).

docs.title: 15.6 Past ke chaar tenses
docs.text:
Kab use karein Tense Example Khatam ho chuka kaam, waqt pata hai Past Simple I met him yesterday. Past me ek lambi background, jiske beech kuch hua Past Continuous I was cooking when he called. Do past kaam — jo pehle hua Past Perfect The train had left before we reached. Past ke kisi point tak kitni der se chal raha tha Past Perfect Cont. She had been waiting for an hour.

Past Continuous + Past Simple ki jodi

Kahani sunate waqt ye jodi baar-baar aati hai: lambi cheez Continuous me, achaanak hone wali cheez Simple me. I was crossing the road when the bike hit me. Main sadak paar kar raha tha jab bike ne takkar maari.

docs.title: 15.7 Future ke chaar tenses
docs.text:
Future ke liye English me kai raaste hain, aur sab "will" nahi hote. Ye farq fluency me bada dikhai deta hai.

Roop Kab Example will + V1 Abhi liya gaya faisla, vaada, andaaza OK, I will help you. be going to Pehle se socha hua plan, ya saamne dikhta nateeja I am going to start a shop. am/is/are + V-ing Pakka, time-table wala plan I am meeting her at six. will be + V-ing Aage kisi waqt chal raha hoga At nine I will be travelling. will have + V3 Deadline se pehle poora By May I will have finished it.

Time clause me future nahi

when, if, after, before, until, as soon as ke baad will nahi aata — chahe baat future ki ho. I will call you when I reach home. "when I will reach" galat hai. Ek vaakya me will ek hi baar.

docs.title: 15.8 Signal words — tense ka pata chalne wale shabd
docs.text:
Kuch shabd lagbhag hamesha ek hi tense ke saath aate hain. Exam me aur bolne me, ye shortcut bahut kaam aata hai.

Shabd dikhe to Tense every day, usually, often, always, never, generally Present Simple now, right now, at the moment, look!, listen! Present Continuous just, already, yet, ever, never, so far, recently Present Perfect for + duration, since + point, how long, all day Perfect Continuous yesterday, last night, ago, in 2019, then Past Simple while, at that time, all evening Past Continuous before, after, by the time, already (past me) Past Perfect tomorrow, next week, soon, in future Future Simple by Monday, by then, by the end of… Future Perfect

docs.title: 15.9 Wo tense galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain
docs.text:
Top tense galtiyan — aur unka sahi roop

  • Galat: Yesterday I have gone to the market.
  • Sahi: Yesterday I went to the market.

  • Kyun: "Yesterday" past ka pakka waqt hai. Present Perfect ke saath past ka waqt nahi aata — wahan Past Simple (V2) aata hai.

  • Galat: He don't know the answer.

  • Sahi: He doesn't know the answer.

  • Kyun: He/she/it ke saath does. Aur does ke baad verb bina -s: "doesn't know", not "doesn't knows".

  • Galat: I am working here since 2019.

  • Sahi: I have been working here since 2019.

  • Kyun: Past me shuru + abhi tak chal raha = have/has been + V-ing.

  • Galat: If I will get the job, I will shift to Mumbai.

  • Sahi: If I get the job, I will shift to Mumbai.

  • Kyun: "if" ke baad present, main clause me will. Dono me will kabhi nahi.

  • Galat: I am having two brothers.

  • Sahi: I have two brothers.

  • Kyun: Rishte aur cheezein "have" se batate hain, "am having" se nahi.

  • Galat: She did not came to class.

  • Sahi: She did not come to class.

  • Kyun: did ne past ka kaam kar diya — ab verb V1 me hi rahega.

  • Galat: I will tell you when he will come.

  • Sahi: I will tell you when he comes.

  • Kyun: Time clause (when/after/before/until) me future nahi — present aata hai.

  • Galat: He has came home.

  • Sahi: He has come home.
  • Kyun: have/has/had ke baad hamesha V3, V2 nahi. come-came-come, go-went-gone, see-saw-seen.

Teen rule jo 80% galtiyan bacha lete hain

1. Past ka waqt (yesterday, ago, last…) dikhe → V2, have/has nahi. 2. have/has/had ke baad V3. do/does/did ke baad V1. 3. Ek vaakya me will ek hi baar — if/when wale hisse me kabhi nahi.

docs.title: 15.10 Practice — Saare 12 tenses
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Yesterday she ___ a new phone.

  • has bought
  • bought
  • have bought
  • is buying

Hint: Past ka pakka waqt diya hai.

Jawaab

bought

'Yesterday' past ka waqt batata hai, aur past ke waqt ke saath Present Perfect nahi chalta — seedha V2 'bought'.

Exercise 2

Look! The baby ___ .

  • cries
  • cried
  • is crying
  • has cried

Hint: 'Look!' ka matlab abhi, is waqt.

Jawaab

is crying

Look! / Listen! / right now jaise shabd matlab kaam abhi chal raha hai — isliye Present Continuous.

Exercise 3

By next March, I ___ in this company for five years.

  • will work
  • will be working
  • will have been working
  • am working

Hint: Aage ki ek deadline tak kitni der.

Jawaab

will have been working

Future ke ek point tak 'kitni der se' batana ho to Future Perfect Continuous — will have been + V-ing.

Exercise 4

The film ___ before we reached the hall.

  • started
  • has started
  • had started
  • was starting

Hint: Do past kaam — kaunsa pehle hua?

Jawaab

had started

Do past kaam ho to jo pehle hua usme Past Perfect (had + V3) aata hai. Film pehle shuru hui, hum baad me pahunche.

Exercise 5

She ___ (go) to the gym every morning.

Hint: 'every morning' = aadat.

Jawaab

goes

Aadat ke liye Present Simple, aur 'she' ke saath verb me -s lagta hai — goes.

Exercise 6

I ___ been waiting here since four o'clock.

Hint: I ke saath kaunsa helping verb?

Jawaab

have

I/you/we/they ke saath 'have', he/she/it ke saath 'has'. Kaam pehle shuru hua aur abhi tak chal raha hai, isliye have been + -ing.

Exercise 7

He didn't ___ (come) to the office yesterday.

Hint: didn't ne past ka kaam pehle hi kar diya.

Jawaab

come

'did / didn't' ke baad verb hamesha V1 me rehta hai — 'didn't came' nahi, 'didn't come'.

Exercise 8

Is vaakya me ek galti hai — us shabd par tap karo.

Yesterday I have gone to the market with my mother.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: have.

Sahi roop: Yesterday I went to the market with my mother.

Past ka waqt (yesterday) hai, isliye Present Perfect ka 'have' galat — seedha 'went' aata hai.

Exercise 9

Galat shabd dhoondo.

My father is having an old scooter.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: having.

Sahi roop: My father has an old scooter.

Jab 'have' ka matlab 'paas hona' ho, to -ing nahi lagta. 'Having lunch' theek hai, 'having a scooter' nahi.

Exercise 10

Ek shabd zyada hai — use pakdo.

Please call me when you reached the station.

Jawaab

Galat shabd: reached.

Sahi roop: Please call me when you reach the station.

Baat aage ki hai, isliye past 'reached' galat hai. 'when' wale hisse me simple present aata hai — 'when you reach'.

Exercise 11

Sahi kram me vaakya banao — Past Continuous aur Past Simple ki jodi.

Shabd: off / the / went / a / when / lights / book / reading / was / I

Jawaab

I was reading a book when the lights went off

Lambi chalti cheez Past Continuous me (was reading), achaanak hone wali cheez Past Simple me (went off). Yahi kahani sunane ka kram hai.

Exercise 12

Tense ko uske kaam se jodo.

A B I write ho chuka, asar abhi hai I am writing doosre past kaam se pehle khatam I have written der se chal raha hai, abhi bhi I had written aadat ya hamesha ka sach I have been writing abhi is waqt chal raha hai Jawaab

I write — aadat ya hamesha ka sach; I am writing — abhi is waqt chal raha hai; I have written — ho chuka, asar abhi hai; I had written — doosre past kaam se pehle khatam; I have been writing — der se chal raha hai, abhi bhi

Simple = point ya aadat. Continuous = chal raha hai. Perfect = ho chuka. Perfect Continuous = kitni der se chal raha hai.

Exercise 13

Ab ye line bol ke dekho — 'have been' ko bina ruke jodna hai.

Jawaab

Bolo: I have been learning English for two years

Bolte waqt 'have been' lagbhag 'hav-bin' sunai deta hai. Aur dhyaan rakho — 'since two years' nahi, 'for two years'.

Aage kya karein

Aaj se ek chhoti aadat banao: din me teen vaakya apne baare me likho — ek past, ek present, ek future. Phir unhe continuous aur perfect me badal kar dekho. Ek hafte me 12 tenses ratne wali cheez nahi, mehsoos hone wali cheez ban jaayenge.

docs.title: Chapter 38: Roz ke vishay
docs.text:
Roz ke vishay — sehat, paisa, shopping, safar, ghar

Grammar aati hai, par chemist ke saamne "gala kharab hai" English me bolna ho to dimaag khaali ho jaata hai? Ye chapter paanch roz ke vishayon ke shabd aur poore vaakya deta hai — sehat, paisa aur bank, shopping aur returns, safar, aur ghar ki marammat. Har vishay me ek table, kuch taiyaar lines, ek mini-dialogue, aur wo Indian English galtiyan jo hum sach me karte hain. Har line par 🔊 hai — suno aur saath bolo.

docs.title: 38.1 Shabd nahi, tukde yaad karo
docs.text:
Akela shabd "fever" yaad karne se kaam nahi chalta — aapko poora tukda chahiye: I've got a fever. Isliye is chapter me har shabd ek chunk (chhote vaakya) ke saath aata hai. Jab bolne ka waqt aaye, to dimaag ko jodna nahi padta, tukda seedha nikal aata hai.

Figure 38.1. Paanch vishay, har ek ke paanch-das tukde. Inhi se roz ki 80% baat-cheet chal jaati hai.

Chunk ka niyam

Shabd ko hamesha uske saathi shabdon ke saath yaad karo: a sore throat, make a payment, a connecting flight, the tap is leaking. Pakki jodiyon ke baare me poora chapter: Kaunsa shabd kiske saath.

Ye chapter shabdon par hai. Doctor, dukaan aur auto wali poori baat-cheet ke liye Roz ki baat-cheet dekho, aur ₹1,25,000 jaise number bolne ke liye Number, date, time, paise.

docs.title: 38.2 Sehat aur doctor — takleef English me
docs.text:
Doctor ya chemist ko sabse pehle batana hota hai ki takleef kya hai. English me iske do aasaan saanche hain: I've got a … (British, bolchaal) ya I have a … (har jagah sahi). Aur jab poore sharir ki feeling ho: I feel …

Hinglish me English me Note Gala kharab / gale me dard I've got a sore throat. sore = dukhta hua Bukhaar hai I've got a fever / a temperature. UK me "temperature" aam Sar dard I've got a headache. "a" zaroori Zukaam, naak beh rahi I've got a cold / a runny nose. band naak = blocked nose Khaansi I've got a cough. dry cough = sookhi Chakkar aa rahe I feel dizzy. feel + adjective Ulti jaisa lag raha I feel sick. US: nauseous Pet kharab I've got an upset stomach. loose motions = diarrhoea Kamzori I feel weak and tired. — Pair mud gaya (moch) I've sprained my ankle. sprain = moch Khujli, daane I've got an itchy rash. rash = daane
  • I've got a sore throat and a slight fever. Gala dukh raha hai aur halka bukhaar hai.
  • I've had a temperature since Monday. Somvaar se bukhaar hai. ("since" ke saath I've had.)
  • I feel dizzy every time I stand up. Jab bhi khada hota hoon, chakkar aata hai.
  • My back hurts when I bend down. Jhukne par kamar dukhti hai. Dard ke liye verb: hurt.

docs.title: Chemist par — dawai lena
docs.text:
India me hum "medical store" kehte hain, aur ye yahan sab samajhte hain. British English me chemist ya pharmacy, American me drugstore. Doctor ki likhi parchi = prescription; bina parchi milne wali dawai = over the counter.

  • Can you suggest something for a sore throat? Gale ke liye kuch de sakte ho?
  • Do I need a prescription for this? Iske liye parchi chahiye kya?
  • What's the dose for a ten-year-old? Das saal ke bachche ke liye kitni matra?
  • Does it have any side effects? Will it make me sleepy? Iska koi side effect hai? Neend to nahi aayegi?

Mini-dialogue — chemist ki dukaan

Haalat: do din se khaansi hai. Aap chemist par ho.

  • Aap: Hi. Can you give me something for a cough? Seedha takleef — "something for a …".
  • Chemist: Is it a dry cough, or is there phlegm? phlegm (flem) = balgam.
  • Aap: It's dry. And my throat's a bit sore. "a bit" = thoda — bolchaal me bahut aam.
  • Chemist: Try this syrup. Two spoons, three times a day, after meals. Din me teen baar, khaane ke baad.
  • Aap: Great, thanks. How much is it? Kitne ka hai?

✗

I am having fever since two days.

✓

I've had a fever for two days.

have / have got

a fever

for

I've had

✗

My stomach is paining.

✓

My stomach hurts. / I've got a stomach ache.

hurt

…ache

docs.title: 38.3 Paisa aur bank — account se UPI tak
docs.text:
Bank aur paise ki English me zyada shabd nahi hain, bas har shabd ki sahi jodi chahiye: paisa withdraw karte ho, deposit karte ho, transfer karte ho, aur payment make karte ho — "do" nahi.

Shabd Matlab Jodi / example account khaata open a savings account balance khaate me kitna paisa check your balance deposit paisa jama karna deposit cash withdraw paisa nikaalna withdraw ₹2,000 from an ATM transfer ek khaate se doosre me transfer money to a friend loan karz take out / repay a loan interest byaaj an interest rate of 9% EMI har mahine ki kisht pay an EMI of ₹8,500 credited / debited aaya / gaya ₹500 was debited statement len-den ki list download a bank statement
  • I need to withdraw some cash. Is there an ATM nearby? Kuch cash nikaalna hai. Paas me ATM hai?
  • My salary is credited on the first of every month. Har mahine ki pehli taarikh ko salary aati hai.
  • The interest rate on this loan is nine per cent a year. Is loan par saalana 9% byaaj hai. (UK: per cent; US: percent.)
  • Money was debited from my account, but the payment failed. Paise kat gaye, par payment fail ho gaya. (Bank complaint ki pehli line.)

docs.title: EMI aur UPI — kisi foreigner ko English me samjhao
docs.text:
Ye dono shabd India me roz bolte hain, par bahar ke log nahi jaante. Agar kabhi samjhana pade, to ye do lines taiyaar rakho:

  • An EMI is a fixed amount you pay every month to repay a loan, including the interest. EMI = Equated Monthly Instalment — har mahine ki barabar kisht, byaaj samet.
  • UPI is a system that lets you send money instantly from your phone, straight from one bank account to another. UPI = Unified Payments Interface — phone se turant bank-se-bank paisa.
  • You just scan the QR code, enter the amount and your PIN, and it's done. QR scan karo, amount aur PIN daalo — ho gaya.
  • Can I pay by UPI, or is it cash only? UPI chalega ya sirf cash? (pay by card / UPI / cheque, pay in cash.)

pay by, pay in

Zariya batana ho to pay by card / UPI / cheque, aur nakad ke liye pay in cash (ya bas pay cash). "I'll pay from card" mat bolo — "I'll pay by card."

✗

Please do the payment by Friday.

✓

Please make the payment by Friday.

make

Please pay by Friday.

✗

Do you have change of 500?

✓

Do you have change for a 500-rupee note?

change for

docs.title: 38.4 Shopping aur returns — fit, exchange, refund
docs.text:
Dukaan me kapda try karna, size badalwana, online order wapas karna — in sab ke liye das-baarah shabd kaafi hain. Sabse zaroori verb hai fit: kapda size me theek hai ya nahi.
